m. a square coin of the value of half a pice; the Hindi adhēlā. Formerly in Kashmir articles of small value were purchased with cowries. Twelve cowries were called a bahāgañ ; twenty-five were called a pū̃ʦhuh ; fifty or half a…
fullMeaning: m. a square coin of the value of half a pice; the Hindi adhēlā. Formerly in Kashmir articles of small value were purchased with cowries. Twelve cowries were called a bahāgañ ; twenty-five were called a pū̃ʦhuh ; fifty or half a hundred were called ȧdi-hyoli -; a hundred was called a hath , and was considered the equivalent of one pice. In the rural parts of the country a pice is still called hath. Cf. bahāgañ, and RT.Tr. ii, 312.

fullMeaning: pron. suff. appended to the finite tenses of verbs, with the force of the acc. dat. or ag. sing. of the 1st pers.: me, to me, by me. If the verbal form to which it is added ends in a vowel, the a of the suffix is usually elided. Thus, karan , they will make, karan-am , they will make me or for me; koru , made, koru-m , made by me, I made. When added to the 3rd sing. fut. or to the fut. impve. the a is not elided, but, together with the final i of these forms, becomes ĕ. Thus, kari , he will make, karĕm , he will make me or for me; kȧrizi , you should make, kȧrizĕm you should make me or for me (Gr.Gr. 183).

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. -nāthas -) or ambar-nāth -, Lord of the Immortals, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 192); N. of a cave about 70 kōs east of Śrīnagar among the sources of the Sind River (Śiv. 114, 622). It contains a large block of transparent ice formed by the freezing of the water which issues from the rock. This is worshipped as a liṅga or emblem of Śiva Amarēśvara. It is a place of great sanctity, and the pilgrimage to it in the month of Śrāvaṇa or June-July attracts many thousands of people not only from Kashmīr but from all parts of India. The pilgrimage is one involving great hardships. See El. s.v., L. 41, and RT.Tr. II, 409. For a description of the modern pilgrimage, see Vigne, Travels, pp. 10 ff.

fullMeaning: pron. suff. of the 3rd pers. sg. in either the acc. or the ag. case, and added to any finite form of a verb. If the verbal form ends in a vowel, the initial a is dropped. Thus, karān chuh-an , thou makest him; koru-n , made by him, he made. If the verb be in the 3rd person, an in the sense of the acc. is not used, as being substituted, as in suh karān chu-s , not suh karān chu-n , he makes him (Gr.Gr. 185). an is also used to indicate the nom. case, when the nom. represents the object of a transitive verb in a past tense, as in trôwuth-an, he was released by thee, thou releasedst him (Gr.M. 1057), so mŏka- lôwuth-an (Śiv. 3).

fullMeaning: a primary suffix forming abstract nouns from certain verbal roots. In the case of three verbs whose roots end in ĕ (viz., chyonu , to drink; khyonu , to eat; and hyonu , to place) the initial a is dropped, and the abstract noun is masc. Thus, cĕn , drinking. In the case of the other verbs with which this suff. is used, the abs. noun is fem. A list of these verbs will be found in Gr.Gr. 120 ff.

m. a secondary suffix which, added to adjectives, forms abstract nouns. It is added to the m. sg. abl. of the adjective, the final i of which becomes y. This y, with the initial a of the suffix, usually becomes ĕ. The presence of…
fullMeaning: m. a secondary suffix which, added to adjectives, forms abstract nouns. It is added to the m. sg. abl. of the adjective, the final i of which becomes y. This y, with the initial a of the suffix, usually becomes ĕ. The presence of the y also causes certain changes in the final consonant of the base. Thus, popu , ripe, m. sg. abl. papi , hence papĕr , ripeness; but nyuku , little, m. sg. abl. niki , hence nicĕr , littleness. Some adjectives of three or more syllables take ār instead of ar . Thus wŏzulu , red, wŏzajyār , redness. For further particulars see Gr.Gr. 138 ff.

fullMeaning: card. c.g. (borrowed from Sanskrit), eight. The eight siddhis (Śiv. 115, 519) are the eight supernatural powers acquired by Yōgins. The ashṭa-dala hṛĕday (Śiv. 519), or eight-leaved heart, is the name of a mystic diagram used in the worship of Shiva. The ashṭa-mūrti (Śiv. 519), or eight forms of Shiva, are the five elements, the sun, the moon, and the sacrificing priest. Eight forms of Shiva are classed as Bhairavas (Śiv. 986). Cf. börav.

fullMeaning: an interjectional suff. used in addressing males. It means literally 'brother!', and is employed as follows:--hē nārān bā, O Nārān, in addressing a priest, a person of the middle class or a servant. If he is old, hata-sö-hē . . . bā or hata-bā-hē . . . bā is used. If a woman addresses a man or a woman respectfully she says hata-bā . . . bā, or if addressing a familiar or junior, hata-bā . . . au or hata-bā . . . a, or when addressing persons by their proper names only, hata-bā . . . a-bāyĕ or hata-bā . . . a-bāyau. Other words are often prefixed, as in ada-bā (v. ada), āhan-bā (v. āhan), and na-bā, No, sir. Cf. Gr.Gr. 99 ff., W. 101, and L. 279. For examples of its use see K.Pr. 49, 232; Śiv. 1244.

A man is born under that Zodiacal sign in which the moon happens to be situated at the moment of his birth. Taking that sign, together with the one immediately preceding it and the one immediately following it, the period of 7 1/2 years during which the planet Saturn is passing through these three signs is that man's baḍ-shĕrwār. Thus, suppose a man is born under Aries, his baḍ-shĕrwār is the 7 1/2 years during which Saturn is passing through Pisces, Aries, and Taurus. -watharū - m. a large rice-field (L. 463, where it is spelt bad wattru).

fullMeaning: f. a certain nominal coin, the value of the eighth part of a British pice. The latter is now used as the equivalent of the old nominal coin (representing a hundred cowries) called the hath or 'hundreder'. Bahāgañ therefore means 'a twelver' (for 'a twelve-and-a-halfer'). As sixty-four cowries now go to a pice, therefore a bahāgañ now equals eight cowries. Cf. ȧdi-hyoli and RT.Tr. ii, 312. bahāgañĕ-hondu - adj. (f. -hünzü -), of or belonging to eight cowries; costing eight cowries.

f. an exercise or game in schools, etc., in which one person recites a verse, and his opponent must immediately recite another verse, commencing with the last syllable of the verse just recited. The first person must then recite…
fullMeaning: f. an exercise or game in schools, etc., in which one person recites a verse, and his opponent must immediately recite another verse, commencing with the last syllable of the verse just recited. The first person must then recite another verse, commencing with the last syllable of the second verse, and so on till one fails and the other is declared conqueror. The game thus somewhat resembles our 'capping verses'.

m. a suffix forming nouns of place, either proper or common, as in Hazrat-bal, N. of a place (RT.Tr. II, 457); saba-bal, the place where a wedding dinner party is carried on; wura-bal, the place for the cooking-fires of a…
fullMeaning: m. a suffix forming nouns of place, either proper or common, as in Hazrat-bal, N. of a place (RT.Tr. II, 457); saba-bal, the place where a wedding dinner party is carried on; wura-bal, the place for the cooking-fires of a bridegroom's party; kō̃da-bal, a brick-kiln or a potter's kiln; graṭa-bal (K.Pr. 71), the site of a Persian wheel, a mill-house. The word is esp. used to indicate the presence of water or a place sacred to a minor deity or spirit; thus, Ganēsh-bal, N. of place (RT.Tr. II, 340); Shāradā-bal, N. of a place (ib. 279); Ganga-bal, N. of a famous bathing-place at the source of the Kashmīr Gaṅgā (ib. 407, Śiv. 1684); vĕtha-bal, any bathing-place on the River Vĕth or Jĕhlam; Mörü-bal, a bathing-place on the River Mār (RT.Tr. II, 416); Pŏkhari-bal, N. of a well-known bathing-place (Pushkara-nāga of ib. 476); krīri-bal, a well; yāra-bal, a bathing-place, a landing-place, quay (Śiv. 178, 1683, 1686); āwarĕñĕ-bal, a place where a funeral pyre is set up; shimashāna-bal, a burning ghāṭ; rāza-bal, a burning ghāṭ. The last three are always on the bank of a river. Cf. Gr.Gr. 165.

or , , the Persian privative particle, prefixed to other words, as in bē-adab, without politeness, insolent. It is equivalent in meaning to the Kāshmīrī suff. rostu (q.v.). Although a Persian prefix it is also commonly employed,…
fullMeaning: or , , the Persian privative particle, prefixed to other words, as in bē-adab, without politeness, insolent. It is equivalent in meaning to the Kāshmīrī suff. rostu (q.v.). Although a Persian prefix it is also commonly employed, usually under the form bĕ , with non-Persian words, as in bĕ-bayĕ, fearless. For words commencing with this prefix see s.vv. It is often used as a mere preposition, governing another noun, and meaning 'without', as in yilm bē bahs, knowledge without argument (K.Pr. 216). Similarly, adverbial phrases, such as bē sabab, without cause, causelessly.

fullMeaning: adj. c.g. a corruption of the Sanskrit Bhāskarīya, i.e. of or connected with a certain Kāshmīrī astronomer Bhāskara (not the famous Indian astronomer of the same name). Used in the following: bösi-nĕchapạtir, -, an almanac based on Ganēśa Daivajña's work entitled the Grahalāghava, which was introduced into Kashmīr by Bhāskara. In Kashmīr, Hindū almanacs have at different times been based on the calculations contained in various Sanskrit works. The oldest authority was the Āryasiddhānta (in use from the year 665 A.D.), which was in course of time (about 1758 A.D.) superseded by the Grahalāghava. Subsequently the Grahalāghava was again superseded by the Āryasiddhānta, but some almanac-makers still adhere to the Grahalāghava. Such almanacs, based on the Grahalāghava, are now known as bösi, or almanacs according to Bhāskara. See JRAS., 1912, pp. 719-21.

fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. bāchĕ ), a single long thin dried branch or twig of a tree or creeper, esp. of a willow cut off in pollarding. Cf. bāṭh 2. bāchĕ f.pl. twigs, esp. the bundles of leafed willow branches and twigs stored for winter fodder in the forks of tree-trunks; see bel. These stores are typical features of the landscape of the country. -gyoḍu m. a bunch of branches; a large mass of leafed tree branches cut in the autumn, tied together by a rope, and stored in the fork of a tree-trunk for use as required for fodder. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf., lit. to make (i.e. cut) branches; (of willows and the like) to pollard or cut off in the autumn of every second year the young withes or osier-twigs that shoot thickly in the spring from old lopping wounds. The smaller twigs and leaves are stored as above and used as fodder for sheep and goats during the winter. The larger are cut up and sold in the bazaar for firewood. -lôwu m. a branch- sheaf, a bundle of slender soft twigs cut from trees in the autumn as fodder for cattle.

(rarely an.) bĕyuku (f. bĕyücü ); pl. nom. m. biy or biyi , f. biyĕ or (c.g.) bĕyĕ ; dat. c.g. biyĕn ; ag. and abl. biyau ; gen. biyĕn-hondu - (f. -hünzü )], another, other, different (Śiv. 618; K.Pr. 242, sg. dat. written bĕyih); the other (Śiv. 1441); another one (pl. some), more, additional (Gr.M.). W. (34) spells this word bėyāk and (137) beyāk. -trākh pron., indef. adj., c.g. (sg. dat. biyis-triyis -, and so on, like byākh), anyone else, someone else. byākhüy adj. (declined as above with y added), altogether different; met. different from everything else, unsurpassed, beyond comprehension (K.Pr. 60). This word byākh is really an irregular compound of bi (q.v.) and akh, one. The obl. cases are those of bi, without akh, to which the emph. particle y has been added.

The tenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the twelfth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the twenty-eighth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirty-first) consonant…
fullMeaning: The tenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the twelfth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the twenty-eighth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirty-first) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the thirtieth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is pronounced, as in India proper, with the tip of the tongue touching the front teeth, and not the gums, the resulting sound being softer and more dental than in English. When this letter is immediately followed by ü or by y (including ĕ, see art. ĕ), it is changed to j. Thus, wôlu , a large ring,but fem. wöjü , a small ring; wūlu , fickle; wōjĕr , fickleness.

fullMeaning: m. a carpenter, a house carpenter (El., Śiv. 337, K.Pr. 41, 178, W. 140). His wife is chöñü 2 , chāna-kŏlay - or chāna-bāy -. Of these the first is generally used as a kind of surname, added to the woman's proper name. Regarding the other two see below. As a title (e.g. Yēkar chān, Yēkar, the carpenter) the gen. of this word is chānunu . chāna-bāy - f. a carpenter's wife. The word is honorific, cf. chāna-kŏlay bel. -kijü - or -kījü f. a carpenter's nail; the last and final nail put into a house by the builder, thus completing the work; met. in any work nearly completed the small amount remaining to be done. Kāshmīrī carpenters are constantly omitting a nail here or some work there in order that they may be recalled and get another job; this is called 'the carpenter's nail' (K.Pr. 41). -kŏlay f. a carpenter's wife. This word is non-honorific. Cf. chāna-bāy ab. and Gr.Gr. 34. -koṭu - m. a carpenter's son; met. a real carpenter's son, a good carpenter (Gr.Gr. 132). -ṭhas m. carpenter's bang, the noise made by a carpenter when he hits a piece of wood with the back of his adze. -ṭŏkh m. fullMeaning: f. the White River, N. of a certain river in Kashmīr, called in Sanskrit Śvētagaṅgā (White Ganges) or Dugdhagaṅgā (Milk Ganges). fullMeaning: adj. (f. dachiñü 2 ; for 1 see dachin), right, not left (K.Pr. 43, 57; H. viii, 7); dexterous, clever, expert (cf. atha-d.); of or belonging to the south, southern, coming from the south; (of a tract of country) situated on the right hand of the sun's course. Kāshmīrīs divide land in this way into 'right-hand' and 'left-hand' country. A 'right-hand' village is better for rice-cultivation than a 'left-hand' one (L. 435). (Note, in the Persian character, and in most works by Europeans founded on Kāshmīrī written in that character, this word is usually written dachun, or dachhun, with its abl. dachani for dachini or dachĕni, owing to the persistent confusion between ĕ and i and between cha and chĕ.) Cf. dachini and dakshin.

e: f. (sg. dat. dahümü ), the tenth lunar day of either fortnight of the luni-solar month. Cf. dahomu, dahum, and dahyumu. --kāh -- f. the tenth and eleventh lunar days, the name of a certain Hindū fast lasting three days. On the…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. dahümü ), the tenth lunar day of either fortnight of the luni-solar month. Cf. dahomu, dahum, and dahyumu. --kāh -- f. the tenth and eleventh lunar days, the name of a certain Hindū fast lasting three days. On the first day only one meal is taken, on the second nothing is eaten, and one meal is eaten in the forenoon of the third. --kāh karüñü -- f.inf. to carry out such a fast; to fast in this way for any three days as a penance for eating impure food or the like.

fullMeaning: m. a lake (Śiv. 1805, 1810); N. of a large lake near Śrīnagar (see El. s.v. and RT. Tr. II, 416; Śiv. 1823, 1841). -ḍuḍa - m. 'a Ḍal-sponger', a man who is in the habit of following picnic parties on the Ḍal lake, and joins them as an uninvited guest; cf. ḍuḍa. --darwāza -- m. the Ḍal gate, the flood-gate of the Ḍal lake. e: conj. 2 (pres. part. ḍalān , Śiv. 765, or ḍalan , Śiv. 910, 986, m.c.; 1 p.p. ḍolu , 2 p.p. ḍajyōv ), to be displaced, moved from one place to another (Śiv. 1569, 1800); to be spread abroad, diffused (of scent, K. 924; of sweat…
fullMeaning: conj. 2 (pres. part. ḍalān , Śiv. 765, or ḍalan , Śiv. 910, 986, m.c.; 1 p.p. ḍolu , 2 p.p. ḍajyōv ), to be displaced, moved from one place to another (Śiv. 1569, 1800); to be spread abroad, diffused (of scent, K. 924; of sweat bursting forth, see guma); to pass off, pass over, pass beyond, pass by or away (Gr.Gr. xxxii; governs abl. of thing passed over, Śiv. 1539, K. 1095); to walk about (El.); to slip, stumble (Gr.Gr. 5, Siv. 1743); to be moved, agitated, distraught (Śiv. 741, 765, 910, 986; Rām. 682, 1052, 1057, 1198; K. 1156, 1157). ḍolu-motu 1 - perf. part. (f. ḍüjü-müʦü -), removed from one place to another; passed over, changed; in a changed condition (Śiv. 1282).

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p.ḍôlu , 2. p.p. ḍājyōv ), to move (a thing) from one place to another, remove (a thing) (Śiv. 1055, 1249); to cause to pass over, to cause to pass by or away (Gr.Gr. 175); (with atha, q.v. for special…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p.ḍôlu , 2. p.p. ḍājyōv ), to move (a thing) from one place to another, remove (a thing) (Śiv. 1055, 1249); to cause to pass over, to cause to pass by or away (Gr.Gr. 175); (with atha, q.v. for special significations) to pass the hand over anything, to smoothe (K.Pr. 93, ḍolamut for ḍôlu-motu), to pat, touch affectionately (Śiv. 423, K. 682, 1148). ḍölith thawun 1 m.inf. (for 2 see ḍālun 3), to remove a thing and put it somewhere else, esp. with intent to deceive.

e: conj. 2 (1 p.p.ḍolu , 2 p.p. ḍajyōv ), to go wrong, be spoiled (lit. and met.). ḍolu-motu 2 - perf. part. (fem. ḍüjü-müʦü -), spoiled, etc. (YZ. 204).
conj. 1 (1p.p. ḍôlu , 2 p.p. ḍājyōv ), to mar, spoil.

conj. 1 (1 p.p.ḍôlu , 2 p.p. ḍājyōv ), to sift, winnow. Cf. adôlu. ḍöli ḍöli thawun m.inf. to winnow gradually and put by (of a large quantity of grain), to winnow bit by bit. ḍölith thawun 2 m.inf. (for 1 see ḍālun 1), to winnow.
conj. 1 (1 p.p.ḍôlu , 2 p.p. ḍājyōv ), to throw, fling, cast, hurl (Śiv. 1644); to apply, put into use, wield (e.g. a pen, Śiv. 1912).
f. a sieve; a winnowing basket, a winnowing scoop.
m. one who acts like a pimp (dala); an evil, mean fellow, one whose character is marked by covetousness, bad conduct, bad temper, and treachery.
adj. (f.dālüvü ), made of leather, leathern.
conj. 3, to pull a person's character to pieces behind his back, to talk scandal about, to backbite. Cf. dal 2.
m. backbiting, talking scandal; biyi-sondi dalwā̃zuvu karun, to talk scandal about another (K.Pr. 165).
adj. (f. ḍalwüñü ), that which is easily movable from one place to another, unstable, unsteady.
(spelling), adj. c.g. unfortunate (El.). Cf. drölid.
m. (sg. dat. dalinis ), husking (of grain, etc.), shredding; splitting, cleaving (timber, etc.); decortication. Cf. daliñ.
f. a rope for tying a cow, etc., a cattle-halter.
), deceit, fraud, trickery; coaxing, wheedling. - bôbu - m. a cheat who teaches others to cheat.

m. (with suff. of indef. art. dāmāh , Śiv. 1006, or dāmā , Śiv. 1434), drinking by suction (e.g. from the breast) (K. 109, 110); supping (as contrasted with putting liquid into the mouth with a spoon, or drinking from a cup)…
fullMeaning: m. (with suff. of indef. art. dāmāh , Śiv. 1006, or dāmā , Śiv. 1434), drinking by suction (e.g. from the breast) (K. 109, 110); supping (as contrasted with putting liquid into the mouth with a spoon, or drinking from a cup) (Śiv. 1109, Rām. 1035, 1522); (with cyonu, to drink) (to drink) a sup, (to take) a sip (Śiv. 1006, 1434, 1786); damā or dāmāh, see ab., a single sip. Cf. añĕma and dŏd. --dyunu -- m.inf. to drink gradually by suction, to suck, sup (as when one is not very thirsty) (K.Pr. 12); to suck (the breast) (Śiv. 1387, 1464). --ganḍun -- m.inf. to suck or sup down in large quantities at each gulp (as in extreme thirst). --lagun -- m.inf. to be used up (like water drunk by a thirsty person), to be all expended (as grain or money previously amassed). dāma cyonu m.inf. to drink by suction, to suck up, sup. --dāma -- adv. (drinking) by sips (Śiv. 1380).

e: m. (sg. abl. dama 3 ), restraint (as in Śiv. 1017, sŏra-dama, by restraining sound, i.e. by remaining silent, with pun on dam 1); self-restraint, in this sense often compounded with shĕm , tranquillity, shĕm-dam, tranquillity and…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. abl. dama 3 ), restraint (as in Śiv. 1017, sŏra-dama, by restraining sound, i.e. by remaining silent, with pun on dam 1); self-restraint, in this sense often compounded with shĕm , tranquillity, shĕm-dam, tranquillity and self-restraint (Śiv. 269, 931, 1033, 1404, 1754, 1811).

e: m. a snare, trap, gin (YZ. 17, where it is possibly confounded with the Hindī dām, a fetter).
m. a dwelling-place, house, abode, in param-dām -, the supreme abode, heaven (Śiv. 1659).
m. the cold experienced at the time of snowfall, great cold. -khāna - m. a very cold place, e.g. a very high mountain site.

m. a long kind of drum beaten at both ends (W. 3). Cf. ḍum-ḍum. ḍam-ḍam wāyun - m.inf. to beat such a drum; hence, to proclaim by beat of drum. ḍam-ḍam wāyĕnwôlu - n.ag. (f. ḍam-ḍam wāyĕnwājeñ - ), a drummer.
m. (for 1, 2, and 3 see dam 1, 2, and 3), the edge, thick flap, or border of the padded cap worn in cold weather.
m. a pair of bellows, cf. daman; asthma (W. 3).
f. the cross-bar across a window or doorway, on which one can lean the arms when sitting close to it, a window-sill.
m. a son-in-law, a daughter's husband or betrothed (among Musalmāns) (L. 267).
adj. c.g. possessing a padded edge or flap (of a cap or the like, for use in cold weather). Cf. dama 4.
f. the water-vessel for the hubble-bubble or huqqa.
f. insistence, vehement desire, exhibited by stamping the feet on the ground. Cf. damöli. damala-hamal karüñü - f.inf. to show or practise vehement insistence. damala-hamal lāgüñü - f.inf., id.
m. a large kind of drum with parchment at each end (not like a kettle-drum) (K. 1009).

m. a skirt, tail, hem, border (Rām. 1305), i.q. dāmāna. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize a person's skirt; met. to implore (Śiv. 179). Cf. dāmāna raṭun. --waṭun -- m.inf. to twist up the skirt, to fold up or lift up one's skirt (so as…
fullMeaning: m. a skirt, tail, hem, border (Rām. 1305), i.q. dāmāna. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize a person's skirt; met. to implore (Śiv. 179). Cf. dāmāna raṭun. --waṭun -- m.inf. to twist up the skirt, to fold up or lift up one's skirt (so as to save it from mud or from being torn by brambles, etc.) (Śiv. 1568).

e: f. (for 1 see dam 1; for 3, 4, see damun 1, 2; sg. dat. damüñü ), a bad smell, esp. the bad smell of stale curd or other food turned sour and gone bad.

m. a skirt, a hem, i.q. dāman, q.v. --chalun -- m.inf. to make a false accusation. -palav - m. the torn edge or skirt of a garment. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize by the skirt; met. to implore, beseech (Śiv. 1732). Cf. dāman raṭun.…
fullMeaning: m. a skirt, a hem, i.q. dāman, q.v. --chalun -- m.inf. to make a false accusation. -palav - m. the torn edge or skirt of a garment. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize by the skirt; met. to implore, beseech (Śiv. 1732). Cf. dāman raṭun. dāmānas mīṭhi dini m. pl. inf. to give kisses to the skirt, to kiss the hem of (a person's) garment, to show great humility (Śiv. 1150).

e: adj. c.g. skirted, having an embroidered skirt or border (of a garment).
f. the act of seizing the skirt, making an entreaty; esp. asking in marriage, proposals for marriage made by the relations of the bridegroom to those of the bride or vice versa.
adj. c.g. foul-smelling, corrupt-smelling (of sour milk or the like gone bad).
f. a woman's veil or mantle; a certain ornament worn on the fore- head.
m. the name given in schools to the syllable ddhaṁ , the final syllable of ēkaṁ siddhaṁ, the first words put down before writing the alphabet.
m. hypocrisy (Rām. 978).

m. the womb, uterus (of women or lower animals); the inner part or inside (of a dish or vessel); the core or centre of a post, pillar, or the like; core, centre generally; a certain aquatic vegetable (K.Pr. 149, also ḍumb).…
fullMeaning: m. the womb, uterus (of women or lower animals); the inner part or inside (of a dish or vessel); the core or centre of a post, pillar, or the like; core, centre generally; a certain aquatic vegetable (K.Pr. 149, also ḍumb). --lagun -- m. to conceive, become with child, become pregnant.

e: see ḍã̄b.
etc., see ḍã̄bal, etc.
c.g. a hypocrite.
see ḍã̄bulu.
see dã̄bur.
adj. (f. ḍambiñü ), i.q. ḍambyuku, q.v. under ḍọ̆mbu.
adv. (at) a moment (lit. one moment), cf. damiy, s.v. dam 1. damī . . . damī . . . adv. at one moment . . . at another moment, at one time . . . at another time (K.Pr. 47).
m., i.q. ḍȧmbi-kānul, see ḍọ̆mbu.
m. a kind of sweetmeat, ginger-candy. -khünḍü- f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ -), a lump of ginger-candy.

f. a piece of the stomach of a sheep or the like, as sold by butchers, sheep's paunch (K.Pr. 55); the stomach (El.). ḍamiñĕ-kalapushu - m. the entire stomach of a sheep, etc., a whole sheep's paunch, as sold by butchers. Cf.…
fullMeaning: f. a piece of the stomach of a sheep or the like, as sold by butchers, sheep's paunch (K.Pr. 55); the stomach (El.). ḍamiñĕ-kalapushu - m. the entire stomach of a sheep, etc., a whole sheep's paunch, as sold by butchers. Cf. ḍȧmbi-kalapushi under ḍọ̆mbu. ḍamiñĕ-māwas - m. a certain festival held on the day of the new moon of the month of Phāgun (February-March), on the night of which pieces of sheep's paunch are offered by Hindūs to Bhairavas or Böravs.

e: m. having a rope round the waist, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 1334).

f. stamping the feet on the ground, a stamp (K.Pr. 202); a religious exercise, ecstatic and frenzied dancing at the shrine of a saint (L. 289, 459). damāli-phakīr - m. a bullying mendicant faqīr, one who, when his wishes are not…
fullMeaning: f. stamping the feet on the ground, a stamp (K.Pr. 202); a religious exercise, ecstatic and frenzied dancing at the shrine of a saint (L. 289, 459). damāli-phakīr - m. a bullying mendicant faqīr, one who, when his wishes are not granted, stamps violently on the ground (K.Pr. 10).

e: m. a drummer, one whose business it is to make proclamation by beat of drum.

conj. 1 (pres. part. damān , or, Śiv. 1854, daman 3 ; 1 p.p. domu ), to blow up a fire (with bellows or the mouth); as vb. impers. in past tenses (past domun ), to roar (of wind or a blast of air on fire) (Gr.Gr. xxxviii); to…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (pres. part. damān , or, Śiv. 1854, daman 3 ; 1 p.p. domu ), to blow up a fire (with bellows or the mouth); as vb. impers. in past tenses (past domun ), to roar (of wind or a blast of air on fire) (Gr.Gr. xxxviii); to roar (as a wild beast) (Śiv. 1854). domu-motu - perf. part. (f. dümü-müʦü -), blown up (with bellows or by the mouth, of fire).

e: m. (sg. dat. damanas ), a pair of bellows (K.Pr. 46). For daman 1 see dam 1, for 2 see s.v., for 3 see damun 1, for 4 see bel. daman-basta - f. the leather bag, alternately inflated with and emptied of air, used as the body of a…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. damanas ), a pair of bellows (K.Pr. 46). For daman 1 see dam 1, for 2 see s.v., for 3 see damun 1, for 4 see bel. daman-basta - f. the leather bag, alternately inflated with and emptied of air, used as the body of a bellows (K.Pr. 46). -nôru - m. the metal nozzle or pipe of a pair of bellows.

e: m. the hilt or handle of a sword; a handle (El.) (of a hammer, see dŏkuru); the handle of a drawer (Gr.M.).

m. an earthen fire-place, esp. one with orifices for cooking, a cooking-stove, oven (Gr.Gr. 10, El., K.Pr. 25, 85, 101, 134, 164, 171, 255, W. 144, K. 161). --karun -- m.inf. to make a cooking-stove, to build a temporary mud…
fullMeaning: m. an earthen fire-place, esp. one with orifices for cooking, a cooking-stove, oven (Gr.Gr. 10, El., K.Pr. 25, 85, 101, 134, 164, 171, 255, W. 144, K. 161). --karun -- m.inf. to make a cooking-stove, to build a temporary mud fire-place; hence, to stop on the road (on a journey) for cooking food (K.Pr. 87). dāna-büṭhü - f. the fire-place of a cooking-stove; i.e. the middle portion of the flat top of a cooking-stove, on which vessels are placed on removal from the open fire. -ḍākh - m. (sg. dat. -ḍākas -), the plastered earth on the top of a stove, burnt red by the heat. -dĕv - m. a cooking-stove demon; a kind of demon, ever gorging himself with food, and having the form of a cooking-stove. -gȧji - or -güjü - f. the stokehole near the bottom of a cooking-stove, through which it is fed with fuel. -golu 1 - m. (for dānagolu 2 see s.v.), the opening of such a stokehole. -goru - m. (f. -gürü -), a man who is skilled in making cooking-stoves, one whose profession is to build such. -mīr - m. a fire-place prince, a big fire-place, a large cooking-stove (K.Pr. 48). -ʦôru - m. the openings on the top of a stove on which vessels are put for the purpose of cooking. -zang - f. offerings made for good luck when a cooking-stove is lit for the first time.

e: m. (properly) a bow (the weapon), but for this the usual word is danŏrdanḍ, q.v.; this word usually indicates Sagittarius, the sign of the zodiac (Rām. 1259, 1261, 1275, K. 132). -lạgan - m. a certain astronomical period, the…
fullMeaning: m. (properly) a bow (the weapon), but for this the usual word is danŏrdanḍ, q.v.; this word usually indicates Sagittarius, the sign of the zodiac (Rām. 1259, 1261, 1275, K. 132). -lạgan - m. a certain astronomical period, the first six ghaṛis or periods of twenty minutes commencing with the rising of Sagittarius. -rāsh - f. the sign Sagittarius.

e: m. a gift, a present; esp. a gift in charity or for pious purposes (Śiv. 1148, Rām. 73, 390, etc.). --dyunu -- m.inf. to give charity (K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 428). --karun -- m.inf. to give charity (Gr.M.). dāna-rostu - adj. (f. -rüʦhü…
fullMeaning: m. a gift, a present; esp. a gift in charity or for pious purposes (Śiv. 1148, Rām. 73, 390, etc.). --dyunu -- m.inf. to give charity (K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 428). --karun -- m.inf. to give charity (Gr.M.). dāna-rostu - adj. (f. -rüʦhü -), wanting in charitable gifts, one who does not give in charity (Śiv. 1738).

e: m. prosperity, good luck, used in the following: dan-bāgĕ - m. praising for benefits received, thanks; good luck, good fortune (Śiv. 494, 821).

(spelling), the Indian chestnut, Ӕsculus indica (L. 70). It is lopped to provide cattle fodder for the winter. On p. 75 L. calls this hunak dun, and states that as a medicine it has cathartic properties. Cf. ḍūnu and hānakh-ḍūnu.

m. a tooth, used for dand, q.v., in the following: -dag - f. toothache. -dawāh - m. medicine for a tooth, a cure for toothache. -ṭakar - m.pl. chattering of the teeth (from ague, cold, or the like). Cf. dand-ṭakar and ḍanṭakar.…
fullMeaning: m. a tooth, used for dand, q.v., in the following: -dag - f. toothache. -dawāh - m. medicine for a tooth, a cure for toothache. -ṭakar - m.pl. chattering of the teeth (from ague, cold, or the like). Cf. dand-ṭakar and ḍanṭakar. -ṭakar aʦȧni - m. pl. inf. an attack of chattering of the teeth to come on. --ṭuwȧni -- m. pl. inf. to close the teeth; met. to speak slowly and deliberately in order to avoid dealing with the relevant matter of a conversation. Cf. dand ṭuwȧni. dȧni-tij - or dȧni-tuji - a toothpick. Cf. dȧndi-tij under dand.

e: (dönü) in dān chö̃ch, f. the blackberry, Rubus fruticosus (L. 73, dhán chánch). Cf. chö̃ch and dönü.
m. the stalk of an apple or pear (El.). Cf. dan 1. -kāḍ - m. a mixture of refuse husks, stalks, etc., of vegetables, etc.
f. (sg. dat. döñü ), a stream (of water or the like, as poured from, or into, a vessel) (noted only in L.V. 39, 40).
see dana 1.
m. being dashed to pieces, of someone or something falling from a height or the like (used esp. in abuse); met. sudden death, however caused.
or -dakh - m. (sg. dat. -dakas -), i.q. dañ-dab, q.v.
m. inḍañ-ḍañ karun - m.inf. to make the sound of ḍañ-ḍañ', to show the hollowness of anything (lit. or met.) by ringing it.
see dönü.
see ḍã̄.

m. grain, corn (K. 1088); a grain, seed (Śiv. 468, of a pomegranate; Rām. 1029, 1126); chick-pea, 'gram' (used for feeding horses) (K.Pr. 71); food generally (K.Pr. 100); a speck, a tiny quantity of anything (Rām. 700); a bead; a…
fullMeaning: m. grain, corn (K. 1088); a grain, seed (Śiv. 468, of a pomegranate; Rām. 1029, 1126); chick-pea, 'gram' (used for feeding horses) (K.Pr. 71); food generally (K.Pr. 100); a speck, a tiny quantity of anything (Rām. 700); a bead; a drop; a pimple, pustule; --˚ seed of such and such a plant. According to El. s.v. the word also means 'steel'. --dāna -- adv. grain by grain, drop by drop (Rām. 168, 286, 698, 1419). --dyunu -- m.inf. to give 'gram' to a horse, to feed a horse. --dyutu-motu --- m. fed, given 'gram' (of a horse); met. reaping the fruits of former actions done in this or a previous birth, these actions being represented as seeds from which spring the results. -lë̆dürü - f. the root of a certain medicinal plant, Berberis sp., which root is good for horses (L. 76, spelt dand-lidar).

e: adj. c.g. and subst. m. wise, learned, clever (W. 22); a wise man, a sage (K.Pr. 47). In Matt. xi, 25, the pl. dat. is written dānahan .

m. a kind of club used in a certain game, in which one club is thrown on the ground and struck with another so as to propel it beyond a boundary-line. -kini phirun - m.inf. to retort, advance arguments on the other side. danan…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of club used in a certain game, in which one club is thrown on the ground and struck with another so as to propel it beyond a boundary-line. -kini phirun - m.inf. to retort, advance arguments on the other side. danan gindun m.inf. to play the ab. game.

e: adj. c.g. granulated; of a granulated appearance; containing grain; bearing fruit in the form of seeds enclosed in a capsule or husk (e.g. a pomegranate).
m. (for 1 see dān 1), N. of a place about 60 miles north of Śrīnagar, the entrance to the Śāradā-kṣētra, or tract made holy by the shrine of the goddess Śāradā. (Cf. RT.Tr. II, 279 ff.)
see dānā.
(L. 464), i.q. dānay, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. danüña ), shaking violently, the act of shaking out dust, etc., from a garment, cloth, papers, or the like. --diñü -- f.inf. to shake down grain in a basket or other receptacle so as to fill it. --gaʦhüñü -- f.inf.…

(sg. dat. danüña ), shaking violently, the act of shaking out dust, etc., from a garment, cloth, papers, or the like. --diñü -- f.inf. to shake down grain in a basket or other receptacle so as to fill it. --gaʦhüñü -- f.inf. sudden shaking or shivering of the body to occur, e.g. when suddenly coming in sight of something ill-omened, or suddenly coming within range of some foul smell.

e: f. any long and difficult business, esp. when it is of no value or useless.
m. a certain kind of demon, the Dānava of Sanskrit literature (Śiv. 704).
m. thanks (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to thank (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. danowa ), i.q. danun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. xl).
f. a tax paid by possessors of sheep, a sheep-tax (L. 464).

or ḍanḍ m. (sg. abl. danḍa 1 or ḍanḍa 1 ), punishment, chastisement, imprisonment, fine (K.Pr. 106, ḍanḍ), corporal punishment, etc.; divine punishment for sin (Śiv. 1912). --dyunu -- m.inf. to punish, to fine (Gr.M.); to pay a…

(sg. abl. danḍa 1 or ḍanḍa 1 ), punishment, chastisement, imprisonment, fine (K.Pr. 106, ḍanḍ), corporal punishment, etc.; divine punishment for sin (Śiv. 1912). --dyunu -- m.inf. to punish, to fine (Gr.M.); to pay a fine (Gr.M.). --hyonu -- m.inf. to take a fine, to fine a person. --karun -- m.inf. to punish (Śiv. 1481, to mutilate). --pyonu -- m.inf. a fine to fall, a fine or punishment to be incurred; ʦĕ pĕyiy danḍ, you will be punished (Gr.M.). danḍa 1 (ḍanḍa) barun , m.inf. to give compensation for harm, damage, loss, or the like occurring to anything borrowed or taken in deposit. --baray -- , f. the payment of such compensation. --dyunu -- , m.inf. to give compensation for loss of or damage as ab. (H. v, 11). --hyonu -- , m.inf. to take in compensation as ab. (H. v, 11). --khārun -- m.inf. to make a claim for compensation as ab. --khasun -- m.inf. to have a claim for such compensation made against one.

e: see dã̄d.
in dand-lidar, see dāna lë̆dürü, s.v. dāna.
or ḍanḍa 2 m. a pole, a post, staff, rod; the pole supporting the hinged mat roof of a boat; a pestle (El.).

or ḍanḍa 3 f.pl. a certain gymnastic exercise (the hands and feet are placed on the ground, and the body swung backwards and forwards from the wrists and ankles). --karañĕ -- f.inf. to perform this exercise.
f. a toothache, i.q. danda-dag under dand.
m. the name of a celebrated forest in the Deccan, the Daṇḍaka-vana of Sanskrit literature (Śiv. 556; Rām. 208, 272, 284, 321, 369, 1144, 1777).
adj. (as subst., f. dandöñü ), toothed, fanged, tusked; one who is disfigured by ugly projecting front teeth or incisors (Gr.Gr. 137, K.Pr. 49).
dānduru , etc., see dā̃dar.
m. the bark of the walnut-tree (El.; L. 352 has dandarsa).
m. (sg. dat. danḍawatas ), prostration of the body, obeisance (K. 133).

fullMeaning: m. 'the destroyer of the ten (kinds of sin)', N. of a certain rare astronomical conjunction occurring on the (1) tenth lunar day of the (2) light half of the month of (3) Zēṭh (Sanskrit Jyaiṣṭha) when, on that day, (4) the moon is in the asterism Hasta, (5) the weekday is Wednesday, (6) the karaṇa, or second half of the lunar day, is Gara, (7) there is vyatīpāta (i.e. when the sum of the longitudes of the sun and the moon amounts to not less than 213˚ 20' and not more than 226˚ 40'), (8) there is the Ānanda yōga (this seems to be a name for the first ghatikā, or twenty-four minutes, also for the twenty-ninth and fifty-seventh ghaṭikās on a Wednesday), (9) the moon is in Kanyā (Virgo), (10) and the sun in Vṛṣabha (Taurus). Bathing at the confluence of the Ganges and the Jumna, and similar sacred spots, with appropriate offerings, is believed by Hindūs to be very efficacious on this occasion (K.Pr. 44, where it is confounded with dashĕhār 2; Śiv. 1793, with pun on dashĕhār 3). This conjunction last occurred in Samvat 1944, equivalent to June 1, 1887.

m. redemption by the tenth (Sanskrit daśamōddhāra), N. of a certain mystic exercise practised by Yōgīs (Śiv. 1655). There are, according to their teaching, ten essential elements (Sanskrit, dhātu) of the body, viz. in order of…
fullMeaning: m. redemption by the tenth (Sanskrit daśamōddhāra), N. of a certain mystic exercise practised by Yōgīs (Śiv. 1655). There are, according to their teaching, ten essential elements (Sanskrit, dhātu) of the body, viz. in order of production, skin (tvak), blood (asṛk), flesh (māṁsa), fat (mēdaḥ), bone (asthi), marrow (majjā), semen (śukra), vital breath (prāṇa), soul (jīva), and energy (śakti). In this system there are also ten (not the usual nine; cf. dwār) doors or openings of the human body, viz. two nostrils, two eye-orifices, two ear-orifices, two mouth-orifices (the windpipe and gullet), and two orifices of excretion. The tenth and most excellent of the bodily elements, i.e. energy, operates through the orifice of rapture, i.e. the urethra (ānandadvāra or śukradvāra), here compared to immortality-giving ambrosia (amṛtātmaśukradvāra). Uddhāra means 'redemption', and the whole compound therefore means redemption brought about by operating the supreme and most excellent of the bodily powers.

Root crops and the like are grown upon them. -ʦakh - m. peat (L. 62).

e: m. pain, agony, anguish, mental (YZ. 574, K.Pr. 167, Rām. 291, 1422) or physical (K.Pr. 23, 53, 65, 76); the pain of sickness, sickness (Śiv. 1855, dödis dag, the pain of sickness); sickness, ailment, disease (El.). The part of…
fullMeaning: m. pain, agony, anguish, mental (YZ. 574, K.Pr. 167, Rām. 291, 1422) or physical (K.Pr. 23, 53, 65, 76); the pain of sickness, sickness (Śiv. 1855, dödis dag, the pain of sickness); sickness, ailment, disease (El.). The part of the body in which pain is felt is put in the dat. Thus, dandas dôdu, a pain in the tooth, toothache; kalas d., a headache; kalējas d., liver complaint; kanas d., earache; zuwas d., pain in the body (Gr.M.). On the other hand, dazanas d., there is pain from a burn (K.Pr. 54); nafsa d., difficulty of breath, breathlessness (YZ. 398); pŏtra d., grief for a (dead) son (YZ. 417), grief of a barren woman longing for a son (K.Pr. 174); andarimi dödi, internal pains, heart-grief (K.Pr. 13). Cf. dag 1. --āsun -- m.inf. to suffer pain, be pained (El.). --hyuhu -- m. something like pain, a feeling of pain. --karun -- m.inf. to ache, be painful (Gr.M.). --lagun -- or --sapadun -- m.inf. to suffer pain, be pained (El.). dādi-sostu - adj. (f. -süʦhü ), pained, suffering pain (Rām. 242). dödi-kôṭi - adj. (f. -köṭü ), grieved, afflicted (El.). (The spelling of this word is doubtful; El. spells dãdkóṭ.) The word is probably incorrect for -kôṭhu, see under dôdu 3.

fullMeaning: m. a pomegranate (the fruit), Punica granatum (L. 73, 348, 350, dán; K.Pr. 146, dain; Śiv. 468). According to El. s.v. there are three varieties of this fruit grown in Kashmīr: ʦọ̆ku dönu, mŏdur d., and jigari d. The pomegranate ripens in September, and is of inferior quality. The word is declined in Gr.Gr. 54. -bạrag - m. the leaf of a pomegranate-tree. -dĕl - m. the soft outer skin of a pomegranate. -hüṭü - f. the wood of the pomegranate-tree, esp. the split wood. -kuji - or -kujü - f. a small pomegranate-tree. -kulu - m. a pomegranate-tree (El.), esp. when large and full-grown. -künḍü - f. the hard outer shell of a pomegranate. -mūrü - f. the young non-fruit-bearing shoot or branch of a pomegranate-tree. -mŏrba - m. pomegranate conserve. -pholu - m. a single pomegranate seed. -pōsh - m. a pomegranate flower (YZ. 527, Rām. 644). -ras - m. pomegranate juice. -shīra - m. a drink made of pomegranate juice and used as a cooling medicine. -thürü - f. a pomegranate bush, a bushy young pomegranate-tree.

fullMeaning: or ḍũ̄̈ga m. a kind of covered boat for passengers with their baggage and servants, and in which the passengers also live (Śiv. 1488, 1683); a ferry-boat (Gr.M.); ḍũ̄̈ga is the boatmen's pronunciation. For an account of this boat see L. 381 (dúnga); ḍū̃gas kĕth, in a boat (Śiv. 1780). -rakh - f. (sg. dat. -rakhi ), the mark on the boat. A man is supposed to drop a cooking-vessel overboard, and to make a mark on the side of the boat where it fell over. Then, when the boat arrives at its destination and the pot is sought for, he points out the mark and says, "here is where it fell overboard, let us dive here for it." Hence, any useless mark made by a fool. -hönzü - m. (his wife is -hānzañ -), a boatman of a ḍū̃ga.

(Gr.Gr. 36). --parmūzun -- m.inf. to wipe out the pot; esp. on the festival of the Śivarātri (commencing on the 11th of the dark half of the month of Phāgun = Feb.-March) ceremonially to empty into a lake or river the contents of a large cooking pot as an offering to the village tutelary deity (kṣētrapāla). ḍuli barȧni m. pl. inf. to fill the pots, to perform the Hindū rite of ceremonially touching a vessel containing fragrant objects, preparatory to offering them to the village tutelary deities Vaṭukanātha and other Bhairavas (see börav). fullMeaning: m. a door, gate, passage, entrance (Śiv. 688, 829, 955, 972, 1033, 1099, 1473, 1911, esp. 1074-82; K. 71, 73, 79, 1123, 1161, etc.); an opening or aperture in the human body (of which there are nine, viz. the mouth, the two ears, the two eyes, the two nostrils, and the organs of excretion and generation; but according to others there are ten, made up by counting the windpipe and gullet separately; cf. dashĕmōddār) (Śiv. 340, 520, 1078, 1469). dwāra-köñü - f. the wood collected for building the framework of a house; the entire wooden framework of a house below the attics, including door-posts, etc. See köñü 4. -pūz or -pūzā - f. the worship of the inferior deities at the entrance to a temple; met. the propitiation of the underlings hanging round the entrance to a royal court or the like by one who desires to obtain an audience; (on the occasion of marriages, etc.) the ceremony of worshipping the god of the threshold (Śiv. 1073, 1074, 1097).

The sixth (or, if we count the aspirate ch as a separate letter, the seventh) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet, the third consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the twenty-ninth consonant when written in…
fullMeaning: The sixth (or, if we count the aspirate ch as a separate letter, the seventh) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet, the third consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the twenty-ninth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of the letter g in the English 'game'. The Sanskrit aspirate sonant gha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the gh is representedby g . Thus, the Hindī ghōṛā , a horse, is represented in Kāshmīrī by guru . Some writers retain this gh in writing. Thus, they write for gara , a house, on the analogy of the Hindī ; but this custom is both useless and misleading. In the present work such words will always be spelt with g , and hence words found in any native book spelt with should be looked up in the English order under g . The character is named gagar-gö, and gösi-ga. The letter sometimes occurring in words borrowed from Arabic or Persian is also represented in Kāshmīrī by g, like which it is pronounced. Thus is pronounced gölib.

fullMeaning: (Śiv. 1278) or gȧnish (Śiv. 1160), m. N. of a certain Hindū god, Gaṇēśa. He was the son of Śiva and Pārvatī and was the god of wisdom and of obstacles. (sg. dat.gardüñü , Rām. 16, 825, 850, 853), the neck (K.Pr. 73, YZ. 146, Rām. 37, 299, 370, etc.); met. decapitation, beheading (K.Pr. 27). --diñü --- f.inf. to decapitate, behead (Rām. 816; H. ii, 8, tas, him). gardañĕ ganḍ m. the articulation of the neck, a name given to the nape of the neck, the cervical ligament.

e: f. wandering, change; revolution; --˚ downfall, misfortune, affliction; (in Kāshmīrī) a circle (El.).
payment, tribute; an alienation of a portion of the revenue of a village in favour of someone (L. 449).
see gürü 1.
m. hardness (lit. and fig.), solidity.
adj. c.g. poor, destitute (K.Pr. 66, 75; W. 118; YZ. 241; Rām. 72, 141, 1135, 1734, 1739); meek, mild; humble, lowly.
f. poverty, indigence; meekness, mildness, lowliness, humility.
adj. c.g. one who is affected by continual longing, unsatisfied even by the attainment of the desired object, but who is still wishing for more and more.
f. a good housewife, a woman who manages her house well (Gr.Gr. 38).
f. an unconscientious woman (?), only noted in K.Pr. 132 (garin), where it is so translated.
m. a bell-ringer, a man whose business it is to strike a gong at certain hours of the day (K.Pr. 67, W. 154); a small bell (El.).

adj. c.g. hot, warm (W. 112, Rām. 1198); in a state of heat; fervid, ardent, zealous; fiery, choleric; warm, rich (e.g. a man or a place of pilgrimage) (K.Pr. 236); active, lively, brisk (as a market) (Rām. 139); (of news)…
fullMeaning: adj. c.g. hot, warm (W. 112, Rām. 1198); in a state of heat; fervid, ardent, zealous; fiery, choleric; warm, rich (e.g. a man or a place of pilgrimage) (K.Pr. 236); active, lively, brisk (as a market) (Rām. 139); (of news) exciting, arousing, causing energy (Rām. 777, 798); as subst. the hot season.

e: f. heat, warmth (W. 112, Siv. 27); hot weather, the hot season; activity, briskness, fierceness, vehemence; sexual passion, lust, heat; fever, the venereal disease.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. garmyōv ), to be hot (Gr.Gr. xviii).
f. weight, burden; heaviness, gravity; heaviness of spirit, depression, grief, vexation (Rām. 1461); scarceness, scarcity, dearth, dearness.

m. Garuḍa, N. of a bird celebrated in Hindū myth as chief of the feathered race and enemy of the serpent race. He was the vehicle of the god Viṣṇu (Vishnu) (Śiv. 720, 732, 793, 1324; Rām. 398, 598, 600).
m. he who sits upon Garuḍa, i.e. whose vehicle is Garuḍa (see garuḍ), N. of the Hindū god Viṣṇu (Vishnu) (Śiv. 160, 1407).
adj. c.g. drowned, immersed; met. overwhelmed (with), buried (in), smothered (in) (something material) (Rām. 141, buried under heaps of gold).

or gaḍun conj. 1 (1 p.p. goru 4 or goḍu , for 1, 2, 3 see s.vv.), to make, form, fashion, put together (as a carpenter); to forge, to work metals (H. v, 5); to malleate, to mould. kalam garun, to mend a pen (Gr.M.). -ʦarun -…

(of living beings) to be hardened, to become obstinate in refusing to do anything, to jib; (of things or actions) to be hard, difficult (Gr.Gr. 169).

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. gôru 2 , for 1 see s.v.), to search eagerly for (Rām. 439, 1487); to remember affectionately, to miss (a friend), every now and then to think of a person and long for his presence and assistance; to inquire (El.);…

(f. görü-müʦü -), missed, longed for, as ab.

e: m. a wooden stand for supporting a water-jar (Hindī ghaṛō̃cā).

m. rubbing down, grinding between two stones (e.g. of sandal-wood) (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunu -- m.inf. to grind down, rub down, abrade, rub smooth; to criticize a person over and over again. gasa āmotu perf. part. (f. --āmüʦü --),…
fullMeaning: m. rubbing down, grinding between two stones (e.g. of sandal-wood) (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunu -- m.inf. to grind down, rub down, abrade, rub smooth; to criticize a person over and over again. gasa āmotu perf. part. (f. --āmüʦü --), worn down, worn away by constant use. --yunu --- m.inf. to be worn away by constant use.

e: for gāsa, in the following: gās-phūs - m. old dry grass or straw; weeds; met. (of clothes or used papers) worthless, only fit to be thrown away.

adj. c.g. ordurous, horribly ugly and filthy (usually of something inanimate).

m. fainting, becoming insensible, swoon (e.g. from hunger, grief, etc.) (Śiv. 499, 1454, Rām. 396). --gaʦhȧni -- m. pl. inf. faintings or insensibility to occur, esp. of coma when a person is at the point of death, or of fainting…
fullMeaning: m. fainting, becoming insensible, swoon (e.g. from hunger, grief, etc.) (Śiv. 499, 1454, Rām. 396). --gaʦhȧni -- m. pl. inf. faintings or insensibility to occur, esp. of coma when a person is at the point of death, or of fainting from extreme hunger.

e: adj. c.g. light (not dark) (El.).
adj. c.g. rubbed away, worn away, worn thin (e.g. a coin).
m. silence (Gr.Gr. 138), esp. acting with heedlessness of consequences, even though warned beforehand. Cf. goshu 1 and 2.
m. brightness, brilliancy, voc. gāshĕra, O thou who art brightness personified! (Rām. 217).
f. (sg. dat. (?) güshüʦü ), an unchaste woman, esp. one who is such with some discretion, a woman disposed to unchastity.
f. a woman who behaves as if she were a prostitute, one disposed to unchastity.
adj. c.g. rubbed down, worn down, with the impression worn off (of a coin or the like).
see gahun.
m. strolling, walking (El.).
m. the time of brightness, i.e. either the light of early dawn or just before nightfall, twilight.
see gahun.
f. (sg. dat. gasīṭi ), the condition of being crowded or tightly packed (of a room, a receptacle, etc.).
see gas.
adj. (f. gāsüvü ), made of straw or grass; met. of no value, worthless (K.Pr. 18).

fullMeaning: m. profound insensibility, a dead faint, being like one dead. --mārȧni -- - m. pl. inf. 'to strike faintings', nearly to die over and over again; met. (with reference to an insect fluttering round a candle at the risk of its life) to walk round and round a thing to inspect it, to be fascinated or infatuated by anything so that one cannot leave it, but must admire it on all sides and long for it (Śiv. 1609; K.Pr. 42, of a man flaunting his clothes, mārān gatai for gata-y). --yunu -- m.inf. fainting to occur (generally). gatan aʦun m.inf. to enter dead faints, to become comatose when at the point of death.

e: f. darkness, obscurity (K.Pr. 67, 193; Siv. 104, 1040, 1066; Rām. 295, 417, 1596, 1610); the shade or darkness thrown by dense black clouds. Cf. Gr.Gr. 72. Cf. añi-gaṭa, p. 31a, l. 16, and Rām. 92, 1257. -kār - m. darkness, gloom…

(sg. dat. -karanas tāpas - ), violent and distressing heat of the sun. -pach - m. (sg. dat. -pachas -), the dark fortnight of a lunar month, the fortnight of the waning moon (L. 354, Śiv. 166). -zolu - m. a dull light, very little light, a glimmer of light just showing on a dark night or through black clouds.

e: m. skill, cleverness, intelligence; wisdom, discrimination, judgment (K.Pr. 87, 218; Śiv. 1212, with pun on gāṭa 2; H. i, 6). -ȧthi - adv. with the hand of skill, cleverly, intelligently, skilfully. --dyunu -- m.inf. to give…
fullMeaning: m. skill, cleverness, intelligence; wisdom, discrimination, judgment (K.Pr. 87, 218; Śiv. 1212, with pun on gāṭa 2; H. i, 6). -ȧthi - adv. with the hand of skill, cleverly, intelligently, skilfully. --dyunu -- m.inf. to give wisdom, to teach (El.). --ʦüñü -- f. conceit for one's own cleverness (whether entitled to entertain such conceit or not); having a high opinion of one's own wisdom or cleverness.

e: m. falling short, insufficiency, failure, want (Śiv. 1212, with pun on gāṭa 1). --pyonu -- m.inf. falling short to occur; expectations to fall short, loss to occur in place of profit.
see gatula.
m. swiftness of the current of a river; met. a rapid torrent (of words), a quick inrush (of wealth), and so on.
m. wisdom, cleverness, skilfulness; vigilance, prudence (El.). gāṭajyāruku jawāb, an answer of intelligence, a pertinent answer (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. gaṭaki ), darkness; esp. spiritual darkness (L.V. 104).
adj. c.g. blackened, darkened, disgraced (of personal character, family, etc.).

m. (sg. dat. gaṭapas ), sudden and unexpected death or destruction without any apparent cause (such as sickness, a blow, or the like). gaṭapa adv. suddenly, unexpectedly (u.w. vbs. of hindering or the like).
m. a kind of gold or silver embroidery, worn by rich women on the borders of their garments, or used as a braid on military uniforms.
conj. 1(1 p.p. gạṭarôwa ), to make dark, to turn (light) into darkness, to turn (day) into night (Śiv. 350).
m. being hacked or cut to pieces (esp. w. reference to the limbs of a human being). Cf. güñü 1.

m. (sg. dat. gaṭāṭōpas ), a covering for a palanquin, carriage, or any article of furniture, etc. (so as to shade or darken it); met. a tumult, a terribly involved battle (in which darkness, preventing recognition of friend or…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. gaṭāṭōpas ), a covering for a palanquin, carriage, or any article of furniture, etc. (so as to shade or darken it); met. a tumult, a terribly involved battle (in which darkness, preventing recognition of friend or foe, is caused by the confused multitude of combatants).

e: f. (sg. dat. gati , Gr.Gr. 70), great swiftness or rapidity of the current of a river or the like, a swift flood (Śiv. 1830); a rise in a river (Gr.Gr. 70).
f. (sg. dat. ?), choking caused by too greedily drinking. -gōjĕ - f.pl. uncertainty as to the complete success of any enterprise.
m. a knot (K.Pr. 76), see bar 1, p. 116b, l. 40.

m. (sg. dat. gātas ), a blot, stain (in character) (Śiv. 1554, Rām. 1667); disgrace (in a family). --dyunu -- m.inf. to give a stain; to bring a disgraceful charge (justified or unjustified) against a person.

m. (sg. dat. gāṭhas ), a landing-place, ghaut, quay, wharf, a place on the bank of a river where boats stop to discharge or take in goods or passengers (K.Pr. 58, W. 153, Śiv. 1806); a ferry, ford; a bathing-place, or a place for…

(sg. dat. gāṭhas ), a landing-place, ghaut, quay, wharf, a place on the bank of a river where boats stop to discharge or take in goods or passengers (K.Pr. 58, W. 153, Śiv. 1806); a ferry, ford; a bathing-place, or a place for washing clothes (on the bank of a river). -dār - - m. the man in charge of a landing-place, who collects the harbour dues, a harbour-master. -dörī - f. the fee or tax paid at a landing-place, harbour dues. -dār-bāy -- - f. the wife of a harbour-master. -dārĕñ - f. a woman who acts as harbour-master, a harbour-mistress. gāṭha-hūnu - m. (f. -hūñü -), the dog at a landing-place (that prowls around eating what it can pick up) (K.Pr. 68); met. a person, clever enough but without application, who wanders about from place to place and does not succeed in making any profit. -wôlu - m. a boatman who sticks to the river bank (and does not go off to work in his boat).

e: m. (sg. dat. gatas ), going, the act of going (i.q. gath 3), esp. --˚ in ata-gath 1 and 2 (q.v.), coming and going (Śiv. 1364, 1808); a turning round, a revolution (El., K.Pr. 128). --karun -- m.inf. to revolve (El.).
adj. c.g., i.q. goṭu 1, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. gatas ), a goer, used --˚ as in wata-gath, a road-goer, a traveller (Gr.M., Śiv. 1829).
m. (sg. dat. gaṭas ), the stem of a huqqa, connecting the fire-bowl with the water-receptacle.

f. (sg. dat. güʦü , Śiv. 1364, Rām. 1426), going, moving, gait, deportment, motion in general; march, going, progress, movement; a means of success, way; state, condition (vaikunṭha- gath, the condition of heaven, i.e. a…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. güʦü , Śiv. 1364, Rām. 1426), going, moving, gait, deportment, motion in general; march, going, progress, movement; a means of success, way; state, condition (vaikunṭha- gath, the condition of heaven, i.e. a condition the same as that of heaven, Śiv. 997); the way, conduct, mighty works (of God) (K.Pr. 102, Rām. 567); refuge, resource; the course of the soul through existence [parama-gath, the supreme course, final beatitude, salvation (Śiv. 19, 102, 1539, 1781, etc.); so gath alone, the way of salvation, beatitude (Śiv. 161, 674, 884, 1759)]; a happy condition, bliss generally (Śiv. 1098, 1246, 1710); dayĕ-gath, the way of God, God's majesty (Śiv. 1652, 1787, Rām. 122), a piece of good luck, bliss granted by God (Śiv. 693, Rām. 1296), the way approved by God, a holy life (Rām. 30). --karüñü -- f.inf. to die after another (e.g. a widow becoming satī after her husband's death, H. iii, 4); to devote oneself to death for the sake of something (e.g. a moth for a lamp) (YZ. 430); to follow a person to the death, to be true till death.

e: f. a tied-up bundle, esp. of clothes or the like.
f. sorrow, grief, the pain of sorrow.
(spelling), a single-stick (L. 464).
m. leanness, thinness (natural or owing to disease, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. -nôwu -), to cause (a person) to go, to despatch, send off on a message. This verb does not mean to cause to go, in the sense of driving, for which pakanāwun is used (Gr.Gr. 176).
see gāṭulu.
f. a comb.
adj. (m. sg. dat. gātakas ; f. gātücü ), a killer, a murderer, a destroyer. Commonly --˚.
adj. (f.gataja ), having a very swift current, in spate (of a river); hence, rapid (of a torrent of words), quickly incoming (of wealth), and so on; excessive, very much. Cf. gath and Gr.Gr. 145.

adj. (f.gāṭüjü , Gr.Gr. 35), wise, clever, shrewd, prudent (K.Pr. 58, 107, 210; Rām. 128, 129); skilful, expert; learned, intelligent; eloquent (El., Rām. 1279. Cf. katha-gāṭulu s.v. kath). Cf. Gr.Gr. 145.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. gaṭyōv ), to become less, lessen, diminish, decrease (Śiv. 1565); to become shrunken (of something green and fresh), to be shrivelled up; to become lessened (by loss of a part).
conj. 1, an old form of garun, q.v. (L.V. 80).
(L. 74), see gwöñü.
i.q. gōr, q.v.
adj. c.g. fair, fair-complexioned (Śiv. 47).
f. N. of the god Śiva's wife, Pārvatī (Śiv. 643, 655, etc.). -shĕnkar - m. Gaurī and Śaṅkara, i.e. Pārvatī and Śiva, looked upon conjointly as one deity (Śiv. 197, 644).
in phĕki-gav m. a hole, a puncture, a hole (in a garment); the orifice in a ripened boil, etc., through which the purulent matter exudes.
see gaʦhun 2.
m. currency, the being in season for sale, the frequent occurrence of buying and selling of any article (e.g. owing to its being in season, or in a country where it is an important commodity).
in gav-rochu -, a cowherd (El. gau-roch). Cf. gāv 2.
sing thou, a Hindī form, used m.c. instead of gĕv in Śiv. 1721, 1812.
f. surrounding and attacking a person (e.g. a thief, the enemy in a war, etc.), capturing by surprise. Cf. gōvarun.
m. Onosma macrocephala (El. gáoza). Cf. bān 1 (p. 109b, l. 4).
or gawöyi 1 m. a witness, one who gives testimony of something which happened in his presence (K.Pr. 78).
m.inf. to be pleasant, to give rise to a pleasant sensation, to be agreeable.
m. (sg. dat. ?), the entering a person (e.g. an evil spirit entering a person, or, met., an idea, etc., to take possession of him).
m. a kind of wild deer, said to resemble a cow in form.
f., i.q. gawöyi 2, q.v.
m., i.q. gawāh, q.v. (H. x, 12).
or gawöhī f. evidence, testimony (H. x, 12).
f. N. of a celebrated town and place of pilgrimage in the Bihār province of India, visited by Hindūs for the purpose of making oblations to the manes of their deceased ancestors (Śiv. 627, 1495).

f. N. of a sacred verse in the Ṛgvēda (iii, 62, 10) repeated by every Brāhmaṇ at his morning and evening devotions. It is personified as the wife of Brahmā and the mother of the four Vēdas (Śiv. 1512, 1526).

m. an instrument for measuring, a yard measure (K.Pr. 221); a yard (of measure), in Kashmīr equal to about 48 finger-widths, and about half an inch longer than the British yard (L. 243; K.Pr. 43, 87, 173, 179, 249; Śiv. 1235,…
fullMeaning: m. an instrument for measuring, a yard measure (K.Pr. 221); a yard (of measure), in Kashmīr equal to about 48 finger-widths, and about half an inch longer than the British yard (L. 243; K.Pr. 43, 87, 173, 179, 249; Śiv. 1235, 1284); the khām gaz is about 15/16 of the full gaz (see khām 1); anything measurable (e.g. land, cloth, etc.) a yard in length. akh gaz zyūṭhu, a yard in length (Gr.M.). gaz-pipal (spelling), N. of a certain drug made from cones of the Himalayan spruce (L. 80). gaza-bodu - m. innumerable yards in length, yards and yards (e.g. of a long strip of cloth, or a road). Cf. bọ̆du 2 or bodu 1 (p. 84a, l. 3). -phyuru - m. the turning of a yard measure, measuring over again as a check on the first measurement.

e: or (El.) gaza m. an elephant. gaza-mŏkh - m. he who has an elephant's face, N. of the Hindū god Gaṇēśa (see Ganēsh, p. 293a, l. 26) (Śiv. 5). -ʦam - m. elephant's hide (Śiv. 166, 816).
m. anger, passion, rage, fury (Rām. 1318); wrong, injustice, oppression; a curse, calamity, affliction, awful event.
(m. enraged, fearful, tremendous, dreadful; (in Kāshmīrī) excessively heavy, tremendous (of a fall of snow, or the like).
adj. c.g. full of rage, enraged, indignant, furious (Rām. 266). In Rām. 497 the word is spelt gazaphnākh.

(cf. Hindī gajar), m. the chimes rung at the expiration of a pahar or watch of the day or night; esp. amongst Kāshmīrī Musalmāns, those rung at the end of the fourth or last watch of the night; hence, the time just before…

e: adj. c.g. capable of being measured with a measuring rod (of things for sale, e.g. cloth).

(sg. dat. gazēndras ), a king of elephants, a noble elephant; esp. a certain famous elephant rescued (when being overpowered by a crocodile) by the Hindū god Viṣṇu under the form of Hari or Harihara, in answer to his prayer of faith. The story is often quoted as an instance of the divine graciousness of Viṣṇu (Śiv. 856, 1471).

e: adj. c.g. of or belonging to the town of Ghaznī (H. i, 1).

e: adj. (f. gaziñü ), a yard long.

(of a crowd of men or number of animals) to be crowded together, e.g. by being all shut up in a small room or by fastening all together by a single rope. --karüñü -- f.inf. to crowd men or animals together as ab.

m. the top part of the throat, the fauces.

or gih m. a house; household affairs, life as a householder, as opp. to an ascetic life (L.V. 55 gēh, 64 gih). gēh bazun m.inf. to be occupied in household affairs, to be a householder, as distinct from an ascetic (L.V. 32).
see gë̆ḍü.
gījü , see gēlun 1.

f. (sg. dat. gĕli ), hitting anything by throwing a stick at it (as when knocking down a fruit from a tree, or the like). gĕla-küṭü - f. a kind of very venomous snake of a grey colour and about a span and a half long. It is said…

(sg. dat. gĕli ), hitting anything by throwing a stick at it (as when knocking down a fruit from a tree, or the like). gĕla-küṭü - f. a kind of very venomous snake of a grey colour and about a span and a half long.
