m. rose-water (El., W. 134); a rose (K.Pr. 40; YZ. 257; Śiv. 55, 187, 188, 190-2, 555; Rām. 197, 397, 644, 650). There are two great varieties of the rose in Kashmīr--lāl gŏlāb, or red rose, and āra-wal (see āra 2), the yellow…
fullMeaning: m. rose-water (El., W. 134); a rose (K.Pr. 40; YZ. 257; Śiv. 55, 187, 188, 190-2, 555; Rām. 197, 397, 644, 650). There are two great varieties of the rose in Kashmīr--lāl gŏlāb, or red rose, and āra-wal (see āra 2), the yellow rose. -tǖrü - f. 'rose-cold', the season when roses bloom in the winter, during which a moderately cool wind blows. -zyuru - m. a collection of rose petals (used as a medicine).

e: or gŏlükhü f. (sg. dat. gŏlaki ), a small stick-shaped piece of collyrium for application to the eyes as a medicine.
f. a collyrium-club, i.e. a club instead of a stick of collyrium, a blow in the eye; met. foul abuse. Cf. gŏlakh.

cf. m. the red poppy, Papaver rhœas. The plant is used medicinally as a cardiac tonic, and its young leaves are much esteemed as a vegetable (L. 72, 76, 462; K.Pr. 102; Rām. 203, 279, etc.). It is said to be specially common in…
fullMeaning: cf. m. the red poppy, Papaver rhœas. The plant is used medicinally as a cardiac tonic, and its young leaves are much esteemed as a vegetable (L. 72, 76, 462; K.Pr. 102; Rām. 203, 279, etc.). It is said to be specially common in barley-fields. El. also gives gul-lāla, and moreover gives gulālā as meaning tulip.

e: m. a slave, bondsman; a servant (El.; YZ. 157; H. vi, 14; viii, passim).
(spelling), m. a curlew, Numenius arquata (L. 124).
m. a pellet-bow; (in Kashmīr) the earthen pellet fired from such a bow; a bolus, a soft kind of pill made up with medicaments and molasses. Cf. gōna.
see gūlu and görü 2.
adj. c.g. victorious; dushmanas-pĕṭh gölib sapanun, to overcome the enemy (Gr.M.).
(K.Pr. 158), said to be incorrect for gari, in the house. According to others it should be göli or gāli, and is a meaningless word.
in the following.-wā̃ḍulu m. a vessel into which water for washing grain is received after use. -wôñu - m. the dirty water in which grain has been washed.
adj. c.g. of the colour of a rose, rose-coloured, rosy, pink. --ṭang -- m. N. of a kind of pear, see ṭang.

m. a cave; esp., in Kashmīr, a solitary piece of level ground surrounded by desert mountains, such as robbers could hide in, a robber's lair. göli-höji - f. a jail, prison (in which robbers find an unwished for 'lair').
m. (inmuha-gọ̆lu -, Siv. 1056), muddiness (of water) (the soul is compared to water which has been muddied by muh or illusion). Cf. guhulu 2.

m. the mouth of a jar, opening of a bag, entrance to a cave (Rām. 462, 464), or the like. Cf. dān 1 and güjü; also basma-golu s.v. basm (Śiv. 1572), and dōri-golu, s.v. dūrü 2. gȧli-öri - or gȧli-yöri- f. the rope or string tied…
fullMeaning: m. the mouth of a jar, opening of a bag, entrance to a cave (Rām. 462, 464), or the like. Cf. dān 1 and güjü; also basma-golu s.v. basm (Śiv. 1572), and dōri-golu, s.v. dūrü 2. gȧli-öri - or gȧli-yöri- f. the rope or string tied round the neck of a jar, and by which it is suspended and carried. gali phirun m.inf. to empty a jar by inverting it and pouring out the contents. --phirith hyonu -- m.inf. to empty out the contents of a jar as ab., and take the whole contents (leaving nothing for anyone else).

e: m. the inside part of the corners of the mouth; the lower part of the cheek, the jowl (K.Pr. 74, 156). In dŏda-golu (s.v. dŏd) this word means 'mouthful'. so rata-go, p. 846a, l.Cf. gal 2. --hyonu -- m.inf. to deny something…
fullMeaning: m. the inside part of the corners of the mouth; the lower part of the cheek, the jowl (K.Pr. 74, 156). In dŏda-golu (s.v. dŏd) this word means 'mouthful'. so rata-go, p. 846a, l.Cf. gal 2. --hyonu -- m.inf. to deny something previously said by the speaker, to dissimulate. gȧli khasȧni m. pl. inf. the corners of the mouth to rise, hence (of the cheeks) to be puffed out (by wind) (K.Pr. 207), or to be swollen (by disease). gali gali adv. in mouthfuls (of giving to drink or the like) (Śiv. 1575). --myūṭhu -- m. a kiss on the inner part of the cheek (obsc.). --ʦopu -- m. a bite on the inner part of the cheek. --zĕv -- f. the tongue in the cheek; met. the condition of being unable to reply when a lie is discovered, being rendered mute, dumbfounded, speechless.

e: m. (sg. dat. gŏlaras ), the shell or skin of a walnut or the like; a nut (El.). Cf. gŏl 2, and ḍūnu-gŏl or -gŏlur, s.v. ḍūnu.
adj. c.g. of, belonging to, or produced in, a village.
see gaʦhun 2.

m. a quality (K.Pr. 36, guan; Śiv. 1060), esp. a good quality (Rām. 39, 1067); the virtue, or property of a medicine, or the like (Gr.M.), or of a special astrological conjuncture (Rām. 1260, 1281); a virtue, such as learning,…
fullMeaning: m. a quality (K.Pr. 36, guan; Śiv. 1060), esp. a good quality (Rām. 39, 1067); the virtue, or property of a medicine, or the like (Gr.M.), or of a special astrological conjuncture (Rām. 1260, 1281); a virtue, such as learning, deftness, mercy, nobility of temperament (Śiv. 886, 966, 1195, Rām. 604); (according to Hindū philosophy) one of the three guṇas or constituents of existing things, viz. goodness, passion, and darkness (Śiv. 193, 447, 797, 977, etc.). Cf. gōn. --gĕwun --, m.inf. to sing the virtues (of so and so), to praise widely, to speak well (of) (Gr.M.). gŏna-mã̄th - m. sg. dat. -mã̄tas -), 'one endowed with good qualities'; hence, a skilled professional singer. -wān - adj. c.g. possessing good qualities, excellent (Śiv. 1077, 1081); virtuous, worthy; accomplished, skilful (Śiv. 1142); effective, possessing virtue (of a medicine, or the like). gŏnau-rostu - adj. (f. -rüʦhü), devoid of good qualities (Śiv. 751).

e: m. a bowstring (El.). This is really another form of gŏn. Cf. gōn-bal.
m. strength in any particular good quality, such as learning, dexterity, or the like. Cf. gŏn and gōn.
m. a pellet bow (El.). Cf. gŏlēla.
or gunahgār m. a sinner (K.Pr. 136). --karun -- m.inf. to sin (K.Pr. 171, H. viii, 11).

m. a bud (K.Pr. 256), a rosebud. -dahān one who has a mouth like a rose- bud (YZ. 16, 145). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be collected together (like a rosebud), to be closely packed; (in Kāshmīrī) to become bewildered, perplexed,…
fullMeaning: m. a bud (K.Pr. 256), a rosebud. -dahān one who has a mouth like a rose- bud (YZ. 16, 145). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be collected together (like a rosebud), to be closely packed; (in Kāshmīrī) to become bewildered, perplexed, confused, nonplussed (in a dispute or the like).

e: f. a small village or hamlet, esp. one newly settled; the land enclosed in the old Mug̱ẖul embankments (L. 211, gund). --kaḍüñü - f.inf. to beg successfully several times in a place in which one has once before begged…
fullMeaning: f. a small village or hamlet, esp. one newly settled; the land enclosed in the old Mug̱ẖul embankments (L. 211, gund). --kaḍüñü - f.inf. to beg successfully several times in a place in which one has once before begged successfully. --nērüñü -- f.inf. when one has the expectation of getting a thing only once from any place, to find oneself able to get it several times from that place.

e: gānḍay , see gö̃ḍ, gã̄ḍay.
m. the earthenware vessel of a kāngrī or portable brazier (El.).

m. a posy, a nosegay (YZ. 89) (usually --˚ after the name of the flower, e.g. pōshĕ-gọ̆ndu, a nosegay of flowers, H. v. 4); a plume of heron's feathers bound up with pearls, precious stones, and gold and silver wire. It is worn…
fullMeaning: m. a posy, a nosegay (YZ. 89) (usually --˚ after the name of the flower, e.g. pōshĕ-gọ̆ndu, a nosegay of flowers, H. v. 4); a plume of heron's feathers bound up with pearls, precious stones, and gold and silver wire. It is worn on a turban on state occasions (YZ. 89, 390, L. 118). gŏndi-tīri - f. (sg. dat. -tīrĕ -), heron's plumes, used as ab. Cf. braga- tīrü under brag.

e: m. the jaw. gȧnḍi pĕni m. pl. inf. the jaws to fall; loosening of the jaw-bones of children due to dysentery.
m. a great log of wood, esp. one not trimmed; met. a great man, a man of high rank and power, i.q. grọ̆nḍu. Cf. gar- gunḍa s.v. gara.
m. the Turkestan pack-saddle, which consists of two straw-filled pommels joined in front (H. xi, 9).
m. a rhinoceros (L.V. 47).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gọ̆ndu ; 2 p.p. gŏnzōv ), to display or express one's thoughts or feelings. This verb is impers. in tenses derived from the p.p. Cf. grāv.

or gundun conj. 1 (1 p.p. gọ̆ndu or gundu ; 2 p.p. gŏ(u)nzōv ), to complain of, to make a complaint about (anything, acc.) (Śiv. 1435); to ridicule. This verb is impers. in the tenses formed from the p.p. Cf. grāv.
m. a posy, bouquet; a handful of anything except grain and grass (El.).
f. 'a female posy', a very beautiful woman (YZ. 548). Cf. gŏnduru.
f.pl. a humble request (for help in any work or the like).

m. a kind of handsel or present given to cowherds and similar servants on monthly wages when they are first engaged. --karun -- m.inf. to make a commencement of cultivation; this is a formal ceremony performed by husbandmen on an…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of handsel or present given to cowherds and similar servants on monthly wages when they are first engaged. --karun -- m.inf. to make a commencement of cultivation; this is a formal ceremony performed by husbandmen on an auspicious day and at an auspicious hour (K.Pr. 247).

e: m. endowed with good qualities, possessing virtue (Śiv. 1060); (of an inanimate thing, such as a medicine) possessing virtue, effective.
see guna 1.
m. (sg. dat. gönikas ), an accompanist, a musician who plays for dancing women, prostitutes, etc.
f. the profession or conduct of a souteneur. See gān 1.
or gunja m. a large tame cat, well-grown and fat.
gönṭh , see gö̃ṭh 1, 2, and 3.
etc., see gō̃ʦh, etc.

f. a stack, a high pile of straw or the like; a granary (El.). gŏñĕ-bāha - m. heating, sweating, fermenting (of such a stack). gŏñĕ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to make stacks; to acquire a great deal of anything (e.g. knowledge, virtue,…
fullMeaning: f. a stack, a high pile of straw or the like; a granary (El.). gŏñĕ-bāha - m. heating, sweating, fermenting (of such a stack). gŏñĕ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to make stacks; to acquire a great deal of anything (e.g. knowledge, virtue, money, or goods).

e: m. a stack, rick (L. 463, Śiv. 1212, Rām. 12); a pile (Gr.Gr. 26).
(f. güñü 2 , for 1 see s.v.), adjectival suff. added to numerals, and signifying 'fold', as in hata-gonu, a hundredfold. Cf. gunu.
f. a harlot, a prostitute (K.Pr. 65, gáni) (f. of gān 1, q.v., Gr.Gr. 37). See El. s.v. gányi for particulars of women of this kind in Kashmīr. göñĕ-war - m.pl. a harlot's coquetry.
adj. (f.güñü 3 ), compact, solid, dense (Śiv. 194); coarse, gross; stout, strong.
f. a small wild fruit, of a dark-red colour and sour taste, growing on a thorny shrub; probably the gaun, Elæagnus parvifolia of L. 74. Cf. gīwāñ.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gūnu , f. gūñü ; 2 p.p.gōñōv ) (in arithmetic) to multiply; (in rope-making, etc.) to twist several strands together; to study over and over again, practise, repeat several times something one is learning.
see gŏndun 1 and 2.
adj. c.g. evil-smelling, stinking (by nature or occupation).
m. a cowherd; esp. the famous cowherd, i.e. Kṛṣṇa (Krushn) (Śiv. 705, 733, 1320, 1380, 1436).
adj. c.g. concealed. Usually --˚, as in ākāra-gŏpath, q.v. s.v. ākār.
f. (sg. dat. gŏphi ), a cave, a cavern (K.Pr. 249, Śiv. 933, 1817, 1894, Rām. 517), a pit, a hole (El., who makes it m.; Gr.M., also m.). gŏphi-golu - m. the opening, or mouth, of a cave.
m. (sg. dat. gōpas ), a cowherd; esp. one of the cowherds of Vṛndāvana, amongst whom Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) spent his youth. Their chief was named Nanda (Śiv. 1461), who was Kṛṣṇa's foster-father.
f., i.q. gŏph, q.v. (Śiv. 1478).
or göfil adj. c.g. unmindful, neglectful, negligent, heedless (K.Pr. 46, göphilō, voc.).

or gūpī f. a cowherdess, a herdmaiden; esp. the herdmaidens who attended on the youthful Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) in Vṛndāvana (Śiv. 705, 992, etc.). -nāth - m. (sg. dat. -nāthas-), the lord of herdmaidens, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 858, 1382,…
fullMeaning: or gūpī f. a cowherdess, a herdmaiden; esp. the herdmaidens who attended on the youthful Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) in Vṛndāvana (Śiv. 705, 992, etc.). -nāth - m. (sg. dat. -nāthas-), the lord of herdmaidens, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 858, 1382, 1423, 1443).

e: f. a dancing girl (H. v, 10).

m. deep thought, reflection, meditation (Gr.M.); (in Kāshmīrī) a private grudge, hidden malice. --karun -- m.inf. to consider carefully, pay attention (to = pĕṭh) (Gr.M.). --rōzun -- m.inf. a private grudge to be left (as the…
fullMeaning: m. deep thought, reflection, meditation (Gr.M.); (in Kāshmīrī) a private grudge, hidden malice. --karun -- m.inf. to consider carefully, pay attention (to = pĕṭh) (Gr.M.). --rōzun -- m.inf. a private grudge to be left (as the consequence of the object of the dislike having interfered with a person's work, etc.). --thawun -- m.inf. to cause a private grudge to be left, as ab.

e: m. molasses, treacle, guṛ (K.Pr. 105, 190).
or gōrü f. a grave, a tomb.
m.onomat. the bubbling or gurgling sound of air passing through water, as in the case of a hubble-bubble or native tobacco-pipe.
see gair.

f. the third lunar day of the light half of the month of Māg (Skt. Māgha = January-February), sacred amongst Hindūs to the goddess Gaurī or Vāgīśvarī, on which a festival is held by teachers and their pupils; a set of verses,…
fullMeaning: f. the third lunar day of the light half of the month of Māg (Skt. Māgha = January-February), sacred amongst Hindūs to the goddess Gaurī or Vāgīśvarī, on which a festival is held by teachers and their pupils; a set of verses, written on coloured paper, together with a picture of Sarasvatī, the goddess of learning, surrounded by an ornamental border, prepared on the occasion of this festival.

e: f. the profession, condition, professional knowledge, or professional acts of a family priest.
or gōramala m. a grave- digger (El.). Cf. gōr 4.
or gōrawār , see gŏr, p. 297b, l. 6.

m. a cat. -ȧchi f. a cat's eye; a human eye resembling in colour that of a cat, a brown eye. -gonju m. 'a puss of a cat', a fine fat tawny cat. Cf. gonju. -kāʦuru - adj. (f. -kāʦürü -), very brown (of a person's complexion or…
fullMeaning: m. a cat. -ȧchi f. a cat's eye; a human eye resembling in colour that of a cat, a brown eye. -gonju m. 'a puss of a cat', a fine fat tawny cat. Cf. gonju. -kāʦuru - adj. (f. -kāʦürü -), very brown (of a person's complexion or skin).

e: m. N. of a certain fruit, a small apricot, Prunus Armeniaca (El. gordol and gurdálú). gŏrdöli-ö̃ṭi- f. an apricot stone. -kuji - or -kujü - f. an apricot-tree. -lünḍü - f. (sg. dat. -lanjĕ -), a branch of an apricot-tree, esp.…
fullMeaning: m. N. of a certain fruit, a small apricot, Prunus Armeniaca (El. gordol and gurdálú). gŏrdöli-ö̃ṭi- f. an apricot stone. -kuji - or -kujü - f. an apricot-tree. -lünḍü - f. (sg. dat. -lanjĕ -), a branch of an apricot-tree, esp. when separated from the tree, with or without fruit hanging from it. -phulay - - f. the flowering of an apricot-tree.

e: or gūril f. (sg. dat. gŏrili or gūrili ), the profession, conduct, or condition of a family priest, or of a teacher, or of a spiritual preceptor (cf. Gr.Gr. 142, gŏr or gōr 1, gūrilözi, and gōrözü).
f. the condition or profession of a gŏryunu, q.v., i.e. of a Hindū family priest, who conducts worship according to the rules of the Tantras and not according to those of the Vēdas. Cf. gōrözü.
m. the planet Jupiter, i.q. brahaspath.
m. a preparation of tobacco and molasses (guṛ) for smoking in a ḥuqqa.
f. the profession or occupation of a teacher, of a spiritual guide, or of a family priest. Cf. gŏrinözü, gŏril, gūrilözi, and Gr.Gr. 143.
see gōr 4.
m. a large rock; esp. a rock placed on the edge of the precipice side of a mountain path to guard wayfarers from falling over.
m. a species of starling (El.). ? = göri- kôvu, s.v. gôru.

m.(f. gürü 2 , for 1 see s.v.), a doer, maker; hence, esp. an artisan, a maker of things for sale, used as a sec. suff.; e.g. aina-goru, a maker of mirrors; lāyĕ-goru, a seller of parched grain; ganḍan-goru, a bookbinder;…
fullMeaning: m.(f. gürü 2 , for 1 see s.v.), a doer, maker; hence, esp. an artisan, a maker of things for sale, used as a sec. suff.; e.g. aina-goru, a maker of mirrors; lāyĕ-goru, a seller of parched grain; ganḍan-goru, a bookbinder; kangañĕ-goru, a comb-maker, a comb-seller; manḍan-goru, a man who kneads cloth in water to soften it (Gr.Gr. 149). The f. gürü indicates a female maker of the thing referred to, while a maker's wife is -gȧri-bāy.

e: f. the dried kernel of the water-chestnut (El.). See göri-gūji under gôru. El. also gives gólí for this word, and gólí-kutsur, as meaning a seller of the kernels. Cf. gūlu. -gaʦhüñü - f.inf. to become such a kernel (which is…
fullMeaning: f. the dried kernel of the water-chestnut (El.). See göri-gūji under gôru. El. also gives gólí for this word, and gólí-kutsur, as meaning a seller of the kernels. Cf. gūlu. -gaʦhüñü - f.inf. to become such a kernel (which is extracted by roasting and splitting); met. to be publicly disgraced or discomfited (e.g. by having one's failings proclaimed or being defeated in an abuse-combat). -karüñü - f.inf. publicly to discomfit as above.

e: adj. (f.gürü 3 ), hard, solid, tough (e.g. wood that cannot be cut); dense, solid, of thick solid material (e.g. a metal vessel that will not ring when struck).
(f. gürü 4 ), see garun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gūru ; f.pl. gōrĕ ; 2 p.p. gōryōv ), to babble in delirium or the like; to talk in one's sleep; to lament (Gr.Gr. xx).
m. a Hindū family priest, who conducts worship according to the rules of the Tantras and not according to those of the Vēdas.
(YZ. 90), ? meaning. Apparently translated as a sg. dat. of gāv, q.v., which is impossible, the word being fem.

m. wrath, rage, anger, passion; displeasure, a hurt feeling (Śiv. 85, Rām. 758); anxiety, trouble, sorrow (Rām. 72, 453, 675, 758, 1088, 1120, 1572, 1675, 1693, 1739). --diwanāwun -- m.inf. to provoke to anger (Gr.M.). --gaʦhun…
fullMeaning: m. wrath, rage, anger, passion; displeasure, a hurt feeling (Śiv. 85, Rām. 758); anxiety, trouble, sorrow (Rām. 72, 453, 675, 758, 1088, 1120, 1572, 1675, 1693, 1739). --diwanāwun -- m.inf. to provoke to anger (Gr.M.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. anger or rage (against someone, in dat.) to occur (K.Pr. 100, Rām. 1556, 1574, 1605). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to drag out anger, to assuage anger, to appease. --karun -- m.inf. to make anger, to enrage, anger.

e: m. bathing, ablution, a bath (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to bathe (El.).
adj. c.g. full of wrath, angry, wroth.

m. brilliancy, brightness, clear visibility (e.g. of a distant peak) (Śiv. 1811); brightness, clearness (of the sky); brightness (e.g. of a garden beautiful with flowers or of a clean well-kept house) (Śiv. 963, 1028); the bright…
fullMeaning: m. brilliancy, brightness, clear visibility (e.g. of a distant peak) (Śiv. 1811); brightness, clearness (of the sky); brightness (e.g. of a garden beautiful with flowers or of a clean well-kept house) (Śiv. 963, 1028); the bright parts of a garden, the flower clusters (Śiv. 1690). Cf. gāsh.

e: (El.), gosh búg (L. 351), and goshibeigi (El.) (spelling of all three), a kind of early pear. See ṭang.
m. a corner, nook, closet; a lobe (of the liver). Cf. jigar.
adj. c.g. (of a human being) starving with hunger, so famished as to be ready to snatch away forcibly another's food, ravenous.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. göshoro ), to make (day) bright, to brighten, i.e. the clouds to blow off and leave the sky clear.
), meat, flesh. --āba or gusht-āba m. a rich soup of pounded or minced meat (K.Pr. 208).

m. silence, not speaking; esp. the silence of one who, though he sees and hears what is going on, says nothing, and acts as if he knew nothing about it; heedlessness, carelessness of consequences after full warning (Gr.Gr. 139).

adj. (f. güshü ), silent (Gr.Gr. 138, 139); esp. one who, although he sees and hears or has been instructed, acts as if he were entirely ignorant, heedless (of instructions), one who after full warning acts without consideration…
fullMeaning: adj. (f. güshü ), silent (Gr.Gr. 138, 139); esp. one who, although he sees and hears or has been instructed, acts as if he were entirely ignorant, heedless (of instructions), one who after full warning acts without consideration of consequences.

e: see gāsa.
m. the name given in schools to the letter gha of the Śāradā alphabet.
f. a woman who is dirty in person, clothes, work, and predisposition.
f. the condition of being littered with a quantity of dirty straw, grass, etc. (of a place or house) (K.Pr. 56, of a garden).
f. presumption, arrogance, insolence, sauciness (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. güsü ), rubbed down, ground down, polished. Used --˚. Cf. aḍa-gosu, p. 11a, l. 22.
m. (sg.dat. gösüs or gāsas , Gr.Gr. 54), a grass-seller, a man who lives by selling grass, hay, straw, etc. -bāy f. his wife.

m. a dip, a dive; diving, plunging; esp. becoming wet through by falling into water or mud. --dyunu -- m.inf. to plunge (oneself or another) into water, to dip, to duck; (according to Baptists) to baptize. --dāwun -- m.inf. to…
fullMeaning: m. a dip, a dive; diving, plunging; esp. becoming wet through by falling into water or mud. --dyunu -- m.inf. to plunge (oneself or another) into water, to dip, to duck; (according to Baptists) to baptize. --dāwun -- m.inf. to cause another to plunge himself (Śiv. 1397), or a third person, into water. -gŏth - f. (sg. dat. -güʦü -), diving over and over again (in a water frolic or the like). --khĕni -- m. pl. inf. 'to eat dives', to be dipped, to suffer immersion, to dive; met. to be plunged in sorrow. -khŏr - (=) m. a diver; anything that dips or is dipped; a sort of firework (so called because, being lighted, it is thrown into water, when it dives, and every now and then shows above the water). --lagȧni -- m. pl. inf. dives to be experienced; met. sorrow, caused by painful reminiscences or memories of wrongs suffered, to be experienced, to have painful memories. gŏtan gaʦhun m.inf. to go into plunges, to be distraught by a multitude of duties all occurring together at the same time.

e: m. narrow gold or silver lace used as an edging for cloth, a narrow fillet of brocade.

(sg. dat. grākas ), a customer, buyer (in a shop) (K.Pr. 219, 229, YZ. 119), or a customer, client (of some professional person), in each case whether occasional or regular. -bāy - f. the wife of the regular client or customer of some professional person (e.g. a barber or a flower-seller); a woman who is such a regular client. grāka-bôyu - m. the buyer-brother, a regular customer or purchaser of things at a shop; a regular client or customer of any professional person. -gara - m. the house of such a regular client (visited regularly by the barber, flower-seller, etc., in the course of his business).

e: m. (sg. dat. grākas ; f. grākañ , Gr.Gr. 38, 106, 136), a sec. suff. forming nouns of agency. Thus, karan-grākh , a doer; khĕna-grākh , an eater; zöñü-grākh , a knower. See Gr.Gr. 106 for the rules for the use of this suffix.…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. grākas ; f. grākañ , Gr.Gr. 38, 106, 136), a sec. suff. forming nouns of agency. Thus, karan-grākh , a doer; khĕna-grākh , an eater; zöñü-grākh , a knower. See Gr.Gr. 106 for the rules for the use of this suffix. With nouns it indicates possession, when the thing possessed accompanies, but does not form part of, the possessor. Thus, lari-grākh , the owner of a house (Gr.Gr. 136). It thus often indicates a profession or trade, as in hāka-grākh , a vegetable seller (Gr.Gr. 38); gāsa-grākh , a grass-cutter (K.Pr. 178).

m. a corn-mill, a grinding mill (K.Pr. 6, 27; L. 456; Śiv. 1503, 1795, 1828; W. 2 has ghraṭu, i.e. groṭu). -anwār f. the revolution of a mill; met. perpetual or continual revolution (of the soul through transmigration) (Śiv.…
fullMeaning: m. a corn-mill, a grinding mill (K.Pr. 6, 27; L. 456; Śiv. 1503, 1795, 1828; W. 2 has ghraṭu, i.e. groṭu). -anwār f. the revolution of a mill; met. perpetual or continual revolution (of the soul through transmigration) (Śiv. 1795, 1914). -bal - m. the ground outside a village, on the bank of a river, where the village corn-mill, driven by the stream, is situated (K.Pr. 71). --dyunu -- m.inf. to give grinding; to put to the mill, to 'grind' a pupil, make him study hard; to wear down a person by refusing him any liberty. -khôru - m. or -khörü - f. in the large water-mill, the large wickerwork receptacle, which is filled with wheat and which delivers it gradually to the millstones. --lagun -- m.inf. to be put into the mill; to be worn down by being refused liberty (e.g. in a prison). -laʦhulu - m. a brush for sweeping up the flour or the refuse coming from a mill. -pahörü - f. the hut on the bank of a river in which the water-mill for grinding corn is kept. -ʦakaj - or -ʦaküjü f. one of the stones (upper or nether) of a mill, a millstone. It is believed that a Yĕch, or fairy, no matter how strong, cannot lift a millstone, and hence anything placed under it is safe from him (K.Pr. 141). -wôlu - m. a miller (K.Pr. 6).

f. a deep well in the bed of a river hidden under the water, usually in mountain streams. Cf. grühüñü 2.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gröshĕrôwĕ ), to cause to be taken, to cause a gift to be taken by another.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gröshĕrôwĕ ), i.q. gröshĕrun 2.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gröshoro ), to take, receive (into the hand, etc., of something given by another).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gröshoro . This verb is impersonal in the tenses formed from the past participles), (of a shower of rain, esp. a violent one) to stop suddenly.
m. eating up all the food before one, clearing out the dishes.
m. the spending by one member of a company of the whole of its joint earnings.
m. the gulping sound made when swallowing a liquid. Cf. graṭh and griṭh, also amañĕ-ta-grŏṭh, p. 28b, l. 21. --nĕngalun -- m.inf. to gulp down together food and liquid.
m. (sg. dat.grŏṭas ), a bubo or boil occurring on the inner part of the thigh or armpit, said to be caused by excessive walking. Cf. grüṭü.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. grŏʦowu ), to splash about, shake up (a liquid in a vessel).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. grŏʦyōv , Gr.Gr. 226), to be splashed about (as a liquid in a vessel), shaken up, agitated. Cf. grakun.
f. the heel, esp. the tendo Achillis; according to El., also the calf of the leg, or the leg genl. (El. also graz).
f. a deep place in a river, esp. in the curve of a large river. Cf. gröñü.
see grū̃phu.
see grand.
m. a half-opened bud.
(spelling), N. of a certain soil, containing a large proportion of clay (L. 319). The word appears to be properly guroṭu, q.v., or its f. gurüṭü.
f. the hard core of a boil not yet ripe, i.e. before matter has fully formed in it. Cf. grŏṭh 2 and gũ̄̈ṭh.

or grūstu m. (sg. dat. grīstis ), a farmer, husbandman, cultivator of the soil; a tenant farmer (El.; K.Pr. 69, 129, 224; L. 456; H. ix, 4, 7). According to El. the word is pronounced grūst in Śrīnagar and grōst elsewhere.…
fullMeaning: or grūstu m. (sg. dat. grīstis ), a farmer, husbandman, cultivator of the soil; a tenant farmer (El.; K.Pr. 69, 129, 224; L. 456; H. ix, 4, 7). According to El. the word is pronounced grūst in Śrīnagar and grōst elsewhere. grīsti-bāy - f. a farmer's wife (H. ix, 1). -gara - m. a village husbandman's house, in which he lives; the condition of such a householder. -kā̃gürü - , f. a rudely made peasant's kangrī or portable fireplace (K.Pr. 129). -pacĕ - adj. c.g. equal in rank to a husbandman, a fellow-husbandman. The expression is used in arranging marriages, etc.

e: see guhu.
see gŏn.

m. dust, clouds of dust; vexation, soreness, ill-feeling, affliction, grief; hence (in Kāshmīrī) the suffering from a violent internal pain (such as headache, etc.); unwillingness to do some work ordered by another.

f. a female sheep, a ewe (El. gaub and gob, K.Pr. gub, gabi, or gabih), (K.Pr. 5, 36, 119, 192, 218; W. 18; L. 463, gab; Rām. 94). gabi-buthu - m. 'ewe-faced', one whose face shows that he is easily frightened, timid-faced.…
fullMeaning: f. a female sheep, a ewe (El. gaub and gob, K.Pr. gub, gabi, or gabih), (K.Pr. 5, 36, 119, 192, 218; W. 18; L. 463, gab; Rām. 94). gabi-buthu - m. 'ewe-faced', one whose face shows that he is easily frightened, timid-faced. gabi-buthi rāmahūnu, a wolf with a sheep's face (K.Pr. 63, W. 21). -dŏd - m. ewe's milk (YZ. 90). -gūdu - m. one who is vile and impotent, a mean worthless fellow. Cf. gūdu. -māz - m. ewe's flesh, ewe-mutton (considered to be flavourless). -rôchu - m. a ewe-guardian, a shepherd. -röchi-bāy -- f. a shepherd's wife.

e: (spelling), m. Viburnum cotinifolium, V. fœtens (El. gúch).

or gūḍu (Gr.Gr. 20) , adj. (f. gṻḍ or gǖḍü , Gr.Gr. 20), hidden, invisible; (of a story, poem, etc.) difficult to understand, difficult, mysterious; (of a road or the like) difficult to be traversed or travelled over, almost…
fullMeaning: or gūḍu (Gr.Gr. 20) , adj. (f. gṻḍ or gǖḍü , Gr.Gr. 20), hidden, invisible; (of a story, poem, etc.) difficult to understand, difficult, mysterious; (of a road or the like) difficult to be traversed or travelled over, almost impassable, difficult of access or issue; (of a person) a dolt, an idiot, one who no matter how one teaches him cannot learn what is taught.

e: (cf. ) or (Rām. 1496) guzarun conj. 3 (2 p.p. gudaryōv ), to happen, befall (esp. of some trouble, grief, or calamity), (H. v, 9, where gudariv is poet. for gudaryōv, viii, 5).
f. an unchaste woman (one who by her unchastity has diseased private parts). Cf. gōda and gūdu.
m. a cow's tethering rope (one end fastened round the neck and the other to a peg in the ground) (K.Pr. 219).
f. in guḍārĕ gĕwañĕ f. pl. inf. to refuse to carry out an order by making pretended excuses.
f., i.q. gurü 1. This is the form in use towards Islāmābād (El.).
m. obsc. the anus, cf. gōda; vulva (El.). Cf. Gr.Gr. 19.
m. a small round metal pot, shaped like a bowl (El.), a lōṭā. -golu - m. the top or mouth of a lōṭā,the part above the neck. -ʦoku m. the bowl of a lōṭā.
m. a child's swinging cot, a swing.
f. the 'thundering' of the human voice in abuse, loud roaring in abuse.

f. a kind of blanket worn on journeys in wet weather. One edge is gathered up and fastened in a bunch. This is put over the head, and the remainder falls over the rest of the body, thus protecting the clothes beneath from the…
fullMeaning: f. a kind of blanket worn on journeys in wet weather. One edge is gathered up and fastened in a bunch. This is put over the head, and the remainder falls over the rest of the body, thus protecting the clothes beneath from the rain.

e: m. onomat. (Śiv. 503).
or (Gr.M.) gugūstulu m. a swing (in which people swing themselves for enjoyment); a swing perch (in a parrot's cage) (Gr.M.). --trāwun --, m.inf. to swing oneself in a swing (Gr.M.).

m. cow-dung; buffalo-dung (K.Pr. 251); manure (El. guh, q.v. for description of the various methods of applying manure) (L. 459, gu). Cf. gŏh. guhi-ambār - m. a pile of cow-dung, a dunghill. -bonu - m. a medium-sized dung-heap…
fullMeaning: m. cow-dung; buffalo-dung (K.Pr. 251); manure (El. guh, q.v. for description of the various methods of applying manure) (L. 459, gu). Cf. gŏh. guhi-ambār - m. a pile of cow-dung, a dunghill. -bonu - m. a medium-sized dung-heap (Śiv. 126). -gān - m. a room in which cow-dung is stored (esp. by cowkeepers who own many cattle). -khürü - f. a woman engaged in collecting or clearing away cow-dung; hence, met. any woman dirty in person and clothing. -kyomu - m. a certain worm bred in cow-dung. -lôdu - m. a large pile or stack of cow-dung, collected in winter with the object of drying it in the summer. -lōla - m. a fool (in conversation, etc.). --liwun -- m. inf. to plaster with cow-dung. -lyobu - m. the amount of cow-dung evacuated by the animal at one time. -nôru - m. the rectum. -ryūnzu - - m. (sg. dat. -rīnzis -), the scarabæus beetle. It makes balls of cow-dung and mud and rolls them along. According to popular tradition it has quarrelled with the sea and makes these balls in order to fill it up (Śiv. 1647, 1648, Rām. 436).

e: m. dirty, muddy, etc. (of water or the like) (Gr.M.). Cf. gọ̆lu.
f. a Gujoru woman (Gr.Gr. 39). See gujoru.

or gūjü , f. the kernel of a fruit (e.g. of a walnut, a cocoa-nut, or water-chestnut) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 66, 100, Śiv. 1807); the kernel or inner meaning of anything, intelligible only to the initiated. Cf. gūlu 2 and Gr.Gr. 36.…
fullMeaning: or gūjü , f. the kernel of a fruit (e.g. of a walnut, a cocoa-nut, or water-chestnut) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 66, 100, Śiv. 1807); the kernel or inner meaning of anything, intelligible only to the initiated. Cf. gūlu 2 and Gr.Gr. 36. gōjĕ-pĕndulu - or -panzulu - m. a complete, unbroken kernel of a walnut (i.e. all the four sections unseparated from each other). -tīl - m. oil derived from kernels (e.g. walnut-oil). -ʦhar - f. a large kind of basket in which walnut kernels and the like are carried about for sale.

e: gujur, or gujuru m. (f. gujaröñü , q.v.s.v., and gujȧri-bāy -, see bel.), a man of a certain pastoral tribe which roams over the hills of Kashmīr and the neighbouring countries, the Gujurs of Swāt, and the Gūjars of Western India…
fullMeaning: gujur, or gujuru m. (f. gujaröñü , q.v.s.v., and gujȧri-bāy -, see bel.), a man of a certain pastoral tribe which roams over the hills of Kashmīr and the neighbouring countries, the Gujurs of Swāt, and the Gūjars of Western India (Gr.Gr. 39). gujȧri-bāy - f. the wife of a Gujoru. -künḍü - f. a Gujoru camp. -koṭu - m. a Gujoru lad. -küṭü - f. a Gujoru lass.

e: orgȧji f. the opening of a native cooking-range through which fuel is fed (K.Pr. 26, 48, 54, 64, 119, 256). Cf. dān 1, gag, and golu 1. gajĕ-ṭhoru - m. the cover or door (usually of earthenware) of this opening.
see galun.
m. a deadly epidemic affecting first the lower animals and subsequently human beings, plague.
m. wheat bran, the husk of ground wheat when sifted apart (K.Pr. 130, translated 'straw').

f. N. of a kind of rice (requiring to be cooked in sixteen parts of water to one of rice, and especially suitable as an easily digested food for invalids). -kand - m. conserve of roses, candied roses. -ĕ-kōsam - m. safflower…
fullMeaning: f. N. of a kind of rice (requiring to be cooked in sixteen parts of water to one of rice, and especially suitable as an easily digested food for invalids). -kand - m. conserve of roses, candied roses. -ĕ-kōsam - m. safflower (Rām. 1006). -marg - m. N. of a well-known flowery valley about 3,000 feet above the valley of Kashmīr, much frequented by Europeans in the heat of summer. Cf. El. s.v. -shan m. a rose (or flower) garden (YZ. 232, Rām. 319, 369). -ĕ-sōsan m. the white iris, commonly planted on graves (L. 248). -ĕ-tölīm m. the pattern of a Kashmīr shawl intended for the manufacturer, that he may see the design of the shawl. Cf. ganḍan-wôlu, s.v. ganḍun 2, and tölīm. -zār m. a rose (or flower) garden (YZ. 46, Rām. 22, 188); a bed of roses (Rām. 1664).

e: m. a species of bracelet, massive and open (El.).
m. the act of churning or beating up by hand of two liquids together (e.g. curdled milk and water).

f. N. of a certain plant, the leaves of which grow along the ground, and the juice of which is used as a cooling drink in fevers, consumption, etc.; according to L. 76, it is an internal styptic. El. has gul, Cichorium intybus,…
fullMeaning: f. N. of a certain plant, the leaves of which grow along the ground, and the juice of which is used as a cooling drink in fevers, consumption, etc.; according to L. 76, it is an internal styptic. El. has gul, Cichorium intybus, and gúl, Plantago major. Cf. baḍa-gula, s.v. baḍa. -byôlu - m. the seed of this plant, used as a medicine for dysentery. -hākh - - m. (sg. dat. -hākas -), the leaf of this plant, which is boiled like a vegetable to extract the juice used as ab. -ras - m. the juice, as ab. -wạthar - m., i.q. -hākh ab.

e: m. a kind of sweet cake (wheat-flower, sugar, curdled milk, with anise and cardamom seeds, made into balls or dumplings and fried in clarified butter). -goru - m. a man who makes and sells these cakes. -kroʦhu - m. the ladle he…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of sweet cake (wheat-flower, sugar, curdled milk, with anise and cardamom seeds, made into balls or dumplings and fried in clarified butter). -goru - m. a man who makes and sells these cakes. -kroʦhu - m. the ladle he uses.

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. gulovu ), to roll something in the mouth, to mumble it without swallowing it.
f. a small ball, a bullet (K.Pr. 86); a pill. Cf. gōla 1. --layüñü-- f.inf. to hit with a bullet (obj. in dat., Gr.M.). --trāwüñü -- f.inf. to fire, or discharge, a bullet (Gr.M.).
f. a widow woman who takes service as a concubine. Cf. gōla 2. gōli-kaṭh - m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas -), a son begotten on a widowed maidservant.
or gul-ĕ anār m. the flower of the pomegranate (Rām. 646, 1018); hence, as adj. c.g. very red, crimson (Śiv. 13).

m. the forearm, the arm between the elbow and the wrist (K.Pr. 10, Rām. 1305, 1418, 1538); the wrist (El.). --˚ it often means one of a pair (of armlets or the like). Cf. bȧhi 1 and bāwoṭu. guli ālawȧni m. pl. inf. to wave the…
fullMeaning: m. the forearm, the arm between the elbow and the wrist (K.Pr. 10, Rām. 1305, 1418, 1538); the wrist (El.). --˚ it often means one of a pair (of armlets or the like). Cf. bȧhi 1 and bāwoṭu. guli ālawȧni m. pl. inf. to wave the forearms; esp. to pass the hands over the head and face in order to pacify, or to show affection (K.Pr. 13). --ganḍȧni -- m. pl. inf. to bind the forearms, to stand in a reverent attitude with the arms folded in front (H. v, 9); to stand with the hands folded together in reverence (Śiv. 718, 721, 791, 1155, 1296, 1394, 1457, 1504; Rām. 494, 505, 852). -ʦoṭu - adj. (f. -ʦüṭü -), one whose forearm is cut, i.e. who has had his hand cut off at the wrist, either as a punishment for theft or as the result of disease (cf. Rām. 1305). guli-myūṭhu - m. a kiss on the forearm; hence, a bracelet or other ornament fastened on the forearm of a child on the occasion of some festival, or on that of a bride at a wedding, by the relations or connexions by marriage. Cf. L. 258, 271, and Rām. 1093. -ʦopu - m. a bite on the forearm (cf. Rām. 1538). -walun-hyuhu -- adj. (f. -walüñü-hishü --), one, e.g. an official, who has fallen under the influence of a plausible servant or friend. -walun-lāyĕkh -- adj. (f. -walüñü-lāyĕkh -), id.

e: (Rām. 839), i.q. gōla 1, q.v.

m. (pl. dat. gōlĕn Gr.Gr. 56), the kernel of a fruit; esp. the kernel of the water-chestnut (Trapa bispinosa) (Gr.Gr. 36, 56). El. golí and gúlyí, both fem. Cf. gôru and görü, also gūji. El. has also gúl, Plantago major. Cf. gula…
fullMeaning: m. (pl. dat. gōlĕn Gr.Gr. 56), the kernel of a fruit; esp. the kernel of the water-chestnut (Trapa bispinosa) (Gr.Gr. 36, 56). El. golí and gúlyí, both fem. Cf. gôru and görü, also gūji. El. has also gúl, Plantago major. Cf. gula 2. gūli-kuʦori - m. (f. kuʦarĕñ ), a water-chestnut sheller, a man who makes a living by shelling water-chestnuts and selling the kernels. The f. is either his wife or a woman who earns her living in this way.

e: m. one who takes care of a herd of horses during the pasturage season (El.). Cf. galwān 2.

m. sweat, perspiration (Gr.Gr. 136, Rām. 1041, 1042). --ḍalun -- m.inf. sweat to burst out owing to modesty or awe. -hotu - adj. (f.-hüʦü -), covered with sweat, sweaty, all in a muck of sweat (Gr.Gr. 136). -shrān - m. a…
fullMeaning: m. sweat, perspiration (Gr.Gr. 136, Rām. 1041, 1042). --ḍalun -- m.inf. sweat to burst out owing to modesty or awe. -hotu - adj. (f.-hüʦü -), covered with sweat, sweaty, all in a muck of sweat (Gr.Gr. 136). -shrān - m. a sweat-bath, the bursting forth of sweat, so that one is as it were bathed in it. --yunu -- m.inf. sweat to come, guma ām, I am sweating (K.Pr. 12).

e: m. doubt, surmise, conjecture, opinion (Gr.M., Rām. 231, 463). --karun -- m.inf. to believe, fancy, conjecture (Gr.M., YZ. 199).
m. slight dirtiness, smuttiness (of something darkened in colour by dirt) (Gr.Gr. 140).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. gumanyōv ), to be discoloured, dirtied, (of something white) to become or be grey (Gr.Gr. xix).
m. an agent, superintendent, manager of a business (El., Gr.M.).
f. a kind of cloth, dimity.
m. a kind of firework, a bomb fired into the air, and there exploded.
m. an arch, vault; a dome, cupola. -shĕbd - m. the sound of a dome; hence, an echo.
or gumunu adj. (f. gumüñü ), slightly dirtied, discoloured, blackened, smutted (Gr.Gr. 130).

f. a pack-saddle, a pair of large saddle-bags used for conveying grain, etc., on an animal's back. They are generally made of goat's hair (El.) (YZ. 421, 427, abl. gon̄ih). guni-tolu- m. one side or sack of such a pack-saddle.
m. a colouring material made up of red chalk and other materials, used to polish gold ornaments, a kind of jeweller's rouge.
(spelling), m. an amethyst (El.).

f. (sg. dat. gunasi ), a poisonous, round-headed, short, thick serpent found in the mountains of Kashmīr. It is said to be black on the back and yellowish on the belly. It is a foot and a half long, and, according to some…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. gunasi ), a poisonous, round-headed, short, thick serpent found in the mountains of Kashmīr. It is said to be black on the back and yellowish on the belly. It is a foot and a half long, and, according to some natives, ash-coloured. Its bite is often fatal (El., q.v. s.vv. ganas and gunas for further particulars; see also L. 155, K.Pr. 79, 212, W. 122, Rām. 1469). gunasa-bacĕ - m. a young gunasa; met. a man who habitually gives sorrow to others. -pūtu - m., id.

e: f. a scorpion (El.).
(spelling), m. a crown, a diadem (El.). Probably incorr. for gọ̆ndu, q.v.
m., i.q. gonḍu 2, q.v. Cf. gar-gunḍa s.v. gara, and K.Pr. 65.
adj. c.g. drowsy, sleepy; (of a sick man) comatose.
m. a turnip (El.). Cf. gŏgul.

or gunusu m. a kind of metal bracelet or armlet. According to El., s.v. gunus, it is a small band adorned with beads, etc., and is worn by Musalmān women. gunȧsi-dāv - f. such an armlet worn thin by use. -horu - m. a pair of…
fullMeaning: or gunusu m. a kind of metal bracelet or armlet. According to El., s.v. gunus, it is a small band adorned with beads, etc., and is worn by Musalmān women. gunȧsi-dāv - f. such an armlet worn thin by use. -horu - m. a pair of armlets. -jūri - f., id.

e: etc., see gũ̄̈ṭh, etc.
(f. guñü ), suff. added to a numeral meaning 'fold', 'times', as in dŏgunu, twofold, double; aiṭha-gunu, eightfold. Cf. gonu 1.

f. (for 2 see gonu ), a piece or fragment, esp. of flesh or fish (H. viii, 13; x, 7; in each case pieces of a python); often --˚, as in gāḍa-güñü, lumps of fish (see gāḍ and K.Pr. 205, -gani), manz-güñü, the middle slice of a…
fullMeaning: f. (for 2 see gonu ), a piece or fragment, esp. of flesh or fish (H. viii, 13; x, 7; in each case pieces of a python); often --˚, as in gāḍa-güñü, lumps of fish (see gāḍ and K.Pr. 205, -gani), manz-güñü, the middle slice of a fish (K.Pr. 136, -gani). gañi-bāgay - f. dividing out by bits (e.g. a tree cut up and divided amongst people).

e: see gonu 1 and 2.
see gŏndun 2.

m. (sg. dat. günzüs or ganzas Gr.Gr. 54), a tanner, a currier (K.Pr. 65 gaṅz). -phakh - m. (sg. dat. -phakas -), 'a currier-stink,' a currier who is poor, wretched, and evil-smelling owing to his occupation; met. any vile person.
m. giving charity or conferring benefits privately, "letting not the left hand know what the right hand doeth."
m. N. of a village at the east foot of the Taḵẖt-ĕ Sulaimān or Gōpādri Hill near Śrīnagar (RT.Tr. II, 290, 454, Śiv. 953).

m. (sg. dat. gupanas), an animal of the cattle class (bulls, cows, calves, generally) (K.Pr. 219, Śiv. 1464); a quadruped (El.); met. a man who leads the life of and has the morals of cattle; pl. cattle (Gr.Gr. 152, K.Pr. 71,…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. gupanas), an animal of the cattle class (bulls, cows, calves, generally) (K.Pr. 219, Śiv. 1464); a quadruped (El.); met. a man who leads the life of and has the morals of cattle; pl. cattle (Gr.Gr. 152, K.Pr. 71, 227). gupan-ḍangij f. a platform built on one side of a cowhouse, on which, for the sake of its warmth, people live in the winter. Cf. ḍangij for particulars. -gān - m. a cowhouse. -gūru - m. a cowherd, a milkman, a dairyman. These men in the spring-time collect large herds of cattle, belonging to others, and drive them away to the mountains to graze. They take their wives and families with them (El. gŏpan-gúr; K.Pr. 172). -khĕji - or -khë̆jü - f. a moderately sized herd of cattle. -khyolu - m. a large herd of cattle, such as is driven out to the mountains for grazing (Gr.Gr. 152). -nĕnd - f. a method of weeding wet rice-fields by causing cattle to splash up and down the wet fields of mud (L. 327, 463). -rôchu - or (El.)-rachan-wôlu -- m. a cattle herd, a man who drives out cattle for grazing and watches them. -wôlu - n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ -), one who possesses herds; one rich in cattle (Gr.Gr. 136).

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. gupu; impve. sg. 2, guph ), to hide, conceal; conj. part. gupith used as adv. secretly (Rām. 21, 519).
f. a woman as stupid as cattle, a stupid woman (f. of gupun, cattle).
m. in gūrukumundī m. Sphæranthus mollis (El.). Cf. mundī.
m.onomat. a rumble, thunder. --karun -- m.inf. to rumble, to thunder (K.Pr. 116, gar gar).

for guroṭu, q.v., in the following:--gura-dāñĕ - m. a kind of paddy with the husk of a light-tawny colour, and large white rice-grains. -kanōra - m. another kind of paddy, 'the light-tawny slave.' It has the tip of the husk…
fullMeaning: for guroṭu, q.v., in the following:--gura-dāñĕ - m. a kind of paddy with the husk of a light-tawny colour, and large white rice-grains. -kanōra - m. another kind of paddy, 'the light-tawny slave.' It has the tip of the husk light-tawny coloured and its grain white. -küʦhü - f. a kind of shrub growing in the wilds. It is used for making the kāngrī or Kāshmīrī portable brazier. Cf. köñü 2. -kāʦuru - adj. (f. -kāʦürü -), (of a man or a beast) of a light-tawny complexion or colour. -mushikh - or -mushĕkh - f. (sg. dat. -mushki -), 'light-tawny musk,' a kind of paddy with light-tawny husk and sweet-scented pale-yellow grain. -ṭö̃jü - f.'the light-tawny pear', another similar paddy, but with a large white grain.

e: or gūra-gūra - m. swinging, dandling, rocking (a child) (Śiv. 329, 1321, 1381; Rām. 210, 211, 1040); met. a gentle rocking of a house by an earthquake or the like.
m. Rubus lasiocarpus (El.).
m. the condition of being of a light-tawny colour, light tawniness. Cf. guroṭu.
m. the Himālaya chamois (El.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. guraṭyōv ), to be light tawny coloured, to be fair coloured (Gr.Gr. xix).
adj. c.g. pompous, haughty; a bully, tyrannous.
m. muddy water. Cf. guruṭu.

(sg. dat. haki ), a market cry, a cry or loud proclamation made in a market by a seller of something which he has not with him, but which is deposited elsewhere. --diñü -- f.inf. to utter such a cry; met. to make a loud public proclamation of some fact, esp. of some fact hitherto kept secret. --dith nērun -- m.inf. having made such proclamation to go forth; met. owing to some trouble or sorrow, to tell one's friends and relations, and then to abandon one's former mode of life, one's hitherto virtuous conduct, or the like. haki khasun m.inf. to utter the market cry, e.g. to go into the market and proclaim that there is a boatfull of fruit, etc., for sale lying by a neigh ouring river bank.

e: m. the cry uttered in driving away cows. --hȧkhi karun -- m.inf. to urge on (a child or a servant engaged in any work), so as to get him to work quicker and finish it soon.

m.inf. to be struck dumb, dumbfounded, struck, confounded, confused, amazed, aghast (= Hindostanī hakkā-bakkā hōnā).

'a doctor's shop'; a place appointed for the assembling of sick persons and of doctors to cure them, a hospital, a dispensary.

fullMeaning: m. (sg. abl. hala 1 ), a plough. A plough and a pestle are the weapons of Balarāma, the brother of Kṛṣṇa (K. 909), and also (Śiv. 13, 1160) of the elephant-god Gȧnish or Gaṇēśa. hala kaḍun m.inf. to draw out from the plough, i.e. to carry on all the agricultural operations necessary for a field from the commencement of ploughing up to the time of sowing.

fullMeaning: m. state, condition, circumstances, case, situation (YZ. 10, 247; Śiv. 700, 812, 1316, etc.; H. vii, 9; ix, 4; Rām. 51, 211, 292, etc.); existing or present state (Śiv. 279, 372); as adv. at present, now (Śiv. 1748). kami hāla, in what condition ? as adv. wonderfully, in wondrous way (Śiv. 814, 943, 972). hāl hölī , the whole state of affairs, an account or story in detail (Rām. 465). --karun -- m.inf. to arrange a state of affairs, to arrange (H. x, 17). -mast - m. a man of position (K.Pr. 133). hāli-hairān - adj. c.g. in a state of confusion, perplexed, distracted, harassed (Rām. 320, 850, 1218, 1662); engaged on some profitless labour, wasting one's time (K.Pr. 142). -hairönī - f. a state of confusion, perplexity, distraction, harassment; profitless labour, waste of time. hālas adv. for the present. hālay (abl. hāla, with emphatic y), in (such and such) a condition, etc. (Śiv. 661, 831, 1330). hālạy adv. just now, even now.

fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. höjü , Gr.Gr. 169), a house, a hall. Generally used --˚, and then sometimes masc. (dat. -hālas -, Gr.Gr. 69), thus hȧsti- hāl, f. an elephant-stable; bö̃di-hāl, f. a prison (YZ. 384, 385; H. ix, 4), but ʦāṭa-hāl, m. a school- house (Kaśmīraśabdāmṛta, II, i, 287).

fullMeaning: m. the front skirt of the phĕran or long gown worn by Kāshmīrīs (K.Pr. 50, 153). e: m. a maker of halawa (q.v.), a confectioner (El. halawóí and halwáí). halwöyi-wān - m. a confectioner's shop.

m. the pole by which a boat is propelled in a river (esp. upstream), a punting-pole (Śiv. 1780, 1841). A boat is usually equipped with two, a longer, called hama-tulu, and a shorter, called hama-tüjü. They are made of young…
fullMeaning: m. the pole by which a boat is propelled in a river (esp. upstream), a punting-pole (Śiv. 1780, 1841). A boat is usually equipped with two, a longer, called hama-tulu, and a shorter, called hama-tüjü. They are made of young deodārs (L. 79). hama-tüjü - f., see ab. In Gr.M. spelt hama-tujü. -tulu - m., see ab. -tuli zīrü - f. pushing with such a pole, punting. --wāyun -- m.inf. to propel (a boat) with a punting pole, to punt (Śiv. 1488, 1805).

fullMeaning: f. a kind of grass growing self-sown in rice-fields, the stalks of which resemble paddy stalks, Panicum colonum. It is an excellent food for horses (L. 71, Śiv. 1111; cf. dŏda-hāma, p. 189a, l. 35). -dāñĕ - m. the grain of this grass. It is like panic seed, is eaten by Hindūs, and is presented as an offering in Hindū temples (L. 334). -lörü - f. a kind of small cucumber, described as elongated in shape, hollow, and with a good flavour.

m. a carrier of burdens, a porter (L.V. 107, voc. hamāli); (in Kāshmīrī) a grain-carrier (he carries it in leather bags each holding a kharwār or about 152 lb.); a man who lives by tending cows and selling their milk, a cowherd,…
fullMeaning: m. a carrier of burdens, a porter (L.V. 107, voc. hamāli); (in Kāshmīrī) a grain-carrier (he carries it in leather bags each holding a kharwār or about 152 lb.); a man who lives by tending cows and selling their milk, a cowherd, a milkman. --wadun -- m.inf. to perform an ancient method of lamentation on the decease of the head of a household. In this the surviving relatives every morning for ten days after the death used to collect a crowd of grain-porters and cowherds and sing to them the deeds of the deceased to the accompaniment of loud wailing.

fullMeaning: m. a hot bath, a Turkish bath, ḥammām, a bagnio, either at home or outside (K.Pr. 75, 160, 242). See L. 281 for particulars. -gȧji - f. the furnace of a Turkish bath (K.Pr. 48). --karun m.inf. to take a course of Turkish baths as a cure for rheumatism. It lasts one or two days.

fullMeaning: m. N. of a certain mantra, or mystic formula used by Śaiva Hindūs. It is said to be a representation of the Sanskrit words sō 'ham, written in reversed order as 'haṁ saḥ, meaning 'I am that', i.e. 'I am one with God', or 'God and I are one'. It is thus used as a name for the sacred syllable ōṁ, in its character of the anāhata śabda (in Kāshmīrī, anāhath, or anāhata, shĕbd) or unobstructed sound, also called the azapā (see anāhata-shĕbd and azapā) or unuttered word. It is described as being almost inarticulate, and as being really uttered only by the deity, indwelling in the breast of the worshipper, and therefore to have no human utterer or obstructer of its sound. It is often represented as being equivalent to the Supreme Himself (Śiv. 1011, 1027, 1064, 1687, 1693, 1783). When this mantra is mentioned, by a play of meanings, it is often capable of being translated by 'swan' (hams 1). Cf. hamsa-nād, bel. hamsa-gad - m. i.q. -nād, bel. (Śiv. 1607). -gath - f. (sg. dat. -güʦü -), the unobstructed path of this mantra, as explained ab. (L.V. 65). -nād - m. i.q. haṁs, ab. Owing to the play on the meaning of haṁs 1 mentioned ab., this formula is represented as having wings to bear the soul to the Supreme (Śiv. 897, 1516, 1827, 1891). Cf. JRAS., 1910, p. 1337.

m. N. of the Hindū god Viṣṇu, one of the members of the triad of great gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. Under the name of Hari, Viṣṇu is looked upon as the special protector of his devotees when in trouble. Hence, he is often called…
fullMeaning: m. N. of the Hindū god Viṣṇu, one of the members of the triad of great gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. Under the name of Hari, Viṣṇu is looked upon as the special protector of his devotees when in trouble. Hence, he is often called upon in the Sanskrit vocative case harē (e.g. Śiv. 733, 1841, etc.), and his name is sometimes even quoted, esp. m.c., in the Sanskrit nom. sg., i.e. hariḥ (e.g. Śiv. 1402). Other Sanskrit forms are also met in Śiv., e.g. harēḥ , the gen. sing. in the sense of the dat. sg. hari-har - (Śiv. 856), hariḥ-har - (Śiv. 1100, 1104) or harī-har - (Śiv. 1164) m. [voc. harē-hara - (Śiv. 1296), harē-haray - (Śiv. 934), hari-hara - (Śiv. 1587), or hariḥ-haray - (Śiv. 1636)], Hari and Hara, i.e. Viṣṇu and Śiva (see har 1); esp. Viṣṇu (the Preserver) considered as one with Śiva (the destroyer). This is considered to be a profound religious mystery. hari-nārāyan - m. i.q. hari 1 ab. (Śiv. 700, Rām. 119). hari-shĕmbhu - m., i.q. hari-har ab., Sanskrit sg. voc. harē- shĕmbhō (Śiv. 1722-3).

fullMeaning: interj. of respect, used by a man to a man, as in hē huzūr, sir; hē nārān, O Nārāyaṇa (L.V. 109; Śiv. 14, 155, et passim; Rām. 50, 51, etc.); the word juv or sö (or sa, Gr.M.) or both are often suffixed to the noun, but juv cannot be used with a word indicating caste. Thus hē nārān juv, hē nārān sö, hē nārān juv sö; hē gana kaul, O Gaṇa Kaul; hē rāma kaul sö, O Rāma Kaul. We cannot say hē gana kaul juv, because kaul is a caste-name. Cf. Gr.Gr. 96 and Gr.M. s.v. Gr.M. gives also forms such as hē söhib-a, hē söhib-a-sa, hē söhib . . . hasa, all meaning 'sir'. In Śiv. 507 (hē bawānī) the interj. is used in addressing a goddess.

fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. hyoku ; f. hë̆cü ; 2 p.p. hĕcyōv ), to act or strive successfully in some difficult task (L.V. 108); to be able, to can. This verb is commonly used to form a potential compound with the conj. part. of another verb. In such cases it generally indicates physical ability as opposed to tagun (q.v.), which implies mental ability (i.e. to be able to do a thing, in the sense of knowing how to do it). Thus, --anith, to be able to bring; --būzith, to be able to hear; --dith, to be able to give, and so on. In this meaning the future tense of hĕkun is usually employed in the sense of the present, as in hĕka arzith, I can earn. Cf. Gr.M. s.v. (L.V. 107; YZ. 48, 142, 222; Śiv. 711, 895, 908, 1099, 1624, 1631, 1633; Rām. 196, 211, 293, 581, 631, 645, etc.). --pyonu -- m.inf. 'striving one's best to fall (to one's lot)', to be compelled to use all one's power's, esp. when the task is beyond one's strength. Cf. hĕka-hĕkh, s.v. hĕkh 2, and hĕkath pë̆ñü, s.v. hĕkath. hĕkan-höjü - f. (applied to a person) vigorous ability, esp. in setting people by the ears, in doing profitless or improper actions, or the like. -hyuru - m. id. -wôlu - n.ag. (f. -wājyĕñ -), possessed of ability, powerful; esp. one who is mighty both in quarrelling and as a carrier of heavy loads. Commonly used with reference to an able-bodied virago.

e: f. (sg. dat. hērüʦü ), N. of a celebrated Hindū festival, the Sanskrit Śivarātri, in honour of the god Shiv (Śiva), lasting for five days from the 11th lunar day of the dark half of Phāgun (in Skr. Phālguna = February-March)…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. hērüʦü ), N. of a celebrated Hindū festival, the Sanskrit Śivarātri, in honour of the god Shiv (Śiva), lasting for five days from the 11th lunar day of the dark half of Phāgun (in Skr. Phālguna = February-March) until the day of the new moon (L. 266, K.Pr. 81, Śiv. 524). It is preceded by a festival of cleansing the house, commencing on the 1st lunar day of the dark fortnight and ending on the 8th. Cf. ḍulu 1 and huru 2. hērüʦü-bôgü - m. N. of a present given by the relations of a Hindū girl to the relations of her husband on this festival. -truwāh - f. (sg. dat. -truwöshü -), the thirteenth lunar day of the dark half of Phāgun, being the middle day of the Hērath festival. According to tradition King Dāmodara II of Kashmīr was changed into a serpent, and was told that he would never leave his snake-form till the whole of the Sanskrit Rāmāyaṇa was read through to him on the night of this date. No one has ever succeeded in accomplishing this feat, and he still lies under the curse (RT.Tr. note to i, 166).

(f. --āmüʦü --), received as a share; met. received as one's lot in life (i.e. a husband by a wife, or a wife by a husband). --bāgay -- f. division into shares, calculation of the amount of each share. --khasun -- m.inf. the share to mount; hence, to be received as one's share. --karȧni -- m.pl.inf. to divide a number of articles into shares, to divide out a number of articles; to cut up a single thing into shares. zah hissa karȧni, to divide or cut in two (Gr.M.). -nomu - m. a very small portion of anything (quasi, as much as can be lifted on a finger-nail). -pāsa - (= ) m. a share of property due from another in whose possession the whole is. -rasa - (= ) m. a share in joint family property, the amount due to each coparcener. -wôlu - m. (f. -wājĕñ -), a shareholder, coparcener.

e: m. (f. hissadariñ ), a shareholder; a partner in a business.

Moreover, although reported as fem., it is masc. in the following. --hyonu -- m.inf. only to mention; in order to remind a person of some thing or action, to utter its name and nothing more.

interj. an exclamatory pleon. suff. used in conversation, as in kyāh-hŏ, what? (H. v, 4).

f. disobedience, obstinacy (esp. of a child, a horse, or the like), in spite of urging. Cf. haḍ 1. In K.Pr. 28 and W. 123, the word is translated 'weeping' (huḍ). The word may be a misprint for hã̄ḍ, q.v. --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to…
fullMeaning: f. disobedience, obstinacy (esp. of a child, a horse, or the like), in spite of urging. Cf. haḍ 1. In K.Pr. 28 and W. 123, the word is translated 'weeping' (huḍ). The word may be a misprint for hã̄ḍ, q.v. --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to show obstinacy (esp. of a child who refuses to study, or a horse that jibs, in spite of beating). --yiñü -- f.inf. obstinacy (generally, not specially of a boy or a horse) to be shown.

e: f. engagement in a difficult but objectless or useless work. Cf. họ̆du. hŏdahari-bāz - m. a man accustomed to engage himself in work which while troublesome and difficult is at the same time useless or purposeless.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hŏdahariladiñ ), (of a person) one who is engaged in work which is troublesome and difficult, and at the same time useless or purposeless; (of a work) troublesome, etc., as ab.
adj. c.g. a person of an angry and obstinate temperament.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hŏḍiladiñ ), one who is attacked with a fit of anger, and refuses obstinately to be placated.

adj. (f. hö̆zü ), (of food) dry, wanting in gravy, oil, ghī, or the like, insipid; plain boiled rice (Gr.Gr. 27); met. (of conversation, or the like) dry, insipid, wanting in affection; (of a task or journey) useless, objectless.…
fullMeaning: adj. (f. hö̆zü ), (of food) dry, wanting in gravy, oil, ghī, or the like, insipid; plain boiled rice (Gr.Gr. 27); met. (of conversation, or the like) dry, insipid, wanting in affection; (of a task or journey) useless, objectless. Kāshmīrīs eat a mouthful of rice and a mouthful of vegetables alternately. If the vegetables are exhausted first, any rice left is called họ̆du, and is not eaten (K.Pr. 82). -họ̆khu - adj. (f. hŏ̈zü-hŏ̈chü -), dry and insipid, as ab. (lit. and met.). Cf. họ̆khu-họ̆du (p. 327b, l. 8). hö̆zü har f. a causeless, objectless, quarrel.

fullMeaning: f. a pearl-oyster shell (Śiv. 1551, 1755; Rām. 1142); the shell of any aquatic mollusc (cf. kŏla-hö̃giñ, s.v. kŏl 2); ? a snail (L. 157, 464, hāngi). --gaʦhüñü -- f.inf. to become an oyster-shell; met. to become excessively thin, to be wasted to a skeleton from disease, grief, etc. hö̃giñĕ-mŏkta - m. a pearl from a pearl oyster (not one from an elephant's frontal bone, or any other similar object popularly counted as a pearl).

(sg.dat. hö̃kali ), a chain (YZ. 280); esp. a door-chain, or similar chain for fastening up a chest or the like; a chain for measuring land (mēnan-hö̃kal, El.). --diñü -- f.inf. to apply the chain, to fasten up a door or a chest with a chain. --lagüñü -- f.inf. the door-chain to be applied; met. one's whole family and relations to be destroyed (as if the house were perpetually shut up). hö̃kali-hār - m. 'the cowry in the chain'; N. of an ancient game, in which cowries are thrown in a chain round a board with 64 squares. -pôwu - m. the staple on the opposite leaf of a door to which a chain is fastened when the door is chained up.

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. hö̃kalôwu ), to cause to shrink up through cold, esp. of food cooled to a jelly or the like. hö̃kalôwu-motu - perf. part. (f. hö̃kalöwü-müʦü -), to cause to be shrunken by cold.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. hö̃kalyōv ), to shrink on account of cold (of the body, or of soft warm food, etc., that cools to a jelly). hö̃kalyō-motu - perf. part. (f. hö̃kalyē-müʦü -), shrunken or shrivelled up by cold.

fullMeaning: adj. (f.hünzü ), the postposition of the genitive case, governing the dative; used with all feminine and all plural nouns, and also with animate nouns in the m.sg. In the last case, the final s of the preceding dat. sg. causes the initial h of the hondu to be elided, so that the postposition apparently becomes sondu, as in ʦūra-sondu, of a thief, for ʦūras-hondu, möli-sondi, of a father, for mölis-hondu. This postposition is occasionally used with adverbs, as in yuri-hondu wŏla, come (to the direction) of here, come hither (H. v. 5).

fullMeaning: does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the jh is, subject to the remarks below, represented by j . Thus, the Hindī jhamak , brilliancy, is represented in Kāshmīrī by jamak(h) . Sometimes the jh is retained in writing. Thus, in El., the word jan, a clang, is written jhan, as in Hindī, but this in no way affects the pronunciation. In the present work j will always be written, and jh never, in transliterating Kāshmīrī words, even when an affected purism induces a scribe to write in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. It must, however, be remarked that, so far as the present writer's experience is concerned, he has never come across any instance of the use of this letter, even in the case of borrowed words.

e: that ja is usually pronounced jĕ , ya following a consonant being always sounded as ĕ or yĕ (see article ĕ). Thus, the word jangul , a forest, is commonly written and pronounced jĕngul , and the borrowed Arabic word jald is…
fullMeaning: that ja is usually pronounced jĕ , ya following a consonant being always sounded as ĕ or yĕ (see article ĕ). Thus, the word jangul , a forest, is commonly written and pronounced jĕngul , and the borrowed Arabic word jald is pronounced by some jalad and by others jĕlad . Conversely, an original jy may be represented by j or even z . Thus, the Sanskrit jyōtiṣa- -, an astronomer, is represented in Kāshmīrī by jūtish or even zūtish , as well as by jyūtish , the former being the usual spelling, although the latter, from a Paṇḍit's point of view, is etymologically more correct.

e: The eighth consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is also the eighth consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and is the seventh consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is…
fullMeaning: The eighth consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is also the eighth consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and is the seventh consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is pronounced, as in India proper, something like an English j, but is rather more dental, i.e. the place of contact between the tongue and the palate is slightly nearer the teeth than is the case in English. In schools, its name is zȧyi zö .

fullMeaning: m. a pair, couple (K. 538); one of a pair, a fellow, mate, match, counterpart. This word and jūri are generally, but not always, used with reference to animate objects, while horu, q.v. is generally used for a pair of inanimate objects. Jōra and jūri cannot be used interchangeably. Jōra is most used with numerals, as in akh jōra (but also akh jūri), one pair; zah jōra, two pairs, and so on; but kōtar-jūri, a pair of pigeons; guri-jūri, a pair of horses, and so on; both atha-jōra and atha-jūri, the two hands, with slightly different meanings; see p. 58b, l. 27. It is also looked upon as the singular of the plural zah, two. See Gr.Gr. 81, 82. Cf. jūri. With the suff. of the indef. art. we have jōrāh, see bel. -bôju - m. (of a man or child) a mate, a fellow; one who is alike another in all particulars and actions. -judöyi - f. separation or disassociation of a pair, esp. the dissolution of the union between husband and wife, the sorrow caused to one by the death of the other (K.Pr. 231). -püṭü - f. a double shawl; a shawl made up of two thicknesses or two widths joined together. jōrāh c.g., pl. any pair, some pair (Rām. 447); about two. This word is declined in the plur., c.g. pl. ag. jōrāhau (Gr.Gr. 81, 93). -khanḍā c.g. about two, but a little less (Gr.Gr. 81, 93).

fullMeaning: or (H. vii, 16) judāh adj. c.g. separated, apart (YZ. 191, Rām. 1304); separate, distinct; apart (from), free (from), void (of) (Rām. 1055); apart, broken in two, split apart, split open (Rām. 1709). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go apart, become separated (H. vii, 16). --karun -- m.inf. to separate (El.).

m. (sg. voc. jōgi , Rām. 1778; pl. dat. jōgĕn , Rām. 73, 784, 1735), a kind of Hindū ascetic, a Yōgī, esp. a member of the kan- phaṭā or 'split-eared' Yōgīs (Śiv. 206, 528, 529, 588, etc.; Rām. 96, 1134). -pāthchāh - (= ) m. 'the…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. voc. jōgi , Rām. 1778; pl. dat. jōgĕn , Rām. 73, 784, 1735), a kind of Hindū ascetic, a Yōgī, esp. a member of the kan- phaṭā or 'split-eared' Yōgīs (Śiv. 206, 528, 529, 588, etc.; Rām. 96, 1134). -pāthchāh - (= ) m. 'the King of Yōgīs,' N. of a certain thorny creeper growing on the lower slopes of the hills. In medicine it is used as an antiphlogistic (L. 76). -pöthar - m. the Yōgī character--one of the stock characters in a theatrical performance. -pāwuru - m. a Yōgī's slipper, a magic slipper, by wearing which a Yōgī is supposed to go from place to place through the air.

fullMeaning: m. the bell-shaped pendant of an earring; an earring with one or more of these pendants (K.Pr. 153). -bölī - m. an earring adorned with pendants. -horu - m. a pair of earrings with pendants. -kan - m. a single one of such earrings.

f. (sg. dat. jōrĕ ), two things, a pair of any two similar things. This word is the same in meaning as jōra 1, but the two words are not interchangeable, one being preferred in some cases, and the other in others; see jōra 1.…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. jōrĕ ), two things, a pair of any two similar things. This word is the same in meaning as jōra 1, but the two words are not interchangeable, one being preferred in some cases, and the other in others; see jōra 1. Thus we have dā̃da-jūri, a pair of bullocks (K.Pr. 187); atha-jūri, the two hands; kōtar-jūri, a pair of pigeons; kȧri-jūri, a pair of bracelets. We have both akh jōra and akh jūri meaning a pair; see p. 20a, l. 8. jōrĕ jōrĕ adv. in pairs (K. 1007). --mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to become unbridled, uncurbed, unrestrained. jōri-judöyi - f. separation of a pair, esp. the separation of husband and wife, the sorrow caused to one by the death of the other (cf. jōra-judöyi, K.Pr. 231), (YZ. 557); discord between a married couple (Rām. 1616). -shāla - m. a double shawl (a grand and expensive garment) (Śiv. 281, 1687).

fullMeaning: or jyuv m. a form of address, a term of respect, Sir, Master, used --˚ after a proper name, as hē nārān-juv ho, Sir, Nārān (Gr.Gr. 96); voc. hata juwa, hie, Sir (K.Pr. 80). Similarly, in Śiv. we have brahmā-juv (697, 848, sg. dat; 802, 1116, 1142); krushna-juv (853); nārad-juv (1336, sg. ag.); rāma-juv (1040, 1781); vidura-juv (1328, sg. gen.); vishnu-juv (581), all these being proper names. In Rām. we have brahmā-j(y)uv (597, sg. dat.; 704, 1745, ag.; 1086, 1177, gen.); lȧkhiman-jyuv (380, 1172, sg. ag.); cf. jiy. This word should be distinguished from zuv , which means 'life'.

m. (sg. dat. juwaras ), the edible seeds of a kind of water-lily, the Euryale ferox (El. jewar, so L. 72, 345; Śiv. 1808). juwar-gōjĕ - f.pl. the kernels of this seed.

fullMeaning: f. N. of a garment worn by men, a long gown with flaps in the skirt. The skirt and breast are open, and sometimes has slits in the armpits. It resembles the alkhölikh, q.v., but is fastened with strings instead of buttons (Rām. 976).

fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. kabaṭi ), a boy's game, the kabaḍḍī of India proper. It is a kind of prisoner's base. A boy enters the territory of the rival party and runs through it. He must cry 'kabaṭh' the whole time, and as long as he does so without taking breath he cannot be made a prisoner.

e: f. jaundice, i.q. kāmal 1 and kã̄bal.

fullMeaning: f. N. of a certain medicinal plant, Solanum nigrum, used as an antiperiodic (L. 71, kámbe; 76, kambai; El. kámbeí); i.q. kāmal 2. kā̃bayĕ-byôlu - m. its seed, used as medicine. -pan - - m. its leaf. -ras - m. its juice. -wạthar - m. its leaf.

(sg. dat. kachas ), the short grass of the field, green grass (esp. the kind that grows in damp soil) (K.Pr. 43, L. 463, W. 144, Śiv. 500), met. a trifle (K.Pr. 181). -nĕnd - f. the first of the four khushābas or weedings by hand of a rice field, i.q. arīʦar (L. 463; cf. 327). kacha-döñü - f. also written kadal m. a bridge (Śiv. 1830). See El. s.v. for a full account of the mode in which bridges are made in Kashmīr. The principle is that of a cantilever. -onu - m. a blind man who sits on a bridge to beg from passers…
fullMeaning: also written kadal m. a bridge (Śiv. 1830). See El. s.v. for a full account of the mode in which bridges are made in Kashmīr. The principle is that of a cantilever. -onu - m. a blind man who sits on a bridge to beg from passers by (who for his selfish ends blocks the traffic, and who gets out of the way only when he hears approaching footsteps); met. any selfish person who in every way pursues his own object without consideration for others. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut a bridge; met. (of a mischievous and extravagant wife) altogether to hinder her husband from crossing over to the other side (where prosperity and peace are to be had) (K.Pr. 70). kạdala-bal - m. the bathing place on the bank of a river and close by a bridge. -kānul - m. the main beams that support the floor of the wooden cantilever bridges used in Kashmīr; cf. kānul. -kūṭu - m. the beams (in general) of a bridge. -ṭhoṭhu - m. the central pier supporting a long Kashmīr bridge. It is usually built of stone or brick.

fullMeaning: m. the foot; a footstep, step, pace (El.); (of a horse) his paces, mode of going (K.Pr. 71); a footprint, the mark of a foot (Śiv. 1666). --dyunu -- m.inf. to set forth (H. x, 11, 12). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise the footstep; walk vigorously, step out (K.Pr. 46; Rām. 1648; L.V. 99). --trāwun -- m.inf. to put down the foot, to walk, to step forward (Śiv. 496, 1088; cf. 1849; H. iv, 5).

fullMeaning: or kā̃gürü or kā̃gar f. (sg. dat. kã̄grĕ or kã̄garĕ , abl. kã̄gri ), the portable brazier, or kāngrī, much used in Kashmīr (K.Pr. kángár, 129, 131, 178; káṅgrí, 50, 128, 129). fullMeaning: or kakuv m. (sg. dat. kakawas ), the Bartavelle or Greek partridge (Perdix rufa) (fabled to subsist on moonbeams, and to eat fire at the full moon). It is believed to be tortured by a perpetual thirst, even though it drink water continually, drop by drop (El. and K.Pr. 101, kakkū; K.Pr. 145, kakkav; L. 119, kak, Caccabis chukar; Rām. 97). --karun -- m.inf. to play the partridge, i.e. to abscond, to run away, esp. to do so without being seen (cf. K.Pr. 145). --pạṭharāwun -- m.inf. to dress the hair over the forehead in a certain way used esp. by prostitutes; cf. kōkala. -rangishi - f. (of a human being) quickness in walking, the habit of or facility in walking quickly (cf. K.Pr. 101, the crow learnt to walk like a partridge). -ṭhūl - m. a partridge's egg. -trēsh - f. a partridge's thirst; met. a thirst which is not quenched by frequently repeated small draughts of water.

(sg. dat. -kōcĕ -), a strip of paper; esp. a long strip of paper rolled up, formerly used in Kashmīr for business accounts or the like. -kyomu - m. a paper-worm, an insect which eats and destroys paper that is not cared for, a fish-insect, book-worm, or the like.

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. kalashĕs ), a jar; esp. (among Hindūs) a sacred jar or cup which is set up before beginning the ritual of worship, and into which water and fruits are cast. At the conclusion of the main worship, and after the jar has been removed, these walnuts are distributed to the members of the congregation to be eaten by them. -lawa - f. the ceremonial sprinkling of the worshippers with water from this jar, after the conclusion of the main ritual. -nörü - f. the above jar. -wörü -below; f., id.

m. N. of one of the two great divisions of the Valley of Kashmīr. It comprises the districts on both sides of the river Vĕth (or Jehlam) below Śrīnagar, while the other, Marāz (q.v.), comprises those above. Śrīnagar itself is…
fullMeaning: m. N. of one of the two great divisions of the Valley of Kashmīr. It comprises the districts on both sides of the river Vĕth (or Jehlam) below Śrīnagar, while the other, Marāz (q.v.), comprises those above. Śrīnagar itself is called Yamrāz. The corresponding Skt. names are respectively Kramarājya and Maḍavarājya (RT.Tr. ii, 15, and II, 436). According to popular tradition, however, the valley was once divided between two brothers named, respectively, Kāmanadēva and Malhanadēva, after whom the tracts were named respectively Kāmarājya and Malhanarājya. For another popular etymology, see El. s.v. Kashmír, and K.Pr. 138.

fullMeaning: postpos. governing abl. (cf. kini, of which it is a variant). It also governs the dative if the governed noun or pronoun is or refers to a human being. It indicates locality, as in kala-kȧni, at the head end (of an animal), and laṭi-kȧni, at the tail end (H. xi, 9); route or method, as in dāri-kȧni (flung out) through the window (H. v, 4); and, esp., motion from, as in yĕs-kȧni, from whom (it will escape) (H. ii, 8).

fullMeaning: m. a cause (see bel.) (L.V. 75, Rām. 1421, K. 174); a reason (Gr.M.; Rām. 61, 1300; K. 4); a motive, purpose; a means (L.V. 76 kārȧni pranavȧki, by means of the praṇava, see bel.); (according to Śaiva theology) a causal deity or creator of the universe. There are three of these, viz. Brahmā (the Creator), Viṣṇu (the Preserver), and Mahēśvara or Rudra (the Destroyer), the last-named being one of the forms of Śiva (Śiv. 64, 678, 1158, 1466, 1728). There are also five causes of the universe, viz. the above three, Sadāśiva (Śiva as the lord of the manifested universe), and Īśvara, or Śiva himself. These five are represented by the praṇava, or mystic syllable ōṁ, which is said to be formed from the union of the pentad a, u, m, bindu, and nāda (see bĕnd), or, again, by the five mystic syllables Śi, vā, ya, na, and maḥ, which together are considered to express the same meaning as ōṁ (Śiv. 914, 1520). ādi-kāran, a first cause; ami kārana, for this reason (Gr.M.); wŏtpatti-kāran, a cause of origin, a Creator (Gr.M.).

(f. -maliñü -), 'ram-dirty,' of the mottled or brownish colour of a ram, half-white, half-clean (Gr.Gr. 141). -maṭa - adj. c.g. plump, equally fully-formed all over (without hollows or lumps). -māz - m. mutton (El., W. 114). -ñūri - f. the hoof of a ram. -pröʦü - f. the corner of a ram's mouth; met. something long and creased in two (esp. u.w. reference to the page of a manuscript, which is always two folios made of one sheet folded lengthwise). -prāʦh-hyuhu -- - adj. (f. -prāʦh-hishü --), like the corners of a ram's mouth, long and creased in two, as in the preceding. -pūtu - m. a ram's son, a young sheep, a young ram (Gr.Gr. 131); N. of a child's game, in which a child is carried across the shoulders, as a lamb is carried.

fullMeaning: m. (sg. abl. kāṭha 1 ), wood, dried wood, a stick, a dried hard stalk (L.V. 38; Rām. 1080, 1200; K. 976). Gr.Gr. 163).

fullMeaning: in kaṭh-kār - m. icy cold weather, the freezing cold of a blizzard, or the like (Śiv. 332). -koshu - or kaṭhyushu m. freezingly cold weather accompanied by wind and icy mist (L. 353, kut kushu; Śiv. 336, 347-8; Rām. 674). -kȧshi-dĕv -- m. lit. a frost-demon; hence, freezing weather, stinging, and, so to speak, biting with hailstones; met. a chilly person, who is always cowering over a fire.

(sg. dat. kaʦhas ), the armpit; the corresponding pit at the root of the legs, the groin. kaʦha-brôru m. a bubo, or glandular swelling, in the armpit, the bag̱ẖal- bilāī of India (believed to be dispersed by getting a cat to lick it). -wāl - m. the hair of armpits. -wüṭü - f. (in a Kāshmīrī coat) the gusset under the armpits. kȧʦhi-tȧlimēlun - m.inf. to get quite close under a person's armpits, i.e. approaching a person secretly in order to give a bribe; hence, to give a bribe. -wödürü f. a bubo (El. kaʦawádir m.). --yunu -- m.inf. to get up to a person by his armpit (i.e. unexpectedly, without his seeing, and not straightforwardly from the front), to make a flank attack.

(sg. abl. kāʦa 4 , for 1, 2, see s.vv.), glass (Gr.Gr. 10, 31, 52); crystal; (in Kāshmīrī) a species of pottery made of a fine kind of clay, from which bracelets and certain vessels are made (Gr.Gr. 10). (f. -gȧri-bāy --), a man who makes bracelets, etc., of this pottery (the fem. is either his wife, or a woman who does this work) (El.); a bottle-maker (El.). -koru - m. a kind of bracelet made of this pottery (El.); cf. kaʦha-kar, s.v. kaʦha. -më̆ʦü - f. the fine earth from which this pottery is made. -tĕmbar - m.pl. cataract (the disease of the eyes). -tĕmbarlad - adj. c.g. fullMeaning: kāyuru , sometimes written kāyiru 1 m. the wood of the yörü, or Himalayan blue pine (El. kāyūr or kāiar, Pinus excelsa; Gr.Gr. 139; K.Pr. 101; L. 79, 80, kairu; 456, kayur). This wood is very soft and easy to pierce; the word is hence used met. to indicate a person who is 'soft', i.e. weak, powerless, unresisting; cf. kāyoru 2 and also aḍa-kāyuru, p. 11a, l. 50. The shavings of this wood are used for torches (L. 80), and its fire is not lasting (K.Pr. 101). kāyiri-ʦüñü - f. charcoal made from the wood of the pine-tree.
