It is found in the mountains of Ladak, Baltistān, and Wardwān. kĕli-phamb -, kili-phamb -, or kīli-phamb - m. the under hair of the ibex. It is imported from Ladak and is a valuable shawl-wool. postpos. governing dat. in, as in athas kĕth, in the hand (K.Pr. 29, YZ. 242, Śiv. 620), thālas kĕth, in a dish; nāvi kĕth, in a boat (Śiv. 1589). Generally speaking it can only be used with words signifying a receptacle or a…
fullMeaning: postpos. governing dat. in, as in athas kĕth, in the hand (K.Pr. 29, YZ. 242, Śiv. 620), thālas kĕth, in a dish; nāvi kĕth, in a boat (Śiv. 1589). Generally speaking it can only be used with words signifying a receptacle or a conveyance. Thus, we cannot say garas kĕth, in a house, or mūlas kĕth, in a root, because a house or a root is not used as a receptacle for putting things into. For this purpose a horse or the like, is looked upon as a conveyance, and we can say guris kĕth, which must be translated 'on horseback'; similarly, nakhas- kĕth, on the shoulder (Rām. 890); khŏni-kĕth (carrying a child) on the haunch (H. xi, 13) (Gr.Gr. 43; Gr.M.; W. 97, kĕt; Śiv. 12, 245, 286, 543, 967, etc.; Rām. 151, 305, 625, 665, etc.; K. 378, 429, 433; H. ii, 7; iii, 2). (sg. dat. khaharüñü 2 ), extreme obstinacy in one's opinion or purpose (of a stupid, foolish, person, who has no real reason for his obstinacy), pig-headedness. --lagüñü 2 -- f.inf. such obstinacy to be practised (by such a person). khaharüñü khasun 2 m.inf. to mount on to obstinacy, to be obstinate, as ab. --khotu-motu 2 --- perf. part. (f. --khüʦü-müʦü ---), obstinate, as ab., pig-headed.

e: see khay 1.

e: m. Villarsia nymphoides (El.). Probably khürü-pōsh -. Cf. khoru 1 and kūrū.

adj. c.g. ashamed, abashed; bashful, modest (El. khajal). --karun -- m.inf. to humiliate, abash; esp. to humiliate a person by directing abusive language at him.
see khālun.

fullMeaning: m. a plan, sketch, outline, tracing, delineation; (in Kāshmīrī) the marks or remains on paper after writing or drawing has been rubbed or wiped out. --trāwun -- m.inf. to make the first drawing or outline (as a guide to the painter) of a picture or design that is to be coloured; to mark the lines of a drawing or pattern on a substance to be engraved (as a guide for the engraver).

e: see khakharāray.
m. (sg. dat. khākas ), dust, earth, ashes (YZ. 19; Śiv. 828; Rām. 156, 444, 874, 1537). With iẓāfat, khāk-i-gam, the ashes of grief (Rām. 441).

e: f. onomat. the rustling or crackling sound made by dried skins, sheets of bark, or the like, when they are moved (K.Pr. 26 khakarāy).

e: see khā̃kyulu.
m. a certain small seed used as an eyesalve; Sisymbrium irio (El.), London-rocket.
(spelling) m. the osseous rim of the orbital cavity (El.). Cf. khã̄khur.
adj. (f. khā̃kijü ), somewhat beloved (u.w. reference to a child whom one loves, but whom one is scolding).
m. a mole; an artificial spot painted on the face to increase beauty, a beauty-spot (El., who gives both khal and khál; YZ. 10, 11, 67, 68).

f. dried skin, leather; the skin of a living being (K.Pr. 156, māz vĕʦĕs na khali, his flesh will not fit into his skin, i.e. he will not be able to contain himself for joy); cf. udürü-khal, p. 15a, l. 40. -khish - f.…
fullMeaning: f. dried skin, leather; the skin of a living being (K.Pr. 156, māz vĕʦĕs na khali, his flesh will not fit into his skin, i.e. he will not be able to contain himself for joy); cf. udürü-khal, p. 15a, l. 40. -khish - f. 'slaughtering of hides'; hence, the skin of a sheep, together with all the edible parts, when it is slaughtered, as opp. to the offal (K.Pr. 237, where the compound is freely translated 'slaughter of beasts'). -würü - f. skin-cake, a kind of stew made of chopped sheep- or goat-skin boiled till it is tender and served with spices. This word is generally used in the plural (-warĕ -).

e: m. a maternal uncle, a mother's brother. Sg. voc. khāla (K.Pr. 260, W. 156).
f. oil-cake, i.q. khȧji. Cf. ȧlishi-khal, p. 25b, l. 5.
f. skin. khāla-dar - m. the chess- board square of skin; hence, the position inside the skin, the womb, being born, human life (Śiv. 1644).
adv. at some time or other, sometimes. -kã̄ʦhāh - c.g. an. someone or other.
see khāl 1.
(for ) adv. only , merely. Cf. khöli.

fullMeaning: adv. (for 1, see khal 1), together, as a whole, wholesale (of a number of articles sold together at an inclusive price); cf. khili. -khanjĕ - adv. all together, good and bad together, all sorts together without distinction. khali 1 (for 2, see kholu) in khali karun m.inf. to mix up bad and good together (of grain, or the like, of which the good grains have been originally separated from the bad).

e: or khalükh m. (sg. dat. khalkhas ), creation; mankind; people; the people or population of a country (Rām. 207, 1130).
m. interference (El.). Cf. khilāl 2.

(spelling and gender) N. of a certain medicinal herb, Senecio Jacquemontiana (L. 75).
f. (sg. dat. khạlarüña ?), the act of widening out, opening out (e.g. a narrow hole); spreading out (a garment, or the like). Cf. kholu and khalun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khạlarôwa ), to widen (e.g. a narrow hole); to spread out, loosen (e.g. a garment). This verb is the caus. of khalun, another form being khạjarāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).

m.inf. to become free, be set at liberty (YZ. 462); (of a woman in labour) to be delivered (of the child); met. to become free of worldly troubles, to die (H. iii, 4). --karun -- m.inf. to set at liberty, release (El.). --sapanun…
fullMeaning: m.inf. to become free, be set at liberty (YZ. 462); (of a woman in labour) to be delivered (of the child); met. to become free of worldly troubles, to die (H. iii, 4). --karun -- m.inf. to set at liberty, release (El.). --sapanun -- m.inf. to become free, be set at liberty (YZ. 136). -wôru - m. a deed of sale (of a horse, cow, or the like), a deed of release.

e: m. (sg. dat. khalatas ), a robe; a robe of honour with which princes or those in authority confer dignity on subjects (K.Pr. 245); the complete set of dresses worn by a bridegroom, a bridegroom's outfit of clothes. khalata-bāha -…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. khalatas ), a robe; a robe of honour with which princes or those in authority confer dignity on subjects (K.Pr. 245); the complete set of dresses worn by a bridegroom, a bridegroom's outfit of clothes. khalata-bāha - m. (at a marriage) the present of gold, etc., ornaments given by the father of the bride to the bridegroom, as a contribution towards the cost of his wedding outfit. khalat-ĕ-shöhī m. a royal robe, a magnificent robe of honour (H. x, 4).

e: f. scattering (articles) hither and thither; confusion, commotion, hurry (El.), bustle, hubbub, rushing about and making a stir (K.Pr. 78). Cf. khalbürü.

f. pricking, pain; care, solicitude, anxiety (Rām. 714); apprehension, misgiving; a cause of anxiety, cause of trouble, impediment (Rām. 110); (in Kāshmīrī) the hidden relics of a disease that remain after an apparent cure.
m. (sg. dat. khalkatas ), a created being, a creature (El.); creation, the world, universe (Gr.M.).
f. freedom (El. khalásí). --diñü -- f.inf. to release.
m. lands under management of government, crown or government land (L. 426).

or (El.) khulun conj. 3 (2 p.p. khalyōv ), to be or become spread out or spread about, to be or become wide. The caus. (or tr.) form of this verb is khạlarāwun or khạjarāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). khalyō-motu - perf. part. (f. khalē-müʦü…

e: conj. 1, another form of khārun, q.v. (1 p.p. khôlu , f. khöjü , H. vii, 19; 2 p.p. khājyōv ), to cause to mount, to cause to ascend; to take upstairs (H. x, 7); to fix (upon a machine) (H. vii, 19); zima khālun, to cause…

e: m. (sg. dat. khalaras ), a kind of small stone mortar, used for pounding medicines, etc.

m. a bend, curl, crook; crookedness, curvature (YZ. 51, 53); bending, flexure; being bent into a fork. --aʦun -- m.inf. bending to enter, fiexure or curvature to occur, esp. when the subsequent straightening would be difficult.…
fullMeaning: m. a bend, curl, crook; crookedness, curvature (YZ. 51, 53); bending, flexure; being bent into a fork. --aʦun -- m.inf. bending to enter, fiexure or curvature to occur, esp. when the subsequent straightening would be difficult. --karun -- m.inf. to bend, crooken; to bend, to twirl (a rosary in prayer) (K.Pr. 212).

e: m. unripe, green, crude, immature (K.Pr. 119; Śiv. 1112; Rām. 1030; H. vi, 15); imperfect, bad, inferior, worthless, of small value (K.Pr. 64; Rām. 298, 383); inexpert, inexperienced; untaught and stupid (K.Pr. 11); not solid or…
fullMeaning: m. unripe, green, crude, immature (K.Pr. 119; Śiv. 1112; Rām. 1030; H. vi, 15); imperfect, bad, inferior, worthless, of small value (K.Pr. 64; Rām. 298, 383); inexpert, inexperienced; untaught and stupid (K.Pr. 11); not solid or substantial, not made of masonry; rough, approximate (as an estimate); lower, smaller (weight or measure, opp. to pŏkhta, the larger of two standard weights, etc.). -gĕv - m. uncooked ghī (clarified butter). --gaz -- m. the smaller yard measure in Kashmīr, being 15/16ths of the pŏkhta yard. It is used for measuring cloth, etc. --paĩsa -- or --pö̃sa -- m. the copper pice formerly current in Kashmīr, now being superseded by the British pice worth about a farthing (cf. hath). Its value varied from time to time (H. vii, 25-6). --rŏpay -- m. the old local Kāshmīrī rupee, now being superseded by the British rupee, and about half its value (L. 242). --sīrü -- f. an unbaked brick, a mud brick. --tab -- m. a kind of fever, low fever; the start of fever when the temperature is low and the pulse is going up, fever with a temperature over 102˚ is called poku tab. -tamā - adj. c.g. entertaining vain desires; hence, (in Kāshmīrī) very covetous, avaricious (K.Pr. 103). --tīl -- m. raw oil, unboiled oil. khāmi-khām - adj. c.g. absolutely raw, not in the least cooked (and so on, in all the uses of khām).

e: m. the sky, heaven (El.).

m. uncured skin, undried and fresh from the animal. --marun -- m.inf. to apply or fix damp skin, as in making the top of a drum; to fix damp skin on the face as a disguise or kind of mask, as was the custom in Kashmīr in former…
fullMeaning: m. uncured skin, undried and fresh from the animal. --marun -- m.inf. to apply or fix damp skin, as in making the top of a drum; to fix damp skin on the face as a disguise or kind of mask, as was the custom in Kashmīr in former times.

e: f. cough and stridor due to obstruction of the larynx, common in Kashmīr owing to specific disease and leprosy. It is rare in England. Cf. khamun.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khamadārĕñ ), become crooked, crookened (of a stick, or the like).
adj. c.g. suffering from cough, etc.; see khama.

f. a sharp-pointed stone or potsherd (Rām. 1250); a large piece of ice from the heavens. These pieces of ice are said to be so large as to kill people (El. khambirri; cf. kham 2). khambarĕ pĕñĕ f. pl. inf. a very violent storm of…
fullMeaning: f. a sharp-pointed stone or potsherd (Rām. 1250); a large piece of ice from the heavens. These pieces of ice are said to be so large as to kill people (El. khambirri; cf. kham 2). khambarĕ pĕñĕ f. pl. inf. a very violent storm of rain or ice, as ab. (compared to a shower of pointed flints), to fall.

e: f. the hollow left in a heap of grain, when a portion of grain is removed from it.
khamijü or khamyulu , in danda-khambyulu, etc., p. 224b, ll. 19 ff.
see khambyulu.
m. leaven, ferment (L. 82).
adj. c.g. silent (Rām. 689).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khomu . This verb is impersonal in tenses formed from the past participles. Thus khomun, it was coughed by him, he coughed), to be subject to attacks of coughing accompanied by stridor due to obstruction of the…

e: see khambyulu.

m. a hole, a pit; esp. a hollow in a pile of grain, caused by taking some of the grain out of it (cf. khambürü and atha-khan, p. 58b, l. 43); the hollow or depression between two mountain peaks; a breach or channel cut in the…
fullMeaning: m. a hole, a pit; esp. a hollow in a pile of grain, caused by taking some of the grain out of it (cf. khambürü and atha-khan, p. 58b, l. 43); the hollow or depression between two mountain peaks; a breach or channel cut in the bank of a flooded river for drawing off superfluous water; a breach cut by the water in the bank of a flooded river (cf. Gr.Gr. 123). --dyunu -- - m.inf. to make such an artificial cut in the bank of a flooded river. --ganḍun -- m.inf. to block up such a cut or breach in the bank of a river so as to stop the flow of water through it. --gaʦhȧni -- m. pl. inf. such breaches in the bank of a river to occur; met. pits to occur (in the belly), extreme hunger to occur (cf. bata-khan, p. 136b, l. 44). khana-bal - m.inf. the place where such a cut or breach occurs in the bank of the main river; N. of a place at the head waters of the river Vĕth (Jehlam) in Anatnāg Pargana, where three rivers meet and together form the Vĕth. See RT.Tr. II, 412, 414 n. It is the upper limit of navigation in Kashmīr, as khādan-yār (q.v.) is the lower limit (K.Pr. 103). -rôchu - - m. the watchman of such a cut or breach. He guards the embankment and directs the course of boats, etc.

e: m. lord, prince; a title of Musalmān nobles; common adjunct to Paṭhān names (H. ii, 1, 12). khāna-bāy - f. the wife of a Khān.
m. a table (not used by Hindūs) (El., K.Pr. 103, YZ. 29).
f. (sg. dat. khöñü ), a mine, a place whence minerals are dug (Gr.M.).

m. a house, dwelling (K.Pr. 4, 37; Rām. 131, 305; H. vi, 4); a receptacle, drawer, compartment; a pigeon-hole (in a desk); a socket; a square (of a chessboard) (Gr.M.); a window-pane (Gr.M.) Often --˚ as in dīwān-khāna, a hall of…
fullMeaning: m. a house, dwelling (K.Pr. 4, 37; Rām. 131, 305; H. vi, 4); a receptacle, drawer, compartment; a pigeon-hole (in a desk); a socket; a square (of a chessboard) (Gr.M.); a window-pane (Gr.M.) Often --˚ as in dīwān-khāna, a hall of audience (Śiv. 968), köd-khāna, a prison (Rām. 587, 684; H. v, 7, 8; vi, 10), kutub-kh., a library, mahala-kh., a palace, etc., qq.v. -dāmād - m. a son-in-law in the house; a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house (as Jacob did in Laban's), and who has to work as a drudge until the marriage, i.e. usually for a period of seven years (L. 267). --dāmödī -- f. the system under which such a son-in-law is taken into a house (L. 267). -möjü - f. a house-mother; hence, a darling and much loved girl member of a family (W. 17). -mājĕr - m. the condition of such a loved girl. -môlu - m. a house-father; hence, a darling and much loved boy member of a family (K.Pr. 104, W. 17); a young gentleman (El.).

e: m. (f. khānadārĕñ ), a family man, a householder (Śiv. 339, 1065, 1313); (from the point of view of the wife) a husband; (fem.) (from the point of view of the husband) a wife.
adj. c.g. possessing compartments or partitions, pigeonholed (e.g. a window or a desk).
f. the state of a master of a family; housekeeping (Śiv. 578, 587, 1049); living in the world, the life of a householder (as opp. to an ascetic life) (Rām. 1621).
m. a Musalmān convent, monastery, a religious establishment for holy men.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khananôwu ), to cause to dig; to cause to be dug, to get (a pit) dug, to have dug (H. x, 13).
m. a table (El.).

m. (sg. abl. khanḍa 1 ), coarse sugar (Śiv. 207, 283, 374, 1169, 1202, 1524). khanḍa-guru - m. a sugar horse, sugar moulded into the form of a horse (given to children. So also sugar in other forms, such as that of a man, a…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. abl. khanḍa 1 ), coarse sugar (Śiv. 207, 283, 374, 1169, 1202, 1524). khanḍa-guru - m. a sugar horse, sugar moulded into the form of a horse (given to children. So also sugar in other forms, such as that of a man, a parrot, an elephant, etc.); cf. -mahan- yuwu, bel. -grohuñu - m. 'sugar-fierce', i.e. one who deals honestly in all his affairs. -hākürü - f. sugar-priced, sold at the price of sugar; hence (of something very valuable) sold at a very small price (only of fem. articles). -mahanyuwu - m. a sugar man, sugar moulded into the form of a man, cf. -guru, ab.; met. a man of a thoroughly pleasing appearance and sweet disposition. -maṭh - m. (sg. dat. -maṭas -), a jar full of sugar; met. a charming, sweet-dispositioned man, sincere, virtuous, and well-to-do. -mŏṭh - f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi -), a handful of sugar; as much sugar as can be contained in the hand. -pholu - m. a small, indefinite amount of sugar. -phuṭüjü - f. a tied-up packet of sugar. -ʦṻn - m. sugar-powder, castor sugar; met. any powder resembling such sugar.

e: m. a part, a portion, piece (K. 430); a division of the earth, a region, country (Śiv. 1257), used --˚ to indicate indefiniteness, with slight diminution, as in kruh, a kōs; kruh khanḍ, about a kōs, but a little less. In such…
fullMeaning: m. a part, a portion, piece (K. 430); a division of the earth, a region, country (Śiv. 1257), used --˚ to indicate indefiniteness, with slight diminution, as in kruh, a kōs; kruh khanḍ, about a kōs, but a little less. In such compounds the noun generally takes the suff. of the indef. art., and khanḍ then becomes khanḍā , as in kruhāh khanḍā; similarly dŏhāh khanḍā, about a day, but something less; rŏpayāh khanḍā, about a rupee, but something less; akhāh khanḍā, nearly one (Gr.Gr. 93, W. 13, khand). --karun -- m.inf. to break into fragments, to break in pieces (K. 429).

e: m. to smile (YZ. 234).
see khanḍ 2.
in khanḍa-hŏgöḍü - f. a kind of dried fish (cf. hŏgöḍü).

in khanḍa-wāv - m. a shawl-weaver, a weaver of the cloth called pashmīna, both made of the fine wool of Central Asian goats (cf. L. 316, 317). Regarding the Kāshmīrī shawl-weavers, see L. as ab., and El. s.v. khándawáo (K.Pr.…
fullMeaning: in khanḍa-wāv - m. a shawl-weaver, a weaver of the cloth called pashmīna, both made of the fine wool of Central Asian goats (cf. L. 316, 317). fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. khörü 1 , Gr.Gr. 71), an ass's load (the ḵẖarwār of Persia and India); a dry measure containing sixteen trakh of 11 19/175 lb. each, and hence equal to 177 129/175 lb. avoirdupois (L. 243). According to El., however, a trakh is about 9 1/2 lb., and a khār is hence 152 lb. (K.Pr. 5, 28, 90, 106, 118, 138, 168; W. 103; Śiv. 591, 1795). By local custom, a khār of rice, maize, and barley consists of only 15 trakhs, or 166 22/35 lb. (L. l.c.). As a measure of land, a khār represents the area which is supposed to require a khār weight of rice-seed, or exactly 4 British acres (L. l.c.). -bôru - m. a load (of grain, or the like) weighing one khār. khār ḍŏḍ khār f. about one or one and a half khār (in weight). --maṭi khasüñü -- f.inf. a khār weight to mount on the shoulder; met. a heavy responsibility to be imposed upon one (e.g. to find oneself responsible for the support of a large family when one is without the necessary means). --zakhöra -- f. about one or two khār (in weight). khörü-hondü - adj. (f. -hünzü -), of a khār; hence (of a basket, or the like) large enough to contain a khār (of grain, etc.). khörüv-pöṭhü ?- or -pöṭhin - adv. in khārs, i.e. in a large number of khārs, in an indefinite number of khārs.

fullMeaning: m. an advance of grain; when grain has been threshed, and has been collected previous to the Government assessment for purposes of taxation, it is supposed not to be touched till Government permission is given. This word signifies a portion of grain taken out of the heap by permission of the official in charge, for the cultivator's immediate needs. fullMeaning: m. N. of a round-leafed swamp-plant (considered by natives to be a kind of lotus, cf. bŏd-khoru, p. 83b, l. 9 and waṭa-kho, p. 1157a, l. 4). Limnanthemum nymphoides (L. 71 khur, Śiv. 1837). It is much valued as a food for cattle which increases the yield of milk. Cf. buḍa-khoru, bŏṭa-khoru, guri-khori, s.vv. buḍa, bŏṭa, and guru. Probably the kúrú of El. which he translates Villarsia nymphoides. m. one who can only grow a small thin chinbeard and cannot grow whiskers, etc. (K.Pr. 110). Such men have the reputation of affability (K.Pr. 100). -dörü - f. the thin little beard of such a man. -khĕn or -khyonu - m. a Khōsa's…
fullMeaning: m. one who can only grow a small thin chinbeard and cannot grow whiskers, etc. (K.Pr. 110). Such men have the reputation of affability (K.Pr. 100). -dörü - f. the thin little beard of such a man. -khĕn or -khyonu - m. a Khōsa's dinner; a dinner party at which there are many trays of food served, all of which the guests succeed in eating, so that nothing is left. The manner of accomplishing this feat is said to have been devised by a smart Khōsa; see K.Pr. 110 for the stories connected with it. -mahanyuwu - m. a man with such a beard.

fullMeaning: or khŏshāl 1 adj. c.g. happy, glad (K.Pr. 106, 181; Śiv. 1318); fortunate. khŏshāl khānas zuv aʦun m.inf. to disturb others in sorrow by a merry noise (e.g. ignorant children shouting in merriment in a house of mourning or where there is illness. In this it is said that khānas is a corruption of kanas, and this phrase is said to mean lit. 'as when a louse goes into a happy ear').

fullMeaning: adj. (f. khö̆shü ), left-handed; able to use the left hand as well as the right, ambidextrous. (f. khōvürü ), right and left reversed (e.g. when one puts the right shoe on the left foot and vice versa, or when one performs right hand actions on the left and vice versa) (K.Pr. 250). -pav - m. one who habitually does everything left-handedly (not only with his hand, but with all his members), one who is sinistral. -war - m. winding to the left, winding counter-clockwise (e.g. a string); cf. the English 'left-handed' screw. -wȧri - adv. counter-clockwise.

e: khōta , or (Gr.Gr. 49) khŏtan postpos. indicating comparison, than. It governs either the abl. or the abl. of the gen. Thus kañi (or kañĕ-handi) khŏta trakuru, harder than a stone. For further particulars, see Gr.Gr. 49, Gr.M.,…
fullMeaning: khōta , or (Gr.Gr. 49) khŏtan postpos. indicating comparison, than. It governs either the abl. or the abl. of the gen. Thus kañi (or kañĕ-handi) khŏta trakuru, harder than a stone. For further particulars, see Gr.Gr. 49, Gr.M., and W. 98; YZ. 27, 186, 200; Śiv. khŏta 166, 434, 497, 784, 1062, 1087, 1290, 1657; khōta 1867-8; Rām. khŏta, 265, 730, 976, 1239, 1272, 1404, 1493; H. khŏta, iii, 8; xii, 10, 19; K. khŏta, 906, 1102). The word is sometimes used to indicate merely the ablative case, as in dŏha-khŏta dŏha, from day to day (Śiv. 410).

e: adj. c.g. irregular in shape, unsymmetrical (esp. of a child's face, or the like).

adj. c.g. of or belonging to the district of Khōtan in Central Asia. --trēl -- f. a kind of apple of moderate size, red in colour, and of superior quality (El. khotunyi trēla, L. 349 khatoni trel). The trēl is a small species of…
fullMeaning: adj. c.g. of or belonging to the district of Khōtan in Central Asia. --trēl -- f. a kind of apple of moderate size, red in colour, and of superior quality (El. khotunyi trēla, L. 349 khatoni trel). The trēl is a small species of apple of good flavour. This is larger, but with equal flavour.

e: postpos. for the sake of, on account of, out of consideration or regard for, on behalf of. It governs either the abl. or the abl. of the gen. Thus kāmi (or kāmĕ-handi) kho, for the sake of the business. The use of the genitive…
fullMeaning: postpos. for the sake of, on account of, out of consideration or regard for, on behalf of. It governs either the abl. or the abl. of the gen. Thus kāmi (or kāmĕ-handi) kho, for the sake of the business. The use of the genitive is, however, principally confined to animate nouns (Gr.M.; W. 98, 99).

fullMeaning: conj. 2 (1p.p. khūʦu , 2 p.p. khōʦōv ), to be afraid, to fear (K.Pr. 59; Rām. 492, 553, 633, 636, 704, 758, 932, 1226, 1749; K. 139, 158, 245, 247). The object may be in the dat. Cf. kyulu. kiji-khrāv - f. a wooden patten with a peg at the fore-end, which is grasped between the toes, and by which the patten is held to the foot. -kū̃shi - f. a kind of high-heeled shoe worn in winter, see kū̃shi.

e: or kaikī or kökī (by Paṇḍits often written kaikayī or kaikēyī , in Sanskrit fashion), f. in Hindū legend, N. of one of the wives of King Daśaratha, Rāmacandra's stepmother, and mother of Bharata. In Sanskrit her N. was 'Kaikēyī'.…
fullMeaning: or kaikī or kökī (by Paṇḍits often written kaikayī or kaikēyī , in Sanskrit fashion), f. in Hindū legend, N. of one of the wives of King Daśaratha, Rāmacandra's stepmother, and mother of Bharata. In Sanskrit her N. was 'Kaikēyī'. By her intrigues she procured Rāmacandra's banishment, in order to secure the throne for her own son. She is hence considered a type of all slanderous intriguers. (Rām. 5, 40, 153, 206, 256, 277, 297, etc., always spelt kīkī; obl. form kīkīyĕ, Rām. 82, 148-9, 155, 182, 261, 266, 282, and (m.c.) kīkiyī, Rām. 83).

e: f. (sg. dat. kili ), a nudge, a thrust with the elbow, knee, or the like, to call attention (cf. khŏni-ko, p. 402b, l. 1) (Gr.Gr. 13); a slap with the edge of the open hand (El.); esp. a slap given in the act of sexual…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. kili ), a nudge, a thrust with the elbow, knee, or the like, to call attention (cf. khŏni-ko, p. 402b, l. 1) (Gr.Gr. 13); a slap with the edge of the open hand (El.); esp. a slap given in the act of sexual intercourse. kila diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give nudges, to thrust and push (e.g. in making way through a crowd) (K.Pr. 56). kili-hondu - m. born of a blow given in sexual intercourse; hence, as a term of abuse, born of casual or secret intercourse, unlawfully begotten. --kili khyonu -- m.inf. to hurt a person with repeated slaps or cudgellings; to poke over and over again (e.g. to poke a corpse on the funeral pyre to make it burn quickly) (K.Pr. 101).

e: (El.), kulmanch (L. 74), kulmānch (L. 79) (spelling and gender), the Guelder, Viburnum fœtens, a honey flower (L. 74). The word is apparently connected with mã̄ch, honey. Cf. kulāra and kwīllim.

postpos. indicating motion from; from the direction of, from near (H. v, 7). Cf. kini.

(Śiv. 1894-5), a by-form of kini, q.v.

m. hatred, rancour, malevolence, malice, spite, grudge, resentment, animosity (El. kín and kínah, Rām. 802).
see kinjü.

m. (in astrology), the centre of a circle; the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth places in a horoscope (Rām. 144, 1262). kindȧrȧ bĕhun m.inf. (of a planet) to be in the centre of its orbit, (?) to be in prime (Śiv. 730, 924).
or kī̃jü f. the cat in the game of tipcat (lȧṭhi kinja loṭhu, L. 464, lat kinch lut, see loṭhu). The word is a by-form of kiji, q.v. kinja is a variant spelling of kinjĕ or kinji.
see kirāy.
m. horripilation, the standing on end of the hair and down of the body (from excitement, surprise, terror, etc.), thrilling, a thrill.

f. hire, rent (of a house, a boat, or the like) (El. kiráí; Gr.M.; khar kirāy, hire due for the services of an ass, K.Pr. 104); fare, hire, freight (ḍākücü kirāy, the postage of a letter, Gr.M.). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to borrow (sic.…
fullMeaning: f. hire, rent (of a house, a boat, or the like) (El. kiráí; Gr.M.; khar kirāy, hire due for the services of an ass, K.Pr. 104); fare, hire, freight (ḍākücü kirāy, the postage of a letter, Gr.M.). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to borrow (sic. El.). kirāyĕ-cīri - - f. the document fixing the rent of a house, a lease (Gr.M.). --hyonu -- m.inf. to take on lease or on hire (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to take on hire, in phrases such as nāv chĕh kirāyĕ karüñü, a boat must be taken on hire (Gr.M.).

adj. c.g. crimson-coloured, crimson, scarlet (L. 459, krimsi. In 251, L. calls the colour dark maroon).
(spelling) f. (?) Ficus carica (El. Ficus caricordes).

adj. c.g. of or belonging to Kirpārām, the boat-loving Sikh Governor of Kashmīr (1825-31). --capa -- m. fancy strokes in rowing, so named by boatmen in honour of Kirpārām (L. 382, kirparámi chappr), and said to have been invented…
fullMeaning: adj. c.g. of or belonging to Kirpārām, the boat-loving Sikh Governor of Kashmīr (1825-31). --capa -- m. fancy strokes in rowing, so named by boatmen in honour of Kirpārām (L. 382, kirparámi chappr), and said to have been invented by him. The following are some of these fancy strokes, the rowers all keeping time together:-- the handles of the paddles (capa) are caused to strike the gunwale at every third stroke; the paddles are thrown out as far as possible and noisily smacked flat on the water at the third stroke; or at each third stroke the blade is struck by the hand, or a salaam is made; or the third stroke is made soft and swishing, distinct from the two vigorous strokes that preceded it (see Pioneer Mail for September 30, 1910).

e: f. mention, report, description (Śiv. 47); celebrating, praising (Śiv. 107).
(spelling, gender, and number), water insects found in flooded fields (L. 80). The word looks like a plural of some word like kirzü. Cf. krṻl 1.
or kisü f. the little, or fifth, finger of the hand (cf. atha-kisü, p. 59b, l. 3) (Gr.Gr. 13; K.Pr. 17; Siv. 701, 994, 1392; K. 326-7); the little toe (El.).

m. (pl. ag. kēshau , Rām. 402; kīshĕv , K. 33), hair (on the head or on the body); esp. a long tress of hair, hair in long tresses (Śiv. 1704, 1725; Rām. 183, 402; K. 33); a ringlet (El.); cf. kih. kīshĕ-hüṭü - f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ…

(pl. ag. kēshau , Rām. 402; kīshĕv , K. 33), hair (on the head or on the body); esp. a long tress of hair, hair in long tresses (Śiv. 1704, 1725; Rām. 183, 402; K. 33); a ringlet (El.); cf. kih. kīshĕ-hüṭü - f. or ku , a prefix implying deterioration, depreciation, deficiency, want, littleness, hindrance, reproach, contempt, guilt, or the like. It is a Sanskrit prefix, but in Kāshmīrī it appears not only prefixed to borrowed Sanskrit…
fullMeaning: or ku , a prefix implying deterioration, depreciation, deficiency, want, littleness, hindrance, reproach, contempt, guilt, or the like. It is a Sanskrit prefix, but in Kāshmīrī it appears not only prefixed to borrowed Sanskrit words, but also to pure Kāshmīrī ones. Words to which this prefix is added will be found below in their proper alphabetical order.

e: f. a bad bone; met. the bone of some wretched fellow fit only to be beaten, or of some low fellow fit only to carry burdens, or the like, as in amis chuh kŏ-aḍijü, he has a bad bone, i.e. he is not worth anything but a beating or…
fullMeaning: f. a bad bone; met. the bone of some wretched fellow fit only to be beaten, or of some low fellow fit only to carry burdens, or the like, as in amis chuh kŏ-aḍijü, he has a bad bone, i.e. he is not worth anything but a beating or to put to bearing burdens.

e: m. (sg. dat. -bāzanas -), a worthless vessel or utensil; met. a totally unworthy person.
adv. in an evil work, in bad conduct, u.w. vbs. signifying expenditure, or the like.
m. ugly-faced, ugly-mouthed; foul-mouthed, scurrilous.

f. (sg. dat. kŏ-küjü -), evil longing, vicious desire. kŏ-küjü - adv. with an evil longing, with desires fixed on or exercised in evil objects or occupations.

adj. c.g. an evil doer, a sinner (Rām. 52).
f. (sg. dat. -kathi ), an ill word, a word that should not be spoken, an abusive or indecent expression.
m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas -), a bad son, one, who by bad conduct, is a disgrace to his parents and family (Gr.Gr. 132).

f. used in the gen. kŏ-kili-hondu -- adj. (f. -hünzü -), born of unlawful (incestuous) sexual intercourse; used in abuse. Cf. kil.

adj. (f. -körü ), (of an animate object) ill-shaped, ugly.

adv. with an evil mind, with evil intention; with an angry mind.
adv. with an evil face; with a face distorted (by anger, or the like).
m. (sg. dat. -nĕcivis -), a bad child (W. 110).
m. an evil or foul vulva. kŏpōnuku adj. (f. kŏpōnicü ), born from a foul vulva, one who is utterly vile in character.

adv. at a bad time; in a time of calamities, etc.; at an inauspicious time; at a wrong time, untimely, unseasonably. A contracted form of this word is kŏzi.

see kŏ-wôku.
adj. (f. kŏ-wöcü -), one who utters ill words, abusive, foul-mouthed.
m. a bad man, a wicked person, a sinner (K.Pr. 202).

adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. -zātas -), of bad, or low, caste, low- born; used also, as a term of reproach, with reference to a well-born person who acts vilely, of a bad disposition, bad-natured (W. 110).
m. a long-prepared opportunity for bringing another under subjection, the successful climax of such a preparation.
(spelling) f. a sheath, scabbard (El. kómb), i.q. kȧmbi, q.v.

adj. capable, able, clever, skilful, competent; a fit or competent person, an able man, etc. (Rām. 1302).
m. N. of ạ certain medicinal plant, used as a cure for herpes.
m. a hump on the back, hump-backedness (K. 428).

adj. (f. kö̆bü ), hump-backed (K. 427); a hunchback, esp. one born so (K.Pr. 116); crooked (El. kŏb); cf. kŏburu. --kulu -- m. a hunchback tree, a tree with a crooked trunk. Such tree is easily climbed and is the rendezvous for…
fullMeaning: adj. (f. kö̆bü ), hump-backed (K. 427); a hunchback, esp. one born so (K.Pr. 116); crooked (El. kŏb); cf. kŏburu. --kulu -- m. a hunchback tree, a tree with a crooked trunk. Such tree is easily climbed and is the rendezvous for this purpose of all the children of the neighbourhood; hence, met. an under-servant, who is the fag and drudge of all the upper servants, and who never has a moment's peace (see K.Pr. 116 for the origin of the metaphor).

e: adj. c.g. of or belonging to Kābul, the capital of Afghānistān. --phrasth -- m. a kind of poplar (L. 81).

m. (sg. dat. kôbulas ), the city of Kābul, the capital of Afghānistān; the country of Afghānistān, which in K. is treated as equivalent to the Kāmbōja of Sanskrit literature (K. 578, 582, 586, 619 ff.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. kŏbyōv ), to become hunchbacked (from disease, accident, old age, or the like).
adj. (f. kŏbürü ), one who has become hunchbacked (by disease, or the like, and who was not born so). Cf. kọ̆bu 2.

or (H. iv, 7) kabar f. a grave, a tomb, esp. a Musalmān's tomb (as in K.Pr. 22) (K.Pr. 138 kabrí). -wö̆bürü - f., id. (El. kabar-wabar). kö̆barĕ wālun m.inf. to cause to descend into a tomb, to inter (H. iv, 7, kabari).

N. of a certain astronomical period in the month of Öshid (Skr. Āśvina = Septr.-Oct.) during which the sun is in Virgo (it corresponds to the Sanskrit Kāmāri-pakṣa, for which, see bel.); hence, the spring crops (wheat, barley,…
fullMeaning: N. of a certain astronomical period in the month of Öshid (Skr. Āśvina = Septr.-Oct.) during which the sun is in Virgo (it corresponds to the Sanskrit Kāmāri-pakṣa, for which, see bel.); hence, the spring crops (wheat, barley, etc.) usually sown in this period. kö̃bari-kāh - m. the timely rain (kāh 2) that falls during this period, and after which the spring crops are sown (L. 328, kámbar ká). -pach - m. N. of this period, in Sanskrit Kāmāri-pakṣa. It is the dark half of the luni-solar month of Öshid (see ab.). During it, not only are the spring crops sown, but also offerings are made by Hindūs to their deceased ancestors (L. 266, Kambar pach). -shrād - m. the oblation (Sanskrit śrāddha) offered by Hindūs to deceased ancestors during this period.

C) m. a lane, an alley, a narrow road between houses (YZ. 40, 253; Śiv. 1466, 1625, 1849; Rām. 44), a shopless street (El. kóchih); an alley leading to a house (L. 462). -phyuru - m. alley-wandering; hence, losing one's way in the lanes of a town; met. losing one's way in some complicated business, losing the thread of an argument, or the like.

fullMeaning: f. a kiln; a potter's kiln (Rām. 1446; H. xi, 11); a brick-kiln (Śiv. 1033); a lime-kiln. -bal - m. the place where a kiln is erected, a brick or potter's kiln (Gr.Gr. 165). --khasüñü -- f.inf. a kiln to arise; met. to become like such a kiln (which contains no imperfectly baked articles, but only well-made perfectly baked ones), hence, a collection of good ('pucka') articles or qualities to exist. m. saffron, Crocus sativus (the plant and the dried flowers (El.; L. 330, 342; K.Pr. 55; Rām. 1092, 1626). It is in great request as a condiment and as a pigment for the tilaka or forehead-marks of the Hindūs. See El. and L. for…
fullMeaning: m. saffron, Crocus sativus (the plant and the dried flowers (El.; L. 330, 342; K.Pr. 55; Rām. 1092, 1626). See El. and L. for particulars regarding the cultivation (El. also kangan, kongs, and kwong). -bakusu - or -bŏkusu - m. the outer dark-coloured calix-leaves of a saffron flower. -mö̆nḍü - f. (sg. dat. mŏnjĕ ), the bulb or root of a saffron plant. -pōsh - m. the saffron flower (El., Śiv. 1180, Rām. 1043). -püṭü - f. the yellow-coloured portion of the stigma of the saffron-flower. -tihijü - f. the orange-red tip of the stigma of the saffron flower. 'to pour forth the saffron-bowl' (an allusion to the old custom of Hindū times, according to which a girl chose her husband at a svayaṁvara, or assembly of candidates for her hand. e: m. N. of a kind of paddy, with a soft and fragrant grain. Cf. kañi-hāl, p. 461a, l. 37, and El. kúnyí dányí; ? L. 332, 463, kanyun.

fullMeaning: (cf. köñī and kāñĕñ) in köñü-pŏhur - m. the top floor or attic of a house of several stories, in which the tenants live during the summer season (L. 461 kuinphor). -pĕṭh - adv. on the top floor, in the attic, as ab. köñi-pōr - m. i.q. köñü- pŏhur, ab. köñiyĕ-pōr - m. i.q. köñi- pōr, but with more emphasis on the fact that it is the topmost floor that is referred to, the very topmost floor, the very attic.

m. a sacrifice, victim, offering, oblation. Yīd kŏrbān, one of the four chief Musalmān holidays of Kashmīr (L. 268), the 'īdu'l-qurbān or 'īdu'ẓ-ẓŏḥā, held on the tenth day of the month Ẕu'l-ḥijja, in commemoration of Abraham's…

Cf. nigayĕ-ko, s.v. nigay. kāri-holu - adj. (f. -hüjü -), crooked necked, wry-necked (by nature or from rheumatism, etc.). -pȧti 1 m. N. of a certain wild flower, described as dark in colour, with small tooth-shaped shoots at the back (pȧti) (Rām. 649, 655). -pȧti 2 - adv. on the back or nape of the neck (Rām. 1615). -thodu - adj. (f. -thüzü -), 'high in the neck,' one who carries his head high in public, one who occupies an honourable position and knows it (cf. Śiv. 971, 1363).

e: m. the slipperiness on the bank of a river in frosty weather.
adj. (f. körü 2 ; for 1, see s.v.), one-eyed (= kônu 4, q.v.) (L.V. 20); crooked limbed, deformed (of a person). köri-shiñi - f. the misfortunes, inconveniences, etc., arising from poverty.

m. the deficiency or distorted shape in a superficies with corners (e.g. a piece of cloth or an area of land) owing to the angles being too large or too small, want of symmetry or deficiency due to want of symmetry of this kind.
see kyāh.
see kū̃su.
or , or kusalyā f. Kausalyā, N. of a wife of king Daśaratha. She was mother of Rāma-candra (Śiv. 1140, 1483; Rām. 83, 191, 1227, kausalyā; 40, 82, 209-10, 225, etc., kusalyā).
m. a violet (El.); safflower (Skt. kusumbha) (YZ. 254, 257; Rām. 645, 1008, 1094). A woman's hands or feet are compared to it for delicacy and beauty (Rām. 189, 355, 1082, 1251).
m. bad company, evil companionship, consorting with evil-doers (Śiv. 1808).

or kaũsar m. N. of a mountain lake in the Pīr Pantsāl Range, in Skt. Kramasaras and the Kōnsar of RT.Tr. It is supposed to mark a footstep (krama) of Viṣṇu, and is an object of the Naubandhana pilgrimage (RT.Tr. II, 393; Śiv.…
fullMeaning: or kaũsar m. N. of a mountain lake in the Pīr Pantsāl Range, in Skt. Kramasaras and the Kōnsar of RT.Tr. It is supposed to mark a footstep (krama) of Viṣṇu, and is an object of the Naubandhana pilgrimage (RT.Tr. II, 393; Śiv. 1170; L.V. 50).

e: m. a treasury; a treasury of words, a dictionary (a Hindū word) (Gr.M.).

fullMeaning: or kushĕl m. health, well-being, welfare; esp. health recovered after illness (a Hindū word). -hum - m. (among Hindūs) a special small oblation offered for the benefit of his family by each participant, after the conclusion of an important general sacrificial ceremony. kŏshĕla-pạthar - m. a letter giving news of welfare; hence, politely, a letter (Gr.M.).

e: f. (sg. dat. köshiyĕ ), the city of Kāśī or Benares. Its tutelary deity is Śiva (Śiv. 672-3, 694, 865, 1257; K. 691, 873, 884, etc.). -nāth -, m. the Lord of Kāśī, a title of Śiva (Śiv. 1409).

in oku-köshulad (p. 19a, l. 20), a word derived from kāh 3 (sg. dat. köshü), the eleventh day of a lunar fortnight, on which Hindūs fast. Hence, oku-köshulad means one who suffers, or who would suffer, from a single one of these…
fullMeaning: in oku-köshulad (p. 19a, l. 20), a word derived from kāh 3 (sg. dat. köshü), the eleventh day of a lunar fortnight, on which Hindūs fast. Hence, oku-köshulad means one who suffers, or who would suffer, from a single one of these fasts, lit. suffering from a single eleventh lunar day.

e: see kôshuru.
f. exertion, endeavour, diligence (Gr.M.).

adj. (f. köshü 1 ), of or belonging to the eleventh lunar day (on which Hindūs fast) (cf. kāh 3); hence, subst. m. a severe fast, such as that which is held on that day. --karun -- m.inf. to fast (Rām. 188).

m. pounded chaff of wheat, barley, maize, or the like, which remains after husking the grain in a mortar (El. kosh and kúsh; cf. kisr, s.v. kĕsürü); a honeycomb (H. ix, 5). In composition this word has a wider signification. Thus…
fullMeaning: m. pounded chaff of wheat, barley, maize, or the like, which remains after husking the grain in a mortar (El. kosh and kúsh; cf. kisr, s.v. kĕsürü); a honeycomb (H. ix, 5). In composition this word has a wider signification. Thus ara-koshu (p. 41a, l. 17) is 'sawdust', and cāhi- koshu (p. 158a, l. 11) is 'used tea leaves'. El., s.v. kúsh, also gives the meaning 'beeswax'; cf. kashürü. kȧshi-dāl - , f. millets, etc., or dāl, in the husk, cooked as a porridge, porridge of unhusked millet. -pholu - m. a single flake, or a very small amount, of chaff, as ab. -ʦŏ̈ṭü - f. a cake made only of chaff, as ab. It is used as a medicine.

e: in kaṭh-koshu, etc., s.v. kaṭh 4, q.v.
sg. dat. of kāh 3.

or kôshyuru adj. (f. köshirü ), of or belonging to Kashmīr, Kāshmīrī; a man of Kashmīr (El.; H. xi, 6); the Kāshmīrī language (El., YZ. 239); (f.) a woman of Kashmīr (El.); the Kāshmīrī language (Gr.M.). -pahān - adj. (f.…

(f. köshirü ), of or belonging to Kashmīr, Kāshmīrī; a man of Kashmīr (El.; H. xi, 6); the Kāshmīrī language (El., YZ. 239); (f.) a woman of Kashmīr (El.); the Kāshmīrī language (Gr.M.). -pahān - adj. (f. köshirü- pahān -), somewhat Kāshmīrī, more or less Kāshmīrī, closely resembling something produced in Kashmīr. köshirü al f. a kind of pumpkin, long in shape and green in colour (cf. El., s.v. al). --mujü -- f. a species of radish (El. köshírí múj). --nāsth -- f. a kind of yellow snuff made of Kāshmīrī tobacco. --zĕv -- f. the Kāshmīrī language (El.).

i.q. kŏstūru, q.v.

kŏstūr , or kastūru m. (pl. dat. kastūrĕn , Gr.Gr. 56), a certain bird, the Grey-winged Blackbird, Merula boulboul (L. 152, kastura). According to El. it corresponds to the shah bulbul and to the hazār dastān or nightingale. It…
fullMeaning: kŏstūr , or kastūru m. (pl. dat. kastūrĕn , Gr.Gr. 56), a certain bird, the Grey-winged Blackbird, Merula boulboul (L. 152, kastura). According to El. it corresponds to the shah bulbul and to the hazār dastān or nightingale. It has a melodious voice, and is valued as a cage-bird (El. kastūr and kostūr; K.Pr. 147, kastur; L. gives kastura both for this bird and for the musk-deer. See kŏstūra; Śiv. 327).

e: see kāsun 1 and 2.
(spelling) f. labour (El.; possibly by this is meant köṭhü 4, or some connected word not elsewhere recorded).
see kotu 2.

see kūtu, p. 485a, l. 34.
f. the leading of a horse in a procession. Such horses, decorated with ornamented trappings, are led at the head of a royal procession, or before a bridegroom, etc.
or kōtāmath , adv. up to where? till when? (W. 93).
or kūṭapāl m. the chief official of a town or fortress, the chief of the police, the captain of a fort (K. 404, 792-3, 819). Cf. kuṭawāl.

f. (sg. dat.kö̆ṭhü , Gr.Gr. 71), N. of a certain medicinal plant Aucklandia Costus. The root, which is fragrant, is a government monopoly. For full accounts of this plant, see El. s.v. kŏṭ and L. 77. L. gives the botanical name…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat.kö̆ṭhü , Gr.Gr. 71), N. of a certain medicinal plant Aucklandia Costus. The root, which is fragrant, is a government monopoly. For full accounts of this plant, see El. s.v. kŏṭ and L. 77. L. gives the botanical name as Saussurea Lappa. Cf. cōb-ĕ-kŏṭh, p. 156b, l. 34; L. 83, 389, 418.

m. (sg. dat. kōṭas ), a coat or cloak (of the English fashion; the English word borrowed) (Gr.M.).
in kō̃th-möjü - f. the eldest woman of a family in a household, the head lady of a family.
f. (sg. dat. kö̆ʦhü ), a hank of thread (esp. of the loose single strands of thread, preparatory to twisting into thread in strands); a ball of sewing-thread (Gr.Gr. 69).

m. a gold necklet; a necklace or rosary (of beads of gold, or silver, or pearls, or jewels, or crystal, or of the earth of Karbalā). -gan - a particular fragrant gum-resin (the exudation of the tree Amyris agallochum), bdellium…
fullMeaning: m. a gold necklet; a necklace or rosary (of beads of gold, or silver, or pearls, or jewels, or crystal, or of the earth of Karbalā). -gan - a particular fragrant gum-resin (the exudation of the tree Amyris agallochum), bdellium (Śiv. 377).

e: m. a granary, a store-room; the wall, circumvallation, or enceinte round a town or fortress (K. 757-8); cf. kūṭh 1 and kuṭhü. -dār - m. (f. -dārĕñ -), a man in charge of a store-room, a store-keeper, a house-steward (YZ. 420).

m. a kind of stocks in which prisoners are confined by the legs; an impalement stake, the stake on which a criminal is impaled, a gallows (El.; K.Pr. 5, 215; Śiv. 1630). köṭhis ladun m.inf. to hang (a criminal) (El.). -pĕṭh āsun…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of stocks in which prisoners are confined by the legs; an impalement stake, the stake on which a criminal is impaled, a gallows (El.; K.Pr. 5, 215; Śiv. 1630). köṭhis ladun m.inf. to hang (a criminal) (El.). -pĕṭh āsun - m.inf. to be hanged (El.).

m. a load, a burden, bundle (especially one awkwardly shaped, and hence requiring to be tied up and difficult to carry) (Gr.Gr. 33, 37; K.Pr. 3); the caulking of a boat or ship (cf. nāwa-ko, s.v. nāv 2); cf. kŏth 2 and kö̆ʦhü 1.…
fullMeaning: m. a load, a burden, bundle (especially one awkwardly shaped, and hence requiring to be tied up and difficult to carry) (Gr.Gr. 33, 37; K.Pr. 3); the caulking of a boat or ship (cf. nāwa-ko, s.v. nāv 2); cf. kŏth 2 and kö̆ʦhü 1. --dyunu -- m.inf. to caulk the seams or holes in a boat or ship. Cf. kŏna. kŏthi-kuchay - m. a servant of a judge or other person in authority who acts as a go-between in taking bribes from litigants on behalf of his master. Cf. kuchay and kọ̆ʦhu.

e: m. the knee (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 200-1, 237; Rām. 285, 1129, 1146; K. 1125). --mūrun -- m.inf. when one is seated on the ground, to move the knees so as to make room politely for another. --nạmarāwun -- m.inf. to bend the knee, to fall…
fullMeaning: m. the knee (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 200-1, 237; Rām. 285, 1129, 1146; K. 1125). --mūrun -- m.inf. when one is seated on the ground, to move the knees so as to make room politely for another. --nạmarāwun -- m.inf. to bend the knee, to fall on one's knee (Gr.M.). --trāwun -- m.inf. to kneel (El.). --yunu -- m. the knee to come, i.e. the ability to crawl on the knees to come (of a child beginning to learn to crawl on its hands and knees) (K.Pr. 260). kŏṭhi-ã̄cĕ - f.pl., see the next. -ö̃ṭü - f. the knee-cap (pl. -ã̄cĕ -). -ganḍ - m. tying the knees (of a person, to prevent his going). -köʦü - f. the poples, ham (El. kúṭkáts); cf. köʦü 3. -në̆ṭhü - f. the patella, knee-cap, knee-pan (El. kútanyíṭ). -ʦŏcĕ - f.pl. cakes made and distributed in honour of the occasion of a child first beginning to crawl on its hands and knees. -wace - f.pl. the knee-joint.

f. (sg. dat. kāchĕ ), the fifth, or little, finger or toe.

adj. f. (sg. dat. kāchĕ ), hard, dry, sapless (used as the f. of kāṭh 3, q.v.); most commonly used with ref. to radishes and similar roots; hence, as subst. f. the hard rind of a vegetable root (cf. mŏnjĕ-ko, s.v. mö̆nḍü 1).
adj. f. (sg. dat. kāchĕ ), habitually lazy, indolent in doing any work. A feminine form, used as a fem. of köṭhi 2, q.v. Cf. kóṭ.
f. a small bag, tied up as a parcel, and carried, like a parcel, on the head or under the arm; dim. of kŏthul, q.v.
or kŏthulu m. (sg. dat. kŏthalas ), a large bundle or parcel (esp. one of awkward shape, and hence requiring much tying up). Cf. kọ̆thu and kŏʦhul.
m. a man who caulks (a boat or ship) (cf. nāwa-ko, s.v. nāv 2).
adj. c.g. causing death, deadly. zahar-i-kötil, deadly poison (Rām. 827).
see katijü.

adj. (f. küʦü ), wet, moist, damp; full of juice, juicy; sappy (L.V. 51). Often used met., as in āra-koto (p. 41a, l. 5) damp with compassion, compassionate, or (YZ. 39; Śiv. 113, 948, 1473, 1527; Rām. 1595) deserving of…
fullMeaning: adj. (f. küʦü ), wet, moist, damp; full of juice, juicy; sappy (L.V. 51). Often used met., as in āra-koto (p. 41a, l. 5) damp with compassion, compassionate, or (YZ. 39; Śiv. 113, 948, 1473, 1527; Rām. 1595) deserving of compassion (p.p. of kaʦun, q.v.).

f., i.q. kŏth 2, q.v.

or koʦhu m. a bribe (El. kauʦ; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 99, khuʦh); cf. kŏthi-kuchay, p. 489a, l. 4. --dyunu -- m.inf. to give a bribe, to bribe (Gr.M.). --khyonu -- m.inf. to take bribes (El.). kŏʦhi-khŏr - or kŏʦhi-khāv - m. a bribe-eater,…
fullMeaning: or koʦhu m. a bribe (El. kauʦ; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 99, khuʦh); cf. kŏthi-kuchay, p. 489a, l. 4. --dyunu -- m.inf. to give a bribe, to bribe (Gr.M.). --khyonu -- m.inf. to take bribes (El.). kŏʦhi-khŏr - or kŏʦhi-khāv - m. a bribe-eater, a bribe-taker.

e: or küʦhü f. a bag, sack, pouch, or wallet, made of cloth (Gr.Gr. 63). Cf. kọ̆thu, of which this word is a fem. dim. (Gr.Gr. 33, 37); cf. also kŏth 2.
see kŏth 1 and 2.
see kŏʦhul.
or kŏʦhulu m. (sg. dat. kŏʦhalas , Gr.Gr.58; f. kŏʦhüjü ?), a porter, esp. one who carries grain (in a kŏth, or leathern sack) (El. kŏtsúl). Cf. kŏth 2.
adj. (f. köʦü 1 , for 2, 3, see s.vv.), a miser, one who will not spend money, even though rich. Cf. katun 2.
f. (for 1, see kôʦu), a kind of scissors or pincers for cutting betel-nut, the sarōtā of India; a pair of scissors (for cutting cloth, etc.) (L.V. 103).
f. (for 1, see kôʦu), the under part of the leg between the thigh and the knee, the ham.
see kūtu, p. 484b, l. 46.
or kāʦan 2 f. in yẹ̆ndra-ko, p. 1199a, l. 24, q.v.

(f. küṭü , q.v.), a seedling-sprout, the first sprout of a young plant (cf. gāsa- koṭu, p. 307b, l. 34; muji-ko, s.v. mujü); a bush, a thicket of bushes (K. 111, 219, 350); a male child (generally used with reference to caste or…
fullMeaning: (f. küṭü , q.v.), a seedling-sprout, the first sprout of a young plant (cf. gāsa- koṭu, p. 307b, l. 34; muji-ko, s.v. mujü); a bush, a thicket of bushes (K. 111, 219, 350); a male child (generally used with reference to caste or profession), usually, but not always, with the idea of praise. It is also occasionally used to indicate the young of animals. Thus, baṭa-koṭu, a (real) son of a Brāhmaṇ, a good Brāhmaṇ; chāna-koṭu, a carpenter's son, a real son of a carpenter, a good carpenter; harạna-koṭu, a fawn (p. 349a, l. 24); mö̃shĕ-koṭu, a buffalo-calf; cf. Gr.Gr. 132 (K.Pr. 174; H. xii, 25). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become insufficient, to be found to be too short, not long enough (K. 166). kȧṭi gūli m.pl. the kernels of water-chestnuts which have just sprouted in the spring-time, see the next; cf. gūlu 2. --göri -- m.pl. young water-chestnuts which have just sprouted in the spring-time; cf. gôru 1. --gāsa -- m.pl. a kind of grass growing in marshy ground, used as a remedy for eye-disease. kȧṭi-har - f. a fight amongst naughty boys; a fight between two young buffalos.

e: in köti-nọ̆mi - m. the being confined in all directions, being stopped from going in any direction, imprisonment; met. taking measures to prevent another exercising his free will as regards income and expenditure, etc., tying up…
fullMeaning: in köti-nọ̆mi - m. the being confined in all directions, being stopped from going in any direction, imprisonment; met. taking measures to prevent another exercising his free will as regards income and expenditure, etc., tying up another's power of expenditure.

e: f. (sg. dat. kŏcĕ ), in kömü-kŏ̈ṭü, q.v., p. 444a, l. 8.
(Śiv. 1014), see katun.

adv. in what place, where? (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 94; Rām. 209, 211, 219, etc.; K. 363, 1161; H. xi, 5); towards where? whither? (El. kŏt; Gr.M.; L.V. 9; K.Pr. 99, kut; Śiv. 410, 416, 1733, 1862); for what reason? why? (Rām. 238, 450).…
fullMeaning: adv. in what place, where? (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 94; Rām. 209, 211, 219, etc.; K. 363, 1161; H. xi, 5); towards where? whither? (El. kŏt; Gr.M.; L.V. 9; K.Pr. 99, kut; Śiv. 410, 416, 1733, 1862); for what reason? why? (Rām. 238, 450). As an interrogative expecting the answer 'no', this word may be used with a sense equivalent to 'nowhere', 'not at all' (Śiv. 1035); cf. kotunanas, kotunas, and katuth. --bā -- adv. where, sir? (used in addressing a male equal). --biñ -- adv. where, madam? (used in addressing respectfully an equal or elder woman). -kun - adv. in what direction? whither? --sa -- adv. where, sir? (used in addressing a male superior). -sanā - adv. where? i.q. kotu, but indicates a shade of doubtfulness, quasi 'I wonder where' (cf. Gr.Gr. 180-1). --ta kōr -- adv. where and where? i.e. nowhere (Śiv. 279). -tām -, -tāmath -, -tāñ -, or -tāñĕth - adv. up to how far? how far? (Gr.M.); somewhere, anywhere. The underlying idea in the mind of the speaker is a doubtful question, as in, e.g. 'is so-and-so anywhere? if so, where?' (Gr.Gr. 256). katū adv. where (used in addressing an inferior)?

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. kỗṭu ; 2 p.p. kö̃cyōv ), to pilfer secretly (esp. from goods entrusted to the thief). kỗṭu-motu - perf. part. (f. kö̃ṭü-müʦü -), pilfered, as ab.
or kotunas adv. in what place? where?; towards what place? whither? Cf. kotu 2.
i.q. könṭur, q.v.

or (Gr.Gr. 58) kōturu m. (sg. dat. kōtaras ; f. nom. kōtürü ), a pigeon or dove (wild or tame) (El.; L. 462, kotar; Rām. 93; K. 922, 947); N. of a sept of Kāshmīrī Brāhmaṇas. A cock pigeon is also nar-kōtur, and a hen is…
fullMeaning: or (Gr.Gr. 58) kōturu m. (sg. dat. kōtaras ; f. nom. kōtürü ), a pigeon or dove (wild or tame) (El.; L. 462, kotar; Rām. 93; K. 922, 947); N. of a sept of Kāshmīrī Brāhmaṇas. A cock pigeon is also nar-kōtur, and a hen is māda-kōtur (W. 17). kōtar-bāz - m. one who trains pigeons, a pigeon-fancier (W. 111). -jūri - f. a pair of doves (Gr.Gr. 82); esp. a pair of doves (male and female) swung, or let loose, in a wedding ceremony, over the bride and bridegroom. -moru - m. a dovecot (K.Pr. 57). -nal - m. 'a dove's leg', a species of pear (L. 350, kotenal). -pūtu - , m. a young pigeon (Gr.Gr. 131); a boy of the Kōturu sept of Brāhmaṇas. -rath - m. (sg. dat. -ratas -), pigeon's blood. It is of a very red colour, and the compound is often used in similes to express extreme redness.

e: f. a small kind of louse, described as red in colour and a great biter.
in kōv ka , the Kāshmīrī name of the letter ka , when written in the Śāradā character (used in schools).
f. a hen crow (El. kāvin, Gr.Gr. 37). See kāv 1.
m. paralysis of half the body, hemiplegia.
m. a hooked stick or crook, such as would be used for pulling down fruit from a tree, or for fastening a rope to (e.g. in the case of a tent- peg). Cf. göri-kôvi, p. 298a, l. 33.
m. dark-coloured, black; cf. kāworu. --kaṭh -- m. a black ram (used in sacrificial offerings to demons).

m. (sg. dat. kŏwatas ), strength, power, virtue, force, vigour, energy, authority (El.). Regarding the gender of this word, see W. 18. kŏwata-rostu - adj. (f. -rüʦhü -), powerless, without strength, unable (El. kuwatrust).
adj. c.g. strengthening, invigorating, tonic, nourishing (of food, medicine, etc.).
often written köida m. a rule, regulation, law, institution (Gr.M.); usual course of procedure, custom, usage, habit, manner, mode, way (Gr.M.). Cf. bē-köida.
often written köim adj. c.g. fixed, established (Gr.M.). -mukām - m. one who acts in the place of another, a locum- tenens (Gr.M.).

or m. a certain bird, described as red in colour, about the size of a sparrow, and as uttering a deep cry when flying up into the air.

fullMeaning: m. a judge; (a Muslim) judge or magistrate (who passes sentence in all cases of law, religious, moral, or criminal), a Qāẓī; in Kashmīr, esp. a Muslim doctor of laws, who decides questions of religion and morality (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 101, 145). -bāy - f. his wife.

sg. dat. of krüṭü, q.v. s.v., and under kroṭu.

m. one who is accustomed to make an uproar, a loud-voiced person.

or krēkh f. (sg. dat. kraki ), a loud noise, outcry (in fighting, from terror, or in lamentation) (cf. nāra-ko, s.v. nār 1) (Gr.Gr. 6, 65, 66; H. iii, 3); an exclamation, a cry (by one person or many) (Rām. 377); met. a loud…
fullMeaning: or krēkh f. (sg. dat. kraki ), a loud noise, outcry (in fighting, from terror, or in lamentation) (cf. nāra-ko, s.v. nār 1) (Gr.Gr. 6, 65, 66; H. iii, 3); an exclamation, a cry (by one person or many) (Rām. 377); met. a loud noise (e.g. the roaring of the sea) (Gr.M.); a complaint (El.). krakh is the form used in Śrīnagar, while krēkh is used elsewhere (El., H.). -cikh - or -cīkh - f. (sg. dat. kraki-ciki - or -cīki -), outcry and shriek, a loud outcry. --diñü -- f.inf. to raise an outcry, to shriek out (on receiving a blow or in pain, etc.), cry aloud (Rām. 407, 949; K. 445, 600; H. v, 7; xii, 7). --karüñü -- f.inf. to shout, to roar (El., K. 232); to complain (El.). --lāyüñü -- f.inf. to cry out, cry aloud (Rām. 390, 1360; K. 443). --tulüñü -- f.inf. to make a noise (El.); to cry out (Gr.M.). kraka-nād - m. an outcry raised by a number of people; the screaming of children (Gr.M.).

e: m. (the f. is kröjü , q.v., and signifies either his wife, or a female potter), a potter (always a Musalmān) (El.; K.Pr. 114; L. 462; W. 17; H. xi, 10, 11). krāla-anzan - m. a kind of rice; cf. anzan. -ḍabur - m. the roof of a…
fullMeaning: m. (the f. is kröjü , q.v., and signifies either his wife, or a female potter), a potter (always a Musalmān) (El.; K.Pr. 114; L. 462; W. 17; H. xi, 10, 11). krāla-anzan - m. a kind of rice; cf. anzan. -ḍabur - m. the roof of a potter's house (flat and not ridged). -kō̃da - f. a potter's kiln. -khŏḍ - m. N. of a quarter in Śrīnagar, near the Haba Kadal bridge, and inhabited by potters. -mọ̆nḍu - m. a kind of vegetable, growing wild in spring in grassy places, Capsella Bursa-pastoris (L. 71). -pan - m. the potter's string with which he cuts the soft vessels from the lump of earth on the wheel. -sangürü - f. N. of a hill on the south-east of the Ḍal lake near Śrīnagar. -ʦaküjü - f. a potter's wheel. -wān - m. a potter's shop (usually his house, where he stores and sells his pots).

e: m. a footstep; progression (Śiv. 1754, 1851); progressive order, uninterrupted progress, series, succession; lata-kram, a step with the foot; hence, a kick (see lath). krama krama gālun - m.inf. to destroy progressively; hence,…
fullMeaning: m. a footstep; progression (Śiv. 1754, 1851); progressive order, uninterrupted progress, series, succession; lata-kram, a step with the foot; hence, a kick (see lath). krama krama gālun - m.inf. to destroy progressively; hence, to keep maltreating or worrying (a servant or the like), to do so over and over again. -rostu - adj. (f. -rüʦhü -), without order, without system (Gr.M.). -sar - m. old N. of a lake and village in the Divasar Pargana. It is supposed to mark a footstep (kram) of the god Viṣṇu. See RT.Tr. II, 393.

e: f. a group of people known by the same title, or carrying on the same profession; nearly equivalent to, but not the same as 'caste' or 'sub-caste', a tribal section (K.Pr. 260, W. 141, L. 304), cf. RT.Tr. II, 430; a surname, a…
fullMeaning: f. a group of people known by the same title, or carrying on the same profession; nearly equivalent to, but not the same as 'caste' or 'sub-caste', a tribal section (K.Pr. 260, W. 141, L. 304), cf. RT.Tr. II, 430; a surname, a nickname, added to a man's original name by reason of his special calling, or because of some special circumstance that has occurred to him (El.; see K.Pr. 115 for examples).

fullMeaning: m. a kind of large covered trunk or basket made of withies, a kind of 'khilta'. Those used by natives of Kashmīr are a little larger than those used by English travellers, and are not covered with leather (El., K.Pr. 1, kranḍ). -wôru - m. a smaller kind of the same.

e: or krangūs m. a kind of cowry, long in shape and with no back.

m. a kind of basket made of withies not closely woven together, so that it has numerous interstices. It is used for carrying vegetables, roots, or the like (El., K.Pr. 115). Cf. kranzulu. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become such a…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of basket made of withies not closely woven together, so that it has numerous interstices. It is used for carrying vegetables, roots, or the like (El., K.Pr. 115). Cf. kranzulu. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become such a basket; met. to be reduced to a skeleton through sickness. kranjali pôñu sārun m.inf. to carry water in such a basket; hence, to be employed on fruitless labour.

e: m. a skeleton (? YZ. 423, Rām. 477).
m. a reed basket (Śiv. 1592). Cf. kranjolu.

m. a miser, one who is mean and niggardly. Cf. krupunu.

(sg. dat. krapas ), chopping, cutting, cutting off, esp. used for cutting wood, or for cutting food with the teeth in the act of eating; cf. krĕph. kraph-kraph - m. onomat. the noise made by the jaws in eating, champing, as in kraph kraph karith khyonu, to make a noise with the jaws in eating.

m. the wild white rose, Rosa Brunonis (El., kru̇r; L. 459, krir, a dog-rose).
m. the earthy smell of newly-baked earthenware pots, such as is observed in a potter's house. krāran-phakh - m. (sg. dat. -phakas -), the stink of boiling oil or the like.
m. N. of a tract on the western outskirts of the city of Śrīnagar.
m. a miller (only El.), i.q. graṭa- wôlu, p. 305a, l. 5.
f. (sg. dat. krüʦü ), a writing, a composition (Gr.M.).

onomat. m. the sound made in swallowing food, the noise of a gulp; cf. krith and kruth 1 and 2. --kaḍun m.inf. to withdraw the sound of gulping, to have eaten to repletion, to be satiated; met. to have all that one desires of…
fullMeaning: onomat. m. the sound made in swallowing food, the noise of a gulp; cf. krith and kruth 1 and 2. --kaḍun m.inf. to withdraw the sound of gulping, to have eaten to repletion, to be satiated; met. to have all that one desires of property, wealth, or the like. --karith -- adv. having made a gulping sound, (to eat, etc.) with a gulping sound.

e: (sg. dat. kraʦi ), N. of a certain lunar mansion, in Skt. Kṛttikā, the Pleiades. It contains six stars. kraʦi-kūrü - f. (pl. nom. -kōrĕ -), a daughter of Kṛttikā, N. of any one of the six stars of Kṛttikā. The pl. is used to…
fullMeaning: (sg. dat. kraʦi ), N. of a certain lunar mansion, in Skt. Kṛttikā, the Pleiades. It contains six stars. kraʦi-kūrü - f. (pl. nom. -kōrĕ -), a daughter of Kṛttikā, N. of any one of the six stars of Kṛttikā. The pl. is used to signify the entire constellation.

e: kriʦh , or krĕʦh f. N. of a certain plant, a green spiny potherb which grows spontaneously on grassy ground, prob. Cousinia Thomsonii, Clarke. This is a thistle-like plant, the leaves of which together with the spines are eaten…
fullMeaning: kriʦh , or krĕʦh f. N. of a certain plant, a green spiny potherb which grows spontaneously on grassy ground, prob. Cousinia Thomsonii, Clarke. This is a thistle-like plant, the leaves of which together with the spines are eaten by villagers as spinach in spring, when they are young and tender. Later on the shoots become woody and the spines very formidable (El. krits). kraʦi-kamürü - f. one of the spines among the flowers of this herb; met. anything extremely thin or slender. -konḍu - m., id. -koṭu - m. (f. -küṭü -), a boy (or girl) who is lean and thin for want of proper nourishment. -kaṭh - m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas ), a child who is lean and wasted for want of proper nourishment; hence, met. an orphan. -pōsh - m. the flower of this plant. The flowers appear among the above spines.

e: kriʦh , or krĕʦh f. N. of a certain plant of the yam species, Dioscorea deltoides. It is used in medicine as a diuretic, and its tubers are used to provide a soap for cleaning wool (L. 75, 78, krits; El. knís or krís); the word…
fullMeaning: kriʦh , or krĕʦh f. N. of a certain plant of the yam species, Dioscorea deltoides. It is used in medicine as a diuretic, and its tubers are used to provide a soap for cleaning wool (L. 75, 78, krits; El. knís or krís); the word is also used for the cleansing material itself. -mūl - m. the tuber of this plant, used as ab.

e: or krĕṭun (Gr.Gr. xv) conj. 3 (2 p.p. kraṭyōv ), to become thin (of someone or something formerly stout or thick). kraṭyō-motu - perf. part. (f. kraṭyē-müʦü -), become thin, as ab.

f. the harvesting, usufruct, or collection of crops, fruit, flowers, etc. (YZ. 31, 254; Śiv. 269, 526, 1720, 1801); the final reaping of a harvest (K.Pr. 247); the village festival on the first day of spring, on which farmers…
fullMeaning: f. the harvesting, usufruct, or collection of crops, fruit, flowers, etc. (YZ. 31, 254; Śiv. 269, 526, 1720, 1801); the final reaping of a harvest (K.Pr. 247); the village festival on the first day of spring, on which farmers commence to plough their fields for the new crop (Paṇḍit's explanation of kṛṣyârambhaḥ).

'black gold', a dark-soiled piece of ground, valuable for orchards or fruit gardens, which is very fertile and produces plenty of valuable fruit.

e: adj. (f. krĕhüñü ), black, dark-coloured (Gr.Gr. 139; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 116, kruhun; L. 159, kruhun; Śiv. 1543, 1704); morally black, black natured. --kṭa- (or -kta-) kāl-hyuhu --(or --)- adj. (f. krĕhüñü -- -hishü -- -), black like…

It is passed by Hindū pilgrims on the way to Harmŏkh, and Śrāddha offerings to the deceased are made on its banks (Rām. 245). -nūn - m. a pure kind of crystallized salt. -wöjü - f. a ring in which a stone is set.

e: see krē̃kh.

n.ag. (f. krēshĕvüñü), one who eagerly longs for anything, one who ardently desires (YZ. 8).

fullMeaning: f. N. of a certain fibre plant, Iris ensata (L. 68, krishm; El. kríshún, Iris pseudacorus). It grows wild on river banks, and besides being used for making ropes, is eaten by sheep. It has bright blue flowers. krĕshimi-raz - ‍ f. a rope made of this fibre. These ropes serve many purposes in agriculture, but the fibre is not very durable (L. 69).

m. abusive reproach, blame giving, scolding (Rām. 754, 1785); the mutual abuse of a number of people. This word is most often used with reference to the wordy warfare of women.

fullMeaning: m. a woman's relations through her father or through her brothers-in-law (El. a tribe, a word used by Hindū women; Gr.Gr. 12, 23; K.Pr. 236; YZ. 23; Rām. 1780). Cf. krônu 1. krāni nērun m.inf. to go outside the (custom) of the family; esp. to give more to a bride than the amount customary in the family; (of a bride) to go forth from her parent's house to live with her husband (Rām. 1036, 1586). kröni-kôsi - adj. (f. -kösü -), removed far from the family; hence, born in a family which has no near relatives; one who has broken all connexion with his relatives. -küṭü - f. a girl who is born in a family which has many respectable relations.

fullMeaning: m. the scab or crust on a sore or wound (El. also król, i.e. krôlu Gr.Gr. 12); the scum or skin that rises on the top of a vessel containing food. --bĕhun -- m.inf. scab to form on a sore. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise the scab from a sore; met. to raise the covering from over something hidden, to divulge a secret, to reveal a hidden matter.

fullMeaning: m. kuśa-grass, Poa cynosuroides, a sacred grass employed at various Hindū religious ceremonies (L.V. 45); N. of one of the sons of Rāmacandra, in Skt. Kuśa. fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. kacĕ , Rām. 1319), a sprout, a seedling sprout, a blade of grass or the like (Śiv. 1049); a female child, a daughter. As in the case of koṭu, q.v., of which it is the f., this word is generally used with reference to a caste or profession, but this f. form is principally used only with reference to some mean or despised profession (cf. kaṭh 2) as in bā̃ḍa-kütü, a buffoon's daughter; wāza-küṭü, a cook's daughter. Hence used in metaphorical expressions, such as (Rām. 1319) shikas-küṭü, a daughter of defeat or misery, i.e. an unfortunate woman. kacĕ-bacĕ - m.pl. fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. kĕvis ), a kind of plant growing in marshes. According to L. 72 (kĕv) it is Chaerophyllum sp., and is looked upon as an excellent substitute for carrots, both by the herdsmen and by the red bears. It has been identified at Kew as really Sagittaria sagittifolia, or Common Arrowhead, but possibly the name may be used for two different plants. For the manner in which its roots are joined together by a fibrous network, see kĕvi-rāṭh, bel., and cf. Śiv. 1807. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to root up one of these plants in the marshes. This is a long, slow business; hence, met. to spend a long time over completing any work. kĕvi-gŏgiji - , f. a kind of turnip; a small potato. -gāsa - m. the edible leaves of the kyowu-plant. -mujü - f. a young tuber of this plant, used as a vegetable. It is globular in shape; cf. mujĕ-kyowu, s.v. mujü. -mö̆nḍü - f. a full-grown large tuber of this plant. It is also globular in shape. -nambal - f. a piece of marshy ground, in which this plant grows plentifully. -rāṭh - f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi -), lit. the tangled roots of this plant, i.e. an underground fibrous network spread over a wide area, made up of the roots of this plant all tangled together. -zag - m. N. of a kind of paddy yielding a red grain when husked (L. 463, kai zag).

fullMeaning: c.g. a secondary suffix forming adjectives of quality, and indicating that the quality not only accompanies the object, but is actually a necessary part of it. Thus from phakh (base phak-), a stink; phakalad, stinking (Gr.Gr. 135; cf. 133). When used as an adjective it is of common gender, but, when used substantively, its fem. is ladiñ , as in bakalad, a chatterer (masc.); bakaladiñ, a chattering woman.

e: f. (sg. dat. lali ), N. of a celebrated mystic poetess of Kashmīr, who lived probably in the fourteenth century. She was a Śaiva by religion, and her verses are still frequently quoted. She is popularly known as Lal Dĕd or…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. lali ), N. of a celebrated mystic poetess of Kashmīr, who lived probably in the fourteenth century. She was a Śaiva by religion, and her verses are still frequently quoted. She is popularly known as Lal Dĕd or 'Granny Lal', and, in Sanskrit, her name was Lallā. Many collections of her verses have been made under the Sanskrit name of the Lallā Vākyāni, or 'Sayings of Lallā'. The most complete edition is that published by the Royal Asiatic Society in 1920 (L.V. 3, 48, 49, etc.; K.Pr. 47, 82). In token of respect Hindūs refer to her as Lalīshŏrī (Śiv. 1656, 1773).

(amongst Hindūs) a god who is a regent or guardian of one of the four quarters (or points of the compass) or of one of the four intermediate points (eight in all). (These are (in Sanskrit) Indra (regent of the East), Agni (of the South-East), Yama (of the South), Nairṛta (of the South-West), Varuṇa (of the West), Vāyu (of the North-West), Kubēra (of the North), and Īśāna (of the North-East) (Śiv. 1147, 1457; K. 335, 538, 1049).)

fullMeaning: m. N. of the tenth month of the Hindū luni-solar year (in Sanskrit, Māgha) (January-February) (Gr.Gr. 51; W. 107, māgh; K.Pr. 60, 128, 147, 171; Śiv. 590, 1162, 1351). --darun -- m.inf. to keep a fast throughout the month of Māg (eating only at night),--a Hindū religious ceremony. -mās - m. the month of Māg (the term used in phrases referring to religious rites). māga-bata - m. cooked rice in Māg, the N. of an offering (bali) of cooked rice scattered on house-roofs and elsewhere for the crows. -noṭu darun - - m.inf. to keep the fast of the Māg water-jar,--a particular vow or fast kept in ancient times by Hindūs. The procedure was as follows:--For the first three days of the month of Māg the celebrant eats only in the evening; he then fasts for a whole day; then for three days eats only in the morning; then fasts for two days; then for three days he eats only at night; then fasts for two days; then again three days night-eating; and so on to the end of the month. Every day, for two praharas (i.e. six hours), he stands in a frozen stream in water reaching up to his navel, and lets ice-cold water trickle on to his head from a jar in the bottom of which a hole has been pierced. -tǖrü - f. the cold of the month of Māg, winter cold. māguku adj. (f. māgücü ), of, or belonging to, the month of Māg.

(sg. dat. -māwạsi -), the lunar day which falls on the new moon of the Hindū month of Bādarapĕth (in Sanskrit, Bhādrapada) (August-September). It is believed that according as rain falls or does not fall on this day, so the prospects of the crops are good or bad (cf. our St. Swithin's day on July 15).

(sg. dat. mahākalpas ), (in Hindū theology) a vast cycle of time (in Sanskrit, mahākalpa), corresponding to the life of Brahmā, which consists of a hundred years of which each day and night is usually said to consist of a kalpa or 4,320,000,000 mortal years; cf. kalpānth. (f. mahaladārĕñ ), the head man of a district or parish, an officer in charge of a ward, an alderman; (in Kashmīr) the officer in charge of a division of a city, the ward-watchman, who guards the village by night, and sees that Government orders are carried out (K.Pr. 105). fullMeaning: m. a suffix used with any numeral except one, two, four, or multiples of four, indicating one and a half seers (or three pounds). Thus tra-man, three times one and a half seers or four and a half seers; pānʦh-man, five times one and a half seers or seven and a half seers; shĕ-man, six times one and a half seers or nine seers; sath-man, seven times one and a half seers or ten and a half seers; nav-man, nine times one and a half seers or thirteen and a half seers, and so on. But a single one and a half seer is manoṭu, q.v.; twice one and a half seers, or three seers, is pānzuwu; four times one and a half seers, or six seers, is trakh, q.v.; eight times one and a half seers, or twelve seers, is za-trakh, or two trakh; twelve times one and a half seers, or eighteen seers, is tra-trakh, or three trakh, and so on for further multiples of four.
