(sg. dat mȧnzilas ), a place for alighting, an hotel, caravanserai; a house, lodging; a mansion of the moon; a story or floor (of a house); a day's journey, a stage (in travelling) (Śiv. 1309, 1627). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to complete a long and wearying stage. --pyonu -- m.inf. a long wearying stage to fall to the lot of a traveller; met. some difficult and toilsome necessity to fall to the lot of a helpless person. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to travel (El., Rām. 207). mȧnzilas wātun - m.inf. to arrive at (the end of) the stage; met. finally to reach the last stage of a difficult and toilsome business, to have the end of such in sight.

e: in the following:--manzīla yunu m.inf. (of a person) sudden ruin to occur.
(El.), see maĩz.
see mandun.
m. a child's swinging-cot, a swing-cradle (Śiv. 352, 1321, 1379 ff.; Rām. 632; K. 118-19). Cf. guga-manzulu, p. 279b, l. 34.
or (H. i, 12) mônzūr adj. c.g. approved of, admitted, accepted, sanctioned (Śiv. 636, 692, 900; H. i, 12).
m. (f. manzürü ), a cripple (El.).

adj. (f.manzimü ), middle, intermediate, internal (Gr.Gr. 152, Śiv. 1467); middling, mediocre, moderately good, middle-class (Gr.M., K.Pr. 136); cf. anzyumu-manzyumu, p. 37a, l. 18. --yôru -- m. (f. manzimü yārĕñ , Gr.Gr. 135, a…
fullMeaning: adj. (f.manzimü ), middle, intermediate, internal (Gr.Gr. 152, Śiv. 1467); middling, mediocre, moderately good, middle-class (Gr.M., K.Pr. 136); cf. anzyumu-manzyumu, p. 37a, l. 18. --yôru -- m. (f. manzimü yārĕñ , Gr.Gr. 135, a female go-between) an intermediary, a go-between (Gr.Gr. 135, 142; W. 149; K.Pr. 260; Śiv. 1670); a broker (Gr.M.); a matchmaker, a go-between who arranges a marriage, a go-between in love matters (L. 261, 268; Śiv. 713; Rām. 134). manzimü yörī f. the action or profession of a matchmaker or broker. --yāraz -- , f. the action or profession of a matchmaker, the office of a go-between (Gr.Gr. 142); the profession of a broker (Gr.M.); the wages or fee paid to a matchmaker.

e: (El.), see māv.
or muāf adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. māphas ), pardoned, forgiven; subst., m. forgiveness (K.Pr. 124). --karun -- m.inf. to pardon (Gr.M.; Śiv. 423, 593).

m. a hut, a small house (K.Pr. 7, 138); an ascetic's leaf-hut in the forest; a shelter or small hut (erected in desolate or forest localities as a refuge for travellers) (RT.Tr. II, 387); a cell, a small room (cf. bata-mar, a…
fullMeaning: m. a hut, a small house (K.Pr. 7, 138); an ascetic's leaf-hut in the forest; a shelter or small hut (erected in desolate or forest localities as a refuge for travellers) (RT.Tr. II, 387); a cell, a small room (cf. bata-mar, a store-room for food (p. 137a, l. 27). This word is not uncommonly --˚ in place names; cf. āhal-mar (p. 17b, l. 38; ālȧʦhi-mar, p. 26a, l. 8). El. also has mar, f., a fort, a castle. --hĕni -- - m. pl. inf. to take huts, i.e. from grief, distress, distaste for the world, or the like, to take to a solitary hermit's life in some cave, in the forest, or the like.

e: m. killing, taking life, slaughter, murder (Gr.Gr. 124; W. 114; Rām. 217, 1032); hitting, beating, striking (cf. ã̄cĕ-mār, p. 53b, l. 11; cō̃ca-mār, p. 157a, l. 31; gir-mār, p. 303a, l. 6). --˚ sometimes indicates a person who…
fullMeaning: m. killing, taking life, slaughter, murder (Gr.Gr. 124; W. 114; Rām. 217, 1032); hitting, beating, striking (cf. ã̄cĕ-mār, p. 53b, l. 11; cō̃ca-mār, p. 157a, l. 31; gir-mār, p. 303a, l. 6). --˚ sometimes indicates a person who kills, strikes, or hits, as in chūrī-mār, a dagger-striker, one who strikes (himself) with a dagger (p. 165a, l. 42). This word also takes the form māra, q.v., s.v., from which in the oblique cases it is indistinguishable. --dyunu -- m.inf. to give killing, to kill (Rām. 103); to give a beating, to drub (Rām. 618, 961, 1276). -ganḍ - m. tying up and beating, a kind of punishment, in which the victim's arms and legs are tied up, and then he is thumped with fists. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. murder to occur. --hyonu -- m.inf. to receive a beating. --khasun -- m.inf. a charge of murder to be brought. --khyonu -- m.inf. to eat a beating, to suffer a beating, to be beaten. --karun -- m.inf. to commit murder. --maṭi khasun -- - m.inf. murder to mount on the shoulder, a charge of murder to be brought (against a person). māra-būth - m. (sg. dat. -būtas -), a demon of murder, a murderous demon (L.V. 71), -dĕv - m. a death-demon, torment caused by an evil death, or due to some evil death. -wārĕñ - f. a midwife who attends the birth of a dead child.

e: m. (a corruption of manḍal 2, in the sense of 'territory'), a province, tract, as in Kashmīra- mar, the land of Kashmīr (Śiv. 1159).

m. a serpent, a snake (cf. kŏla-mār, p. 437a, l. 28) (YZ. 35, 64, 141). mār-i-pēʦān, a serpent of convolutions, a kind of serpent that makes itself into a ring round its victim, and thus kills it at its leisure (Rām. 913).
m. the Hindū god of love, Cupid; love, passion. māra-motu - m. extreme love, affection, fondness (YZ. 37); an ardent lover (Rām. 1585).

f. (sg. dat. mörü 1 , Gr.Gr. 75; for 2, see môru 2; for 3, see s.v.), N. of a canal issuing from the Ḍal lake, and passing behind that part of the city of Śrīnagar which lies on the right bank of the river Vĕth (Jĕhlam). It…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. mörü 1 , Gr.Gr. 75; for 2, see môru 2; for 3, see s.v.), N. of a canal issuing from the Ḍal lake, and passing behind that part of the city of Śrīnagar which lies on the right bank of the river Vĕth (Jĕhlam). It empties itself into the ā̃cār marshes north-west of the city (cf. RT.Tr. II, 416) (K.Pr. 137), a lake genl. (El.). mörü-bal - m. N. of a landing place with masonry steps on the bank of the Mār (Gr.Gr. 165). -hönzü - m. a boatman living or plying on the river Mār (they have a bad name); met. an impudent, dishonest, evil-conducted fellow. -hānzañ - - f. the wife of such a boatman; met. an impudent, unchaste, dishonest woman. -wôñu - m. the water of the Mār (noted for its purity) (Gr.Gr. 73); lake-water genl. (El. mãrwóin).

e: m. killing someone or some animal, murder; as adj. c.g. beaten, killed (El. márah, K.Pr. 138); cf. mār 1. -cīri - f. a letter announcing a death. -gã̄ḍay - f. the action of binding and beating a person (cf. mār-ganḍ, p. 586b, l.…
fullMeaning: m. killing someone or some animal, murder; as adj. c.g. beaten, killed (El. márah, K.Pr. 138); cf. mār 1. -cīri - f. a letter announcing a death. -gã̄ḍay - f. the action of binding and beating a person (cf. mār-ganḍ, p. 586b, l. 38). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to death or to beating, to be killed (YZ. 477; Rām. 701, 868, 972, 1424; H. x, 7, 8, 13); met. to be obstructed, impeded. -hāʦh - f. (sg. dat. -hāʦi -), a charge or accusation of murder. -hāʦh yiñü - f.inf. an accusation of murder to be made (against a person). --karun -- m. to knock down finally, to give a knock-out blow, to kill (e.g. by a sudden blow) (Rām. 1585, 1726 (met.)); (of a business) to knock down a work or an occupation, to obstruct it so that it cannot be resumed. -mār - f. (for gend., see Gr.Gr. 75), a fight between a number of armed men; utter killing, death in every part of the body (Rām. 1484); (on the occasion of an epidemic) a multitude of deaths. -māray - f. mutual beating or striking, a broil, affray. --sö̃panun -- m.inf. (so-and-so's) death to have occurred; hence, to have become dead, to be dead and gone (Rām. 1381); cf. māray sö̃püñü, s.v. māray. -wātul - m. a public executioner (Gr.M.; H. viii, 4, 11-13; x, 12). -wātüjü - f. a female executioner (for executing women); the wife of an executioner.

e: in mara-phēra - m. turning of wish; hence, (after agreeing to do something, or being ordered to do it) to do it unwillingly, e.g. in distributing something, to worry the recipients by grudging or delay, even while consenting to…
fullMeaning: in mara-phēra - m. turning of wish; hence, (after agreeing to do something, or being ordered to do it) to do it unwillingly, e.g. in distributing something, to worry the recipients by grudging or delay, even while consenting to carry out the distribution. Cf. marwāna.

e: in the following:--mara-mar - f. general mortality, a great number of deaths occurring in any locality (owing to epidemic, massacre, etc.); the near approach of death, the last flicker of life (when all hope of recovery is…
fullMeaning: in the following:--mara-mar - f. general mortality, a great number of deaths occurring in any locality (owing to epidemic, massacre, etc.); the near approach of death, the last flicker of life (when all hope of recovery is abandoned). -mara - m. the abandonment of all hope of life, being at the point of death.

e: a suffix added to cardinal numerals to indicate 'about'. Thus, from aiṭh, eight; aiṭha- mara, about eight; daha-mara, about ten (p. 199a, l. 15) (W. 103). Also added to manz, in; see p. 584a, l. 22. Cf. Gr.Gr. 84, where the…
fullMeaning: a suffix added to cardinal numerals to indicate 'about'. Thus, from aiṭh, eight; aiṭha- mara, about eight; daha-mara, about ten (p. 199a, l. 15) (W. 103). Also added to manz, in; see p. 584a, l. 22. Cf. Gr.Gr. 84, where the suffix is given as amara, the initial a being the termination of the oblique case of the numeral.

e: m. a field of battle, tumult (El.); quarrelling, strife (K.Pr. 137); an assembly, meeting, congregation (Śiv. 89; H. vii, 23).
), repairing, repair (El., Gr.M.); --karun -- m.inf. to repair (El.).
m. the end of death, death (K. 540).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. maranôwu ), to cause to be pasted or joined together (causal of marun 1, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 175).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. māranôwu ), to cause to kill, to incite to kill, to have (so-and-so, or such-and-such an animal) killed, to cause to be slain (Rām. 1473, 1476); to cause to be slain, and hence, to capture a piece (in chess) (Rām.…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. māranôwu ), to cause to kill, to incite to kill, to have (so-and-so, or such-and-such an animal) killed, to cause to be slain (Rām. 1473, 1476); to cause to be slain, and hence, to capture a piece (in chess) (Rām. 1314); to ruin, mar, spoil (Rām. 1160).

e: m. Desmodium tiliæfolium (El.). Cf. camkāth.
f. wages paid for beating (a person, cattle or other animals); N. of a certain game, in which small balls are aimed at a mark.
n.ag. (f. maravüñü ), one who is dying, a person at the point of death.
n.ag. (f. māravüñü ), one who kills, a slayer (Śiv. 856, 1321); a murderer, a homicide (K. 64); a beater, one who beats, a flogger. ʦhāla mārawunu, one who leaps (cf. p. 593a, l. 6) (Śiv. 1322).

f. killing, beating, i.q. māra, used --˚ as in hūni-māray, p. 336b, l. 48; māra-māray, p. 587b, l. 7. --karüñü -- f.inf. to slay, kill, murder (Śiv. 578). --sö̃panüñü -- f.inf. to become killed, to be killed.
m. disease, sickness, illness, malady, distemper (K.Pr. 138). marza-dĕv - m. a severe sickness, a deadly or incurable disease (ascribed to possession by a demon).

m. one of the two great divisions of the Kashmīr valley, embracing the whole south-east end. The ancient name was Maḍavarājya. The other division is called Kamrāz (Kramarājya), q.v. for further particulars; cf. RT.Tr. II, 436…
fullMeaning: m. one of the two great divisions of the Kashmīr valley, embracing the whole south-east end. The ancient name was Maḍavarājya. The other division is called Kamrāz (Kramarājya), q.v. for further particulars; cf. RT.Tr. II, 436 (K.Pr. 138; H. xi, 5). marāzuku adj. (f. marāzücü ), of, or belonging to, Marāz.

e: m. a man, vir, male human being (W. 149; K.Pr. 103, 250, 260; Śiv. 974). marda-mahanyuwu - m. a male man, i.e. a thoroughly masculine man, an able-bodied man endowed with all his wits, a real man. -nāl - m. the neck- piece of a…
fullMeaning: m. a man, vir, male human being (W. 149; K.Pr. 103, 250, 260; Śiv. 974). marda-mahanyuwu - m. a male man, i.e. a thoroughly masculine man, an able-bodied man endowed with all his wits, a real man. -nāl - m. the neck- piece of a man's garment. -noru - m. the sleeve of a man's garment. -phĕran - m. a man's phĕran, i.e. the garment worn by Kāshmīrīs of both sexes, somewhat like a night-gown with wide sleeves. -pöthar - m. the work of a man, or work suitable for, or intended for, a man, man's work (as distinct from woman's work). -pôʦhu - m. a man's undergarment (made of cotton, and worn next the skin). -zan -, man or woman (H. vii, 23).

e: m. rubbing, shampooing; anointing (with unguents) (K. 973).
adj. c.g. manlike, virile; manly, brave; of, or pertaining to, or suitable for, a man.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mardôwu ), to rub away, to wear out (a garment, dish, or the like) by use; to rub down with ointment a boil or the like. mardāwana āmotu perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦü --), rubbed away, worn away by use (e.g. a…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. mardôwu ), to rub away, to wear out (a garment, dish, or the like) by use; to rub down with ointment a boil or the like. mardāwana āmotu perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦü --), rubbed away, worn away by use (e.g. a garment, dish, or the like); (of a boil or the like) reduced by rubbing down, as ab. mardāwana yunu m.inf. pass. to become worn away by use, as ab.; (of a boil, etc.) to be reduced, as ab. mardôwu-motu - perf. part. (f. mardövü-müʦü -), rubbed, as ab. (in both senses).

e: see marēd.
f. manhood, virility, manliness, valour (Rām. 487).
f. oppression, tyranny; (in Kāshmīrī) met. the conduct of a lovely woman, amorous sport (H. x, 12).

f. (sg. dat. marēdi or mardi ), a certain pinkish-white powder formed from a certain stone. It is used for marking swastikas, circles, or other mystic religious signs. --wahārüñü -- f.inf. to spread out this powder, i.e. by means…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. marēdi or mardi ), a certain pinkish-white powder formed from a certain stone. It is used for marking swastikas, circles, or other mystic religious signs. --wahārüñü -- f.inf. to spread out this powder, i.e. by means of a charm or similar mark, to prevent the access of outsiders to any act or person. mardi-pholu - or marēdi-pholu - m. a quantity of this powder. -phĕkh - or marēdi-phĕkh - f. (sg. dat. -phĕki -), id. -rakh - or marēdi-rakh - f. (sg. dat. -rakhi -), a line marked with this powder (e.g. at a sacrificial rite, the mark of a swastika or mystic circle, or a boundary line circumscribing the operations). -rakh trāvüñü - f.inf. (at a sacrifice, etc.) with this powder to mark the boundary line enclosing the holy ground within which the operations take place, and within which access is prohibited to unauthorized persons or things.

e: m. a road, a way, a path (lit. and fig.) (Gr.M.; L.V. 63, 82; Śiv. 1655, 1801); (in pl.) ways (i.e. customary actions) (Gr.M.)

m. death (YZ. 559, 562); (in Kāshmīrī) grief caused by a death (esp. of one on whom many depend) (cf. jāna-marg, p. 374b, l. 28). --pharun -- m.inf. ruin caused by the death of someone on whom the ruined person was dependent to…
fullMeaning: m. death (YZ. 559, 562); (in Kāshmīrī) grief caused by a death (esp. of one on whom many depend) (cf. jāna-marg, p. 374b, l. 28). --pharun -- m.inf. ruin caused by the death of someone on whom the ruined person was dependent to occur. marga-būñü - f. (sg. dat. -bōñĕ -), a woman who has grown old and seen many of her descendants and relations die before her. -hotu - - adj. (f. -hüʦü ), afflicted and sorrowing owing to the death of someone very dear. -vyotu - adj. (f. -vë̆ʦü -), full of sorrow for the same reason.

e: f. a valley or plateau high up among the mountains (full of wild flowers, with level ground and a cool pleasant climate). Frequent --˚, as in gul-marg, p. 283b, l. 23.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. margaladiñ ), one who is sorrowing for the death of a dear one (esp. of one on whom the person sorrowing was dependent).
f. twists and turns; crisp, curly, or waving hair; quavering, trilling, or shaking of the voice; a crenated arch; a tassel for tying up and closing the end of a pillow.
interj. welcome! hail! God bless you! bravo! (Śiv. 657; H. ii, 10).
m. dressing (for wounds), ointment, salve (K.Pr. 146).

adv., used --˚, an old obl. case of mār 1, q.v. 'by striking by'; hence, through, by reason of, on account of, in consequence of, as in dŏkha-māri, by reason of sorrow, i.e. compassionately, pitifully (p. 206b, l. 2).

f. a violent epidemic, cholera, etc. (cf. mörī). mȧrica-buḍi - f. a particularly deadly epidemic killing quickly, cholera. mȧrica-dĕv - m. the demon of an epidemic such as cholera. mȧrica-dĕviñ - f. the female demon of the same.…
fullMeaning: f. a violent epidemic, cholera, etc. (cf. mörī). mȧrica-buḍi - f. a particularly deadly epidemic killing quickly, cholera. mȧrica-dĕv - m. the demon of an epidemic such as cholera. mȧrica-dĕviñ - f. the female demon of the same. mȧrica-kôni - m. a death from cholera or similar violent epidemic. ? Cf. kān 1.

e: m. a kind of woollen cloth woven in varied colours (? = merino). marīnuku adj. (f. marīnücü ), made of this cloth. marīna-sondu - adj. (f. -sünzü -), id.
or yīmarjal m. the iris (Iris pseudacorus) (El.).
m. a carrier who conveys goods on mules or ponies, a muleteer (L. 364, 383, 459).
m. the wild goat of Ladak, the Markhor (Gr.M.).
f. a certain tube believed to exist in the heart, the vitals, a vital part of the body.
f. the hidden or secret meaning of anything, the pith, or essential, meaning; the secret or hidden intention of a person.
f. pl. the joints of any limb.
m. a rustling sound, rustling, murmuring, murmur; crackling, crackle; sound of crunching, etc.
m. marble, usually in the phrase sang-ĕ-marmar, employed with the same meaning.
m. a road covered with hard frozen snow (and, hence, made passable owing to freedom from mud and inequalities).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, or produced in, Marāz, q.v.
f. a lamentation for the dead, a dirge (esp. the one sung during the Moḥarram in commemoration of Ḥasan and Ḥusain).
m. a glazed earthenware jar (used for keeping preserves and pickles, etc., in); a vessel of the finest porcelain which poison cannot penetrate.
m. station, post of honour, rank, dignity (L.V. 87, K.Pr. 145); time, turn. Cf. marith martaba, p. 592b, l. 18.
see maṭan.
m. (sg. dat. martĕlūkas ), the world of mortals, the world (Rām. 551).

m. pepper, black pepper (El. also marits; K.Pr. 62 (misprinted marats), 138, 233; K. 373). --mathun -- m.inf. to pound pepper; met. goading oneself, i.e. (in fury, despair, etc.) beating oneself, tearing one's own face with one's…
fullMeaning: m. pepper, black pepper (El. also marits; K.Pr. 62 (misprinted marats), 138, 233; K. 373). --mathun -- m.inf. to pound pepper; met. goading oneself, i.e. (in fury, despair, etc.) beating oneself, tearing one's own face with one's nails or the like. --ʦāpun -- m.inf. to chew pepper; met. shouting out to people generally when in a rage. marʦa-gŏsôñu - m. (sarcastically) a peppery saint, u.w. ref. to a child (esp. a boy) who is of a passionate disposition. In Sanskrit literature there are various legends of peppery saints, whose curses caused great mischief. -pŏnd - f. (sg. dat. pŏndi ), pepper-sneezing; met. pride, haughtiness, vainglory, arrogance. -pŏnda trāwañĕ - f. pl. inf. to emit pepper-sneezes; met. arrogantly to display rage (esp. to one's inferiors). -pī˜piñ - , f. a teetotum (a kind of top); a kind of musical instrument (played by blowing into it) (cf. pī˜piñ). -ṭĕchĕr - m. pepper-heat; irritability (of character). -wã̄gun - m. long pepper, red pepper, a pod of red pepper, a red chilli, Capsicum sp. (L. 346; H. v, 6). -wã̄gan-āra -- m. a chain or string of red chillis, dried and kept for winter use. (They are strung on a thread, like a necklace.)

e: f. conj. 1 (1 p.p., f. marʦövü . This verb is construed impersonally in the feminine (cf. marʦüñü)), inward wrath to be caused to a person, indignation to be caused to a person.

conj. 1 (1 p.p., f. mürʦü . This verb is always construed impersonally in the feminine, with the logical subject in the dative, as in marʦān chĕ-s , there is inward wrath to him, i.e. he is inwardly wrathful; cf. Gr.Gr. 182, 188,…

Gr.Gr. 182, 188, 215); inward wrath to attack, indignation to be felt, impatience to be felt (Gr.Gr. 117, 119, 192, 248).

e: see māryuku.

fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. moru , Gr.Gr. 223; also optionally conjugated like marun 2, Gr.Gr. 204. (f. mürü-müʦü -), pasted on.

e: m. private intention (to do something contrary to instructions), doing something (with a private contrary intention); cf. mara 1. --phērun -- m.inf. a secret intention (as ab.) to be changed.
m. (El. márúk and maryuku), a noose, a lasso (El.); a hangman's noose; a scaling ladder used by thieves (El.); a horse's halter (El.). Cf. möli-māi, p. 566b, l. 22.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. marzaladiñ ), suffering from an incurable disease.
m. Origanum vulgare (El.).

m. wine. It is made out of the juice of the grape, which grows luxuriantly in Kashmīr (El.; L.V. 104; K.Pr. 5, 102, 138, 139; YZ. 193, 209, 343, 366; Śiv. 1203, 1220, 1260, 1326, 1823, 1844, 1874; H. vii, 31). -khôsu - m. a…

f. madness, lunacy, the conduct of a madman (Gr.Gr. 143); conduct like that of a madman. mȧtilāza karañĕ f. pl. inf. to do mad actions, to act like a madman.
m. object, intention, aim, purpose (El. mutlab) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 139); the meaning or purport (of anything) (Gr.M.). Cf. matbal.

f. a mother, used ˚--, as in -rǖpi - adj. c.g. having the form or character of a mother; performing the duty of a mother (L.V. 54).

m. madness, lunacy (Gr.Gr. 140, Rām. 709, K. 290). --anun -- , m.inf. to bring madness, to cause madness; madness to arise. --yunu -- m.inf. madness to arise.

fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. maʦhi ), the upper- arm (between the shoulder and the elbow) (properly the region of the biceps and triceps, El.) (sg. dat. -gagaras -), a certain animal inhabiting the mountain forests, described as a large kind of winged rat, ? a flying fox. --ʦāpañĕ -- f.inf. to bite one's arms; hence, to feel and exhibit great regret (e.g. by silent weeping or the like). -zōr - m. muscular strength of the arms. maʦhi-ganḍas thawun - - m.inf. to keep (for someone) with great care (as if keeping it tied under the arm). -khash - m. a wound on the arm; met. worry owing to having to incur great expense, or to losing a large sum of money. -māz khyonu - m.inf. to eat the flesh of one's arm; to show anxious desire.

e: f. (sg. dat. maʦhi ), pounded meat (it is pounded to a paste in a mortar). maʦhi-dāl - f. a dish of this pounded meat, with crushed pulse. -ganḍ - m. a piece of pounded meat roasted or fried. -woru - m. a soup containing balls…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. maʦhi ), pounded meat (it is pounded to a paste in a mortar). maʦhi-dāl - f. a dish of this pounded meat, with crushed pulse. -ganḍ - m. a piece of pounded meat roasted or fried. -woru - m. a soup containing balls (or cakes) of this pounded meat fried in oil.

e: f. (sg. dat. maʦhi ), conciliatory treatment, persuasiveness, persuading by gentle means, consolation (Gr.Gr. 147). --diñü -- f.inf. to treat in a conciliatory manner or persuasively.

see maʦhyulu 1.

adj. (f. maʦhilü [sic]), hard, tough (e.g. grain hard to pound).
adj. (f. maʦhijü ), kindly, affectionate, tender, consolatory (Gr.Gr. 147); arousing affection, interesting, enchanting (i.q. a work, a book, etc.).

fullMeaning: conj. 3 (2 p.p. matyōv ), madness to arise, to become mad, to become foolish (K.Pr. 139, 215; YZ. 15; K. 263, 284); to rave abusively, violently to give vent to abuse. mȧti mȧti drāmotu - perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦü --), (esp. of a child) well known as passionate and unruly (cf. the next). mȧti mȧti nērun m.inf. maddened and maddened to go forth; hence, (esp. of a child) to be widely known as passionate and unruly. matyō-motu - perf. part. (f. matyē-müʦü -), gone mad, attacked with lunacy; engaged in raving abuse (against another).

e: or mō , adv. (prohibition particle, i.q. ma, q.v., but more respectful) (L.V. 30, 36, 72; Śiv. 274, 1003, 1324, 1635, 1671, 1702, 1815; Rām. 727, 816, 1041, etc.). na mō, i.q. mō (Rām. 1231). Cf. mav, mōv.
or (= ) m. a fit or proper time, occasion, opportunity (Gr.M.).
m. a time, a season (of the year) (Gr.M.).
see mōth.
adv., i.q. mau, i.e. a prohibitive particle, the same as ma, q.v., but more respectful (Śiv. 1008; Rām. 9, 97, 1030). Cf. mōv.

f. the back of the hand from the wrist to the root of the fingers, the metacarpus (El. máo); a cutting, a branch cut off from a parent tree to be planted separately (El. máo) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1819). --diñü -- f.inf. to apply the palm…
fullMeaning: f. the back of the hand from the wrist to the root of the fingers, the metacarpus (El. máo); a cutting, a branch cut off from a parent tree to be planted separately (El. máo) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1819). --diñü -- f.inf. to apply the palm (to the mouth to conceal it); (in weighing goods) to touch (the scales) with the palm of the hand (so as to make the article weighed appear more than it really is), to give false weight. māvi māvi adv. in handfuls, fistfuls (Śiv. 1212). --roṭu tōl -- , , m. weighing fairly (in which the beam of the scales hang from a string fastened to the middle of the beam and held in the palm of the hand); giving false weight by privily pressing the beam of the scales with the palm of the hand.

e: (for 2, see māwuru) f. N. of a certain river (the Māhurī of Sanskrit) in Mȧchipūr Pargana (RT.Tr. II, 425).
adj. c.g. stoical, sober-minded, philosophic.
f. the dewlap of an ox.

or mŏwal 1 f. N. of a certain plant, the cockscomb (Amaranthus cruentus). Bread-cakes made from the seed are a common food with the peasants (El. mawur). According to L. 75 (mowal) its seeds are used in medicine as a demulcent.
adj. c.g. (of a cloth) possessing an edge or fringe.
according to L. 463, N. of a kind of rice, a good cropper with a red grain.
m. a rebel (K.Pr. 245).

f. (sg. dat. often written māwȧsi ), the day of the new moon, when the sun and moon dwell together or are in conjunction; the 15th day of the dark half of every lunar month (cf. khĕʦi-māwas, p. 424a, l. 46) (L.V. 22; Śiv. 209,…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. often written māwȧsi ), the day of the new moon, when the sun and moon dwell together or are in conjunction; the 15th day of the dark half of every lunar month (cf. khĕʦi-māwas, p. 424a, l. 46) (L.V. 22; Śiv. 209, 526, 740). --hë̆ñü -- - f.inf. to observe the rites of the night of the new moon. --thavüñü -- f.inf. to keep or observe ritely the night of the new moon. māwȧsi-hondu - adj. (f. -hünzü -), of, or belonging to, the night of the new moon (Śiv. 1042).

e: m. something in exchange, compensation, return, retaliation; a fitting reply, a retort (Rām. 841).

m. the edge or fringe of a cloth. māwȧli-trọ̆pi - m. a kind of hem joining the edges of two cloths. -ʦhyonu - adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñü -), having the edge or fringe torn. -ʦoṭu - adj. (f. -ʦüṭü -), having its edge or fringe cut off.
adj. (f. māvürü 2 ?), (of a person) reserved, uncommunicative, secretive.

f. magic, illusion; love (for earthly things) (L.V. 67); illusion (in the sense of māyā, q.v.) (K. 18, 247, 295, 409); love, affection (K.Pr. 201, may; YZ. 474; Śiv. 39, 103, 536, 1136, 1140, 1472, 1619, 1743; Rām. 158, 270, 303,…
fullMeaning: f. magic, illusion; love (for earthly things) (L.V. 67); illusion (in the sense of māyā, q.v.) (K. 18, 247, 295, 409); love, affection (K.Pr. 201, may; YZ. 474; Śiv. 39, 103, 536, 1136, 1140, 1472, 1619, 1743; Rām. 158, 270, 303, 987, 1363, 1516, etc.; K. 470, 1101-2); sitting apart secretly, on secret watch (cf. bröri-māy, p. 125b, l. 40; hāpath-māy, p. 342b, l. 42; mūdi-māy, p. 549b, l. 9) (YZ. 383, 490); cf. māyā. --bögarüña -- or --böjarüña -- f.inf. to divide out love, to behave lovingly to every one, to show a very kindly general disposition. --gaʦhüñü -- f.inf. affection to come into existence, love (for so-and-so) to be felt (for the first time). --karüñü -- f.inf. to remain hidden and watchful, to act secretly (Rām. 1465). --lāgüñü -- f.inf. to put on secrecy, i.e. to pretend to be asleep, or motionless and inattentive, in order to discover some hidden matter, to play the spy in this way. māyĕ-hondu - adj. (f. -hünzü -), of, or belonging to, affection; hence, one who exhibits a general affectionate disposition. -rǖpi - adj. c.g. acting in the character of a deceiver, (f.) a Delilah (L.V. 54). -rosu - or -rostu - adj. (f. -rüʦhü -), void of affection, heartless, unfeeling, unkind.

e: or mai f. wine, spirituous liquor (K.Pr. 131; Śiv. 1863; Rām. 513, 1489); nectar, a drink which restores a dead man to life (Rām. 1500). mai-khāna m. a wine house, wine shop (El. mekhāna, K.Pr. 131).
adj. c.g. used --˚, consisting of, composed of, as in shiwa-may (L.V. 16) consisting only of Śiva; shŏda-ʦĕtta-būda-may, consisting of pure discrimination (Śiv. 1850).
i.q. ma or mā, prohibitive particle (H. v, 2, poet.).

f. illusion, trick, artifice, deception; an illusory image, a phantasm; (or māy, q.v.; K. 18, 247, 295, 409) an illusory phantom (often personified) sent forth by the Deity to confound sinners (K. 17, 42, 48, 72, 78-9, 214, 293,…
fullMeaning: f. illusion, trick, artifice, deception; an illusory image, a phantasm; (or māy, q.v.; K. 18, 247, 295, 409) an illusory phantom (often personified) sent forth by the Deity to confound sinners (K. 17, 42, 48, 72, 78-9, 214, 293, 301, 409, 592-3, 757, 774, 960); spiritual illusion, an illusive power depending on the Deity, whereby mankind believe in the existence of external objects which are in fact purely ideal, the illusory power which prevents man from recognizing his identity with the Supreme (Śiv. 17, 30-1, 34, 46, 96, 158, etc.; Rām. 179); the external world, Nature personified; worldly (as distinct from spiritual) prosperity, opulence, riches (Śiv. 84, K. 1157); compassion, pity, sympathy; love, affection (cf. māy). This word and māy and māyĕ are commonly used interchangeably. -gan - adj. c.g. well supplied with accumulated wealth, rich, wealthy; cf. māyĕ. -kạtsupera;ra - m. a little store of wealth (cf. kạtara), esp. the secret savings of a miser. -pholu - m. a hidden hoard of wealth. -sôwu - adj. (f. -sövü ), possessing much wealth, wealthy, rich; cf. māyĕ-sāvĕr, s.v. māyĕ. -wôlu - m. (f. -wājĕñ -), possessing wealth, wealthy, rich. -zāl - m. the noose of affection, the bonds of love; the noose of illusion (Śiv. 67, 424); a figure drawn on the ground by the Brāhmaṇs at the burning of a Hindū corpse (El.).

e: adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. māyātītas ), one who has passed beyond illusion (see māyā), one who is not subject to illusion (Śiv. 1458).

m. source, root, origin, essence, substance; wealth, money, cash, means (El. máyih) (cf. māyā); capital, stock, principal; ferment, leaven; a kind of gruel given to an invalid or to one who is convalescent (cf. ana- māyĕ, p. 29b,…
fullMeaning: m. source, root, origin, essence, substance; wealth, money, cash, means (El. máyih) (cf. māyā); capital, stock, principal; ferment, leaven; a kind of gruel given to an invalid or to one who is convalescent (cf. ana- māyĕ, p. 29b, l. 49); paste (for fixing paper, etc.), glue (El. máyí, Gr.M.); glue, size (Gr.M.); grain (swelling, but not ripe) (L. 460, máyah). -sāvĕr - , m. (of a person) plenteousness of wealth; (of a thing or work) richness in essential attributes, greatness of intrinsic value; (of paper, etc.) the condition of being thoroughly covered with paste or size. Cf. māyā- sôwu, s.v. māyā.

e: adj. c.g. thick, solid, strong, substantial; rich, wealthy; fermented; (of paper) well covered with paste, sized, smooth (Gr.M.). Cf. māyĕ.

adj. c.g. deceitful, fraudulent; N. of a demon (Rām. 457).

m. taste, savour, relish, smack (K.Pr. 16, 255) (cf. nūna-mo, s.v. nūn); a titbit; delight, pleasure, enjoyment (Gr.M.; K. 25, 223, 648, 650, 716); jest, joke, fun, sport, amusement. --gaʦhȧni -- m. pl. inf. flavours to go, i.e.…
fullMeaning: m. taste, savour, relish, smack (K.Pr. 16, 255) (cf. nūna-mo, s.v. nūn); a titbit; delight, pleasure, enjoyment (Gr.M.; K. 25, 223, 648, 650, 716); jest, joke, fun, sport, amusement. --gaʦhȧni -- m. pl. inf. flavours to go, i.e. to exhibit apparent disgust (for something really longed for). --hyonu -- m.inf. to take flavour, to taste, to enjoy (lit. and fig.); to take pleasure, to enjoy oneself, to revel. --karȧni -- m. pl. inf. to enjoy oneself; to enjoy or amuse oneself (at the expense of), to make sport or fun (of), to laugh (at). --lagun -- m.inf. pleasure, enjoyment, to be experienced (K. 148, 220, 277). -motu - adj. (f. -müʦü -), enjoyment-mad, full of enjoyment (K. 255); giving enjoyment, ravishing, rapturous. -rostu adj. (f. -rüʦhü -), tasteless (El.). --ʦānun --- m.inf. to cause taste to enter, to give (one) a taste (of); to show (one) some sport or fun, to afford (one) enjoyment. --wuchun -- , m.inf. to test the taste (of), to see how (a thing) tastes; to show indifference (to something unpleasant). --yunu -- m.inf. enjoyment, flavour, or pleasure to be felt.

e: adj. c.g. tasty, savoury, tasteful, palatable, delicious (lit. and fig.).
adj. c.g. of, or relating to, a religion, or sect, etc. (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. mazākas ), taste, relish; wit, humour; (in Kāshmīrī) false comforting, consoling a person with promises which are not fulfilled; a practical joke (K.Pr. 125). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. disappointment to occur. --karun --…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. mazākas ), taste, relish; wit, humour; (in Kāshmīrī) false comforting, consoling a person with promises which are not fulfilled; a practical joke (K.Pr. 125). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. disappointment to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to console or conciliate with false promises. mazāka-wôlu - m. (f. -wājĕñ -), one who is accustomed to console or conciliate with false promises.

e: f. (sg. dat. māzüñü ), a kind of twig broom (Gr.Gr. 121).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. māzanôwu ), to cause (a person) to like (something previously disliked), to cause (a person) to acquire a taste (for).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. māzonu ), (of something previously not wished for, or disliked) to make (it) an object of desire, to acquire a taste for. māzonu-motu - perf. part. (f. māzüñü-müʦü -), become an object of desire. Cf. māzun.

m. a place of visitation; a Musalmān shrine; (amongst Musalmāns) a sepulchre, tomb, grave, a graveyard (L. 271). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to the tomb; hence, to become dead (used in imprecations, etc.). -bal - m. a Musalmān…
fullMeaning: m. a place of visitation; a Musalmān shrine; (amongst Musalmāns) a sepulchre, tomb, grave, a graveyard (L. 271). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to the tomb; hence, to become dead (used in imprecations, etc.). -bal - m. a Musalmān graveyard.

e: f. (sg. dat. māzarüʦü ), an apology; (in Kāshmīrī) words of welcome (to a guest on arrival), hospitality (K.Pr. 203); hospitable pressing to eat (at a feast, etc.) (Śiv. 1072).
n.ag. (f. māzavüñü ), one who has acquired a taste (for something not previously liked); one who cleans out dregs from the inside of a vessel.
adj. c.g. firm, fixed, fast, tight (Gr.M.); strong, stout.
f. (sg. dat.mazēṭhi ), madder, the plant and its dye (L. 344, majjit; 68, mazait = Rubia cordifolia or its substitute Geranium nepalense). Cf. maĩz; El. majíth or manjít, both m.

m. a place of manifestation, scene of a deed, a theatre, stage (El., K.Pr. 86); the object or manifestation (of divine vengeance, etc.); the breaking out of a deadly epidemic. --wŏthun -- m.inf. an epidemic to break out. --yunu…
fullMeaning: m. a place of manifestation, scene of a deed, a theatre, stage (El., K.Pr. 86); the object or manifestation (of divine vengeance, etc.); the breaking out of a deadly epidemic. --wŏthun -- m.inf. an epidemic to break out. --yunu -- m.inf., id.

e: adj. c.g. (as subst., f. mazharladiñ ), one who is afflicted by an epidemic disease.
m. the contents of a writing or letter, import, sense, tenour, purport (Rām. 842).
adj. c.g. one who consoles with promises which he does not fulfil, conciliating with false promises.
m. the man in charge of a Musalmān graveyard.

f. harm, injury, hurt, detriment. --tulüñü -- f.inf. (of a person) to become utterly exhausted or fatigued and incapable of doing more. --lagüñü -- f.inf. great exhaustion or fatigue to be experienced.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. môzu ; 2 p.p. māzōv ), to acquire a taste (for), to become addicted (to) (esp. with reference to something not previously desired) (Gr.Gr. 121); to clean out the inside of a vessel, to wipe out dregs. Cf. māzanun.…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. môzu ; 2 p.p. māzōv ), to acquire a taste (for), to become addicted (to) (esp. with reference to something not previously desired) (Gr.Gr. 121); to clean out the inside of a vessel, to wipe out dregs. e: see bŏh.
m. the cry of a cat, mewing, mew; cf. myauv. -brôru - m. (f. -brörü -), a mew-cat, a cat accustomed to mewing; a crying child (that mews like a cat).
see më̆ṭü.
see myūṭhu 2.
m. sweetness (of food, speech, voice, lit. or fig.; cf. atha-o, p. 59b, l. 40); taste (El.). Cf. myūṭhu 2.
m. (f. mēgiñü , q.v.), N. of a certain untouchable caste, the Mēgh or Mēg of the Panjāb hill-country. mēga-bāy - f. the wife of a Mēg.
f. a woman of the Mēg caste (see mēg) (but the wife of a Mēg is mēga-bāy).
or mihnath m. (also occasionally, as in Gr.M., f.) (sg. dat. mĕhanatas or, if f., mĕhanüʦü (Gr.M. 1836)), toil, exertion, labour (El., Gr.M., K.Pr. 142 (mĕhnatas, sg. dat.)).
adj. c.g. laborious, diligent, industrious, painstaking (Gr.M.).
m. a guest; a poor orphan (who is always somebody's guest) (K.Pr. 261).
or (El.) mahmāndörī f. hospitality. --karüñü -- f.inf. to show hospitality, to entertain (El.).
see maĩzi-rāth, s.v. maĩz.
m. a Major (the English word); (in Kāshmīrī) a superior officer, e.g. a head groom or master of the horse (H. x, 5, 12, 13).
see mēlun.

f. (sg. dat. mēkhi ), a nail, a pin of wood or iron; a peg, tent-peg; a stake, pile, post; a wedge, spike. --bagārüñü -- f.inf. after abusing and threatening (a person, esp. a woman) to award punishment, to add injury to insult.…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. mēkhi ), a nail, a pin of wood or iron; a peg, tent-peg; a stake, pile, post; a wedge, spike. --bagārüñü -- f.inf. after abusing and threatening (a person, esp. a woman) to award punishment, to add injury to insult. --diñü-- f.inf. to fasten, or hammer in, a nail, etc.

e: f. the ceremony of investing a youth with the brahmanical thread (El. mēkhla). --tārüñü -- f.inf. to carry out this investiture. mēkhali mahārāza - m. the hero of this investiture, the youth who is invested. -wôlu - - m. the…
fullMeaning: f. the ceremony of investing a youth with the brahmanical thread (El. mēkhla). --tārüñü -- f.inf. to carry out this investiture. mēkhali mahārāza - m. the hero of this investiture, the youth who is invested. -wôlu - - m. the particular youth (among his brothers in a family) who is to be so invested; the father or other guardian of the youth; a priest or other person worthy of performing the ceremony.

fullMeaning: adj. c.g. of or relating to a Mogul. --cāhy -- or --cāhi -- or --cāy -- f. a kind of tea (the drink). According to El. (s.v. chái) it is prepared as follows:--For every tōlā (half-ounce) of tea five cups of water are poured upon it in the bahugun or teapot. It is then boiled for half an hour, when more cold water is added, along with condiments and sugar, after which it is boiled for half an hour more; milk is then added. It is now ready for drinking. The colour is reddish.

f., i.q. muru 1, q.v., used in the following:-- murü barüñü f.inf. to put alms into the front skirt of a garment (cf. muru wahārun, s.v. muru 1). When any respected old man died in poverty it was formerly the custom for one of…
fullMeaning: f., i.q. muru 1, q.v., used in the following:-- murü barüñü f.inf. to put alms into the front skirt of a garment (cf. muru wahārun, s.v. muru 1). When any respected old man died in poverty it was formerly the custom for one of his children (esp. his youngest daughter-in-law) to hold out her skirt in this way, into which the relations of the deceased put contributions towards the funeral expenses, etc. --gaʦhüñü -- f.inf. the front of a garment to go, i.e. to be worn out or torn. --yiñü-- f.inf. loss to occur (as the result of some work involving great labour, and from which profit was expected, but which has received an unexpected check). muri bĕhun m.inf. to sit on (another's) front skirt, to sit close to a person (to see that he does his work properly). --bihith dörü khǖnzüñü -- f.inf. to sit close to a person and pluck his beard, i.e. under pretence of displaying affection to abuse a person by using gentle language.

e: f. the fine core, nucleus, or pith of a fruit, grain, or wood.
adj. (f. mūrü 1 ), husked (of grain), used --˚, as in aḍ-mūru, p. 11b, l. 22.

m. the front part of a man's or woman's long coat (the lower part of which hangs down, and can be lifted up like an apron to receive anything); a sleeve (El. múr), the width of sleeve or trousers at wrist or ankle (Gr.Gr. 19);…
fullMeaning: m. the front part of a man's or woman's long coat (the lower part of which hangs down, and can be lifted up like an apron to receive anything); a sleeve (El. múr), the width of sleeve or trousers at wrist or ankle (Gr.Gr. 19); see murü. --dārun -- m.inf. to hold up the front skirt of a coat (to receive, e.g. grain); met. to beg for alms, to ask for something (Rām. 1486). --wahārun -- - m.inf. to spread out the skirt; esp. to hold out the skirts (as ab.) for alms, but without asking for anything. This, in former times, was a custom in Kashmīr when some respected old man died in poverty. His children used then to collect contributions in this way to provide funds for the necessary funeral rites, etc. Cf. murü barüñü, s.v. murü, bel. muri-düji - f. a patch sewn on to the front of such a coat. -mã̄gay - f. very humble petitioning (indicated by holding the front skirt as ab.) (K.Pr. 174). -palav - m. the front of a coat, as ab. -ʦoṭu - adj. (f. -ʦüṭu -), (a coat) of which the front has been torn.

e: m. a jingling repetition of shuru, a child, as in shuri-muri, children, etc., i.e. a man's family, his household (Gr.M., K. 786).

f. (pl. nom. mūrĕ , not mōrĕ , Gr.Gr. 62), a small branch, a spray, a withe, a twig (i.q. mur, q.v.) (cf. atha-mūrü, p. 60a, l. 31; dönü-mūrü, p. 223b, l. 9; dö̃tan-mūrü, p. 258b, l. 35) (Gr.Gr. 20, 62; Rām. 1121. 1190, 1250; K.…

(cf. atha-mūrü, p. 60a, l. 31; dönü-mūrü, p. 223b, l. 9; dö̃tan-mūrü, p. 258b, l. 35) (Gr.Gr. 20, 62; Rām. 1121. 1190, 1250; K. 91). mūrĕn māz tulun m.inf. to raise the flesh with twigs, to flog a man with twigs on the bare flesh.

e: f. a charge of an offence brought by the guilty person against an innocent person. --karüñü -- f.inf. to bring such a charge.

or mūḍun , conj. 1 (1 p.p. mūru ), to shell or husk (grain, pulse, etc.) by rubbing between the hands, etc. (Gr.Gr. 19, 121, 127); to rub the skin (e.g. of the palm of the hand) gently with the tips of the fingers (to allay…

(f. mūrü-müʦü -), husked, rubbed, eaten, etc., as ab.

(f. musürü-müʦü -), unloosened, opened, etc., as ab.

cf. muṭhu), Cyperus longus, rotundus (El.).

m. a kind of vetch or pulse, Phaseolus aconitifolius, the mōṭh of India proper (Gr.Gr. mōṭh, 23; L. 330, 363, mothi; K.Pr. 119, 189; Rām. 1504). muṭhi-buzay - f. a conflagration reducing to ashes in a moment; cf. buzun. -dāl - m.…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of vetch or pulse, Phaseolus aconitifolius, the mōṭh of India proper (Gr.Gr. mōṭh, 23; L. 330, 363, mothi; K.Pr. 119, 189; Rām. 1504). muṭhi-buzay - f. a conflagration reducing to ashes in a moment; cf. buzun. -dāl - m. a pottage of this pulse. -koshu - m. the shell of this pulse. -mās - f. a woman who shows pretended affection (quasi, saying, 'I am your aunt'; cf. mās 3. Such is here looked upon as worth merely a single grain of this pulse). -mǖ̃thar - f. an old custom in Kashmīr schools, in which, when a boy begins to learn to write, this and other pulses, parched, are distributed amongst all the pupils of the school; cf. kara-mǖ̃thar (p. 466a, l. 2). -pholu - m. a single grain of this pulse (looked upon as representing no value). -phȧli-yāriz -- f. friendship (worth only) a single grain of this pulse; temporary and hypocritical friendship.

e: adj. (f. mū̃ṭhü ), dull, stupid, muddle-headed, lazy (Gr.Gr. 140); cf. mö̃ṭh. mū̃ṭhi-trọ̆pi - m. a kind of sewing, in which two edges of cloth are joined together.

[L. 462; YZ. 106 (untied), 165 (swept the hair off her face); Śiv. 26, 66, 207, 247, 990, 1399, 1646, 1702, 1725, 1747; Rām. 274 (tore off their garments), 523 (opened their eyes), 1135, 1466, 1618 (open a door), 1772 (opening the heart)]. muʦarôwu-motu - perf. part. (f. muʦaövü -müʦü -), i.q. muʦoru-motu, q.v., s.v. muʦarun.

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. muʦoru ), to loosen, untie, undo (a knot, bolt, bonds, and so on), to cause to open or be opened (Gr.Gr. 121; Gr.M.; YZ. 458; Śiv. 396, 520, 949, 1078, 1469, 1763, 1890; Rām. 141, 624, 842, 1344; K. 90, 160) (rag…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. muʦoru ), to loosen, untie, undo (a knot, bolt, bonds, and so on), to cause to open or be opened (Gr.Gr. 121; Gr.M.; YZ. 458; Śiv. 396, 520, 949, 1078, 1469, 1763, 1890; Rām. 141, 624, 842, 1344; K. 90, 160) (rag muʦarüñü, to open a vein, bleed (a person)); to unravel or explain a difficult or complicated statement or state of affairs, to disclose. ȧchi (or achĕ) muʦarañĕ, to open the eyes (Śiv. 168; Rām. 125; H. xii, 22); bar muʦarun, to open a door (Rām. 1569, 1637, 1639; K. 69, 73; H. viii, 3, 10; xii, 23); jigar muo, to open the liver, to open out one's heart and display bitter sorrow, divulge a secret, or the like (Rām. 263, 269; cf. sīna muo, Rām. 1235; H. vii, 21); lōl muʦarana yunu, love to be released, love to burst forth (K. 681, 857). Cf. musarun and muʦarāwun. muʦoru-motu - perf. part. (f. muʦürü-müʦü -), opened, etc., as ab. muʦaran-war - , - m. ravelling a string, untwisting a twisted string; met. causeless anger. muʦarana yunu m.inf. pass. to become untied, opened, etc.; to disclose some long-kept secret about oneself.

fullMeaning: m. a (person's) name (W. 110; L.V. 8; Śiv. 677, 1014, 1113, etc.; Rām. 394, 1655; K. 127, 215; YZ. 256; K.Pr. 260); cf. nāv 1. --ganḍȧni -- m. pl. inf. to bind names; hence (of a bard) to recite a poetical narrative (of events, or of heroes), to recite a literary work. --rōzȧni -- m. pl. inf. f. (sg. dat. nāmüñü ), (among Hindūs) N. of the vessel of wood or copper containing offerings and libations made in place of the śrāddha, or full memorial rite, in the name of a deceased child who has died before investment with…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. nāmüñü ), (among Hindūs) N. of the vessel of wood or copper containing offerings and libations made in place of the śrāddha, or full memorial rite, in the name of a deceased child who has died before investment with the sacred thread. Śrāvaṇa = July-August) at the bathing place of Kapāla-mōcana. --diñü -- f.inf. to make this offering.

e: f. a certain term in gambling. (One player holds in his fist an unknown number of cowries, and his opponent guesses how many will remain over (three, two, one, or none) after dividing the whole number by four. The game thus is on…
fullMeaning: f. a certain term in gambling. (One player holds in his fist an unknown number of cowries, and his opponent guesses how many will remain over (three, two, one, or none) after dividing the whole number by four. The game thus is on the lines of our 'odd and even'. If the whole number is exactly divisible by four, so that there is no remainder, the result is called nand.) nanda-pur - f. the name of this gambling game.

or nārud or nārad m. (in Hindū mythology) the N. of a divine Rishi (in Skt., ṛṣi) or Saint, regarded as one of the four sons of Brahmā, and one of the ten principal munis or rishis. He acted as a messenger between gods and men,…
fullMeaning: or nārud or nārad m. (in Hindū mythology) the N. of a divine Rishi (in Skt., ṛṣi) or Saint, regarded as one of the four sons of Brahmā, and one of the ten principal munis or rishis. He acted as a messenger between gods and men, was a friend of Krishna (Kṛṣṇa), a leader of the heavenly musicians, and the inventor of the vīṇā, or lute. In the story of Krishna he often appears as a kind of Tempter, leading on Kaṁsa and other evil people to further wickedness, so as to insure their destruction. He had a reputation for promoting quarrels by tale-bearing (false or true) (Śiv. 392, 631, 639, etc.; Rām. 590, 847, 943; K. 38, 296, 340, 358, 383, 387, 573, 584, 741, 896, 930-9, 1000); hence, anyone who makes quarrels, one who sets people at variance (esp. by tale-bearing, etc.).

fullMeaning: or nāsth f. (sg. dat. nāsti ), snuff (according to El. most of the snuff used in the Valley is imported from Peshāwar. (sg. dat. -chö̆zü ), craving for snuff (e.g. when a habitual snuff-taker is deprived of it). -ḍaba - m. a snuff-box. -düjü - f. a pocket handkerchief used by snuff-takers for wiping the nose. -goru - m. a snuff-maker or -seller. -gȧri-wān -- m. a snuff shop. -gọ̆ʦürü - f. a small bag for holding snuff, a snuff-bag. -khüñü - f. the mucus expelled by snuff. -mushikh - m. (sg. dat. mushikas ), a pinch of snuff (L. 464, nást mushk). -phĕkh - f. (sg. dat. -phĕki -), 'snuff-powder,' as much snuff as can be lifted up in the hollow of the bent fingers. -phuṭȧjȧ - f. a parcel of snuff (e.g. for use when travelling). -phuṭulu - m. a larger parcel of snuff than the foregoing. -phyoku - m., i.q. -phĕkh, ab. -phyoṭu - m. as much snuff as can be lifted on the ends of two or three fingers. -pūri - f. a packet of snuff. -shōda - m. a person addicted to snuff-taking, a slave to the habit. -shīshĕ - m. a glass jar for holding snuff.

fullMeaning: f. when the stigmas of the saffron flower have been collected, the remaining sun-dried flowers are beaten with sticks and winnowed. fullMeaning: or nīla-nāg - m. N. of a Nāga king or snake-deity (see nāg 2) (Śiv. 1169). It was by following his advice that Kashmīr is said to have been freed from Piśācas, and rendered habitable by men all the year round. Before that the country had been occupied by Piśācas for six months in each year. His habitation was close to the famous spring now called Nīla-nāg, near the village of Vērnāg, and is the traditional source of the river Vĕth or Jehlam (RT.Tr. II, 411). There is another small lake called by his name situated in a valley between two spurs descending from the Pīr Panʦāl range (ib. 474).

(f. -zīṭhü -), (of a garment) long-sleeved (cf. zēṭhĕn narĕn, a sign of respectability, K.Pr. 262). nari-nērē - adv. very near, close by (Rām. 248); cf. nyūru 3. -noru - adv. from sleeve to sleeve; hence, secretly, privately (esp. between two persons). -noru bōzun - ? m.inf. fullMeaning: m. a jar, a pitcher, a jug with a long neck (cf. ā̃cār-no, p. 9b, l. 47; māga-noṭu darun, p. 551b, l. 33) (Śiv. 1503, 1559, 1818; H. iii, 5, 9; xi, 13; K.Pr. 11, 12, 82, 155, 159, 160); an earthen- ware well-bucket (cf. nȧṭi-bāv, p. 146b, l. 27). nȧṭi-öri - f. a circular ring of grass-rope used for supporting a full jar on the head or on the ground, etc. -bĕha - m. a wooden or rope ring for supporting a full jar. -golu - m. the neck of a water-jar. -kāh - f. fullMeaning: m. m. the radial-like spokes of the large wheel of a spinning wheel (yẹ̆ndar, q.v.). This wheel consists of a large number of spokes issuing close together as radials from the hub. Two of these wheels are side by side on the same…
fullMeaning: m. the radial-like spokes of the large wheel of a spinning wheel (yẹ̆ndar, q.v.). This wheel consists of a large number of spokes issuing close together as radials from the hub. Two of these wheels are side by side on the same axle, and are further connected together by a string running alternately round the end of one spoke to the end of the corresponding spoke on the opposite wheel, and so back again, till all the spokes are connected each with its opposite number. The whole thus forms one broad wheel of which the circumference is formed by the numerous strings crossing from spoke to spoke. Round this circumference is passed the driving band, which, when the large wheel is revolved, turns the small wheel on which the thread is spun (cf. kônu 1) (Śiv. 1014).

fullMeaning: f. censure, denunciation, reproach, a rebuke; taunting; putting to shame (esp. on some public occasion), dishonouring (an honoured person, by reproaching him for former misdeeds) (Śiv. 1112; Rām. 683, 1038, 1062, 1154, 1778; YZ. 19, 371; K.Pr. 115, 119 (read pāma nai), 163, 250). --lagüñü -- f.inf. censure to be attached (to, dat.), to be blamed, to be publicly censured (Rām. 339, 1060). pāma daga f.pl. disclosing former misdeeds (up to now hidden) by public reproaches, public taunting. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to use public reproaches to another (in the course of abuse), to taunt publicly (W. 139, K.Pr. 107). --hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to be a victim of public reproaches or censure, to be publicly taunted. --pām -- f. mutual reproaches, mutual taunting. --rōzañĕ-- f. pl. inf. censures to remain to a person, a person (dat.) to get a bad name or an evil reputation (H. x, 3). -waturu - m. a flood of abusive taunts (K.Pr. 259, pāmatur). pāman lagun m.inf. to become subject to public taunts.

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. pambachas ), the nut of the lotus. It is eaten as a delicacy by both Hindūs and Musalmāns (El., L. 72, Śiv. 1801). According to L. 76, it is the lotus plant itself (Nelumbium speciosum) which is used medicinally as a nervine tonic. pambach-dĕl - m. the outer bark of the lotus nut. -gūji - f. the kernel of the lotus nut. -hūnu - m. the nucleus-shoot of the kernel of the lotus nut (cf. hūnu 2). -künḍü - f. (sg. dat. -kanjĕ -), the hard shell of the lotus nut. -māl - f. a garland made of lotus nuts.

m. the lotus (Nelumbium speciosum) (cf. lĕmbi-po, p. 524b, l. 21) (L. 72; W. 3; Śiv. 26, 44, 54, 57, 167, 180, 187, 189, etc.; Rām. 93, 186, 533, 548, 1095, 1494, 1632; K. 1, 59, 926-7, 1176; YZ. 96, 152; K.Pr. 138); a lotus-flower (Gr.M.). The lotus grows abundantly in the Kashmīr Valley. The seeds, stalks, and roots are eaten. It blooms in August and September. The nuts (pambuch) are regarded as a great delicacy. The stalks (nadoru) ripen in October. The broad leaves are used as plates (El.). The word is really a compound of pam and pōsh. Pam also takes the form pamb, q.v. pampōshĕ-bạrag - m. the lotus leaf. -düjü - f. a lake or lagoon full of lotuses in full bloom, -dal - m. the lotus leaf. -ḍal - m. a lake full of lotuses. -wöjü - f. a ring made of the hollowed pericarp of a lotus; a gold ring of similar shape. -wạthar - m. (sg. dat. wạtaras ), a lotus leaf.

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. parmānʦhanas ), the ceremony of the second entrance, i.e. of the first visit after marriage, or else the visit previous to cohabitation, of a newly-married couple to the bride's father's house (Śiv. 56, paramāʦhun; K.Pr. 167). According to El. (paramántsun) this word means 'the third day after marriage'. See L. 269 ff. parmānʦhan-bôgu - m. the present given to the bridegroom by the bride's parents, etc., on the occasion of this festival. -ḍuḍa - m. an uninvited guest who sponges at the feast of this festival at the house of the bride's father. -mahārĕñ - f. the bride on this occasion. -mahārāza - m. the bridegroom on this occasion.

(sg. dat. parmūzanas ), wiping off; esp. after making offerings to gods or demigods on certain Hindū festivals, the emptying of the remains in the vessels that had contained the offerings over the roots of some plants, on to a river bank, or other suitable place (cf. ḍulu-pu, p. 212b, l. 6).

or pārthī-pūzā - f. (among Hindūs) the worship of the Pārthiva-linga. These diminutive lingas are made of clay taken from the foot of the Taḵẖt hill. The usual number worshipped at one time are eleven, or 111, or 1,100. They are…
fullMeaning: or pārthī-pūzā - f. (among Hindūs) the worship of the Pārthiva-linga. These diminutive lingas are made of clay taken from the foot of the Taḵẖt hill. The usual number worshipped at one time are eleven, or 111, or 1,100. They are thrown into the river on the evening of the same day (see RT.Tr. ii, 128, note) (Śiv. 740, i.q. pārthiwa-pūzā, Śiv. 209).

m. (sg. abl. pāsa 1 ), watching, guarding; observance, consideration, attention to, regard, respect, sake, sense, deference (Śiv. 592, 1315, 1467, 1670, 1745). According to El. it is used with names of God, meaning 'for the sake…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. abl. pāsa 1 ), watching, guarding; observance, consideration, attention to, regard, respect, sake, sense, deference (Śiv. 592, 1315, 1467, 1670, 1745). According to El. it is used with names of God, meaning 'for the sake of'; so W. 97, pāsa, Śiv. 1257. --bōzun -- m.inf. to show respect (to), to treat with honour. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. respect to occur, respect to be achieved. --karun -- m.inf. to make respect, to cause a man to behave decently; to treat a person politely, to grant politely (Rām. 161). --pyonu -- m.inf. compassion to be shown (to a poor man in difficulties); politeness or patience to be shown (on the intercession of some honourable person). --wuchun -- m.inf. to bear patiently (another's fault). pāsa-wôlu - m. (f. -wājĕñ -), one who has many respectful adherents.

fullMeaning: m. a thatch, roof (of a house or boat), shingle, mat cover (of a boat) (cf. burza-po, p. 130b, l. 49; nar-po, p. 646a, l. 46; nāṭa-po, p. 660b, l. 15; nāwa-po, p. 666b, l. 16; potu po, s.v. potu; pĕʦi-po, s.v. pë̆ʦü) (El.; Gr.M.; L. 463, pash; 464, pachi (?); Śiv. 784, 1245; K.Pr. 156, 167). (f. pashë̆cü ), of, or belonging to, a thatch (K.Pr. 2). pashĕs khasun m.inf. to climb on to the roof (of a house); met. to become filled with haughtiness, to assume a lofty bearing.

(sg. dat. patharas or patharis ), a levelled area (such as the floor of a room, a courtyard of a house, or a levelled piece of ground near a house), bare ground (cf. dā̃-po, p. 230b, l. 43); the spreading or scattering here and there of things lying or thrown about on the ground (cf. pōshĕ-po, p. 779a, l. 12). pathȧri gaʦhun m.inf. to go on the level ground, i.e. to go by land (instead of by boat), to go afoot. --karȧni -- m. pl. inf. to make scatterings, to scatter about (e.g. to scatter hither and thither heaped up grain, and so to render it valueless). --wöñü -- adv. on, or all over, the floor or bare ground.

e: f. a level piece of ground, a plateau (cf. gŏgaji-pa, p. 279a, l. 21; and pathur) (L. 460, patri); the spreading or scattering about of things lying or fallen on the ground, the accumulation of such in a number of small heaps…

e: f. a small village, a hamlet, in āra-po, p. 41a, l. 48, q.v. (prob. the same as the preceding).
m. a village accountant, the official who keeps the village fiscal registers, a land steward (H. ix, 10). I.q. paṭwörī, q.v.

m. a kind of copper or bell- metal pot or pan with a wide mouth (the patīla of India), used for cooking. According to El. (s.vv. paitila and patila) it is a Musalmān vessel corresponding to the Hindū bahugun, q.v. It is used as a…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of copper or bell- metal pot or pan with a wide mouth (the patīla of India), used for cooking. According to El. (s.vv. paitila and patila) it is a Musalmān vessel corresponding to the Hindū bahugun, q.v. It is used as a teapot.

e: patimü , see patyumu.

f. a braid, or fillet, of hair, worn by women in a bow-shaped form on each side of the forehead, generally worn by prostitutes (El. paṭyini. According to El. it is worn by Paṇḍitānīs). pȧṭiñĕ thawañĕ f. pl. inf. to arrange hair…
fullMeaning: f. a braid, or fillet, of hair, worn by women in a bow-shaped form on each side of the forehead, generally worn by prostitutes (El. paṭyini. According to El. it is worn by Paṇḍitānīs). pȧṭiñĕ thawañĕ f. pl. inf. to arrange hair in this fashion.

e: adj. c.g. one who habitually wears hair braided in a bow-shape on each side of the forehead (see paṭiñ). This method of wearing the hair is principally adopted by dancers and prostitutes.
(spelling and gend.) Aconitum heterophyllum, i.q. nar-māda, p. 646b, l. 14, q.v. (L. 74).
f. (sg. dat. pativrati ), a devoted, faithful, and loyal wife (Śiv. 668; K. 1080, 1168).
f. a board with a handle, used by plasterers for consolidating or smoothing a plastered surface.

Cf. paṭākh, paṭösi, and pŏṭösi.

e: or pŏtolu m. a large doll (cf. kāwa- patolu, p. 495a, l. 30). Cf. pŏtüjü and pŏtulu.

f. a certain carpenter's tool used for carving patterns on a board. Cf. paṭöki, paṭākh, and pŏṭösi.

m. leaves of the Cinnamomum albiflorum (El.). Cf. pạtar 2.

f. (sg. dat. paʦüʦü ), trust, confidence, belief (in a person, etc.).
f. incompleteness, insufficiency, falling short of the desired result, or of the necessary quantity (for securing any result). Cf. pāʦun.
pö̃ʦh , see pānʦ.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. paʦhidārĕñ ), that in which one may have confidence, i.e. that which ultimately fulfils expectations (e.g. a cow bought when it is not in milk, but which in due course gives plentiful milk, or a piece of…

(as subst., f. paʦhidārĕñ ), that in which one may have confidence, i.e. that which ultimately fulfils expectations (e.g. a cow bought when it is not in milk, but which in due course gives plentiful milk, or a piece of land in which seed is sown, and which ultimately bears a fine crop).

e: f. hospitable reception (of a guest), hospitality.
f. hospitable reception (of a guest), hospitality, entertainment (Gr.M.). --karüñü -- f.inf. to entertain, to show hospitality (Gr.M.). pȧʦhilāzi - adv. hospitably.

(f. püʦü-müʦü -), one who is trusted, as ab. paʦan-wôlu - n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ -), one who trusts, as ab.; (when work to be done by another is delayed) one who is patient or forbearing in awaiting its accomplishment.

m. (El.), i.q. poṭu 2.

m. (sg. dat. pātakas ), going to hell, experiencing the tortures of hell; experiencing any evil-smelling and filthy place; suffering from any dangerous disease, trouble, or extreme poverty.

f. a plank over a water- channel (used like a bridge); a hanging shelf.

m. an official belonging to a village, whose duty it is to keep an account of the various crops reared by the villagers (El.; L. 400, 404, 426, 435). Cf. paṭhwöri.

adj. (pāṭivü ), made of silk, silken. Cf. pôṭu.

m. a foot, a leg, in khara-pāv karān, doing the legs of a centipede, i.e. in great haste (p. 407b, l. 8, q.v.).

f. a quarter, the fourth part of anything (El. páo; W. 105, pau); a certain weight, a quarter of a sēr, i.e. about twenty tōlās or half a pound (a sēr being about two pounds) (Śiv. 1828; K.Pr. 28, 201, 224); a span, twelve…
fullMeaning: f. a quarter, the fourth part of anything (El. páo; W. 105, pau); a certain weight, a quarter of a sēr, i.e. about twenty tōlās or half a pound (a sēr being about two pounds) (Śiv. 1828; K.Pr. 28, 201, 224); a span, twelve finger-breadths, the length between the point of the extended thumb and the point of the extended little finger (cf. atha-pāv, p. 61b, l. 4); something (e.g. a piece of cloth or a piece of land) measuring a span; a kind of wooden peg used for fastening the wooden beams distributed through a brick wall in order to strengthen it. pāv-nafrē , a quarter unit of cultivators in Kāshmīrī revenue terminology, i.e. a bachelor entitled to one and a half acres of irrigated land (L. 402, pao nafre). See naphar. pāwa-ganḍ - m. to fasten the pegs in the wooden beams, as ab. --pāv karüñü -- f.inf. to fix peg upon peg, to fix a number of pegs, as ab.

adj. c.g. pure, hallowed, holy (Gr.M. paritr).
or pāvürü f. surrounding on all sides, crowding (a person) in all directions (e.g. by a number of persons or, met., by calamities, etc.) (cf. āwürü-pü, p. 71b, l. 19); the being surrounded, as ab.

m. wind, moving air (Śiv. 983, 1825, 1869); the vital air, breath (L.V. 17, 25, 33, 37, 42; Śiv. 983, 1469, 1827, 1870; Rām. 9, 1659). --sandyā -- f. N. of a sacred bathing place in Kashmīr, sacred to the goddess Samdhyā (Śiv.…

e: m. purifying, purificatory, purifying from sin.

conj. 1 to cause to be felled (by a third party), to cause to be dropped (e.g. into a river or the like); to cause a loss (by a third party) in a business or the like (K.Pr. 87); to cause another to fall into prison or the like.…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 to cause to be felled (by a third party), to cause to be dropped (e.g. into a river or the like); to cause a loss (by a third party) in a business or the like (K.Pr. 87); to cause another to fall into prison or the like. yād po, to cause memory to fall, to cause a person to remember, to call to another's memory (Śiv. 73, 1884).

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. pôwu ), to cause to fall, to fell, to lay low, knock down (Gr.Gr. 23, 172; Śiv. 353, 1715; Rām. 340, 376, 707, 709, 1552; K. 693, 830; H. iii, 9; K.Pr. 201, 263); to cause to lie down, to cause to repose; to put…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. pôwu ), to cause to fall, to fell, to lay low, knock down (Gr.Gr. 23, 172; Śiv. 353, 1715; Rām. 340, 376, 707, 709, 1552; K. 693, 830; H. iii, 9; K.Pr. 201, 263); to cause to lie down, to cause to repose; to put down (on to or into anything) (cf. atha po, p. 61b, l. 43) (Śiv. 1711, 1875); to cause to fall, to bring into existence, to cause to come into existence (cf. bājar pāvüñü, p. 98a, l. 24; mal pāwun, p. 564a, l. 16 (Śiv. 28, 1758; K. 552-3); pushĕ po, p. 780a, l. 28; shĕkh po, s.v. shĕkh 2); to let drop, let fall; yād pāwun, to cause memory to fall, to call to (a person's) memory (Śiv. 1002, 1822, 1909; Rām. 1630; H. vi, 11); pathar po, to knock down to the ground, to fell (cf. p. 798b, l. 27) (Śiv. 1626) This verb is the causal form of pyonu, q.v. pôwu-motu - perf. part. (f. pövü-müʦü -), felled, knocked down. pövith thawun m.inf. to knock down and leave there, to bring low; to drop and abandon.

e: m. a small house, a (poor man's) cottage (cf. lari-po, p. 531b, l. 11); an abode (K.Pr. 54, 111). pāwȧrȧ-han - f. a small cottage, a tiny cot.
m. a sandal, a slipper (cf. jūgi-pi, p. 371b, l. 22).

m. water or any drinkable liquid, esp. milk (L.V. 54); (in Kāshmīrī) reviving (a dried up plant) by watering it (Śiv. 1863). --aʦun -- m.inf. (of a withered plant) revival by watering to enter, to be revived by watering; (of a…
fullMeaning: m. water or any drinkable liquid, esp. milk (L.V. 54); (in Kāshmīrī) reviving (a dried up plant) by watering it (Śiv. 1863). --aʦun -- m.inf. (of a withered plant) revival by watering to enter, to be revived by watering; (of a person weakened by illness) to convalesce (owing to the application of appropriate remedies). --phērun 1 -- m.inf. convalescence or revival to return, strength to come back (of a withered plant, a person weakened by illness, or the like). --phirawun 1 -- m.inf. to revive (a withered plant by means of watering, a person weakened by illness by means of proper medical treatment, and so on). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause revival to enter, to revive (a withered plant) by watering it; to give strength (to a person weakened by illness) by means of appropriate treatment.

e: m. a means, expedient, device, resource, plan, contrivance (for doing something successfully) (cf. bacan-po, p. 80b, l. 44; pakan po, p. 728b, l. 4; pōshĕn-po, p. 781b, l. 34) (Rām. 934, 1045, 1232, 1477, 1580, 1674; K. 87, 361,…
fullMeaning: m. a means, expedient, device, resource, plan, contrivance (for doing something successfully) (cf. bacan-po, p. 80b, l. 44; pakan po, p. 728b, l. 4; pōshĕn-po, p. 781b, l. 34) (Rām. 934, 1045, 1232, 1477, 1580, 1674; K. 87, 361, 570, 651, 756, 775, 802, 882, 895, 980; H. ix, 11). --karun -- m.inf. to make a device (for something), to contrive an expedient, to take measures (Śiv. 519, 1137). pāyĕ-boḍu - adj. (f. -büḍü -), possessing great resources, of great dignity, high and mighty (YZ. 25, 240, 543); cf. baḍi pāyĕ, p. 84b, l. 39. -rostu - adj. (f. -rüʦhü -), without expedient, without resource; (of some action or occupation) that for which the necessary means are wanting; (of a disease or the like) that for which no remedy is available. -sostu - adj. (f. -süʦhü -), possessing many expedients, having many resources, helpers, or the like; (of a disease or the like) that for which many remedies are available.

e: m. a foot, a foot-print (YZ. 40, 232, 407); a trace, mark, vestige, clue (cf. raga-pay, s.v. rag; rata-po, s.v. rath) (Śiv. 1601, 1700-1, 1729, 1863, 1885; Rām. 521; H. iii, 3); a sign, gesture, hint, intimation (as to the…
fullMeaning: m. a foot, a foot-print (YZ. 40, 232, 407); a trace, mark, vestige, clue (cf. raga-pay, s.v. rag; rata-po, s.v. rath) (Śiv. 1601, 1700-1, 1729, 1863, 1885; Rām. 521; H. iii, 3); a sign, gesture, hint, intimation (as to the whereabouts of something) (cf. nāma-po, p. 636b, l. 19; a person's address, the place where he lives (Gr.M., Rām. 1487)). Cf. pata 1. --anun -- m.inf. to bring a clue, search out a clue (to), get to the bottom (of a mystery or secret). --hyonu -- m.inf. to follow up a clue, to search out the entire truth (about something) (Śiv. 439). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out a clue, to find out all the facts after much trouble (cf. raga-pay kaḍun, s.v. rag). --phērun 2 -- m.inf. a clue to be discovered, information to come (about something hidden). --phirawun 2 -- m.inf. to give a person a clue, to give information about (some mystery or something hidden). --thawun -- m.inf. to watch, or attentively consider, a clue. payā-pay - adv. successively, one close upon another, close together (i.q. payham, q.v., s.v.). payĕs wātun m.inf. to arrive at the clue, to gain thorough knowledge (of something secret) (Śiv. 821, 937; Rām. 1478, causal). --wötith -- conj. part. used as adj. c.g. one who has become thoroughly acquainted with (another's secret). --wātawunu -- n.ag. (f. --wātavüñü --), id.

e: m. strength, durability, (of a human being) healthy longevity (Śiv. 196). pāyĕs pyonu m.inf. to come to one's senses (i.e. to abandon unprofitable or unworthy conduct and take to respectable life) (Śiv. 94, 315, 1298, 1722, 1751;…

fullMeaning: f. a fence, hedge, hedgerow (cf. kȧnḍi-pi, p. 455a, l. 32, which, however, is reported as masc.) (K.Pr. 156). --diñü -- f.inf. to put a fence (round a garden or field), to fence in. payĕ-kāṭh - m. the wood, small branches, or twigs, etc., used to form a fence. -mūrü - f. one of the twigs filling up the spaces between the main posts of a fence. -zanḍ - m. all the wood, twigs, etc., requisite for making a fence as collected together ready for use.

or pāyyuchu m. (f. pāyĕch-bāy - is his wife, see bel., while pāyĕchĕñ , q.v., is either a woman belonging to this class of outcaste Brāhmaṇs, or else a woman who supports herself by acting as one), a man (esp. a Brāhmaṇ) who…
fullMeaning: or pāyyuchu m. (f. pāyĕch-bāy - is his wife, see bel., while pāyĕchĕñ , q.v., is either a woman belonging to this class of outcaste Brāhmaṇs, or else a woman who supports herself by acting as one), a man (esp. a Brāhmaṇ) who supports himself by accepting funeral offerings and similar gifts, and who is in consequence outcasted. In India he is called a Mahābrāhmaṇa (a sarcastic title). --dyunu -- m. to make gifts to one of these men on the occasion of an obsequial ceremony (such as that held on the eleventh day after death). --khyonu -- - m.inf. (such a man) to eat the obsequial food on such an occasion. pāyĕch-bāy - f. the wife of such an outcaste Brāhmaṇ. -koṭu - m. the son of such a Brāhmaṇ. -küṭü f. his daughter. -kaṭh - m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas -), the son of such a Brāhmaṇ (when contempt is indicated). pāyĕchi-pôni - m. the conduct or occupation of such an outcaste Brāhmaṇ; similar vile conduct performed by any other person. -tônu - m. the occupation or livelihood of such a Brāhmaṇ; the conduct of such.

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. poyu ), to heat (a metal) red hot, to purify, refine, melt, or smelt (a precious metal) by heat, to scorch, torrify (cf. atha po, p. 62a, l. 1; buthu po, p. 142a, l. 8); to bake (earth), to make bricks, pottery,…

fullMeaning: or phuhüñü , conj. 1 [1 p.p. f. phühü or phuhü ; 2 p.p. f. phahyēyĕ or phuhyēyĕ . This verb is impersonal, the logical subject being put in the dative, thus phahi-y , there will be inward anger to thee, i.e. thou wilt be inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 203). In tenses capable of expressing gender they are always put into the feminine, thus phahān chĕ-s , there is inward anger to him, he is inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 182); phühüs , he was inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 215); the verbal noun or infinitive may be either masculine or feminine (Gr.Gr. 192). Thus phahun 2 (q.v.) or phahaña , inward anger, the former referring to the anger of a man, and the latter to that of a woman (Gr.Gr. 120). The causal of this verb is phuhanāwun, not phuharāwun (Gr.Gr. 174)]. Severe pain to be felt in some part of the body, to be painful, to ache (Gr.Gr. 188, 215, 248); inward wrath or hostility to be felt, secret anger to burn within one (against some one). --diñü -- (-) f.inf. by calumny or the like to urge on one who already has an inward anger against a person to still further anger; to add fuel to the flame of hostility. --lagüñü -- f.inf. inward wrath or hostility to be further increased (by calumny, opposition, or the like). --phahañadiña -- - f.inf. again and again to add fuel to the flame of a person's wrath or hostility.

e: adj. c.g. mixed up with, or full of, pounded chaff, etc. (of rice, etc., pounded in a husking mortar). See pŏyĕ.
adj. c.g. full of, or mixed up with, powdered chaff, etc. (cf. pŏyĕ).
f. a bamboo ladder; the cross-beam supporting a roof.
f. an anklet of gold or silver. pöyili-horu - m. a pair of anklets. -khōr - m. a single anklet.
or pözü 1 m. (sg. dat. pözüs , Rām. 93), a falcon, a hawk (W. 114, pāz; Rām. 93; K. 947; H. vi, 16; viii, 7; K.Pr. 65, 161, 167, 199). -wôlu - m. a falconer.

m. one who wears his clothes on the wrong parts of the body (e.g. wearing a shoulder-cloth on his head and so on), or who, wearing them in the right situations, puts them on wrongly, a sloven. Cf. probu 1.

m. (sg. dat. prabātas ), the early dawn (technically, a hour before sunrise), sunrise, day-break (according to El. morning from sunrise to nine o'clock) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 352, 1333, 1358, 1413, 1465, 1542, 1549, 1641, 1702; Rām. 1109;…
fullMeaning: m. e: f. (of dress) slovenliness, unkemptness, wearing the wrong clothes on the wrong parts of the body or the right clothes wrongly put on.
see prāṭun.

adj. c.g. chief, principal, preeminent, main, best, most eminent (Śiv. 1659, 1768); (as subst.) a chief person, a person of eminence (K. 24).
m. evening, nightfall, the first part of the night (Śiv. 1724).
m. N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa, in Skt. Pradyumna (K. 734, 736, 739, 745, 746, 789, 820).
m. moonshine (El. prágásh); met. beauty like that of the moon (YZ. 376).
f. (sg. dat. prahi ), love, affection, adoring love (L.V. 83, 105).

fullMeaning: m. possession by a demon (believed to cause fainting, madness, fury, fever, etc.) (cf. dŏda-po, p. 190a, l. 2). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. fury (as if due to possession by a demon) to arise (Rām. 1383). --karun -- m.inf. to enrage, fill with fury, cause delusion (from opposition, terror, seeing a ghost) (as though possessed by a demon). --pö̃than -- m. possession by a demon (inducing fever, delusion, miscarriage) of a baby or of a pregnant woman passing haunted places by night. prāha-hotu - adj. e: adj. (as subst., f. prāhaladiñ ), one who is afflicted by demoniacal possession.
f. in pyā-prahāray, see pyā.

e: see pray.

fullMeaning: m. fashion, manner, mode, kind, description (Gr.M., Śiv. 1577, K. 12); species (El.). prakāra adv. in (such-and-such) a manner (cf. ami po, p. 54b, l. 48; amiy po, p. 55a, l. 48) (Śiv. 955). praköri adv. in (such-and-such) a manner (cf. ami po, p. 54b, l. 49; amiy po, p. 55a, l. 49) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1050, K. 200); with the genitive of a personal or similar pronoun, it indicates cause, as in myöni po, because of me, on account of me.

e: m. the four outer walls of a house from ground to roof.
m. an introduction, preface (of a book or the like).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. prạkhaṭyōv ), to be or become manifest, appear, become visible, i.q. prakaṭun, q.v. prạkhaṭyō-mota - perf. part. (f. prạkhaṭyē-müʦa -dotbelow;), become manifest, that which has become exposed to view.

(f. prakrüʦü-hünzü -), of (so-and-so's) nature, bearing the same nature (as so-and-so, gen.) (Śiv. 1425).

e: f. the Skt. form of prakrath, q.v. -par - adj. c.g. devoted to (the true knowledge of) primal matter, one who is able to distinguish between primal matter and the Supreme Deity (Śiv. 20).

(f. prālabücü ), of, belonging to, connected with, or the result of, one's fate.

m. N. of a certain demon, in Skt. Pralamba (K. 251).

m. dissolution, destruction, annihilation (Rām. 1235); the destruction of the whole universe at the end of an age (Śiv. 203, 854); general destruction, any extensive devastation (Rām. 1601, K. 909). --gaʦhun -- , m.inf. utter…
fullMeaning: m. dissolution, destruction, annihilation (Rām. 1235); the destruction of the whole universe at the end of an age (Śiv. 203, 854); general destruction, any extensive devastation (Rām. 1601, K. 909). --gaʦhun -- , m.inf. utter destruction (e.g. in one moment, of one's entire possessions and family) to occur. pralayĕ-kāl - m. a time of general destruction (e.g. the time of a devastating conflagration, inundation, or the like).

e: m. a rule, sanction, standard, authority, judgment, opinion (either general or of a single person); proof, proof or arguments brought forward in a law case (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. abl. prāna 2 ), an onion, Allium sp. (cf. baḍa-po, p. 82b, l. 27; ganḍa-po, p. 239b, l. 18) (L. 72, 75, 346, 462; L.V. 89, 90, 101; YZ. 121). According to El. it is not eaten by Hindūs of the Valley. prāna-bagāra - m.…

m. a couch, a seat, throne (cf. pōshĕ-po, s.v. pōsh 1) (Gr.M.; Rām. 1147, 1713; K. 339, 924, 936, 1047, 1130; H. xii, 18); a bed (K.Pr. 154); the finial of a shrine (L. 460); cf. paryö̃kh. pranga-khūru - m. the leg of a bedstead.

fullMeaning: conj. 3 (2 p.p. pranyōv ), to be or become white; to become white, to become clean (of something washed); to become clear, to lose turbidity; to flow (El.). pranyō-motu - perf. part. (f. pranyē-müʦü -), become white; become clean, clear.

e: conj. 3 (2 p.p. prānyōv ), to be, or become, old, become worn out (Rām. 994). prānyō-motu - perf. part. (f. prānyē-müʦü -), become old; worn out.
m. (sg. dat. prapanʦas ), development, diffusion, amplification, expansion (Śiv. 1728); prolixity, diffuseness, copiousness (in style or composition).

fullMeaning: m. N. of an ancient Indian sage (in Skt., Pulastya), one of the mind-born sons of Brahmā. His son was Viśravas. Viśravas had one son, Vaiśravaṇa, by his wife Dēvavarṇinī, and by another wife, Kaikasī, three sons, Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, and Vibhīṣaṇa, and one daughter, Śūrpanakhā. Kaikasī was of demon (Rākṣasa) origin, and her children were all Rākṣasas. Of her three sons, Vibhīṣaṇa was pious. The others acted fully up to their demon origin. Their half-brother, Vaiśravaṇa, was also named Kubēra, and was the god of wealth. The above is the account given in the Sanskrit Rāmāyaṇa (VII; ii ff.), but in the Kāshmīrī Rāmāyaṇa (622 ff.) Pulastya is not the grandfather, but the father of all these, and all, including Vaiśravaṇa, are borne by Kaikasī. On the other hand, in 611 Vaiśravaṇa is referred to as Pulastya's grandson. In Rām. 622 the word is spelt Pulastē m.c.

fullMeaning: m. religious merit (acquired by the performance of religious actions) (Śiv. 1737); rectitude (El. pūn); solemn meals eaten during the first ten days after the death of an old and respected member of a Hindū family; see --ranun, bel. -dān - m. a religious or pious gift; making religious or pious gifts. --khyonu -- m.inf. to eat the solemn meals after a death, as ab. -pratāph - m.
