m. an arrangement in sets, series, or gradations of a number of things (e.g. plucking fruit, etc., as they ripen, set by set, what ripens first, first, and what ripens later, later); the arrangement in order (of precedence, or…
fullMeaning: m. an arrangement in sets, series, or gradations of a number of things (e.g. plucking fruit, etc., as they ripen, set by set, what ripens first, first, and what ripens later, later); the arrangement in order (of precedence, or rank) of a number of people (e.g. the allocation of seats at a dinner). For examples, see below. pūruku gen. (f. pūrücü ), of, or belonging to, a series (e.g. of collecting crops as they ripen, or the order of guests at a public meeting or at a dinner). Thus, gŏḍañiki pūrücü kapas, the cotton of the first series, i.e. the cotton which ripened first, and was first plucked; dŏyimi pūrücü kapas, the cotton which is next plucked, owing to its having ripened somewhat later; gŏḍañiki pūrücü sālarĕñ, a lady guest among those invited to sit down to eat in the first row.

fullMeaning: or (among Hindūs) sö interj., a contraction of söhib, Sir, used in polite address by a man to a man. It is the equivalent of the Hindī jī, and is appended as a kind of vocative suffix, with or without a preceding interjection, as in nārān sö, hē nārān sö, or he nārān juv sö, all equivalent to 'Nārān!' used respectfully, as if we should say 'Nārān, Sir!' (cf. kotu-sa, p. 484a, l. 41; ada-sö or ada-kyā-sö, yes, Sir, p. 13a, ll. 45, 50; āhan-sö, id., p. 18a, l. 5) (El. sa, sah; Gr.Gr. 96; Gr.M.; L. 279, sa) so ha-sa (p. 351b, l. 42) and ha-sö (ib.), hata-sa or hata-sö (p. 355b, l. 11), and hata sö-hē (ib., l. 12) (H. ii, 4, 9; x, 1, 2, 5, etc.; xii, 1, 10). e: or occasionally (e.g. K. 105, 369) san 2 or sanā (i.e. sana + a 3) adv. an interrogative particle indicating doubt, hesitation, anxiety or the like. It is usually added to another interrogative word. Sometimes sana (not sanā) is…
fullMeaning: or occasionally (e.g. K. 105, 369) san 2 or sanā (i.e. sana + a 3) adv. an interrogative particle indicating doubt, hesitation, anxiety or the like. It is usually added to another interrogative word. Sometimes sana (not sanā) is added to the verb of a sentence. Thus kyā-sanā khĕwān chuh (or chw-ā), (I wonder), is he eating; khĕwān chw-ā-sana is he really eating (Gr.Gr. 180). It will be observed that the interrogative particle ā (see ā 3) can be used with this word (cf. amā- kyā-so, p. 27a, l. 18; kar-sanā, p. 465a, l. 23; kati-so, p. 483b, l. 39; kotu-su, p. 484a, l. 43; kūtu-su, p. 485a, l. 16; kĕtha-so, p. 488a, l. 30) (L.V. 39, kyā-s˚; Śiv. 47 (kus-s˚), 1600 (id.); Rām. (kyāh-s˚, etc.) 78, 202, 221, 253, 596, 834, 1074, 1143k, 1306, 1348, 1366, 1391, 1408, 1421, 1492-3; K. (marinā-san, why should he not die) 105, 369; (kyāh-sana, etc.) 165, 213, 287, 328, 608, 919, 1134; YZ. 187).

fullMeaning: f. a N. of Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech and learning. Under this name (Skt. Śāradā) she is the patron goddess of Kashmīr. fullMeaning: or shūrpanakhā f. N. of a female demon, in Skt. Śūrpaṇakhā. She was sister of Rāvaṇa, and wished to marry Rāma. Rāma referred her to his brother Lakṣmaṇa, but he too refused her. fullMeaning: m. the confluence of two rivers (cf. sọ̆nu 1 and sand), used in the following compound:-- sŏnda-brörü - f. N. of one of the holiest of Kashmīr holy places, the sacred spring of the goddess Sandhyā, called in Sanskrit Trisaṁdhyā. It is said at certain periods in the early summer to flow intermittently, three times during the day, and three times during the night. It is situated in the Bring Pargana in the south-east of the Valley (RT. Tr. II, 469, Sundạbrạ̄r, El. Sundabrãr, Śiv. 1168).

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. sŏrzanas ), the final ceremony of the Śivarātri festival, beginning in Kashmīr on the 12th of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (February-March), lasting for five days, and ending on the first lunar day of the light half of the month, i.e. the day of the new moon. Cf. waguru. sŏrzan oku dŏh m. the first lunar day (i.e. the day of the new moon) of the light half of Phāgun on which the festival ends. -māwas - f. according to some, the festival begins on the 11th of the dark half of Phāgun, not the 12th. These call the day of the new moon by this name.

e: m. the iris, Iris nepalensis (El.; L. 75, 248; Rām. 397, 403, 648, 1018, 1091; YZ. 13, 96, 150). According to El. it is the great graveyard flower with the Musalmāns of the Valley and is of four species, yellow, white, red, and…
fullMeaning: m. the iris, Iris nepalensis (El.; L. 75, 248; Rām. 397, 403, 648, 1018, 1091; YZ. 13, 96, 150). According to El. it is the great graveyard flower with the Musalmāns of the Valley and is of four species, yellow, white, red, and blue. In Rām., however, it is always alluded to as a typically dark-coloured flower, in contrast, e.g., to the rose. The root of the red species is used as a remedy for amenorrhœa, and for noises in the ear. According to L. the plant is used medicinally as a stimulant and expectorant.

N. of a site in the Mạchipur Pargana of Kashmīr where volcanic phenomena are observed. At certain periods vapour issues from fissures in the ground. The Skt. name was Svayambhū. See RT.Tr. i, 34 (note). According to Stein (l.c.) the place is now called 'Sayam' (Śiv. 305, 1121, 1174, 1425). sŏyĕm-bū m. the Self-existent, a title of the Supreme Deity, esp. in the character of Brahmā, Vishnu, or (Śiv. 835) Shiwa (Śiva). sŏyĕm sō m. the name given in schools to the Śāradā character equivalent to the Nāgarī sva (in Kāshmīrī sŏ). It is the first syllable of the Skt. word svasti, which is part of the Skt. phrase ōṁ svasti ēkaṁ siddhaṁ, which is uttered before enunciating the alphabet (see JRAS., 1916, p. 681).

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. sīlis , abl. sēli ), N. of a game formerly played by boys in Kashmīr. It is said to be extinct for half a century. In it a peg or post to which a long rope is fastened, is firmly fixed in the ground. One boy holding the other end of the rope taut, runs round in a circle, while the others try to catch him. He wards them off by kicking. If any boy succeeds in catching him, the captor takes his place, and so on till each has had his turn. The winner is the boy who succeeds in making the greatest number of complete circles.

With an interrogative, tām gives a meaning of indefiniteness, as in kȧhi-ti, somehow or other, p. 388a, l. 2 (K. 1119); kar-to, at some time or other, p. 465a, l. 28; kati-to, somewhere, anywhere, p. 483b, l. 41; kotu-tu, id., p. 484a, l. 49; kūtu-tu, of some indefinite quantity, p. 485a, l. 18. In all these, the underlying idea is a doubtful interrogative, as we should say 'is so-and-so anywhere?' (Gr.Gr. 256; Gr.M.; L.V. 86; Śiv. 1725, 1861; Rām. 1417). Used by itself, as an adv. tām means 'for a short time', 'a little', as in 'rest a little'. Synonyms of this word are tāmath, tāñ, and tāñĕth, qq.v.

fullMeaning: adv. and postpos. as far as, up to, including (cf. az-to, p. 74a, l. 28; ȧzi-ti, id., l. 41; pagāh-to, p. 683a, l. 47) (Rām. 547); just then, in the meantime; indeed (to emphasize an expression), really, truly, completely; as a correlative to yāmath, etc. (as far, as long, as ----) so far, or so long (Rām. 538). Used by itself, as an adv., tāñĕth means 'for a short time', 'a little', as in 'rest a little'. With an interrogative, tānĕth gives a meaning of indefiniteness, as in kȧhi-tāñĕth, somehow or other, p. 388a, l. 5; kar-tāñĕth, at some time or other, p. 465a, l. 34. In such cases the underlying idea is a doubtful interrogation, as if we should say 'is so-and-so anywhere?' (Gr.Gr. 256). Synonyms of this word are tām, tāmath, and tāñ, qq.v.

m. N. of an ancient festival which still survives in the Marāz Pargana, in the south-east of the Valley, and which is held on the full moon of the month of Ṯs̱ithar (Skt. Caitra = March-April), and is celebrated by lighting…
fullMeaning: m. N. of an ancient festival which still survives in the Marāz Pargana, in the south-east of the Valley, and which is held on the full moon of the month of Ṯs̱ithar (Skt. Caitra = March-April), and is celebrated by lighting bonfires of grass and wood. The tradition is that in former days all the inhabitants of Kashmīr used to leave the country on the full moon of Öshid (Skt. Āśvina = September-October) and stay away for the winter. The festival is held to commemorate their return on the full moon of Ṯs̱ithar, i.e. on the beginning of spring. The bonfires are supposed to destroy the darkness of winter. --zālun -- m.inf. to celebrate this festival by kindling bonfires, and so destroying the winter darkness.

fullMeaning: adv. and conjnct. also, indeed, even, as in suh ti ʦah ti, he also, thou also (Gr.Gr. 255); tō-ti (Hindī tau bhī), even then, etc., see tōti; kari-ti, he will indeed make (Gr.Gr. 180; Gr.M.; W. 99, 153; L.V. 32, 48, 106; Śiv. 3, 21, 73, 119, 171, 211, 364, 498, 582, 622, 656 (tī m.c.), 704, and elsewhere; Rām. 166, 216, 236, 262, 295, etc.; K. 18, 20, 26, 48, 61, etc.; H. ii, 4; vi, 11; viii, 5, 8, etc.; K.Pr. 146). ti is also used as a conjnct. connecting plural words (ta 1, q.v., being used to connect singular words), as in mahanivi ti gupan ti āy, both the men and the cattle came (Gr.Gr. 255; W. 153; Śiv. 1776; H. iii, 8). ti na . . . ti na, neither . . . nor (W. 153). ti ta conjnct. and also (K. 611). ti ti 1 , that also (K. 582), see tih, but ti . . . ti 2, . . . , conjnct. both . . . and (H. x, 13; xii, 12). Added to an indefinite pronoun, it strongly emphasizes the indefiniteness, as in kã̄h ti, anyone even, anyone at all (p. 390a, l. 12; H. i, 5; vii, 23); kē̃h ti nā, nothing at all (L.V. 9, 11; so Śiv. 1072, 1476; Rām. 710, 1295, 1492; K. 78, 87, 97, etc.); kã̄ʦh ti nō sath, no substance at all (L.V. 41); kö̃h ti na khĕth, no harm at all (L.V. 77); so kã̄h ti (Rām. 164, 1497); kĕ˜h ti (H. viii, 9).

Cf. tŏṭh and ṭŏṭh. ṭŏṭi , m.pl. cotton-seeds (in quantity); (of a servant or the like) fatigue, weariness, worry (caused by being sent hither and thither, and never having any rest). -ã̄cār - 'worry-pickles', (to a servant or the like) worry caused by not being allowed to come and go (i.e. by being kept at his work, etc.). --anȧni -- m. pl. inf. to cause worry (to a servant, etc.) by constantly sending him hither and thither. -byôlu - m. a single cotton-seed as found amid cotton which has been extracted from the husk. -carkh - m. (sg. dat. -carkas -), an instrument for extracting the seeds from cotton, a cotton-carder. -honḍu hyuhu - m. conj 1 (1 p.p. trạsarôwa ), to cause to fear, terrify (by some terrifying spectacle) (Gr.Gr. 7). trạsarôwa-mota - perf. part. (f. trạsaröva-müʦa -), terrified, as ab.
card. (pl. dat. trasatatan ), seventy-three (Gr.Gr. 79).
ord. (f. trasatatima ), seventy-third (Gr.Gr. 79).
adj. (f. trasatatiña ), costing or worth seventy-three (rupees, etc.); earning seventy-three, as ab.

fullMeaning: f. an instrument for cutting, a knife, scissors (cf. jigar-to, p. 371b, l. 48; kalam-to, p. 439b, l. 47) (Rām. 1268, 1539); a piece cut off, a cutting. --hë̆ñü -- or --karüñü -- f.inf. to cut off the edges of anything (such as paper, cloth, or the like), to trim.

e: or trishākal adj. c.g. three-branched, having three segments (esp. of something such as a tree, which has ordinarily two branches, or as a walnut, which has ordinarily two segments) (K.Pr. 229, trĕhshákal).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. trasyōv ), to become afraid or alarmed (at some terrifying sight), to fear; cf. traʦun, and tarsun. trasyō-motu - perf. part. (f. trasyē-müʦü -), overwhelmed with fear, as ab.
(f. trasīra 2 , for 1, see s.v.), weighing three seers (of two pounds each); (m. or f.) a vessel or receptacle containing or measuring three seers.

e: f. (sg. dat. traṭi 2 , for 1, see trọ̆ṭu), lightning, a thunderbolt (cf. hĕnga-to (met.), p. 339a, l. 49; naba-to, p. 619a, l. 22; nȧbi-ti, ib., l. 34; nāra-to, p. 648a, l. 42; pā̃-to, p. 748a, l. 25; rūda-to, p. 826b, l. 11)…

(sg. dat. traṭi 2 , for 1, see trọ̆ṭu), lightning, a thunderbolt (cf. hĕnga-to (met.), p. 339a, l. 49; naba-to, p. 619a, l. 22; nȧbi-ti, ib., l. 34; nāra-to, p. 648a, l. 42; pā̃-to, p. 748a, l. 25; rūda-to, p. 826b, l. 11) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1558, Rām. 458, K. 110, K.Pr. 253); a meteorite (El.). e: adj. (f. tratöpa ), three times put in the sun, thrice spread out in the sun to dry (of damp grain or the like). Cf. tôpu and tāph.
adj. (traṭüpa ), for three parties, from three points of view, and so on, see ṭopu 3.
adj. (f. tratrüca ), measuring three trakhs (of six Kāshmīrī seers, see trakh 2); (m. or f.) a receptacle containing, or measuring, three trakhs.
adj. (f. tratröca ), measuring three trakhs as in the preceding; (m. or f.) an appliance for measuring this amount; (m. or f.) a receptacle containing, or measuring, this amount.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. trạʦarôwa ), to terrify, fill with fear, cause to be afraid (esp. by displaying some formidable spectacle) (Gr.Gr. 7). trạʦarôwa-mota - perf. part. (f. trạʦaröva-müʦa -), caused to be terrified.

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. troʦu ; 2 p.p. traʦyōv ), to fear, be afraid, terrified (esp. when caused by some formidable sight) (Gr.Gr. 226). Cf. trasun and tarsun. troʦu-motu - 1 p.p. (f. trüʦü-müʦü -), terrified, as ab. traʦyō-motu -…
fullMeaning: conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. troʦu ; 2 p.p. traʦyōv ), to fear, be afraid, terrified (esp. when caused by some formidable sight) (Gr.Gr. 226). Cf. trasun and tarsun. troʦu-motu - 1 p.p. (f. trüʦü-müʦü -), terrified, as ab. traʦyō-motu - 2 p.p. (f. traʦyē-müʦü -), terrified as ab. into a swoon.

e: in trāwa-trāv - m. (of some vessel) brimful (El. tráwa-tráwa; Śiv. 520, 1802).
f. the act of depositing (and leaving there), the act of abandoning (cf. tula-trāv, p. 1000a, l. 36). See trāwun.
m. leaving, letting go, abandoning; emission, pouring forth; scattering (cf. dȧli-ti, p. 212a, l. 3). This word is the abs. noun of trāwun (q.v.) in all its meanings.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trāwanôwu ), to cause to let go, or to cause to be let go (El.). Causal of trāwun (q.v.) in all its meanings (Śiv. 1849, cause to put forth; 1896, cause to abandon).
card. (pl. dat. trawanzāhan ), fifty-three (Gr.Gr. 78).
ord. (f. trawanzöhima ), fifty-third (Gr.Gr. 78).
see trawuhura.
n.ag. (f. trāwavüñü ), one who lets go, etc. (in all the meanings of the verb trāwun, q.v.) (cf. nār-to, an incendiary, p. 647a, l. 22) (Śiv. 861, betake oneself to (rest)).
adj. (f. trawöra ), having three covers, trebly wrapped up, trebly enclosed.
adj. (f. trawörashiña ), of, or belonging to, three years; three years old.
adj. (f. trawöṭa , sg. dat. trawācĕ ), having three joints, joined in three places. Cf. wôṭu.
or trĕwuh card. (pl. dat. tra(trĕ)wuhan ), twenty-three (Gr.Gr. 77).
adj. (f. trawarisha ), of three years, produced three years ago, three years old.

(f. -hünzü -), of, belonging to, produced on, or begun on the third lunar day.

e: f. the inner nature (of any person or thing) (Śiv. 1239, 1622); favouring, assistance, partizanship (cf. rāyĕ-trāyĕ, p. 854b, l. 25). --wuchüñü -- f.inf. to inspect the inner nature, to test the inmost character (of any person or…
fullMeaning: f. the inner nature (of any person or thing) (Śiv. 1239, 1622); favouring, assistance, partizanship (cf. rāyĕ-trāyĕ, p. 854b, l. 25). --wuchüñü -- f.inf. to inspect the inner nature, to test the inmost character (of any person or thing). trāyĕ tōlun m.inf. to weight out over and above the fixed amount (Śiv. 1476). Cf. tarawun.

e: i.q. trĕh 1, q.v., in the following:-- trayĕ-gŏn - m. the three qualities (Śiv. 237, 514; cf. trĕ-gŏn). -lūkh - m. the three worlds taken collectively (Śiv. 957); cf. trailūkh, trizagath. --lōʦan - m. he who has three eyes, N. of…
fullMeaning: i.q. trĕh 1, q.v., in the following:-- trayĕ-gŏn - m. the three qualities (Śiv. 237, 514; cf. trĕ-gŏn). -lūkh - m. the three worlds taken collectively (Śiv. 957); cf. trailūkh, trizagath. --lōʦan - m. he who has three eyes, N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1044), i.q. trilōʦan, q.v.

(f. tra(trĕ, tri)yimü (, )), third (Gr.Gr. 76; Śiv. 863, tri˚; Rām. trĕ˚, 84, 180, 381, 385, 466, 1051, 1139, 1151, 1205, 1259-60, 1277, 1564, 1716; K. tra˚, 1145-6; trĕ˚, 27; H. trĕ˚, viii, 7, 8; xii, 19; YZ. 14, 104; K.Pr. 70). trayimi or trȧyimi adv. for the third time.

e: m.pl. the three guṇas, qualities, or constituents of existing things, viz. goodness, passion, and darkness (see p. 857b, l. 35) (Śiv. 1643, Rām. 1774). See trayĕ-gŏn, s.v. trayĕ 3.
see tray.
see triy.

(for 2, see trēkyunu) f. a scale-weight for weighing one trakh (see trakh 2), a trakh-weight. Cf. the next.

adj. (f. trēkiñü 2 , for 1, see s.v.), of the weight or measure of one trakh (see trakh 2), (of some one thing) weighing a trakh; (of a vessel) having a contents of one measured trakh. Cf. trökyunu 2.

f. an apple (cf. ambȧri-ti, p. 27b, l. 5; batpurī-to, p. 145a, l. 32; khar-to, p. 407a, l. 36; nābȧdi-ti, p. 620a, l. 1; sil-to, p. 909a, l. 25 (L. 349)). trēla-kuji - or -kujü - f. a small apple-tree. -kulu - m. a kind of…

(or, according to some, m.) thirst (cf. achĕn-to, p. 9a, l. 17; kakav-to, p. 433a, l. 9; nūna-to, p. 641a, ll. 20, 25) (El. m.; Gr.Gr. 136, m.; Gr.M.; L.V. 37; K. 1092; K.Pr. 63); strong desire, greed, avidity, covetousness (Gr.M.); drinking-water (for quenching thirst) (cf. phŏṭi-ti or phȧṭi-ti, p. 715b, l. 43; shō̃ṭh-to, p. 899b, l. 34) (Śiv. 342; Rām. 235-6, 1174, 1393-5, 1439; K. 230, 702; H. viii, 7; K.Pr. 155); any liquid for drinking (Rām. 398); water poured in libations to ancestors (cf. pŏtra-to, p. 799b, l. 38); soil that will not hold irrigation water (L. 321); cf. trĕshnā. --lagüñü -- f.inf. thirst to be experienced, to be thirsty (with dat. of person thirsty) (El. m.inf.; K. 835; H. viii, 7). --wēsh -- f. thirst (a jingle of trēsh) (El., who makes the word m., but we should expect it to be f.). trēshĕ-hotu - adj. e: or (q.v.) trĕnaway card. emph. even all three (Gr.Gr. 85; Śiv. 64 (trash˚), 977, 1168 (dat. trĕshĕwȧni), 1529; K. 1031, trashĕway; K.Pr. 142).
card. emph. even all three (Gr.Gr. 85).

trĕyĕ , trĕyau , see trĕh 1 and tray.

m. a nominal coin now worth three times eight cowries, i.e. 24 cowries. Cf. bahāgañ and bahāgoñunu.
adj. (f. triböjü ), stupid, addle-painted, dull-witted.

e: m. a group of three, a triad, trio (Gr.Gr. 82). Cf. trakh 1 and trila.

see trakh 1.
m. (of a tree) having a triple stem ascending from one trunk, three stemmed; (of a pillar or the like) branching into three.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. triköshiladiñ ), one who fasts (religiously), or goes without food (owing to want, illness, or the like), for three days (see köshilad, p. 481a, l. 3).
card. thirty millions, three crores. There are said to be this number of gods (Śiv. 433, 635, 698, 719, 723, 1520; Rām. 68, 88, 1054).
m. a group of three, a triad, trio (Gr.Gr. 82). Cf. trica and trakh 1.
m. the Lord of the three worlds (Heaven, Earth, and Hell), a title of Shiv (Śiva) (i.q. trailōkyĕ-nāth, ab.) (Śiv. 387). Cf. trizagath.
m., id. (Śiv. 832). The Skt. form of this word is Trilōkêśvara.
m. He who has three eyes, a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 363, 976, 1345). Cf. trinētr.

e: m. He who possesses three eyes, a title of Shiv (Śiva) (the three eyes being respectively the sun, the moon, and fire) (Śiv. 153, 514). Cf. trilōʦan.
m. the figure '3', the written sign for the numeral three.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. trinyōv ), to be, or become, prosperous in having many sons, grandsons, etc., to be blessed with many descendants. trinyō-motu - perf. part. (trinyē-müʦü -), become prosperous (as ab.).
a medicine composed of the three myrobalans, Terminalia chebula, T. bellerica, and Phyllanthus emblica.

m. he who is the three Pushkaras (Pushkara, being the name of three different places of pilgrimage), a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Skt. tripuṣkara) (Śiv. 1172).

onomat. m. 'snap', 'crack' (cf. tras and trās 2), used in the following:-- tris gaʦhun m.inf. the sound caused by breaking, felling, or striking such things as a dried branch, a piece of wood, or the shoulder-blade to occur.…

'snap', 'crack' (cf. tras and trās 2), used in the following:-- tris gaʦhun m.inf. the sound caused by breaking, felling, or striking such things as a dried branch, a piece of wood, or the shoulder-blade to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to make this sound (e.g. by tearing a dried branch off a tree). --milawun -- m.inf. breaking, etc., with such a sound to occur.

e: f. the old N. of a sacred spring in Kashmīr, the modern Sŏnda-brörü (q.v., p. 918b, l. 32) (RT.Tr. 469, Śiv. 1496).

a woman, a female (as distinguished from a male of man or beast) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 957, 974, 1044, 1103, 1345, 1436, 1822; Rām. 624, 773, 848, 1151, 1238, 1575, 1767; K. 52, 273, 288, 435, 617, 986); a wife (El. tréí, trí; Śiv. 339,…
fullMeaning: a woman, a female (as distinguished from a male of man or beast) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 957, 974, 1044, 1103, 1345, 1436, 1822; Rām. 624, 773, 848, 1151, 1238, 1575, 1767; K. 52, 273, 288, 435, 617, 986); a wife (El. tréí, trí; Śiv. 339, 711, 1438; Rām. 81, 1260, 1641, 1643, 1652, 1686; K. 48, 744, 918, 946, 1107). triyĕ-bāv - m. woman's nature, womanhood (Śiv. 960, 1130; Rām. 629; K. 747, 1105); effeminacy. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to marry wives, i.e. to marry many wives, to have a large seraglio (K. 132). trī-warna - f. an individual of the woman kind, a woman (with all the characteristics of a woman) (Rām. 1051).

m. N. of a certain food-grain, buckwheat (cf. ʦṻna-tro, s.v. ʦṻn) (El. trúmba, Fagopyrum esculentum; L. 76, 330, 338, trumbá).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trŏmbowu ), to prick (with a needle); cf. trŏmbun. trŏmbowu-motu - perf. part. (f. trŏmbüvü-müʦü -), pricked (as ab.).

m. a needle-prick, used in the following:--trŏmbi dini m. pl. inf. to prick (holes, e.g. in the tough skin of a fruit). trŏmbi tārȧni m. pl. inf. to prick holes at a distance from each other in the skin of the egg-plant fruit or…
fullMeaning: m. a needle-prick, used in the following:--trŏmbi dini m. pl. inf. to prick (holes, e.g. in the tough skin of a fruit). trŏmbi tārȧni m. pl. inf. to prick holes at a distance from each other in the skin of the egg-plant fruit or similar fruit preparatory to cooking. Cf. trusu.

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. trọ̆mbu ), to prick with a needle; cf. trŏmbawun. trọ̆mbu-motu - perf. part. (f. trö̆mbü-müʦü -), pricked (with a needle).
f. a circle (of people). -- karüñü -- f.inf. to sit in a circle, to form a circle of seated persons.

or trömü f. a copper dish (used only by Musalmāns) out of which food is eaten (El. trām, 'it corresponds to the thāl of the Hindū'; H. iii, 1; viii, 3, 11); cf. thāl. trāmi-bata - m. (at wedding feasts or the like) the food…
fullMeaning: or trömü f. a copper dish (used only by Musalmāns) out of which food is eaten (El. trām, 'it corresponds to the thāl of the Hindū'; H. iii, 1; viii, 3, 11); cf. thāl. trāmi-bata - m. (at wedding feasts or the like) the food contained, or served, in copper vessels for the Musalmān guests.

e: m. a kind of pocket-cloth, a cloth (usually an old worn rag) in which various articles are knotted separately. Cf. trọ̆ngu.

m. a bundle or collection of rags (esp. bits of old worn-out clothes). Cf. trongu and zacĕ-tro, s.v. züṭü. trŏngi wālȧni m. pl. inf. to wear (clothes, etc.), to rags. --wasȧni -- m. pl. inf. (of clothes) to become very ragged, to…
fullMeaning: m. a bundle or collection of rags (esp. bits of old worn-out clothes). Cf. trongu and zacĕ-tro, s.v. züṭü. trŏngi wālȧni m. pl. inf. to wear (clothes, etc.), to rags. --wasȧni -- m. pl. inf. (of clothes) to become very ragged, to be a mere collection of rags.

e: m. a dark hole or chasm (in the ground); a dark recess or closet (in a house or the like) (cf. hēri-tro, p. 345b, l. 16); in daba-tronu, p. 181b, l. 32, tronu is apparently confounded with tryūnu, q.v.
adj. c.g. sewed, stitched (cf. barma-to, p. 123b, l. 15).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. trọ̆parôwa ), i.q. trọ̆parun, q.v. to cover tightly, obstruct, shut (Śiv. 1703). trọ̆parôwa-mota - perf. part. (f. trọ̆paröva-müʦa -), i.q. trọ̆poro-moto, s.v. trọ̆parun. trọ̆parövith thawun m.inf. i.q. trọ̆parith…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. trọ̆parôwa ), i.q. trọ̆parun, q.v. to cover tightly, obstruct, shut (Śiv. 1703). trọ̆parôwa-mota - perf. part. (f. trọ̆paröva-müʦa -), i.q. trọ̆poro-moto, s.v. trọ̆parun. trọ̆parövith thawun m.inf. i.q. trọ̆parith thawun, s.v. trọ̆parun.

e: trŏparun , or trupurun conj. 1. (1 p.p. trọ̆poro or trupuru ), to cover tightly, obstruct (e.g. by hanging a curtain over a window), to shut an orifice by covering it (cf. dārĕ trọ̆parȧna, p. 238a, ll. 44, 48; layĕ trọ̆parañĕ, p.…
fullMeaning: trŏparun , or trupurun conj. 1. (1 p.p. trọ̆poro or trupuru ), to cover tightly, obstruct (e.g. by hanging a curtain over a window), to shut an orifice by covering it (cf. dārĕ trọ̆parȧna, p. 238a, ll. 44, 48; layĕ trọ̆parañĕ, p. 542b, l. 40) (L.V. 101); to close tightly any opening (cf. ȧchi trọ̆parañĕ, p. 8b, l. 40) (Rām. 1769). Cf. trapun. trọ̆poro-moto - or trupuru- perf. part. (f. trọ̆pürü-müʦü - or trupurü- ), covered, shut tightly, as ab. trọ̆parith thawun m.inf. to shut up or cover tightly (a door, window, etc.).

e: m. sewing, stitching (cf. barma-to, p. 123b, l. 11; kanjĕ-to, p. 455b, l. 32; mū̃ṭhi-ti, p. 605a, l. 20; māwȧli-ti, p. 611b, l. 27). --dyunu -- m.inf. to sew, to stitch (with dat.). trŏpi kaḍȧni m. pl. inf. to sew in a particular…
fullMeaning: m. sewing, stitching (cf. barma-to, p. 123b, l. 11; kanjĕ-to, p. 455b, l. 32; mū̃ṭhi-ti, p. 605a, l. 20; māwȧli-ti, p. 611b, l. 27). --dyunu -- m.inf. to sew, to stitch (with dat.). trŏpi kaḍȧni m. pl. inf. to sew in a particular way, to quilt, sewing together two layers of cloth with cotton between.

e: f. N. of a certain medicinal plant (described as somewhat poisonous and having very bitter leaves).
f. a crowding together in a confined space, a cramming together, used --˚ lari-to, p. 531b, l. 13. Cf. trapun and the next.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. trōryōv ), (of a sore or wound) to dry up, form a scab (cf. krôru). trōryō-motu - perf. part. (f. trōryē-müʦü -), become dry, as ab.

or , m. hardness, harshness, roughness (esp. of something once soft and tender, but become dry) (cf. atha to, p. 63b, l. 12); irascibility of temper (cf. atha-to, as ab.); conjunctivitis, ophthalmia (El. trŏshĕr, trŏshur).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trọ̆shĕrôwĕ ), to make (something soft or tender) rough or hard (Gr.Gr. 7).

adj. (f. trö̆shü ), hard, rough (e.g. as wood or the like) (cf. aḍa-to, p. 12a, l. 26; atha-to, p. 63b, l. 10; tala-to, p. 996b, l. 7); passionate, irascible (esp. only so externally, but inwardly mild-tempered) (K.Pr. 216).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. trŏshyōv ), (of something soft or tender) to become rough, hard. trŏshyō-motu - perf. part. (f. trŏshyē-müʦü -), become rough or hard, as ab.
in lö̃ʦha-trö̃ʦh, p. 539b, l. 33, q.v.

or troṭu m. (sg. abl. traṭi 1 , for 2, see traṭh), a necklace of several strands, and adorned with moonshaped gold beads (cf. māla-to, p. 565a, l. 44; rachi-to, p. 824b, l. 10) (El. trauṭh, ṭruṭ; Śiv. 1557; Rām. 512; K. 85; H.…
fullMeaning: or troṭu m. (sg. abl. traṭi 1 , for 2, see traṭh), a necklace of several strands, and adorned with moonshaped gold beads (cf. māla-to, p. 565a, l. 44; rachi-to, p. 824b, l. 10) (El. trauṭh, ṭruṭ; Śiv. 1557; Rām. 512; K. 85; H. xii, 5; YZ. 374 (ṭroṭ)).

e: in trowa-nĕnd (L. 463, trowanind), f. the fourth and last weeding of a rice crop. Perhaps trowa is incorrect for trāwa; cf. trāwun. See nĕnd 2.

1 p.p. of trāwun, q.v. (f. trövü ), used --˚ in such compounds as atha-trôwu, free-handed, liberal (p. 63b, l. 14); dȧli-ti, loose-skirted, wasteful, extravagant, uneconomical (the skirt being used for holding things) (p. 211b,…
fullMeaning: 1 p.p. of trāwun, q.v. (f. trövü ), used --˚ in such compounds as atha-trôwu, free-handed, liberal (p. 63b, l. 14); dȧli-ti, loose-skirted, wasteful, extravagant, uneconomical (the skirt being used for holding things) (p. 211b, l. 50).

e: f. a footpath (for a single person to walk on). trŏyĕ trŏyĕ phērun m.inf. strolling about in lanes (without object, or for passing the time).
(spelling) m. balsam (Balsamina impatiens) (El.). Cf. tatūre, and (?) the preceding.
see trukun.
see trukun.
m. (sg. dat. trukas ), the act of crunching with the teeth (cf. trukun) (Gr.Gr. 122).

or tryukhu adj. (f. truchü or (Gr.Gr. 72) trichü ), quick, clever, ingenious, acute, sharp-witted, intelligent (El. truk; Gr.Gr. 30, 72, 140, tryukhu; Gr.M.; K.Pr. truk, 76, 146, 160, 216). Cf. tryukhu.
in trū̃khu dyunu m.inf. to stir up, instigate, stimulate (esp. to arouse or stir up again some anger that had subsided).

f. the act of crunching up hard food (such as grain) between the teeth, chewing, mastication (Gr.Gr. 120). trukiñĕ-pholu - m. 'crunch-grain', grām, pease, or other such hard grain that, when eaten, is crunched between the teeth.
m. the noise of chewing or gnawing hard or dry food, the sound of a crunch (cf. aḍa-tro, p. 12a, l. 23); cf. trukun and ṭukh. --truku -- m. crunching, a sound of repeated crunches.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. truku , f. trucü ; 2 p.p. trucyōv ), to crunch (something hard, such as grām or other grain) between the teeth, to chew, masticate (Gr.Gr. 120, 122); to gnaw or cut (like a rat) (cf. boru tro, p. 118a, l. 20); cf.…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. truku , f. trucü ; 2 p.p. trucyōv ), to crunch (something hard, such as grām or other grain) between the teeth, to chew, masticate (Gr.Gr. 120, 122); to gnaw or cut (like a rat) (cf. boru tro, p. 118a, l. 20); cf. ṭukun and truku. truku-motu - , perf. part. (f. trucü-müʦü -), crunched with the teeth, as ab.; gnawed or cut, as ab.

e: N. of a certain poisonous plant, Impatiens Roylei (L. 76). ? Cf. the next.
m. (sg. abl. trōli ), weariness, or exhaustion, caused by excessive exertion or labour.
m. a kind of lute with wire strings.
m. (sg. dat. trunāwartas ), 'the whirler of straws', N. of the Demon of the Whirlwind (in Skt. Tṛṇâvarta) who attempted to carry off Krushna (Kṛṣṇa), but was slain by him (K. 123, 180).
or trungu m. distress, harassment, persecution (caused by stinging language uttered by another). --dyunu -- m.inf. to provoke, irritate, re-arouse former anger.
see trū̃zu.
see tryūnu.
m. a panther (El. trúnts). Cf. trū̃zu.
(spelling and gend.) the planting of rice-seedlings (L. 463, trupai).
f. contentment, satisfaction (L.V. 12, Śiv. 1430). Cf. traphath.

m. the initial stage of fever (marked by chilly ague with a high temperature); cf. traph-tṻrun, p. 1029a, l. 18. --nīrith yunu -- m.inf. fever to be relieved by its 'coming out' (i.e. sweating, etc., produced by exercise).

m. a prick or pierce with a pointed instrument, such as a needle, skewer, a thorn, or the like; cf. trọ̆mbu. --dyunu -- m. to prick or pierce, as ab.; met. to use stinging language. --lagun -- m.inf. a prick, as ab., to be…
fullMeaning: m. a prick or pierce with a pointed instrument, such as a needle, skewer, a thorn, or the like; cf. trọ̆mbu. --dyunu -- m. to prick or pierce, as ab.; met. to use stinging language. --lagun -- m.inf. a prick, as ab., to be experienced, to be pierced or pricked.

e: card. (pl. dat. truwāhan ), thirteen (Gr.Gr. 76). Cf. trayōdashĕ.

(sg. dat. truwöshü or truvüshü ), the thirteenth lunar day of a lunar fortnight (cf. hērüʦü-tü, p. 351a, l. 4). truvüshü-hondü - gen. (f. -hünzü -), of, or belonging to, or born, or produced on this day (Śiv. 524).
m.pl. 'thirteens', used as a multiplicative with numerals above ten, as in kāh truwöhi akh hath ta tĕyĕtöjih, eleven thirteens are a hundred and forty-three (Gr.Gr. 86).
ord. (f. truwöhimü ), thirteenth (Gr.Gr. 76).
or truvüshü , see truwāh 2.

m. votive oblations made on behalf of a woman on the fourth day after delivery of a child. --khārun -- or --khasun -- m.inf. (if the woman is delicate or weak) a slight quartan feverish attack to come to her on this day.
m. a kind of panther (El. trúṅts, trúnts). It is believed to try to eat the moon, by jumping up towards whenever it sees it. Cf. trunzu.
see trĕh.
in likha-tryukhu, p. 518b, l. 12, and lyukhu-tryukhu, p. 543b, l. 41, qq.v.; cf. trukhu of which it is an alternative form (Gr.Gr. 30, 72, 140).

(sg. abl. trēli ), threefold, of three kinds (noted only in Śiv. 1844, abl. trēli, which is probably m.c. for trila, q.v.). trēli-karm - m. the threefold (class of) actions (all actions being either virtuous (Skt. puṇya), sinful…
fullMeaning: (sg. abl. trēli ), threefold, of three kinds (noted only in Śiv. 1844, abl. trēli, which is probably m.c. for trila, q.v.). trēli-karm - m. the threefold (class of) actions (all actions being either virtuous (Skt. puṇya), sinful (Skt. pāpa), or of mixed character (Skt. miśra)) (Śiv. 1844).

e: or trūnu m. (sg. dat. trīnis , abl. trēni ), the covering of a limb (such as a glove or stocking) (cf. atha-tro, p. 63b, l. 16; khŏra-tro, p. 409b, l. 35). In daba-tryūnu or -tronu (p. 181b, l. 32) the word seems to mean 'injury…
fullMeaning: or trūnu m. (sg. dat. trīnis , abl. trēni ), the covering of a limb (such as a glove or stocking) (cf. atha-tro, p. 63b, l. 16; khŏra-tro, p. 409b, l. 35). In daba-tryūnu or -tronu (p. 181b, l. 32) the word seems to mean 'injury to a limb'.

e: (ʦhã̄ ) m. according to El. (s.v. tsáṅ) this word means 'salt' (which is imported into Kashmīr from Ladakh and the Panjāb). The word is a corruption of the Ladakhī Tibetan tsha.
see ʦoṭu and ʦaṭun.
see ʦaṭun.
m. the upright post on the top of which swings a well-lever (cf. tōla-ʦo, p. 999b, l. 27).
in ʦaḍa-wôru - m. an earthenware vessel for milk or the like, the same as ʦoḍu, q.v., but smaller in size (Śiv. 1368, 1502).
f. need, requirement, necessity. --ʦalüñü -- f.inf. need to depart, competent provision to be secured, means for carrying out to become available.
(El. ts˚), see ʦhāḍanāwun.

f. a fringed woollen shawl, mantle, sheet (worn over the shoulders and back and reaching low) (cf. bŏṭa-ʦo, p. 128b, l. 26; kapar-ʦo, p. 463b, l. 42; pā̃-ʦo, p. 748a, l. 29; pȧṭi-ʦi, p. 789b, l. 33; rugöli-ʦi, p. 828b, l. 21;…
fullMeaning: f. a fringed woollen shawl, mantle, sheet (worn over the shoulders and back and reaching low) (cf. bŏṭa-ʦo, p. 128b, l. 26; kapar-ʦo, p. 463b, l. 42; pā̃-ʦo, p. 748a, l. 29; pȧṭi-ʦi, p. 789b, l. 33; rugöli-ʦi, p. 828b, l. 21; satara-ʦa, p. 947b, l. 27) (El. also, a veil; K.Pr. 126). --gilavüñü -- f.inf. 'to flourish the shawl', (of some invisible power) to grant suddenly or unexpectedly a favour (esp. suddenly and unexpectedly curing the sickness of an invalid). ʦādari-baṭa - m. a Brāhmaṇ or Paṇḍit who (even though placed in high authority) habitually wears only a woollen shawl (i.e. who is of a modest, unostentatious character). -jōr - m. a pair of shawls joined together, a double shawl (cf. jōr 1). -püṭü - f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ -), a narrow shawl (made of a single width of cloth). -shikhuru - m. (sg. dat. -shikharas -), a rag of a shawl, a dirty piece of an old worn out shawl. -züṭü - f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ -), a worn out ragged dirty old shawl. El. also gives tsádir-wádir (ʦādar-wādar), m. a shawl.

e: (El. ts˚), ʦáḍun (El. ts˚), see ʦhāḍun.
m. (sg. dat. ʦã̄ganas ), N. of a certain medicinal fruit. ʦã̄gan-kulu - m. the tree on which it grows.
m. suction, sucking (esp. of a juicy fruit or food) (cf. atha-ʦah, p. 63b, l. 27) (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunu -- m.inf. to suck (a juicy fruit, or the like), (of a baby) to suck (the breast).
f. (sg. dat. ʦahüña ), sucking, suction; sipping, tasting.
n.ag. (f. ʦahavüña ), one who sucks (cf. mȧchi ʦo, p. 547a, l. 30); one who sips, tastes.
in ʦȧhi ta ʦatajihi adv. very slowly, with difficulty and delay (u.w. vbs. of producing or the like).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦoho , f. ʦüshü ; 2 p.p. ʦashyōv , Gr.Gr. 225), to suck up, suck (cf. mȧchi ʦahüña, p. 547a, l. 26) (El. tsihun; Gr.Gr. 124, 210, 225; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 234); to sip, taste (El. tsáhun, tsuhun). ʦahan-wāri - adv. by…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦoho , f. ʦüshü ; 2 p.p. ʦashyōv , Gr.Gr. 225), to suck up, suck (cf. mȧchi ʦahüña, p. 547a, l. 26) (El. tsihun; Gr.Gr. 124, 210, 225; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 234); to sip, taste (El. tsáhun, tsuhun). ʦahan-wāri - adv. by gradual tastes, by a series of tiny sips or bites (u.w. vbs. of eating) (cf. wôru 9). -vēri - adv. for tasting, merely for tasting (not for eating) (used ˚--). ʦahith nyunu m.inf. to suck dry, to dry up (something juicy, by sucking, or by leaving in the sun, or by cooking, or the like).

e: (El. tsáí), see ʦhāy.
or ʦöl m. a garment (borrowed from Skt.) in the word kŏ-ʦail (Śiv. 750), p. 494a, l. 9, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. ʦaitanĕs ), consciousness, feeling, sensation (Śiv. 194, 1525); (in Śaiva mysticism) the Supreme Consciousness, the Supreme Experiencing Principle, a N. of the Supreme (L.V. 16; Śiv. 1043, 1406, 1415, 1515, 1545,…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. ʦaitanĕs ), consciousness, feeling, sensation (Śiv. 194, 1525); (in Śaiva mysticism) the Supreme Consciousness, the Supreme Experiencing Principle, a N. of the Supreme (L.V. 16; Śiv. 1043, 1406, 1415, 1515, 1545, 1548).

e: see ʦālun.

obl. form of ʦakh 1 and 2. Also used in the following:-- ʦaka-lār - f. speedy running (after a person), speedy pursuit. -pal - m. i.q. ʦŏka-pal, s.v. ʦọ̆ku, q.v. -tahörü - f. a funeral feast. -ʦürü - f. a very industrious woman…
fullMeaning: obl. form of ʦakh 1 and 2. Also used in the following:-- ʦaka-lār - f. speedy running (after a person), speedy pursuit. -pal - m. i.q. ʦŏka-pal, s.v. ʦọ̆ku, q.v. -tahörü - f. a funeral feast. -ʦürü - f. a very industrious woman (quasi, as busy as a sparrow, see ʦürü 4).

e: m. N. of an alluvial plateau below Vijabrôra, q.v. where there was once a famous temple dedicated to Viṣṇu Cakradhara (RT.Tr. II, 461); a wielder of a discus (cf. ʦakhar); hence, a N. of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (cf. Śiv. 710) or (Śiv.…
fullMeaning: m. N. of an alluvial plateau below Vijabrôra, q.v. where there was once a famous temple dedicated to Viṣṇu Cakradhara (RT.Tr. II, 461); a wielder of a discus (cf. ʦakhar); hence, a N. of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (cf. Śiv. 710) or (Śiv. 1161) Shiv (Śiva).

e: adj. c.g. wheel-shaped, circular and flat. Cf. ʦaküjü and ʦakul.
m. one who is in the habit of eating the savoury relish named ʦakh (q.v.).
(L. ts˚), see ʦakav.
m.pl. alarm (caused by apprehension of the recurrence of former injury); cf. ʦakȧṭa. --ʦānȧni -- m. pl. inf. to cause such alarm (esp. in threatening or scolding a child).
m.pl. in ʦakȧṭa ʦānȧni m.pl.inf. to intimidate (a child or the like, by scolding, punishment, or the like, so that he shrinks from another interview). Cf. ʦakar, and the next.
f. (sg. dat. ʦakaṭüña ), (from cold or the like) shrinking, withering, shrivelling.
f. (sg. dat. ʦakaṭi ), shrinking, withering, shrivelling (e.g. a limb from cold, or a flower, or leaf).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦakaṭyōv ), to shrink, shrivel, wither (e.g. from cold). ʦakaṭyō-mota - perf. part. (f. ʦakaṭyē-müʦa -), shrivelled, shrunken, as ab.
or ʦākav m. a certain bird, the ruddy sheldrake or Casarca rutila (L. 128 tsakáo).
m. (sg. dat. ʦakas ), the act of setting on fire, kindling, setting alight; N. of a certain greasy uncooked sweet relish eaten with food. ʦaka-khāv - m. one who is in the habit of eating this relish.

m. (sg. dat. ʦakas ), a round clod of earth with grass, etc., growing on it, a round lump of turf (suitable for building an embankment), peat (cf. ḍēmba-ʦo, p. 217b, l. 38; hili-ʦo, p. 331a, l. 10) (L. 62, Rām. 42). ʦaka-nāv - f.…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. ʦakas ), a round clod of earth with grass, etc., growing on it, a round lump of turf (suitable for building an embankment), peat (cf. ḍēmba-ʦo, p. 217b, l. 38; hili-ʦo, p. 331a, l. 10) (L. 62, Rām. 42). ʦaka-nāv - f. a barge for carrying peat or vegetable manure gathered from the Ḍal lake (K.Pr. 66).

e: m. (sg. dat. ʦākas ), a group of four, a four, a double pair (cf. dūra-ʦo, p. 239a, l. 4) (Gr.Gr. 83); used as a multiplicative, as in trih ʦākh bāh, three fours (are) twelve (cf. Gr.Gr. 86, W. 104); cf. ʦula. --pĕni -- m. pl.…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. ʦākas ), a group of four, a four, a double pair (cf. dūra-ʦo, p. 239a, l. 4) (Gr.Gr. 83); used as a multiplicative, as in trih ʦākh bāh, three fours (are) twelve (cf. Gr.Gr. 86, W. 104); cf. ʦula. --pĕni -- m. pl. inf. loving longing to befall a person, or to be experienced. ʦāka-wörü - f. a state barge with rowers seated before and behind the raised canopy for the passenger (El. tsákawár, m.; Śiv. 1363). Cf. contra, ʦhaṭa-wörü, p. 1062a, l. 26. ʦākhāh khanḍā m. a group of a little less than four, about four, four or so (Gr.Gr. 83).

thou enteredst, see aʦun (cf. K. 251, 323, 506, 600).

(El.; Rām. 309, 473, 785, 865, 917, 1377, 1453; K. 443). --karüñü --, f.inf. to be in, or fly into, a passion (Gr.M., K. 359). --yiñü -- f.inf. anger to come (to, dat.), anger to be felt (by, dat.), to be provoked (subject, dat.) (El.; Rām. 532, 551; K. 325, 441, 680; K.Pr. 115). ʦakhi gaʦhun m.inf. to go into anger, to become angry (K. 40, 163, 192, 233); -hotu - adj. (f. -hüʦü -), smitten by wrath, full of rage (H. vii, 14).

e: or (q.v.) ʦakr m. (sg. dat. ʦakras ), a wheel; a circle; a discus (the missile) (cf. ʦakadar) (Śiv. 710; Rām. 224; K. 59, 872, 881-2, 884, 1059); a circle of individuals, a group of individuals (L.V. 63); a wide extent of country…
fullMeaning: or (q.v.) ʦakr m. (sg. dat. ʦakras ), a wheel; a circle; a discus (the missile) (cf. ʦakadar) (Śiv. 710; Rām. 224; K. 59, 872, 881-2, 884, 1059); a circle of individuals, a group of individuals (L.V. 63); a wide extent of country extending from sea to sea; (in astrology) a particular part of a person's fate (e.g. löni-ʦi, the part of a woman's fate concerned with her marriage) (Rām. 421); (in mystic Śaivism) one of the seven circles or convolutions (Skt. cakra) along the spinal cord (Skt. suṣumnā) (see L.V. pp. 12 ff.) (Śiv. 1891). ʦakras phērun m.inf. to walk in a circle (e.g. round someone or something) (Śiv. 1221).

e: f. a feigned cough (e.g. to warn a thief, or to awake a sleeper) (Gr.Gr. 33, 37). Cf. ʦās.
m. a piece of dried plaster (that has fallen off a wall on drying).
f. anger (esp. that of a child or of a subordinate). --kaḍüñü -- f.inf. to vent such anger (on someone).
f. a potter's wheel. Cf. ʦakutodjutod.
adj. c.g. (of dish, bowl, or the like) possessing a circular, or ring, base.
or (q.v.) ʦakhar m. a circle (a corruption of Skt. cakra), used in the compound shailā-ʦakr, p. 880a, l. 38, q.v. See ʦakhar for other uses.
m. the shape of a discus, a mark resembling a discus (K. 397); as adj. c.g. wheel-shaped. See ʦakhar.

adj. c.g. (sg. dat. ʦakrawartas ), (as an epithet of a king) ruling a wide tract of country (extending from sea to sea, cf. ʦakhar), ruling as a universal monarch, ruling as an emperor (Rām. 1280; K. 5, ˚wart).
m. 'Lord of the discus' (cf. ʦakhar), a N. of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (cf. Śiv. 710); a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1179, 1221, 1508).

e: m. (sg. dat. ʦākatas ), circumambulation, going round, circuit; going round (someone or something) (keeping him or it on the right, as a token of reverence). --lagun -- m.inf. (instead of going by the direct route) to have to go…

e: f. (sg. dat. ʦāli ), the palm of the hand stretched out and hollowed (cf. atha-ʦo, p. 64a, l. 16; yë̆ḍü-ʦü, s.v. yĕḍ); the amount contained in such a palm, a handful of this nature (cf. ȧshi-ʦāla, p. 48a, l. 1; nūna-ʦāl, p. 641a,…

(sg. dat. ʦāli ), the palm of the hand stretched out and hollowed (cf. atha-ʦo, p. 64a, l. 16; yë̆ḍü-ʦü, s.v. yĕḍ); the amount contained in such a palm, a handful of this nature (cf. ȧshi-ʦāla, p. 48a, l. 1; nūna-ʦāl, p. 641a, l. 26; pã̄-ʦāl, p. 748a, l. 33) (Śiv. 662, 702, 1250, 1255, 1688; Rām. 1039).

e: f., in pötra-ʦāl (p. 804a, l. 29, and Rām. 612) and in yë̆ḍü-ʦāl, a form of indigestion, s.v. yĕḍ, qq.v.

(cf. ʦalun) in ʦala-lār - m. (lit.) running in flight (from someone); hence (in reading or the like) hastily running (through the matter), galloping through (a book, a recitation, or the like). -ʦitta - sg. voc. O restless mind!…
fullMeaning: (cf. ʦalun) in ʦala-lār - m. (lit.) running in flight (from someone); hence (in reading or the like) hastily running (through the matter), galloping through (a book, a recitation, or the like). -ʦitta - sg. voc. O restless mind! (L.V. 72).

e: adv. a particle used to emphasize a prohibitive negative. Thus ma gaʦh, do not go, but ʦala ma gaʦh, do not go on any account; so ʦala ma kar, do not do (it) at all. --bā -- adv. id., but used in addressing a male person of equal…
fullMeaning: adv. a particle used to emphasize a prohibitive negative. Thus ma gaʦh, do not go, but ʦala ma gaʦh, do not go on any account; so ʦala ma kar, do not do (it) at all. --bā -- adv. id., but used in addressing a male person of equal rank. --biñ -- adv. id., but used in addressing a female of equal, or superior, rank. --sö -- adv. id., but used in addressing an elder male, or a male of superior rank.

e: f. (sg. dat. ʦālüñü ), a small shovel, or spoon-like instrument, used for stirring up a fire (El. used in a kā̃gürü, or portable brazier; K.Pr. 129); anything of a similar shape (cf. pamba- ʦo, p. 733b, l. 37).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦalanôwu . This verb is one of the causals of ʦalun. The other is ʦạlarāwun, q.v., see Gr.Gr. 174), to cause to run away, to put to flight (Rām. 867, K. 999).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦạlarôwa . This verb, like ʦalanāwun, is a causal of ʦalun, see Gr.Gr. 174) to cause to run away, to put to flight (K. 1023).
n.ag. (f. ʦālavüñü ), one who bears, one who endures (Śiv. 1254).

fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦôlu , f. ʦöjü ; 2 p.p. ʦājyōv ), to bear, endure (cf. atha ʦo, p. 64a, l. 20) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 271, 419, 824, 1247, 1253, 1446, 1758; Rām. 196, 203, 218, 291, 617, 643, 1027, 1289, 1386, 1570, 1575, 1581, 1711; YZ. 60, 346; K.Pr. 239, 241). ʦālan-bāna - m. the habit, or nature, of endurance, endurance, patience, long-suffering. -wôlu - n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ -), one who bears or endures, resigned, long-suffering, unruffled by nature, imperturbable.

e: f. skin, hide, bark, rind (of man, beast, tree, fruit, or the like) (cf. hāpath-ʦo, p. 342b, l. 47; khar-ʦo, p. 407a, l. 38; nuñü ʦo, p. 641a, l. 47; potu ʦo, p. 788a, l. 45; shĕza-ʦo, p. 903b, l. 13; samūr-ʦ, p. 914a, l. 45;…
fullMeaning: f. skin, hide, bark, rind (of man, beast, tree, fruit, or the like) (cf. hāpath-ʦo, p. 342b, l. 47; khar-ʦo, p. 407a, l. 38; nuñü ʦo, p. 641a, l. 47; potu ʦo, p. 788a, l. 45; shĕza-ʦo, p. 903b, l. 13; samūr-ʦ, p. 914a, l. 45; sōra-ʦo, p. 931a, l. 23) (El.; Gr.Gr. 148; W. 111 ʦo˙m; Śiv. 166, 816, 894; Rām. 635; K.Pr. 217); according to El. the word also means 'volume'; cf. ʦarmun. --mã̄ḍi yiñü -- f.inf. the skin to be kneaded (p. 548b, l. 40), i.e. to become hardened, or toughened, by practice; hence, genl. to become hardened to heavy labour by continued practice. --phalüñü -- f.inf. the skin to become worn away (phalun 2) (esp. by helping to carry a heavy load or the like). ʦama-dȧji - (or -düjü -) f. (out of friendship or the like) telling or recounting a person's good qualities even when he is patently committing a fault; pretending a virtue when one has it not (cf. gāna-ʦamadüjü, p. 288a, l. 25); -ḍanḍ - m. bodily help, i.e. help given by a friend with some part of his body (such as his hands, feet, or back); -doru - adj. (f. -dürü -) (of anything animate or inanimate) hard-skinned, tough-skinned, hard-barked. -ʦürü - f. 'a skin-sparrow', i.e. a bat. ʦami āsun m.inf. 'to remain on the skin', i.e. the responsibility of carrying out (some duty) to lie (upon someone).

e: see aʦun.
ʦamadüjü , see col. a, l. 28.
m. something possessing a skin or bark; hence, the felled trunk of a tree from which the branches have been lopped (esp. when still retaining its bark).
adj. c.g. possessing a skin, as in nūna-ʦo, p. 641a, l. 28; esp. hard-skinned, tough-skinned.

f. (sg. dat. ʦāmüñü ), cheese (El. m., Gr.M. f.). ʦāmañĕ-(or ʦāmüñü-)mŏ̈nḍü -(-) f. a ball of cheese, an entire cheese, a cake of cheese (Gr.Gr. 75). -ṭīrü - f. a large mass of curds before making into cheese. -ʦakul - m. (sg.…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. ʦāmüñü ), cheese (El. m., Gr.M. f.). ʦāmañĕ-(or ʦāmüñü-)mŏ̈nḍü -(-) f. a ball of cheese, an entire cheese, a cake of cheese (Gr.Gr. 75). -ṭīrü - f. a large mass of curds before making into cheese. -ʦakul - m. (sg. dat. -ʦakalas -), a circular piece of cheese (prepared as a relish).

e: m. (his wife is ʦamarĕñ or ʦamar-bāy -), a worker in leather, currier, shoemaker, cobbler, harness-maker (El. tsamar, tsomor; Gr.Gr. 148; W. 111 ʦo˙mūr). -bāy - f. his wife.
in ʦamar-gāv - f. the Yak (Bos grunniens) (highly valued for its bushy tail, used as a fly-whisk); ʦamar-wôlu - m. a maker of fly-whisks (see ʦāmar).
m. the tail of the Bos grunniens (used over a god or a great person as a ceremonial fly-whisk) (L.V. 73; Śiv. 1175, 1515; K. 932, 985, 1132, 1151). See ʦamar.
see ʦamar.

adj. (f. ʦamarüva ), made of iron, iron (see ʦamura) (Rām. 631; H. xii, 16, 17, ʦamruwu; K.Pr. 190). ʦamaruwa kara ʦāpun m. to chew peas of iron; hence, met. to be occupied in some very difficult work (cf. H. as ab.). In H. xii,…
fullMeaning: adj. (f. ʦamarüva ), made of iron, iron (see ʦamura) (Rām. 631; H. xii, 16, 17, ʦamruwu; K.Pr. 190). ʦamaruwa kara ʦāpun m. to chew peas of iron; hence, met. to be occupied in some very difficult work (cf. H. as ab.). In H. xii, the word is explained by the pandit as 'leathern', but the meaning 'made of iron' is certainly the correct one. So also in K.Pr. 190. In the modern language it is confused with ʦam, leather.

e: conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦamaṭhyōv ) (of something naturally juicy) to dry up, wither (cf. ʦamun) (El. to wither, decay). ʦamaṭhyō-motu - perf. part. (f. ʦamaṭhyē-müʦü -), dried up, withered, as ab.
m. admiration, surprise; a show, spectacle, wonderful object (Śiv. 1777).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. ʦomu ), and conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦamyōv . The causal of this verb is ʦọ̆marāwun, q.v.) (of some liquid or juice in a green plant) to be reduced in amount (by drying, evaporation, boiling down, or the like) (cf. ras-mas…

(f. ʦümü-müʦü -), reduced (by cooking, evaporation, etc.), as ab. ʦamith gaʦhun m.inf. to become abashed or ashamed (owing to being tongue-tied); to be disgraced (in the eyes of respectable people by the circulation of evil reports). ʦamyō-motu - , perf. part. (f. ʦamyē-müʦü -), become reduced, as ab.; (of advice or the like) agreed to, adopted.

e: m. iron (this is a Burushaskī word, and in various forms is current over the whole Dard country. In Ksh. it is reported as an old word, now seldom used).
f. the odour of a cowhouse (arising from the mixture of fodder, cowdung, and urine). --wŏthüñü -- f.inf. such an odour to arise.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦānanôwu ), i.q. ʦānun, q.v., to cause to enter (Śiv. 126).
m. a garment (noted only in YZ. 234, 541). Cf. canda, a pocket.
in wȧniwȧni ʦandan , s.v. wanun 1, q.v.

or ʦandar m. (sg. dat. ʦạ(a)ndras ), the moon (cf. bāla-ʦo, p. 104a, l. 42; phal-ʦo, p. 692a, l. 18; punimü-ʦü, p. 741a, l. 40; yẹ̆ndar ta ʦo naʦun, s.v. yẹ̆ndar) (El. tsandar, the new moon, crescent-shaped moon; L.V. 9, 22, 109;…
fullMeaning: or ʦandar m. (sg. dat. ʦạ(a)ndras ), the moon (cf. bāla-ʦo, p. 104a, l. 42; phal-ʦo, p. 692a, l. 18; punimü-ʦü, p. 741a, l. 40; yẹ̆ndar ta ʦo naʦun, s.v. yẹ̆ndar) (El. tsandar, the new moon, crescent-shaped moon; L.V. 9, 22, 109; Rām. 406, 575, 1484, 1486, 1774; YZ. 34; K.Pr. 253); a moon-shaped ornament worn on the head (used esp. by children). ʦạndra-grohun - m. (sg. dat. -grahanas -), an eclipse of the moon. -hāl - m. a kind of paddy with a soft white grain. -kalā - f. a digit of the moon; the crescent of the moon immediately before or after the new moon (Śiv. 98 (N.P.), 1490). -kalādār - m. he who wears the crescent moon, i.e. who has it for his crest, a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 75). -kalapushu - m. a kind of round cap ornamented with moon-shaped pieces of gold, silver, etc. -shēkhar - m. he who has the moon for his crest, a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1586). -ṭöcü - f. a kind of child's cap ornamented as ab. -ʦṻḍ - m., i.q. -shēkhar, ab. (Śiv. 976, 1035, 1538, 1574); a N. of Vishnu (Śiv. 740). -wār - m. Monday (El. tsandarwár, Gr.M., W. 106 ʦandawār). Cf. sūmwar.

e: m. (sg. dat. ʦạndarakas ), one of the moon-shaped marks, or eyes, on the expanded tail of a peacock (cf. mōr-ʦo, p. 587b, l. 49).
f. 'The Furious', a N. of Durgā, the wife, or energic form, of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1515); a hasty, impetuous woman (L.V. 77).
f. (sg. dat. ʦȧnḍiki ), a meeting, assembly (esp. of gamblers or similar reprobates).

m. (sg. dat. ʦandanas ), sandal-wood (cf. rakh-ʦo, p. 830b, l. 15; rakta-ʦo, p. 831b, l. 34) (El.; L. 78 tsandum, probably a misprint; L.V. 42; Śiv. 973, 1080, 1155, 1613, 1902; Rām. 692, 739, 1080; K. 425-6, 528, 926, 976; K.Pr.…

(sg. dat. ʦandanas ), sandal-wood (cf. rakh-ʦo, p. 830b, l. 15; rakta-ʦo, p. 831b, l. 34) (El.; L. 78 tsandum, probably a misprint; L.V. 42; Śiv. 973, 1080, 1155, 1613, 1902; Rām. 692, 739, 1080; K. 425-6, 528, 926, 976; K.Pr. 159, 229). ʦandan-bura - m. the bark of the sandal tree (cf. bura 2); a powder made from a bark-like strip of sandal-wood (cf. bura 1). -dār - adj. c.g. bearing sandal-wood, i.e. sprinkled, or covered, with sandal-wood (YZ. 57, of a bed). -hār - m. a kind of necklace of three, five, or seven strands (the candra-hār of India, of which name this word is a corruption) (L. 262 chandanhár). -köjü - - f. a flat stone on which sandal-wood is ground to powder. -kwöjü - f., id. -küñü - f., id. -mỗkun - m. a small lump of sandal-wood used for being reduced to powder on a grinding stone.

m. a receiver of blows, i.e. an obstinate boy, or the like, who refuses to learn or obey orders, and is hence subject to frequent chastisement. Cf. ʦünḍü.

the internal malleolus (El. tsanun); the ankle (El. tsunun); a peach (the fruit) (cf. bŏṭa-ʦo, p. 138b, l. 38) (El. tsúnú, tsunun, Amygdalus Persica; W. 116 ʦunun; L. 348 tsunnan, 462, tsannan). ʦanȧna-ö̃ṭa - f. a peach-stone.…

m. fraud, deceit, deception, roguery, knavery (Gr.Gr. 124; Gr.M.; Śiv. 874; Rām. 944, 1417; K. 209, 1020; K.Pr. 218, 241); a clever device or expedient (Rām. 410, 585, 697, 988; K. 653, 1025; YZ. 172); a device (for accomplishing…
fullMeaning: m. fraud, deceit, deception, roguery, knavery (Gr.Gr. 124; Gr.M.; Śiv. 874; Rām. 944, 1417; K. 209, 1020; K.Pr. 218, 241); a clever device or expedient (Rām. 410, 585, 697, 988; K. 653, 1025; YZ. 172); a device (for accomplishing something), a machine (cf. gagar-ʦho, p. 280a, l. 12; pā̃-ʦho, p. 748a, l. 31 (f.); Rām. 44); (in a machine or tool, etc.) a pin, handle (for turning a wheel, or otherwise setting in action) (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 33) (Śiv. 1747, 1828, 1914). -boru - m. a door which by secret mechanism shuts itself so that it cannot be opened by one not in the secret. -tôru - m. a kind of bolt for fastening a pair of doors opening in the centre. ʦhala bala adv. by fraud and force, by trickery, by stratagem (K. 821). -ʦhidürü - f. fraud, knavery, trickery, imposture (cf. Hindī chal-chidr). -ʦhidrözü - f. fraudulent, or knavish, conduct (cf. ab.). -wôlu - n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ -), one who habitually deceives, a cheat (by nature or habit), a dishonest rogue. ʦhȧli bȧli adv. by fraud or force, by stratagem, by trickery (cf. tȧli bȧli ʦhȧli, p. 996a, l. 18); whether one wills or not (K.Pr. 111, 203).

e: f. a jump, leap, spring (El. tshál, running). --anüñü -- f.inf. to take a jump, make a leap (Śiv. 1528). --diñü -- f.inf. to give a jump, make a single leap (generally with the idea of leaping off something) (Śiv. 709; Rām. 562,…
fullMeaning: f. a jump, leap, spring (El. tshál, running). --anüñü -- f.inf. to take a jump, make a leap (Śiv. 1528). --diñü -- f.inf. to give a jump, make a single leap (generally with the idea of leaping off something) (Śiv. 709; Rām. 562, 745, 1408). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to take a leap, make a single jump (Rām. 561). --mārüñü -- f.inf. to leap, to jump over (Rām. 778). --niñü -- f.inf. to take a leap, make a single jump (Rām. 548). --tārüñü -- f.inf. to jump across (something) (Rām. 553, 555). ʦhāla diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give jumps, to leap about (e.g. as in pleasure or the like) (Śiv. 267, 660, 1680). --hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to take leaps, to go along leaping (Rām. 886). --mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to make many jumps, to jump over and over again, to progress in leaps, to leap along (Śiv. 528, 764, 820, 972, 1322, 1380, 1615; Rām. 820, 1097, 1328).

(f. ʦhünḍü-müʦü -, sg. dat. ʦhanjĕ-maʦĕ -), searched for, sought, etc., as ab.

(cf. bayĕ-ʦho, p. 148b, l. 23; kala-ʦho, p. 435b, l. 2; pŏhi-ʦhi, p. 648b, l. 7; par-ʦho, p. 751a, l. 23; shīna-ʦho, p. 885a, l. 11) (Rām. 206); a wind-storm genl. (cf. nāra-ʦho, p. 648b, l. 2) (Rām. 1610, nārañĕ ʦhaṭa = flaring flames). ʦhaṭa-rūd - m. a rainfall blown about by a violent wind-storm (and not falling straight down). -shīn - m. snow falling during a blizzard (i.e. blown about in violent whirls and not falling straight down). -wörü - f. a certain kind of small boat capable of withstanding violent wind-storms (El. tsáṭawãr, 'the smallest, lightest, and swiftest of all the boats used on the Kashmīr lakes. It is so light and small that it is not at all endangered by the prevalent wind-storms which are often very violent on the Wulur and other lakes. It has but one or two boatmen in it.' L. 381 tsatawar; Śiv. 1682, 1804). Cf. contra ʦāka-wörü, s.v. ʦākh.

e: f. (sg. dat. ʦhaṭi ), shaking up and down (as in shaking out a garment to drive out the dust); winnowing grain (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 64a, l. 8; potu-ʦhu, p. 788a, l. 32) (Gr.Gr. 126); cf. ʦhraṭh. --diñü -- f.inf. to give a winnowing…

(sg. dat. ʦhaṭi ), shaking up and down (as in shaking out a garment to drive out the dust); winnowing grain (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 64a, l. 8; potu-ʦhu, p. 788a, l. 32) (Gr.Gr. 126); cf. ʦhraṭh. --diñü -- f.inf. to give a winnowing (to); to examine something carefully in order to remove dirt, to pick, sift. --kaḍüñü -- f.inf. to shake out dust, etc., from anything. ʦhaṭa mārañĕ f. pl. inf. to bound up, fly up, bounce up, shoot up (cf. yāwanas ʦho māo, s.v. yāwun). --ta grāyĕ mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to move the body in a swaggering fashion, to strut swaggeringly, bridle (due to pride in wealth, etc.). ʦhaṭi baṭi nērun m.inf. to become dexterous, adroit, skilled, skilful.

(sg. dat. -hākas -), green vegetables similarly stewed. -ras - m. gravy extracted from meat by long cooking and flavoured only with a little salt and pepper (given to a sick person).

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. chạtaras , abl. chạtara , and so on, but pl. nom. chạthar ), an umbrella, esp. a large umbrella held over kings or a small silver umbrella put over the idol in a temple; a sort of umbrella made of flowers, etc., used at festivals (an ordinary umbrella is chạtȧrȧ, q.v.); (?) a certain pot-herb, Megacarpœa polyandra (L. 72, chattr). chạtara-būña - f. an umbrella plane-tree; hence, met. a woman with many children, grandchildren, and other relations. -gulu - m. N. of a well-known village in Lār (Lahara) Pargana, close to Rāmarādan, for which see RT.Tr. I, 114 (iii, 467 n.). -hāl - f. (sg. dat. -höjü -,, Gr.Gr. 69), a certain kind of rice with a soft white grain, which is very fruitful.

fullMeaning: or ʦhĕnnun , conj. 2 (1 p.p. ʦhyonu or ʦhyonnu ; f. ʦhë˘ñü or ʦhë˘ññü ; 2 p.p. ʦhĕñōv or ʦhĕññōv ), to be, or become, cut, cut off, severed (cf. khōr ʦho, p. 410a, l. 25) (Gr.Gr. 123, 204; L.V. 83); to be torn, split (Gr.Gr. 174, 204; Gr.M.; Rām. 749); to be cut off (e.g. the head in decapitation) (Rām. 471); (of thread or the like) to be cut, broken (El.); to be cut off, brought to an end (cf. mūl ʦhĕnȧni, p. 567a, l. 6; pankath ʦhĕnüñü, p. 741a, l. 22; pö̃th ʦhĕnüñü, p. 796b, l. 31; rūzi ʦhĕnun, to be cut off from one's livelihood, p. 858a, l. 35) (Śiv. 415, 1424; Rām. 768, 1052, 1340, 1749; K.Pr. 233); to become exhausted, or worn out (by a long journey, excessive labour, or the like) (Śiv. 589, 1001, 1770); to become separated, apart (Śiv. 1341, 1676, 1752, YZ. 83). ʦhyonu-motu - , perf. part. (f. ʦhë˘ñü-müʦü -), cut, torn, cut off, etc., as ab.; exhausted, as ab. The causal of this verb is ʦhĕñarāwun or ʦhĕnanāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).

e: or ʦhipal adj. c.g. (of something animate) in the habit of hiding, a skulker, stealthy, a lurker, one who lies in ambush; (of something inanimate) habitually hidden, seldom findable.

f. (sg. dat. ʦhĕpi ), remaining hidden, hiding, concealment of oneself; cf. ʦhiph. --diñü -- f.inf. to give concealment, to be or become hidden (cf. pānas ʦhĕpa dāwañĕ, p. 263a, l. 7, Śiv. 1756; dēv ʦhĕpa diwanövin, p. 263b, l.…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. ʦhĕpi ), remaining hidden, hiding, concealment of oneself; cf. ʦhiph. --diñü -- f.inf. to give concealment, to be or become hidden (cf. pānas ʦhĕpa dāwañĕ, p. 263a, l. 7, Śiv. 1756; dēv ʦhĕpa diwanövin, p. 263b, l. 39, Śiv. 123; both with causal meanings) (Śiv. 913; Rām. 1007, 1089, 1273). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to take concealment, (esp. of an inanimate object) to become closely hidden. -- ʦhyunu ta grāy -- m. (in order to puzzle or deceive another) hiding and revealing oneself alternately. ʦhĕpa-chörü - f. a certain children's game, a kind of blind man's buff (in which the blindfolded player has to find another who is hidden. When he succeeds, the rôles are reversed) (Śiv. 1374, ʦhĕpa-ʦh örü); cf. chörü. --dyunu --- m.inf. to hide oneself, conceal oneself (K. 600). -ʦhĕph - f. hiding oneself (wandering from one place of concealment to another) (Rām. 1426). ʦhĕpi adv. secretly, in hiding, hidden (K. 244). For ʦhĕpi ʦhĕpi, see ʦhĕpun.

fullMeaning: conj. 3, to hide oneself, conceal oneself (noted only in the following forms):--ʦhĕpi ʦhĕpi freq. part., hiding oneself frequently, or in various places; hence, as subst. f. (in this sense also ʦhĕpi ʦhĕpi ), the children's game of hide and seek (K. 220). ʦhĕpith conj. part. used as adj. c.g. hidden, concealed, secret (L.V. 60). Cf. ʦhĕph.

e: (cf. ʦhĕwun and ʦhĕzun), adj. c.g. extinguished, quenched (YZ. 515, of sorrow). Usually found in the following:-- ʦhĕta gōmotu , perf. part. (f. --gömüʦü --), (of fire or the like) become extinguished, quenched (H. xii, 23; YZ.…
fullMeaning: (cf. ʦhĕwun and ʦhĕzun), adj. c.g. extinguished, quenched (YZ. 515, of sorrow). Usually found in the following:-- ʦhĕta gōmotu , perf. part. (f. --gömüʦü --), (of fire or the like) become extinguished, quenched (H. xii, 23; YZ. 524); (of a person) extinguished, i.e. famished with hunger, starving; (of a period of time) elapsed, wiped off (YZ. 7). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of fire) to become quenched, extinguished (cf. nār ʦho go, p. 647a, l. 24) (Rām. 58, 1028, 1784; YZ. 148). --karun -- m.inf. to quench, extinguish (El. tseta k˚; Śiv. 122, 417; Rām. 731). -kāyuru - m. kāyuru, or wood of the Himalayan blue pine (p. 501a, l. 50), a fire of which is not lasting, but quickly goes out (see K.Pr. 101); any wood with similar properties.

e: f. (sg. dat. ʦhẹ̆ṭarüña ), rendering impure, causing impurity to occur.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆ṭarôwa ), i.q. ʦhẹ̆ṭarun, q.v. ʦhẹ̆ṭarôwa-mota - perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆ṭaröva-müʦa -), i.q.ʦhẹ̆ṭoro-moto, s.v. ʦhẹ̆ṭarun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆ṭoro ), to render impure, to cause something previously pure to become impure, to defile (cf. ös ʦho, p. 46b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 7, K. 136); met. to render (pure food or the like) impure (by putting it into the…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆ṭoro ), to render impure, to cause something previously pure to become impure, to defile (cf. ös ʦho, p. 46b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 7, K. 136); met. to render (pure food or the like) impure (by putting it into the mouth and eating it). ʦhẹ̆ṭoro-moto - perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆ṭürü-müʦü -), rendered impure (as ab.).

e: m. (sg. dat. ʦhĕṭas ), food fallen from the dish on to the ground at the time of eating, remnants of food, leavings of a meal, orts; cf. ʦhyoṭu. --sīrü -- f. the portion of the lump of cotton-wool left over in the fingers on the…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. ʦhĕṭas ), food fallen from the dish on to the ground at the time of eating, remnants of food, leavings of a meal, orts; cf. ʦhyoṭu. --sīrü -- f. the portion of the lump of cotton-wool left over in the fingers on the conclusion of spinning (see sīrü 2). --tulu -- m. the leavings of grass- fodder after a cow, or the like, has been fed. ʦhĕṭa-pholu - m. a grain of cooked rice or the like thrown from or fallen from the dish on to the ground at the time of eating.

e: f. (of something previously pure), the condition of being, or having become, impure or unclean (Gr.Gr. 142, spelt ˚yārüz).
adj. (f. ʦhĕṭiyārĕñ ), one who deals in impure or unclean food, a seller, or maker of such; one whose conduct is impure or unclean.
f. the condition of being impure or unclean (Gr.Gr. 142).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhĕṭyōv ), to become impure, to become unclean, to become refuse and untouchable (Rām. 1049). ʦhĕṭyō-motu - perf. part. (f. ʦhĕṭyē-müʦü -), become impure, etc., as ab.
m. (of fire) the being on the point of being extinguished, the being nearly out.
f. (of rain or the like) cessation (cf. rūda-ʦho, p. 826b, l. 16). ʦhĕviñĕn adv. at the time of such cessation (cf. rūda-ʦho, p. 826b, l. 18).
f. (sg. dat. ʦhẹ̆warüña ), the act of extinguishing (a fire or the like) (cf. nāra-ʦho, p. 648b, l. 7); allaying (rage or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹwarôwa ), i.q. ʦhẹ̆warun, ab., q.v. (cf. nār ʦho, p. 547a, l. 28). ʦhẹ̆warôwa-mota - perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆waröva-müʦa -), i.q. ʦhẹ̆woro-moto, ab., q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆woro ), to extinguish (a fire, conflagration, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 7); to allay, appease (rage, etc.), quench (thirst), etc. (Gr.M.). ʦhẹ̆woro-moto - perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆vürü-müʦü -), extinguished (by…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆woro ), to extinguish (a fire, conflagration, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 7); to allay, appease (rage, etc.), quench (thirst), etc. (Gr.M.). ʦhẹ̆woro-moto - perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆vürü-müʦü -), extinguished (by someone), as ab.; appeased (by someone), as ab.

e: m. (of rain or the like) cessation (cf. rūda-ʦho, p. 826b, l. 21). ʦhĕwawạñĕn adv. at the time of cessation (cf. p. 826b, l. 23).

f. the being extinguished, extinguishment (cf. ʦnāra-ho, p. 648b, l. 11); (of rage, hunger, thirst, or the like) allayment, appeasement, abatement, cessation (cf. dah-ʦha, p. 198a, l. 16; daha-ʦha, p. 198b, l. 28; rūda-ʦho, p.…
fullMeaning: f. the being extinguished, extinguishment (cf. ʦnāra-ho, p. 648b, l. 11); (of rage, hunger, thirst, or the like) allayment, appeasement, abatement, cessation (cf. dah-ʦha, p. 198a, l. 16; daha-ʦha, p. 198b, l. 28; rūda-ʦho, p. 826b, l. 24; tapa-ʦho, p. 1014b, l. 10).

e: conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhĕvyōv ), (of fire) to be extinguished (cf. nār ʦho, p. 647a, l. 25); (of rage or the like) to be allayed, appeased; cf. ʦhĕta and ʦhĕzun. ʦhĕvyō-motu - perf. part. (f. ʦhĕvyē-müʦü -), extinguished; allayed.

f. a kind of thatching grass (Śiv. 338). ʦhĕyĕ-ḍēmb - m. an artificial or floating island on which this grass grows spontaneously. -goru - m. a professional thatcher. -horu - m. a long thin strip of wood (cf. hürü 1, of which…
fullMeaning: f. a kind of thatching grass (Śiv. 338). ʦhĕyĕ-ḍēmb - m. an artificial or floating island on which this grass grows spontaneously. -goru - m. a professional thatcher. -horu - m. a long thin strip of wood (cf. hürü 1, of which this is a masculine form), used in the tying of a thatched roof. -kān - m. an arrow made from a stem of this grass. -lürü - f. a thatched house (of brick or stone and two or three stories high). -nār - m. a fire of this grass (which burns fiercely and is extinguished with difficulty). -pahörü - f. a thatched hut. -tulu - , m. a single stem of this grass; a very small amount of this grass.

e: conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhĕzyōv ), to become extinguished, (of daylight) to fade away, become extinct (L.V. 22). Cf. ʦhĕta and ʦhĕwun.
f. (sg. dat. ʦhī˜ʦhi ), a woman very slim from birth, a naturally slender woman (cf. ʦhyū̃ʦhu 2).
m. (of a human being) natural slimness, slenderness (cf. ʦhyū̃ʦhu 2).
ʦhī˜ʦhü , see ʦhyū̃ʦhu 1 and 2.
m. a thin stick, a twig (cf. ʦhyū̃ʦhu 2).

m. cutting off, cessation, stoppage (of something going on steadily, e.g. a river, a flow of water or of speech, income, progression of a person walking, and so on). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such a cessation to occur.
f. in ʦhĕnna-ʦhidöy, s.v. ʦhĕnna. Cf. ʦhid.
f. in ʦhala-ʦhidürü and ʦhidrözü f. in ʦhala-ʦhidrözü, both s.v. ʦhal, q.v. Cf. Hindī chidr.

f. dandling (a baby), tossing it playfully up and down, i.q. ʦhih ʦhih ab.
see ʦhyūlu.

m. (sg. dat. ʦhilivis ), an artful pretext (made up for bringing an accusation against some one). --raṭun -- m.inf. (in picking holes in a person's character) to seize upon such a pretext (for an accusation).

f.pl. faint or dull sunlight, dusk. -milawan - f. (sg. dat. -milavüñü -), the union of the two dusks (evening and nightfall), twilight. --milawun -- adv. at the time of twilight. --milawạñĕn -- adv. id. (used esp. with verbs…
fullMeaning: f.pl. faint or dull sunlight, dusk. -milawan - f. (sg. dat. -milavüñü -), the union of the two dusks (evening and nightfall), twilight. --milawun -- adv. at the time of twilight. --milawạñĕn -- adv. id. (used esp. with verbs indicating coming or the like).

e: m. a cut (caused by a knife or the like). Cf. ʦhĕn.

fullMeaning: onomat. the explosive spluttering sound caused by water, gravy, or similar liquid being added in cooking to heated oil, ghī, or the like; cf. ʦhar. -baz - m. cooking involving such spluttering (e.g. when gravy is added to hot oil as ab.). See bazun 1.

see ʦhī˜ʦhar.
see ʦhī˜ʦhyunu.
f. (sg. dat. ʦhipi ), i.q. ʦhĕph, q.v.
see ʦhọ̆ṭu and ʦhŏ̈ṭü 2.

m. shortness (esp. shorter than usual, e.g. a man shorter than usual, a rope too short, a short tree which is usually tall, and so on), dwarfness, undersizedness (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 29) (El. tsŏchar; W. 112, ṯs̱o˙char);…
fullMeaning: m. shortness (esp. shorter than usual, e.g. a man shorter than usual, a rope too short, a short tree which is usually tall, and so on), dwarfness, undersizedness (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 29) (El. tsŏchar; W. 112, ṯs̱o˙char); abridgedness, compressedness, conciseness, brevity (Śiv. 1598). Cf. ʦhọ̆ṭu.

e: or ʦhö̃ḍü (sometimes written ʦhöḍ , ʦhöḍ ) , f. (sg. dat. ʦhājĕ or ʦhã̄jĕ ), searching for, seeking (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 31) (Gr.Gr. 121, 126); searching (a place for something), exploring (for), rummaging, ransacking (for)…
fullMeaning: or ʦhö̃ḍü (sometimes written ʦhöḍ , ʦhöḍ ) , f. (sg. dat. ʦhājĕ or ʦhã̄jĕ ), searching for, seeking (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 31) (Gr.Gr. 121, 126); searching (a place for something), exploring (for), rummaging, ransacking (for) (cf. gar-ʦho, p. 296a, l. 19). Cf. ʦhã̄ḍ, ʦhanḍ or ʦhŏnḍ. --diñü -- f.inf. to institute a search, to search (something for something), to hunt for (in) (esp. of a thief or the like searching in receptacles, etc., for plunder).

e: m. a lock of hair worn on the crown of the head of a Hindū, a topknot (cf. hanga-ʦho, p. 338b, l. 44) (El. tsog, Śiv. 124); the arrangement of the hair, plaited with silk, worn hanging down behind by Ksh. girls (El.); the…
fullMeaning: m. a lock of hair worn on the crown of the head of a Hindū, a topknot (cf. hanga-ʦho, p. 338b, l. 44) (El. tsog, Śiv. 124); the arrangement of the hair, plaited with silk, worn hanging down behind by Ksh. girls (El.); the tasselled head of a cob of Indian corn or maize. --bŏḍun -- m.inf. 'the topknot to be sunken', hence, to become utterly unworthy (owing to inherent viciousness and consequent disrepute). ʦhögi-laṭiri - f. 'a topknot-tail', hence, a long topknot (Śiv. 124). ʦhögi-monḍi - m. the root (or base) of a top- knot (where it joins the skull).

e: m. i.q. ʦhōh, q.v. in the following: ʦhŏh dini m. pl. inf. to act zealously and happily, to apply oneself heart and soul (to any task) (Rām. 791, 794); esp. to seek with zeal, zealously and unceasingly to search for (Śiv. 341,…
fullMeaning: m. i.q. ʦhōh, q.v. in the following: ʦhŏh dini m. pl. inf. to act zealously and happily, to apply oneself heart and soul (to any task) (Rām. 791, 794); esp. to seek with zeal, zealously and unceasingly to search for (Śiv. 341, 493; Rām. 514); to roam through, to wander ceaselessly through and through (Śiv. 422); to act fearlessly and without restraint, to give free rein (to one's feelings, etc.) (cf. lŏkacyāras ʦhŏh dini, p. 517b, l. 27). --dyunu -- m. sg.inf. to give happiness, to cause to feel unrestrained rapture (L.V. 44). --mārȧni -- m. pl. inf. to act fearlessly and without restraint.

e: m. after entering into the midst of any business (e.g. into a position of authority, or into expenditure of money) acting fearlessly and without restraint, becoming zealously and busily engaged in any task; happiness, pleasure,…
fullMeaning: m. after entering into the midst of any business (e.g. into a position of authority, or into expenditure of money) acting fearlessly and without restraint, becoming zealously and busily engaged in any task; happiness, pleasure, rest in the midst of occupation (K.Pr. 59, 171). Cf. ʦhŏh.

fullMeaning: adj. c.g. (as subst., f. ʦhŏkaladiñ ), blemished or disfigured by marks of scorching or parching, (esp. of food) spoiled and made useless (by this cause); filled with conceit in one's own shrewdness, proud of one's own cleverness (Gr.Gr. 135, sly).

e: m. (sg. dat. ʦhŏkas ), semi-combustion, (of food, or the like) the being half-burnt; speechlessness (cf. ʦhŏkun) (Gr.Gr. 123); conceit in one's own shrewdness, pride in one's own cleverness (Gr.Gr. 135, slyness). --dyunu --…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. ʦhŏkas ), semi-combustion, (of food, or the like) the being half-burnt; speechlessness (cf. ʦhŏkun) (Gr.Gr. 123); conceit in one's own shrewdness, pride in one's own cleverness (Gr.Gr. 135, slyness). --dyunu -- m.inf. to burn or heat half (i.e. partially). --khyonu -- m.inf. (of food being cooked or fried) to be half cooked, to be partly cooked, to be partly burnt. --lagun -- m.inf. partial, or slight, burning or parching to occur (to something); burning or harrowing (of the heart or feelings) to be felt (due to grief, sickness, hunger, or the like). ʦhŏka-shikār - m. killing for sport (and not for food). -tikh m. (sg. dat. -tikas -), a small piece of goat's flesh toasted (over burning charcoal, and not thoroughly cooked).

e: conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhŏkyōv ), (at the beginning of a discussion, or when busy in some work, or when being instructed or trained, and so on) to become obstructed, stopped, hindered, to become powerless, become silenced, speechless…
fullMeaning: conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhŏkyōv ), (at the beginning of a discussion, or when busy in some work, or when being instructed or trained, and so on) to become obstructed, stopped, hindered, to become powerless, become silenced, speechless (Gr.Gr. 122). ʦhŏkyō-motu - perf. part. (f. ʦhŏkyē-müʦü -), obstructed, hindered, as ab.; (of a human being, horse, or the like) (in studying, carrying out some work, walking, or the like) stopped, hindered, unable to proceed.

e: f. apprehension, fear, terror (esp. of something unseen or expected).
f. secret knowledge (by which the accomplishment of some difficult task is rendered easy), private experience.

f. silence, muteness (El. tshŏpah and tsŏpah; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1598, 1639; K.Pr. 219). -dab - m. keeping silence (esp. under the influence of fear or the like). -dam - m. obstinate silence (even under provocation), obstinate muteness.…
fullMeaning: f. silence, muteness (El. tshŏpah and tsŏpah; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1598, 1639; K.Pr. 219). -dab - m. keeping silence (esp. under the influence of fear or the like). -dam - m. obstinate silence (even under provocation), obstinate muteness. --karüñü --, f.inf. to keep silence (El.; Gr.M.; W. 88 ʦo˙pah karaṇi; Śiv. 81, 1638; Rām. 1465; YZ. 83, 439, 452). --karith --, conj. part., as adv. silently, without saying anything (Gr.M.; H. xii, 4). ʦhŏpi sg. obl. by silence, esp. by silent meditation (L.V. 2). -manthar - m. the mystic formula of silence, i.e. the Śaiva mystic formula (Skt. ajapamantra) in which no words are uttered, but which consists only in a number of exhalations and inhalations (L.V. 40).

e: f. secret conduct, secret, or underhand, dealing.
m. taciturnity, slowness of speech, reticence; (in work or action) slowness, slackness (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 44).
adj. (f. ʦhŏ̈pü ), habitually silent, taciturn, slow of speech (El, tsŏpah, dumb; Gr.Gr. 27; K.Pr. 219); slow in action, slack at work (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 42).

adj. (f. ʦhürü 1 ), empty, void, devoid (of), deprived (of), free, or freed (from), without (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 45; phala-ʦho, p. 692b, l. 10; ruma-ʦho, p. 834a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 10; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1806; K.Pr. 219, 239); empty…

(f. ʦhürü 1 ), empty, void, devoid (of), deprived (of), free, or freed (from), without (cf. atha-ʦho, p. 63b, l. 45; phala-ʦho, p. 692b, l. 10; ruma-ʦho, p. 834a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 10; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1806; K.Pr. 219, 239); empty (of property), beggared. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of something previously full) to become empty, to be emptied. ʦhariy (Rām. 364) or ʦhoruy (Rām. 986) uselessly, in vain; only, merely, nothing but (K.Pr. 132, ʦhurui).

m. a short stick, club, walking stick (according to El. s.v. tsoṭa, this is the word employed in Śrīnagar, elsewhere ḍã̄g, q.v. is more usual) (cf. ranga-ʦho, p. 837a, l. 34) (H. iii, 1, 2); a pestle.

e: m. a kind of Hindū oblation or offering scattered into the air before the house door or on to the roof of the house, intended for the Yōginīs, or female attendants on Shiv (Śiva), as they travel in the air. It is supposed to ward…
fullMeaning: m. a kind of Hindū oblation or offering scattered into the air before the house door or on to the roof of the house, intended for the Yōginīs, or female attendants on Shiv (Śiva), as they travel in the air. It is supposed to ward off, or carry away, misfortune. It consists mainly of rice with pieces of sheep- or goat-liver or -heart, and is generally offered on Tuesday or Saturday. --khitra-pāl --- m. this offering united with a similar offering to certain Bhairavas, see khitra-pāl and börav. ʦȧṭi-khāv - m. an eater of these offerings, a man who habitually eats them. ʦaṭi-kani lagun - m.inf. for the relief of another from calamity, to offer oneself as an oblation.

m. (f. ʦröjü , q.v.) a leather-worker, carrier, shoemaker (of untouchable caste) (Gr.M.); a kind of police-spy or detective (there being usually one in charge of each quarter of a town. A woman (ʦröjü) may sometimes occupy the…
fullMeaning: m. (f. ʦröjü , q.v.) a leather-worker, carrier, shoemaker (of untouchable caste) (Gr.M.); a kind of police-spy or detective (there being usually one in charge of each quarter of a town. A woman (ʦröjü) may sometimes occupy the post) (Gr.Gr. 36; H. v, 7; K.Pr. 107, 221, 224); a jailor (YZ. 370, 381). According to K.Pr. 144, the word is the name of a Moslem sect, which has the choice of three employments. They can become, jailors, or bootmakers, or beggars. Moslems outside the sect do not eat with them. For their origin, see K.Pr. 98. ʦröli-zāphal - m. a nutmeg brought in former times to a house by a friend or relation, as a harbinger of good luck, on the occasion of a festival (such as that on the birth of a son).

fullMeaning: (sometimes written ʦuviñ ; Gr.Gr. 119, 192) conj. 1 (in the tense formed from the past participle, and in these tense only, this verb is impersonal and is only in the feminine gender, the subject being in the case of the agent. Thus ʦuvüth , it was quarrelled by thee, i.e. thou quarrelledst. In the plural, it indicates many quarrels, as in ʦuvĕth , thou quarrelledst many times. See Gr.Gr. 188, 214, 220, 233. 1 p.p. f. ʦuvü ), to quarrel, esp. of a verbal quarrel or mutual abuse (cf. har ʦo, p. 343b, l. 17) (Gr.Gr. as ab. and 117, 119, 192; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 37). ʦuvü-müʦü - perf. part. f. a quarrel been made (between so-and-so). ʦuvith diñü f.inf. to instigate a quarrel. [Although technically impersonal, the grammatical subject of this verb is really some fem. word, such as har 4, meaning a quarrel, which is understood. Thus ʦuvüth, ab., is literally '(a quarrel) was quarrelled by thee'.]
