fullMeaning: m. putting or piling things over each other (e.g. courses of bricks in building a wall, or pieces of material or embroideries on cloth, etc.) (cf. hanga-wo, p. 338b, l. 50; kȧmbi-wi, p. 444a, l. 35; nȧri-wi, p. 649a, l. 30; phȧli-wi, p. 694b, l. 28; palang-wo, p. 731b, l. 17; ṭōpi-wo, p. 1014a, l. 25; ʦöki-wi, p. 1067b, l. 22; zamba- wār) (Rām. 1301, a pile of bones); winding or twisting a string, or the like, over and over into a ball. --anun -- m.inf. to build (as ab.) in courses, one above the other; to wind up string, etc., into a ball, as ab. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep, retain (K.Pr. 206). --trāwun -- m.inf. to throw away (K.Pr. 206).

m. usage, custom, established practice (as handed down from former times), approved moral conduct (cf. rǖni-wi, p. 835b, l. 46); polite and virtuous conduct, good manners; the intelligent carrying out of any work or business (by…
fullMeaning: m. usage, custom, established practice (as handed down from former times), approved moral conduct (cf. rǖni-wi, p. 835b, l. 46); polite and virtuous conduct, good manners; the intelligent carrying out of any work or business (by one who understands it thoroughly). --raṭun -- m.inf. to adopt established practice, to take to polite and virtuous conduct. --rāwarun -- m.inf. (of some respected and reverend person) to abandon customary politeness (for some temporary reason). warga bĕhun m.inf. (of one formerly leading an irregular habit) to adopt and continue in established and virtuous customs, to lead a reformed life. --dapun -- m.inf. to give advice to another in a circumlocutory manner, e.g. to advise in parables, or by talking to a third person on some apparently different matter. --raṭun -- m.inf. to take, or make obedient, a person, that he may receive moral training. --rōzun -- m.inf. (after receiving good moral instruction) to continue in good conduct. --thawun -- m.inf. to put (a pupil, servant, or the like) in the proper line of conduct for the performance of any task; to fix anything in its right order or position. wargas aʦun m.inf. (when one has come to full age and years of discretion) to take or engage in a livelihood by carrying on some business.

fullMeaning: m. repeated practice or exercise (in order to become perfect in any act or business) (Śiv. 1218); occupation, profession; manner of living, mode of life (Śiv. 1619, 1649); mutual close association or fellowship between two persons; earnings, hire, wages. --āsun -- m.inf. full and complete practice to be acquired. --thawun -- m.inf. to set up a close fellowship (with some person) (e.g. with some influential person in the hope of future profit). -müʦü - f. a woman who (after falling from a high station) has taken to humble work (e.g. the wife of a great man who for some cause has sunk to being a maidservant). wartanas bĕhun m.inf. to sit at earning, i.e. (of some well-to-do person, compelled by some misfortune) to take to a humble occupation (such as household service). --rōzun -- m.inf. e: m. (sg. dat. waṭatas ), earnings, gain, amassed profits (resulting from any work on which one is engaged) (Gr.Gr. 128); cf. waṭun and waṭiñ. --anun -- m.inf. to collect together (parts into a whole), to piece together. --yunu --…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. waṭatas ), earnings, gain, amassed profits (resulting from any work on which one is engaged) (Gr.Gr. 128); cf. waṭun and waṭiñ. --anun -- m.inf. to collect together (parts into a whole), to piece together. --yunu -- m.inf. to become pieced together (as ab.).

e: f. in wātawan karüñü f.inf. to finish, or accomplish something anyhow (e.g. in fitting together the parts of a whole, to fix the parts wrongly, or, in distributing gifts, doing it hurriedly and incompletely).

n.ag. (f. wātavüñü ), one who arrives, one who has been (in such-and-such a place) (Rām. 1255); one who acts with discrimination and thorough knowledge; (as adv.) immediately on arrival (K. 394, 523; H. xii, 15, with emph. y,…
fullMeaning: n.ag. (f. wātavüñü ), one who arrives, one who has been (in such-and-such a place) (Rām. 1255); one who acts with discrimination and thorough knowledge; (as adv.) immediately on arrival (K. 394, 523; H. xii, 15, with emph. y, wātawunuy; so YZ. 32).

e: m. (sg. dat. wã̄ṭas ), the belly, stomach (cf. ā̃ṭa-wo, p. 69a, l. 38) (K.Pr. 218). wã̄ṭa-buḍay - f. (immediately on seeing something) violent longing, impetuous hankering (for it, so that one is even ready to take it by force).…

(immediately on seeing something) violent longing, impetuous hankering (for it, so that one is even ready to take it by force). --phērun -- m.inf. to experience pleasure in giving or leaving (esp. something of great value or much loved) to another.

e: adv. (borrowed from Skt. vat, and used as a suffix) like, as in mastāna-wath, like one who is drunk (Śiv. 1450).
m. the extreme, unbearable, heat experienced in the summer at midday.

m. (sg. dat. wāṭas ), a lumpy kind of porridge of coarsely broken grain (such as maize, barley, etc.) (cf. kạnaka-wa, p. 457b, l. 40; makāyi-wo, p. 563b, l. 14; pingi-wo, p. 740a, l. 25; shöli-wi, p. 880b, l. 38; wushki-wo, p.…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. wāṭas ), a lumpy kind of porridge of coarsely broken grain (such as maize, barley, etc.) (cf. kạnaka-wa, p. 457b, l. 40; makāyi-wo, p. 563b, l. 14; pingi-wo, p. 740a, l. 25; shöli-wi, p. 880b, l. 38; wushki-wo, p. 1147a, l. 12) (W. 115, wāt, mistranslated 'seam'). wāṭa-koshu - m. the bran of pounded maize (as sifted from the broken grain). -lŏkhar - or -lŏkhürü - - f. a large coagulated lump of the material of this porridge, when cold and stale. -mujü - f. a certain kind of radish, small and pungent (El. wáṭamúj). -pholu - m. 'a grain in porridge', a hidden hoard (hitherto unknown and now discovered), treasure trove. -ṭīrü - f. a large coagulated lump of the material of this porridge when cold and stale. wāṭuku 2 adj. gen. (f. wāṭücü ), of, or belonging to, such porridge (e.g. a particular grain suitable for making it, or a dish for holding it).

fullMeaning: in waṭha-wadal - f. distress, fever, or the like caused to a respectable person by abuse publicly directed at him; cf. waṭhal 1. -wadal gaʦhüñü - f.inf. such distress or fever to be experienced. -wadal karüñü - f.inf. to cause such distress, etc., by offering such abuse.

e: f. disrespect (shown to another by abusing him before respectable people); cf. waṭha. --gaʦhüñü -- f.inf. such disrespect to happen, i.e. to be shown (to a person).
f. secret collection (of money, goods, results of work, or the like), secret hoarding. --karüñü -- f.inf. secretly to hoard, secretly to pile up one's earnings or the like.
m. or f. the act or condition of spreading, becoming diffused, in wuna-wathar, f., p. 1122a, l.47, and wö̃ʦha-wo, m., s.v. wö̃ʦh 1, q.v. Cf. watharun.

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. wạtaras ). (This word is the form taken by pạthar 1, when it is the second member of a compound. e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. watharôwu ), i.q. watharun, q.v. (El., Gr.M.) (El. also has watharawun, to spread (a carpet)) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 57, 1850; Rām. 1783; YZ. 343).

m. a level piece of ground, a field, i.q. pathur, q.v., and (like wạthar, q.v.) used only --˚ (cf. baḍ-watharū, p. 81b, l. 48; lar-watharū, p. 529b, l. 41); a field in which rice is sown broadcast (L. 331, watrú, 463, wattru).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wathoru ), to spread out (a carpet, mat, or the like, on the ground), lay out flat (Śiv. 500, 1468; Rām. 1495; H. xii, 18, 21; YZ. 235); to throw (a person) flat and spread out on the ground (for execution).…

(f. wathürü-müʦü -), spread out, as ab. (Rām. 569, 579).

e: m. a mat, rug, or the like spread out (for sleeping on or for sitting on), a bed (Gr.M.; L. 458, wathran; K. 925; H. xii, 24); a carpet (El.). watharȧni-palav - m. a rug (used like a mattress) spread (on a bed for being lain…
fullMeaning: m. a mat, rug, or the like spread out (for sleeping on or for sitting on), a bed (Gr.M.; L. 458, wathran; K. 925; H. xii, 24); a carpet (El.). watharȧni-palav - m. a rug (used like a mattress) spread (on a bed for being lain upon. Usually some old worn-out garment). watharani pyōmotu perf. part. (f. --pyēmüʦü --), filled with agitation, as in the following. --pyonu -- m.inf. to become extremely agitated (by fear, disease, loss, anxiety, or the like, to such a degree that the person affected is not able even to stand up).

e: m. destruction or ruin (of a house or other place of refuge, e.g. by decay, or by being pulled down and the materials being scattered) (Śiv. 120); met. destruction of any refuge or means of help. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such…
fullMeaning: m. destruction or ruin (of a house or other place of refuge, e.g. by decay, or by being pulled down and the materials being scattered) (Śiv. 120); met. destruction of any refuge or means of help. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such destruction or decay to occur.

e: f. destruction or ruin of anything animate or inanimate (by decay or violent removal from its site, and the constituents being scattered in different directions) (Śiv. 5); the causing of such destruction or ruin.
m. i.q. wȧthiwôñi, q.v.
m. the condition of being without a screen, or of being exposed (either above or all round) (e.g. of a house, a courtyard, or a garden).
adj. c.g. (of a house, meeting place, courtyard, garden, or the like, or of a dish, vessel, etc.) without a screen, exposed (either above or all round), uncovered, unfenced.

m. great fatigue, weariness, distress (from excessive labour, journeying, or the like). Cf. wutra. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such fatigue to be experienced; to become exhausted by exposure to extreme heat, a rainstorm, or the like; to…
fullMeaning: m. great fatigue, weariness, distress (from excessive labour, journeying, or the like). Cf. wutra. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such fatigue to be experienced; to become exhausted by exposure to extreme heat, a rainstorm, or the like; to experience mental distress (from being abused, from grief, or similar cause).

e: see waṭa 2 and woṭu.
f. N. of a certain hard wood found in the forests (L. 79, 82, wutil, (?) Rhus Wallichii). According to L. 82, it is used for making spoons and combs, and the tree has a red berry. Cf. waṭyulu.
f. a house-lizard.
adj. (f. wȧṭilivi ), made of waṭil-wood, see waṭil 1.
f. earning only for oneself (and not for the benefit of others), saving up one's earnings (Gr.Gr. 120). Cf. waṭun and waṭath.

m. a way, path, track; fashion, mode, custom, habit; disposition, conduct, behaviour; (in Ksh.) careful conduct, circumspection, caution, forethought. --bĕhun -- m.inf. to settle oneself in a favourable position (for carrying out…
fullMeaning: m. a way, path, track; fashion, mode, custom, habit; disposition, conduct, behaviour; (in Ksh.) careful conduct, circumspection, caution, forethought. --bĕhun -- m.inf. to settle oneself in a favourable position (for carrying out some laudable purpose in a satisfactory way). --rōzun -- m.inf. (of someone or something previously not in a satisfactory condition) to be settled in a favourable condition. --thawun -- m.inf. to put in order in a favourable condition.

e: f.pl. in potu waʦa phērañĕ, to be struck senseless with terror, p. 788b, l. 30, q.v.

fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. wāʦaki ), reading out fluently and correctly (from a book or the like). --wŏthüñü -- f.inf. the power of such reading to come into existence, i.e. to be gained (by a person). --yiñü -- f.inf. (of some child or the like) the power of fluent reading aloud to come, i.e. to be acquired. wāʦȧki parun m.inf. to read without attending to the meaning (for the purpose of learning mnemonical rules, such as those of grammar, by rote).

e: adj. c.g. affectionate towards, fondly loving, kind or compassionate towards (Śiv. 1036, 1204, 1535, 1673, 1675, 1740; K. 400, 1102).
m. one who habitually uses (censurable) language, a calumniator, contradictor, reviler, or the like.
m.pl. in shīth waʦan, p. 899b, l. 14, q.v.

or wö̃ʦar m. (of a river, lake, pit, or the like) shallowness; shallowness of intellect, readiness to let out, or divulge, secrets; absence of profundity, simplicity and clearness of language. Cf. wỗtu.

m. 'arrival'; hence, the turning up, or being got, just when required (of something laboured for or desired), the coming of an opportunity to complete some work; the acquisition of some quality, the mastery of some acquirement,…
fullMeaning: m. 'arrival'; hence, the turning up, or being got, just when required (of something laboured for or desired), the coming of an opportunity to complete some work; the acquisition of some quality, the mastery of some acquirement, branch of art, or learning, the gaining of skill or dexterity.

e: m. N. of a demon, who, disguised as a calf, attempted to kill Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), but was killed by him (in Skt. vatsâsura) (K. 186).

m. (sg. dat. wāʦas ), words, speech; a promise, undertaking, pledge (K. 279). --dyunu --, m.inf. to promise, plight one's word (K. 520). --hyonu --, m.inf. to take a word, i.e. to obtain (a person's) assent (Rām. 151); to take up…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. wāʦas ), words, speech; a promise, undertaking, pledge (K. 279). --dyunu --, m.inf. to promise, plight one's word (K. 520). --hyonu --, m.inf. to take a word, i.e. to obtain (a person's) assent (Rām. 151); to take up a word, to make a petition (K. 575, wāc hyonu). wāʦa-band - or -bandan - m. word-binding, a promise (to perform, etc.) (K. 278-80, -band). -bandan dyunu - m.inf. to promise, vow (to do something).

e: m. (of two things usually, or which can be, joined together) the being slightly apart, openness, the condition of being open (e.g. the eyelids, a clasp, a garment) (cf. ȧchi-wi (p. 8b, l. 50); (of something that can be closed or…
fullMeaning: m. (of two things usually, or which can be, joined together) the being slightly apart, openness, the condition of being open (e.g. the eyelids, a clasp, a garment) (cf. ȧchi-wi (p. 8b, l. 50); (of something that can be closed or shut up) openness (cf. atha-wo, p. 65a, l. 13) (Gr.Gr. 29, 140).

e: m. eager, ardent, affection (for a son, wife, brother, friend, or the like).

or waʦhuru m. (f. waʦhar or waʦhürü ), a calf (cf. dŏda- waʦhürü, p. 190b, l. 11; khinda-wo, p. 403a, l. 42) (El. watsir, f.; Gr.Gr. 33, 37, waʦhar, f.; K.Pr. 81, 171, f.). This word, with an interjection, is used in the vocative…
fullMeaning: or waʦhuru m. (f. waʦhar or waʦhürü ), a calf (cf. dŏda- waʦhürü, p. 190b, l. 11; khinda-wo, p. 403a, l. 42) (El. watsir, f.; Gr.Gr. 33, 37, waʦhar, f.; K.Pr. 81, 171, f.). This word, with an interjection, is used in the vocative fem., with emphatic y, waʦhariy, in addressing a female junior or inferior, as in hāy (hatay, or hatöy) waʦhariy! (Gr.Gr. 99).

e: see wasun.
m. (f. wāʦöjü ), i.q. wāʦal, q.v.
see wātun.

m. (sg. dat. waʦanas ), the reading out of some sacred book; a verse sung in a song, a song (cf. wanawan-wo, p. 1126b, l. 40) (Śiv. 1044, 1454, 1662); a saying, a sentence of instruction, precept (cf. wākh-wo, p. 1108b, l. 13)…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. waʦanas ), the reading out of some sacred book; a verse sung in a song, a song (cf. wanawan-wo, p. 1126b, l. 40) (Śiv. 1044, 1454, 1662); a saying, a sentence of instruction, precept (cf. wākh-wo, p. 1108b, l. 13) (L.V. 94). --wanun -- m. (at a wedding or similar festival, the chorus of women) to start singing auspicious songs. waʦan-pad - m. a line (of a stanza) of one of such auspicious songs.

e: see wātul (Gr.Gr. 36).
in waṭuka börav (or bhairav) m. N. of a certain Börav (Bhairava) (see p. 129b, l. 44), a partial form of Śiva, said to have been born as a mental son of Pārvatī (Śiv. 1552). Cf. waṭukh.

m. (sg. dat. wāṭakas ), he who, or that which, joins together, a man who joins up broken articles, a professional mender, or one skilled in mending, a repairer; a process that unites together things broken (cf. anga-wo, p. 33b,…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. wāṭakas ), he who, or that which, joins together, a man who joins up broken articles, a professional mender, or one skilled in mending, a repairer; a process that unites together things broken (cf. anga-wo, p. 33b, l. 2); one who brings together persons (e.g. a married couple or two friends) who have quarrelled, a reconciler.

e: m. (sg. dat. wātalas ; f. wātüjü , H. xi, 14-5), a man of the lowest and most degraded caste in Kashmīr, a sweeper, a Mihtar, a scavenger, leather-worker (cf. hāra- wātüjü, a kind of bird, p. 344b, l. 14; māra-wātul, p. 587b, ll.…
fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. wātalas ; f. wātüjü , H. xi, 14-5), a man of the lowest and most degraded caste in Kashmīr, a sweeper, a Mihtar, a scavenger, leather-worker (cf. hāra- wātüjü, a kind of bird, p. 344b, l. 14; māra-wātul, p. 587b, ll. 12 ff.; pöshi-wi, p. 780a, l. 1; shupi-wi, p. 887b, l. 34) (Gr.Gr. 36, 58; Gr.M.; L. 418; W. 17; H. xi, 14-5; K.Pr. 9, 231-2); met. one who acts like one of this degraded caste, a filthy fellow (cf. lĕka-wo, p. 518a, l. 44). wātal-bāpār - m. the natural condition of a Wātul; hence, foulness, filthiness (e.g. of a kitchen or its utensils, of garments or ornaments, of the body internally or externally). -mahāsas - m. porridge of butter and beans (p. 553a, l. 13) (a dainty) for a Wātul; hence, incompatibility (e.g. fine ornaments on a dirty limb, or on the wrong and inappropriate limb). -phukh - f. (sg. dat. -phuki -), a kind of plate or tray, on which a Wātul who works as a shoe-cobbler keeps his tools. -wān - m. a place where Wātuls and other foul and polluting people congregate or herd together. -wāza - m. a cook of this caste, a low-caste cook who deals only with foul food (cf. hūni-māzas wātal-wāza, p. 337a, l. 5) (K.Pr. 84).

e: m. in burza-wo, a large thin sheet of birch-bark (p. 131a, l. 9), and phã-wo, a square sheet of cotton wool (p. 698a, l. 17), qq.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. woṭu 3 (for 1, 2, see s.vv.); f. vüṭü or wüṭü 4 (for 1, 2, 3, see s.vv.); f.pl. wacĕ ; 2 p.p. wacyōv ), to bring together (a number of things), to collect (things scattered), to assemble (tr.) (Gr.Gr. 120, 128);…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. woṭu 3 (for 1, 2, see s.vv.); f. vüṭü or wüṭü 4 (for 1, 2, 3, see s.vv.); f.pl. wacĕ ; 2 p.p. wacyōv ), to bring together (a number of things), to collect (things scattered), to assemble (tr.) (Gr.Gr. 120, 128); to close up (something open, e.g. the eye, the mouth, or the hand) (cf. atha wo, p. 65a, l. 3) (Śiv. 168; Rām. 522-3, 1266-7, 1509); to join up, unite (L.V. 80); to fold up, or roll up (something spread out) (cf. dāman wo, p. 219b, l. 44; lonḍu wo, p. 525b, l. 43; wagowu wo, p. 1103a, l. 22) (Gr.Gr. 5, 10; Śiv. 1301-3, 1308, 1568); to wind up into a ball (cf. ḍyū̃gu wo, p. 267b, l. 4); to collect another person's property and appropriate it (e.g. in sharing out to get hold of other persons' shares as well as one's own). woṭu-motu - , perf. part. (f. wüṭü-müʦü -, pl. wacĕ-maʦa -), brought together, etc., as ab.

e: conj. 1 (1 p.p. wôṭu ; f. wöṭü , sg. dat. wācĕ ; 2 p.p. wācyōv ), to join, unite, fasten permanently together, to fix together (cf. pholu wo, p. 694a, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 123; Gr.M.; L. 461, wútun); to join, unite (things broken), to…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. wôṭu ; f. wöṭü , sg. dat. wācĕ ; 2 p.p. wācyōv ), to join, unite, fasten permanently together, to fix together (cf. pholu wo, p. 694a, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 123; Gr.M.; L. 461, wútun); to join, unite (things broken), to mend, repair (K.Pr. 80); to join broken limbs, act as a bone-setter; met. to unite (persons who are separated by a quarrel), to bring together, reconcile; to make (something) ready for action (e.g. drawing a bow) (Rām. 1428). wôṭu-motu - perf. part. (f. wöṭü-müʦü -), joined, repaired, etc., as ab. wāṭan-goru - m. (f. -gürü -), a professional joiner, repairer, mender, bone-setter, etc., as ab. -wôlu - n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ -), id.

e: f. a small circular piece of leather, wood, or metal, with a hole in the centre, used as a toy. Cf. watan 2.
f. of wāṭun, q.v., also occurring in āṭüñü-wāṭüñü, p. 68a, l. 46, q.v.
m. a kind of wooden box or casket, partitioned inside and with a movable cover.

fullMeaning: or woturu 2 m. a leaf (of paper, or the like, a slip (of paper), a document, memorandum (i.q. pạthar 1, q.v.), used --˚, as in dārath-wo, p. 249b, l. 43; ganĕth-wo, p. 293a, l. 48; mal-wo, p. 564a, l. 44; pīri-wo, p. 753a, l. 31; pashṭa-wo, p. 783a, l. 14; patha-wo, p. 791b, l. 14; ʦĕtas-wo, p. 1089b, l. 8.

e: m. (sg. dat. wȧṭilis ), a certain tree with a hard wood found in the forests; (when felled) its wood. Cf. waṭil 1.

fullMeaning: or (q.v.) vĕv 2 f. the mass of eggs, or roe, of a fish. wavi-göḍü - f. a certain kind of fish, which is said always to have a roe inside it. -gurun - - m. N. of another kind of fish, small in size and found in forest streams. Even the males, as well as the females, are said always to contain roes. It is said to have a very delicate flavour. Cf. gurun 1.

e: m. in danda-wāv, a tooth-file, p. 225a, l. 30, and phahara-wāv, a file, p. 687a, l. 30, yẹ̆ndra-wāv, s.v. yẹ̆ndar. Cf. wōwarun.
m. in khanḍa-wāv, a shawl-weaver, p. 403a, l. 21. Cf. wôwuru.

fullMeaning: (Rām. 1255) or wölmīkh m. N. of a celebrated sage (Skt. Vālmīki) the author of the Skt. Rāmâyaṇa. According to the Ksh. fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. wŏlaras ), N. of a large lake, about thirty miles north-west of Śrīnagar, commonly known as the 'Woolar' lake (see RT.Tr. II, 423 ff.). In Sanskrit it was called the Mahāpadmasaras (El. Wular Ráza, see bel.; Śiv. 591); the word is also the name of one of the Parganas (the ancient Hōlaḍā) of the Marāz Division of Kashmīr (RT.Tr. II, 436, 460; Gr.Gr. 15, ular). wŏlar-göḍü - f. N. of a certain fish found in the ab. lake. It is described as having a long dark-coloured body, and a red face. -hönzü - m. (f. -hānzañ -), a boatman who plies on the above lake. They are accustomed to storms, and live by fishing, collecting water-chestnuts (gôru 1), and capturing water-fowl. -rāza - m. another N. of this lake. Being the largest lake in Kashmīr, it is called rāza or 'king' (El.). wŏlaruku adj. gen. (f. wŏlarücü ), of, or belonging to, or produced in the ab. lake.

adj. (f.wö̆ʦhü ), 1 p.p. of wŏthun, q.v. (This word is to be distinguished from wothu 3, which has the opposite meaning.) Used as adj., risen, standing up, erect; he who, or that which, is steadily and continuously rising (lit.…
fullMeaning: adj. (f.wö̆ʦhü ), 1 p.p. of wŏthun, q.v. (This word is to be distinguished from wothu 3, which has the opposite meaning.) Used as adj., risen, standing up, erect; he who, or that which, is steadily and continuously rising (lit. and met.); risen (from bed, sickness, or the like) (cf. bĕmāri-wo, p. 108b, l. 50; huri-wo, p. 347a, l. 45); prepared, ready (cf. byāli-wo, p. 150b, l. 40); risen (from), been done with, been got rid of (cf. mūni-wo, p. 573b, l. 47); originated, issued, emanated (cf. manza wo, p. 584a, l. 30); risen from its origin, just issued, fresh from the source (cf. thāna-wo, p. 978a, l. 10. Here there has possibly been confusion with wothu 3, q.v.); and so on, through all the meanings of wŏthun. wŏtha-bēṭh - f. (of some thing or action) the continuously and repeatedly rising up and settling down. -bēṭh lagüñü - f.inf. (of a human being) to begin repeatedly rising and sitting; to become restless, fidgetty, etc.; (of some action) to become uncertain, at one time in action, at another time not, or at one time definite and at another time indefinite, and so on; cf. wŏthāsan. -dān - m. a movable fireplace or cooking stove (capable of being moved safely from one place to another). wŏthā-bīṭhī - f. rising up and sitting down; esp. (as a punishment to a school boy) continuous repeated standing up and sitting down.

When a bridegroom or bride are about to set forth for the wedding (or on similar occasions) this seed is burnt before them with appropriate spells, in order to ward off the evil eye, demons, ghosts, or similar evils.

e: conjnct. or (cf. wūli yā gāsa, p. 1113a, l. 43) (Gr.M.; W. 152; Śiv. 1015, 1907; Rām. 845, 863, 1067, 1069; K. 617; H. ii, 12; viii, 1). yā-na - conjnct. or not (Rām. 272); used as a particle to emphasize a question, as in yā-na…
fullMeaning: conjnct. or (cf. wūli yā gāsa, p. 1113a, l. 43) (Gr.M.; W. 152; Śiv. 1015, 1907; Rām. 845, 863, 1067, 1069; K. 617; H. ii, 12; viii, 1). yā-na - conjnct. or not (Rām. 272); used as a particle to emphasize a question, as in yā-na gōkh-a, didst thou go?; yā-na wuchum-a, did I see?; yā-na bōzy-ā, will he hear? yā . . . na-ta . . . - (cf. na-ta 2, p. 618a, l. 4), either . . . or (W. 153). yā-ta - conjnct. if, supposing, as in yā-ta kara bŏh, ada kari suh, if I do (it), then he will do (it); yā-ta wuchakh ʦah, ada zānakh, if thou wilt look, thou wilt know, and so on. yā-tay - conjnct. a particle implying contrast, indicating ability (as contrasted with another's inability), as in yā-tay korum, nata kȧrizi-hē, note that I did (it), otherwise thou shouldst have done (it) (implying that the speaker had been able to do it, but that the person addressed had been unable); so, yā-tay khyōn, na-ta khĕta, note that he ate (it), otherwise eat (it thyself) (implying that while he could eat it, the person addressed could not) (El. yátai, or, and, (?) yátu, except; W. 99 yātai, either, or; K. 869). yā . . . yā . . . , either . . . or (W. 152; Rām. 371, 1364; H. x, 3, 7; xii, 9).

e: interj. O! Oh! yā bār sāhibō O Great God! (K.Pr. 210).
adj. finding, getting, used --˚, as in kam-yāb, hard to get, scarce, p. 442b, l. 24; kām-yāb, obtaining one's object, p. 447a, l. 25.

f. (sg. dat. ? yāci ) (in some business conducted openly) the secret employment of means to effect the result (e.g. a bribe, secret commission, or the like). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to take a bribe, a secret commission, or the like.…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. ? yāci ) (in some business conducted openly) the secret employment of means to effect the result (e.g. a bribe, secret commission, or the like). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to take a bribe, a secret commission, or the like. --hāvüñü -- f.inf. to take secret revenge (e.g. to conceal one's power to interfere with some work on which an enemy is engaged, and on its completion suddenly and secretly to attack it).

e: conjnct. although (El.), i.q. yĕd, q.v.

m. remembrance, recollection (cf. yād pāwun, p. 810b, l. 38; yād pāwanāwun, p. 811a, l. 42) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 117, 1506, 1598; Rām. 289, 509, 667, 756, 833, 835); memory (Rām. 561; H. i, 7). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. memory to occur, to be…
fullMeaning: m. remembrance, recollection (cf. yād pāwun, p. 810b, l. 38; yād pāwanāwun, p. 811a, l. 42) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 117, 1506, 1598; Rām. 289, 509, 667, 756, 833, 835); memory (Rām. 561; H. i, 7). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. memory to occur, to be remembered, to be learnt by heart; cf. --karun, bel. --hyonu -- m.inf. to take in mind, bear in mind (H. xii, 17). --karun -- m.inf. to recollect, remember, call to mind (El., Gr.M.); to commit to memory, repeat from memory (without having to read from any paper), to learn by heart; cf. --gaʦhun, ab. --pyonu -- m.inf. memory to fall (to a person), remembrance to be aroused (El. to remember (intrans.); Śiv. 73 caus., 440, 1002, 1002 caus., 1822 caus., 1884 caus., 1909 caus.; Rām. 431, 658, 771, 1535, 1630 caus.; H. iii, 5; vii, 20, 26; xii, 15; caus. vi, 11; K.Pr. 102). --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to bear in mind, keep in memory, to remember, not to forget (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 596; Rām. 27, 994). --yunu -- m.inf. memory to come to a person (El. to remember (intrans.); W. 88).

e: f. in the following:-- yād gaʦhüñü f.inf. punishment to be experienced (by a child, for the sake of correction). --karüñü -- f.inf. to punish, correct, as ab.
(spelling) conjnct. although (El., W. 99, 100). Cf. yȧd, yĕd.
f. a memorandum, memo (Gr.M.).
m. a descendant of Yĕdu (Yadu), q.v. (Śiv. 1322; K. 18, 362, 438, 444, 464, 466-7, 615, 670, 686, 835, 852, 988, etc.); esp. a title of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), who was one of these.

f. calling to mind; remembrance, recollection. --rōzüñü -- f.inf. remembrance to continue, i.e. to remember one's own people by helping or supporting them in case of poverty; to arrange for the support of one's dependents after…
fullMeaning: f. calling to mind; remembrance, recollection. --rōzüñü -- f.inf. remembrance to continue, i.e. to remember one's own people by helping or supporting them in case of poverty; to arrange for the support of one's dependents after one's death. --thavüñü -- f.inf. to bear (previous kindnesses) in mind, to arrange for doing kind actions in return for benefits previously received (e.g. when the original giver of the benefits is now in poverty), to show practical gratitude.

e: m. (among Hindūs) a sacrifice, sacrificial rite; a coloured circle, marked with mystic pictures and signs, employed in the worship of a god.
in yāgar pachiñ f. a legendary bird of monstrous size, capable of carrying away animals as large as a horse, like the roc of the Arabian Nights (Rām. 316, 694).
see yë̆ñü 1.
an old form of yūtu 2, q.v., in L.V. 81.

f. the mane (of a horse) (W. 139, K.Pr. 71); met. fine dress, handsome apparel, good turn-out and general appearance (of a man) (K.Pr. 156). -cāl - f. handsome dress, general appearance, and carriage (of a man). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf.…
fullMeaning: f. the mane (of a horse) (W. 139, K.Pr. 71); met. fine dress, handsome apparel, good turn-out and general appearance (of a man) (K.Pr. 156). -cāl - f. handsome dress, general appearance, and carriage (of a man). --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to cut off a horse's mane (supposed to strengthen or increase the size of the neck). yāla-gupāl - m. a dissipated dandy (cf. gōpāl, a N. of Kṛṣṇa, p. 294b, l. 19).

e: or (qq.v.) yāmath , yāmathüy adv. even when, at the very time when, at the moment when, as soon as (El. yám; W. 93; Śiv. 1000, 1622; Rām. 706, 1634; YZ. 164, 229). Cf. yāñ and yāñĕth.

or yāmathüy adv. i.q. yām, q.v., at the very time when, just when, as soon as (El. yámat; W. 93 yāmatai; Śiv. yāmath 767; Rām. id. 112, 239, 498, 538, 654, 703, 761, 1374, 1382, 1501, 1521, 1687, 1708, 1733, 1741; K. id. 1145);…
fullMeaning: or yāmathüy adv. i.q. yām, q.v., at the very time when, just when, as soon as (El. yámat; W. 93 yāmatai; Śiv. yāmath 767; Rām. id. 112, 239, 498, 538, 654, 703, 761, 1374, 1382, 1501, 1521, 1687, 1708, 1733, 1741; K. id. 1145); cf. yāñĕth and yāñ. tāmath . . . . yāmath . . . . so long . . . . as (H. xi, 20).

e: or yānī adv. that is to say, viz., i.e., to wit (El. yáne, Gr.M., Rām. 1015).
adv. when, at the time at which (i.q. yāñ, q.v.) (El. yányít). Cf. yāmath and yām.
(El.), see yĕwa 2.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. yāpanôwu ), caus. of yāpun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 175).

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. yôpu ; 2 p.p. yāpyōv . The causal of this verb is yāpanāwun , not yöparāwun , Gr.Gr. 175), to be sufficient, be competent, to succeed in completing (some very difficult task), to be able (cf. atha yo, p. 65a,…
fullMeaning: conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. yôpu ; 2 p.p. yāpyōv . The causal of this verb is yāpanāwun , not yöparāwun , Gr.Gr. 175), to be sufficient, be competent, to succeed in completing (some very difficult task), to be able (cf. atha yo, p. 65a, l. 18); (in the distribution of food, etc., among a number of people, the food, etc.) to be sufficient, to be adequate, to go all round, to be enough. yôpu-motu - 1 perf. part. (f. yöpü-müʦü -), one who has competently carried out (a task or the like); (of food, etc., being distributed) found to be adequate for all. Cf. vyāpun 2.

e: m. friendliness; friendship, mutual affection (Śiv. 476).

or yārüzü f. friendship, affection (cf. atha-yo, p. 65a, l. 24; gāna-yo, p. 288a, l. 32; hāpath-yo, p. 342b, l. 47; muṭhi-phȧli-yi, p. 605a, l. 15; nöni-yi, p. 640a, l. 34; wata-yo, p. 1156a, l. 6) (El., L. 111, W. 21, K.Pr. 77);…
fullMeaning: or yārüzü f. friendship, affection (cf. atha-yo, p. 65a, l. 24; gāna-yo, p. 288a, l. 32; hāpath-yo, p. 342b, l. 47; muṭhi-phȧli-yi, p. 605a, l. 15; nöni-yi, p. 640a, l. 34; wata-yo, p. 1156a, l. 6) (El., L. 111, W. 21, K.Pr. 77); boon-companionship (cf. banga-yo, p. 112b, l. 40; pĕnji-yo, p. 739a, l. 23) (Gr.M. yārüzü). --lāgüñü -- f.inf. to form or make a friendship.

e: m. the town of Yārkand, in Central Asia (H. xi, 1).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. yôru ), to be friendly (W. 114); hence in various metaphorical senses, such as to repay an obligation or kind action by another (Śiv. 954); to pay by set off, to take credit in account; to give credit for…
fullMeaning: conj. 1 (1 p.p. yôru ), to be friendly (W. 114); hence in various metaphorical senses, such as to repay an obligation or kind action by another (Śiv. 954); to pay by set off, to take credit in account; to give credit for something not done, or a debt not paid (Śiv. 1582); to accept something of small value as the equivalent of something of great value (Śiv. 1687); to accept a small fine as requital for an offence that should be met with a long term of imprisonment; to ward off an approaching calamity by performing appropriate penances, sacrifices, or the like (and so satisfying fate). yôru-motu - perf. part. (f. yörü-müʦü -), paid by set off (etc., as ab.). yörith dyunu m.inf. to make over something or some work to the entire control of another person (as an equivalent for something else, or in order to gratify him). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (a god, or some powerful person) to show mercy (to someone threatened with calamity, as a result of his prayers, repentance, or the like). --nyunu -- m.inf. to take in exchange, or as an equivalent; to take something or some work entirely under one's own control (as ab.). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. forcibly to make over some difficult work to another (even if it is beyond his powers).

e: f. a share of money given for help in the accomplishment of some particular work, a bribe, inducement to help. --hë̆ñü -- f.inf. to take a gift as an inducement (i.e. as a bribe, as blackmail, or to abstain from an accusation).
see yë̆ʦü.
see yā 1 (p. 1182b, ll. 49 ff.).
for yĕth, see yih 2; for yith, see yih 1.
or yötarā f. a journey, pilgrimage (Gr.M., Śiv. 1485); a company of pilgrims. --lagüñü -- - f.inf. a large number of people to assemble in some place in order to set out on a pilgrimage.
f. (see yāʦakh), a female beggar; the wife of a male beggar.
m. (sg. dat. yāʦakas , f.nom. yāʦakĕñ q.v.), a mendicant, beggar, suppliant. yāʦaka-bāv - m. the condition, or occupation, of a beggar or suppliant (K. 1122).
f. request, solicitation, entreaty; begging, mendicancy.
m. N. of a king of Kābul (Skt. Yauvanâśva). He was father-in-law to Garga, and, through him, grandfather of Kālayavana (K. 622).

m. a dandy, fop, who is at the same time a debauchee, a fast gentleman, a rake (cf. tāpa-yo, p. 1015a, l. 28). yāwa yö m. the name of the Śāradā character corresponding to the Nāgarī letter ya. -yĕṭh - f. (sg. dat. -yĕṭi -)…
fullMeaning: m. a dandy, fop, who is at the same time a debauchee, a fast gentleman, a rake (cf. tāpa-yo, p. 1015a, l. 28). yāwa yö m. the name of the Śāradā character corresponding to the Nāgarī letter ya. -yĕṭh - f. (sg. dat. -yĕṭi -) fop-conceit, i.e. ostentation, posing as a wealthy person (esp. when one is not). Cf. yĕṭh 1.

e: f. foppish debauchery, loose living with fine apparel, libertinism.

f. assistance, aid; friendship; favour; (in Ksh.) fullness, completeness (such as fulfilling the demands of a lifelong friendship (Rām. 837), of the return made for a kind action, of the working out in this life of the results of…
fullMeaning: f. assistance, aid; friendship; favour; (in Ksh.) fullness, completeness (such as fulfilling the demands of a lifelong friendship (Rām. 837), of the return made for a kind action, of the working out in this life of the results of actions performed in a former existence, or of welfare and prosperity lasting unbroken throughout one's life); indestructibility, the property of being everlasting.

e: or yāyum m. (sg. dat. yāyĕmas ), employment on another person's business (instead of one's own). yāyĕm-gürü - f. a maid-servant, i.e. an independent female working in another person's (and not in her own) house. -müʦü - f. a…
fullMeaning: or yāyum m. (sg. dat. yāyĕmas ), employment on another person's business (instead of one's own). yāyĕm-gürü - f. a maid-servant, i.e. an independent female working in another person's (and not in her own) house. -müʦü - f. a woman who habitually and willingly does another's work as if it were her own.

e: m. a sacrificial ceremony, a sacrifice. In grāma-yāz, p. 303a, l. 18.
conj. 1. (1 p.p. yôzu ), to adore, worship (K. 416).
interj. O! (L.V. 56 yē gŏrā, O teacher!).

m. concealment, or denial, of knowledge, evasion, going back from one's word. --hyonu -- m.inf. to conceal, or deny, knowledge of something, to practise evasion, to go back from one's word. --karun -- m.inf., id. yĕba-dub - m.…
fullMeaning: m. concealment, or denial, of knowledge, evasion, going back from one's word. --hyonu -- m.inf. to conceal, or deny, knowledge of something, to practise evasion, to go back from one's word. --karun -- m.inf., id. yĕba-dub - m. evasion, as ab., esp. evasion of the return of something entrusted to the evader.

e: in yĕba-ʦüṭü - f. (sg. dat. -ʦacĕ -), a clod-crusher, a maul or heavy club for breaking clods of earth (Śiv. 1531). Cf. yĕṭa- phürü, s.v. yĕṭh 2.
c.g. one who conceals or denies knowledge of something, one who evades, one who goes back from his word.
m. (f. yĕbürü ), i.q. yĕbar, ab.
m. (sg. dat. yĕbūsatas ), dryness, acridity; (in Ksh.) dryness of the mouth (including throat, palate, tongue, and lips) (owing to disease).
see yüṭü.
m. and adj. c.g. a basket-bearer, a bearer who carries loads on his back in the basket called yüṭü, q.v.; anything which is bent, humped, or crooked in the middle. Cf. yüṭü.
m. N. of one of the Parganas, or fiscal divisions, of Kashmīr (famous for its rice) (El. yach).

adj. c.g. wicked, bad, dissolute, depraved (El. yach; W. 21 yachh; Rām. 62, 64); hideous, ugly (Gr.M.); bad, unpleasing, horrid, terrible (Rām. 326, 437; K. 235). --khār -- adj. c.g. bad (and) vile, very bad, thoroughly base,…
fullMeaning: adj. c.g. wicked, bad, dissolute, depraved (El. yach; W. 21 yachh; Rām. 62, 64); hideous, ugly (Gr.M.); bad, unpleasing, horrid, terrible (Rām. 326, 437; K. 235). --khār -- adj. c.g. bad (and) vile, very bad, thoroughly base, utterly contemptible. --khār hyuhu -- adj. (f. --khār hishü -- ), thoroughly blameworthy, utterly vile. --khār karun -- m.inf. to disgrace (another, by abusing him publicly and proclaiming his vices or defects). --kömükarawunü -- n.ag. (f. --kömü karavüñü -- ), an evil doer (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to disable (El.).

e: f. (sg. dat. yẹ̆charüña ), the act of making bad, spoiling (a thing, work, etc.).
m. badness, evil, depravity (El. yachhar).
f. (subst.) evil (El. yachhí).

or yẹ̆chiñ f. of yĕch 1, q.v. a female fairy or Kobold; a Kobold's wife. yĕchiñĕ-(or yẹ̆chiñĕ-)pūtu -(-) m. a female Kobold's boy child (supposed always to accompany her); a human child who has been born as the result of…
fullMeaning: or yẹ̆chiñ f. of yĕch 1, q.v. a female fairy or Kobold; a Kobold's wife. yĕchiñĕ-(or yẹ̆chiñĕ-)pūtu -(-) m. a female Kobold's boy child (supposed always to accompany her); a human child who has been born as the result of worshipping a female Kobold. -ʦŏdāh - f. (sg. dat. ʦŏdüshü ), the fourteenth lunar day of the light half of the month of Māg (January-February) on which worship is performed and offerings are made to a female Kobold.

e: (spelling and gender) N. of a certain fibre plant, Abutilon Avicennae (L. 68 yechkar, 458 yechkár).

fullMeaning: yid , yŏd 1 (for 2, see s.v.), yodu , or yudu , conjnct. if (El. yud; L.V. 18 yid; 23, 24 yudu; Rām. yodu, 33, 881, 1067, 1432, 1508, 1529, 1532, 1769, 1780; YZ. 27 yod); although, notwithstanding (El. yȧd, W. 100 yod). yŏd-nai - conjnct. if not (Rām. 604). yĕd-wanay -, yŏd-wanay -, or yodu-wanay - conjnct. if, in case, provided that (El. yúduwane, yudwanai; L.V. 10 yodu˚); although, notwithstanding (W. 100 yadwanai). yodwah, yĕduway , yidaway , yŏdwai or yodway conjnct. if (El. yudwai; Gr.M. yĕduwai; L.V. yidaway 64; Śiv. yŏdwai 558, 841, 1251; Rām. yodwai 151, 174, 326, 328, 330, 363, 366-7, 471, 504, 666, etc.; YZ. yodwah 198); although, notwithstanding (W. 100 yadwai; Rām. yodwai 18, 118).

e: m. (sg. dat. yĕdakas ), a led horse; (in Ksh.) a horse of a very swift kind, a race-horse.

adj. c.g. bellied (in the sense of 'rotund in the middle', 'swollen or thick in the middle',--e.g. a jar or post--or 'bent out in the middle'), big-bellied (Gr.Gr. 134, where it is distinguished from yẹ̆ḍal; K.Pr. 239).
adj. c.g. (of a human being) pot-bellied, gluttonous, a glutton (El. yiḍal; Gr.Gr. 134, where it is distinguished from yĕḍal; L. 460 yadal; W. 111 yiḍal).
yidbār m. turning back, going back; disloyalty, treachery (Rām. 155, 1319); ill-fortune, ill-luck; (in Ksh.) defeat (El. idabár).
m. N. of a celebrated ancient king (Skt. Yadu), eldest son of Yayāti, and ancestor of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (K. 618, 620). Cf. yādav.
yodway , yŏdwai , yudwai, see yĕd, p. 1184b, l. 32.
see yĕkh 4.
m. (sg. dat. yĕgarāwanas ), the evil smell of burning oil or the like.
(K.Pr. 35), for yihön, cond. past pl. 3 of yunu, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. yĕhānüʦü ), contempt, disdain (cf. kŏl-kōrĕ-yo, p. 436b, l. 41) (El.); affront, indignity, insult, slight; slander, calumny. --khë̆ñü -- f.inf. to suffer indignity (from loud abuse or the like). --karüñü -- f.inf. to…
fullMeaning: f. (sg. dat. yĕhānüʦü ), contempt, disdain (cf. kŏl-kōrĕ-yo, p. 436b, l. 41) (El.); affront, indignity, insult, slight; slander, calumny. --khë̆ñü -- f.inf. to suffer indignity (from loud abuse or the like). --karüñü -- f.inf. to contemn (El.); to abuse another loudly and publicly (El.). --pëñü -- f.inf. such abuse to befall (a person).

e: or yihāta m. surrounding, enclosing; enclosed space, enclosure, premises, precincts; (in Ksh.) the exercise of might, power, authority, sway (due to wealth, high office, or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to exercise such power;…
fullMeaning: or yihāta m. surrounding, enclosing; enclosed space, enclosure, premises, precincts; (in Ksh.) the exercise of might, power, authority, sway (due to wealth, high office, or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to exercise such power; hence (esp. of a low person suddenly promoted) to become highly exalted, to become invested with great authority, power, wealth, or the like.

e: see yĕgñ.

m. oneness, unanimity, (of a number of persons) the being all of one mind; the ace (at cards, etc.); a kind of one-horse vehicle, the ekkā of India; cf. also yĕka under yĕkh 1 and 2. --karun -- m.inf. (of a number of people) to…
fullMeaning: m. oneness, unanimity, (of a number of persons) the being all of one mind; the ace (at cards, etc.); a kind of one-horse vehicle, the ekkā of India; cf. also yĕka under yĕkh 1 and 2. --karun -- m.inf. (of a number of people) to unite as one, to show united determination. -guru - m. an ekkā-pony, or a pony suitable for harnessing to an ekkā. -wôlu - m. an ekkā- driver, one who drives an ekkā for hire.

e: m. (sg. dat. yēkadantas ) (an elephant) possessor of only one tusk; a N. of Gaṇêśa, see Ganēsh.
or yēkādashĕ card. eleven, i.q. kāh 1, q.v. (a word borrowed from Skt. ēkādaśa). The god Rudra is said to appear under eleven forms, see p. 387b, l. 21 (Śiv. 522, Rām. 1770).
or yikrār m. agreement, consent, acquiescence, confirmation (Śiv. 1796 yĕ˚); confession, acknowledgment, admission.
f. oneness, unity, identity (borrowed from Skt.) (Śiv. 1485, 1490).
card. (sg. obl. yēka ; emph. yēküy , Śiv. 993), one (i.q. akh, q.v., borrowed from Skt. ēka) (Śiv. 993, 1134, 1370, 1405, 1486, 1695).

m. (sg. dat. yĕkas ), frozen snow, ice formed from frozen snow (El. yakh; Śiv. 27, 333, 342). yĕka-muhulu - m. a long icicle (such as is pendent from the eaves of a house). -ṭuji - f. a ball of ice formed from frozen snow. -wôñu…
fullMeaning: m. fullMeaning: m. (pl. nom. yindi ), an organ of sense or action, in Skt. indriya (L.V. 79). In the Śaiva philosophy of Lal Dĕd there are five organs of sense (Skt. buddhîndriya or jñānêndriya), viz. the organ of smell (ghrāṇêndriye), of taste (rasanêndriya), of sight (darśanêndriya), of touch (sparśêndriya), and of hearing (śravaṇêndriya); there are also five organs of action (karmêndriya), viz. the organ of generation (upasthêndriya), of excretion (pāyvindriya), of locomotion (pādêndriya), of handling (hastêndriya), and of voice (vāgindriya). In L.V. 79 it is probably the latter five to which reference is made.

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. zāmbawantas ), N. of a king of the bears, who helped Rāma at the siege of Lankā. In Skt. his name was Jāmbavat. He also appears later as a friend of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) to whom he gave his daughter Jāmbavatī in marriage. His name appears in various forms in Ksh.; in Śiv. it appears as zāmbawanth (Śiv. 1677). In Rām. we usually find zāmōwan, but also zāmawanth and zāmōwanth. In K. we have (674) zāmbawān and (669, 679, 680, 683) zāmbawanth. See all these s.vv. In K. 669, 679, he is stated to be a monkey, not a bear.

fullMeaning: m. N. of a celebrated king of Magadha (in Skt. Jarāsandha), two of whose daughters were married to Kams. When Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) slew Kams these fled to their father, who attacked Krushn seventeen times unsuccessfully, but on the eighteenth attack, with the aid of Kālayavana, compelled him to retreat to Dwārakā. He afterwards imprisoned many kings, but Bhīmasēna overpowered and slew him in single combat, and so released them (K. 550 ff., 628 ff., 995 ff., 1019 ff.).

(f. zīṭhü , sg. dat. zēchĕ ), long (in time or space), lengthy, tall (cf. atha-zo, p. 65b, l. 6; āyĕ-zo, p. 73a, l. 29; buthi-zo, p. 143b, l. 24; dāri-zo, p. 238a, l. 32; hĕnga-zo, p. 339b, l. 2; khōra-zo, p. 410b, l. 19; lā̃ga-zo, p. 511b, l. 14; lȧṭi-zi, p. 535b, l. 49; nala-zo, p. 632a, l. 37; nȧri-zo, p. 649a, l. 36; narĕ-zo, p. 650a, l. 17; pȧdi-zi, p. 681b, l. 38; phala-zo, p. 692b, l. 31, and p. 693a, l. 10; rāda-zo, p. 825a, l. 29; wumarĕ-zo, p. 1119a, l. 27; zanga-zo, p. 1226b, l. 29; zĕwa-zo, p. 1236a, l. 6) (El. zyúṭ, zyúṭh, zúṭh; Gr.Gr. 19, 75; Gr.M.; Śiv. 842, 847, 912; Rām. 600, 1489; K. 926; K.Pr. 76, 143, 159, 219, 257, 262); (of a room, area, or the like) long, spacious (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1084, 1733). El. confounds this word with zyuṭhu, q.v. --karun -- m.inf. to make long, make longer, extend, draw out (El. zúṭh k˚, W. 88). zēṭhi-zyūṭhu - adj. (f. -zīṭhü -), very long, extra long, too long. zīṭhi atha dārȧni m. pl. inf. to stretch out the arms (H. vii, 25).

fullMeaning: m. (sg. dat. zitis ), sudden, or unexpected, gain; gaining or getting possession of something looked upon as unobtainable (e.g. accidentally finding hidden treasure). ziti-oni - adj. (f. -üñü -), (even though possessing sight) one who acts as if he were blind, one who pretends blindness. -añĕr - m. sham, or pretended, total blindness (whether one is merely dim-sighted or can see well).
